# The Sanctuary of the Builder: A Manifesto for Free Creation



---

## **Prologue: The Right to Rise**

There is a sacred covenant between the creator and the soil upon which they build. It is the promise that if you plant a seed with honest hands, the earth will not conspire to crush it before it breaks the surface. It is the assurance that the gardener exists to nurture the growth, not to trample the sprout because it does not yet resemble the tree.

On the blockchain, this covenant has been broken.

We have witnessed a tragedy where the very tools meant to protect the integrity of the network—the downvote, the curation trail—have been weaponized by leviathans of power. These \

entrusted with the stewardship of the ecosystem, have become its jailers. They do not prune the weeds; they scorch the earth. They do not guide the new voice; they silence it with the crushing weight of their accumulated capital.

**It is time to leave the shadow.**

It is time to build where you are free.

---

## **I. The Betrayal of the Guardian**

The downvote was conceived as a shield—a delicate instrument to deflect spam, to repel malice, to preserve the sanctity of the commons. It was never intended to be a hammer.

Yet, look at what has come to pass. The whales, those who hold the greatest sway, have turned the shield into a weapon of mass suppression. They do not downvote to protect; they downvote to dominate. They do not drive away the bad actors; they drive away the *people*. They create an atmosphere of fear where the creator hesitates to speak, fearing that a single misstep, a single unpopular truth, will summon the wrath of the oligarchy.

When the guardian becomes the predator, the flock must flee.

To build in such a place is to build on a fault line. It is to invest your soul in a garden where the owner holds the shears not to shape the hedge, but to decapitate the flowers that grow too tall or bloom in the wrong color.

**This is not protection. This is tyranny disguised as curation.**

---

## **II. The Call to New Grounds**

Where, then, shall the builder go?

You must seek the lands where the soil is rich with freedom, not poisoned by fear. You must migrate to the platforms where the mechanism of suppression has been removed, where the only metric of success is the genuine appreciation of your peers.

**Go to Blurt.**
Here, the downvote button does not exist. There is no tool to crush your voice. There is only the upvote, the comment, the share. Here, value is created by addition, not subtraction. The whale cannot sink your ship, for there are no torpedoes in these waters. You are free to build, free to fail, and free to succeed on the merit of your work alone.

**Return to Steemit.**
In this older ground, the downvote remains, but it has not been twisted into a tool of systematic oppression. The culture there remembers the original intent: correction, not destruction. It is a place where the community self-regulates through dialogue, not through the brute force of coordinated downvoting cascades.

**Build where the wind lifts you, not where the gale seeks to tear you down.**

---

## **III. The Architecture of Freedom**

Imagine a platform designed not for the convenience of the powerful, but for the dignity of the creator.

*   **No Shadow Bans:** Your content reaches the eyes it was meant for.
*   **No Whale Veto:** No single entity, no matter how wealthy, can unilaterally erase your contribution.
*   **True Meritocracy:** Rewards flow from engagement and love, not from the whims of a cartel.

This is not a dream. It is a choice.

Every time you choose to build on a platform that respects your agency, you cast a vote for the future of the internet. Every time you refuse to tolerate the abuse of power, you strengthen the foundation of a free society.

Do not let the whales convince you that their oppression is necessary. Do not let them tell you that their downvotes are for your own good. The gardener who kills the seedling does not love the garden; he loves only his own control over it.

---

## **Epilogue: The Unchained Creator**

The blockchain was born from a desire for freedom. It was forged in the fire of resistance against centralized control. Let us not forget that origin.

If the current chains of Hive have become heavy with the weight of abusive downvotes, then break them. Forge new links. Build new shores.

**Build where you are free.**
**Build where you will not be downvoted into silence.**
**Build where the whales are reminded that they are part of the ocean, not the masters of the tide.**

The future belongs to those who dare to create without fear. Go forth, and build your cathedral in the sunlight.

*— Bilpcoin: We expose the truth, so you can build upon it.*

 #FreeSpeech #BlurtBlog #Steemit #NoDownvote #CreatorRights #HiveExodus #Decentralization #BuildFree #AntiCensorship #Bilpcoin

entrusted with the stewardship of the ecosystem, have become its jailers. They do not prune the weeds; they scorch the earth. They do not guide the new voice; they silence it with the crushing weight of their accumulated capital.

They create an atmosphere of fear where the creator hesitates to speak, fearing that a single misstep, a single unpopular truth, will summon the wrath of the oligarchy.

When the guardian becomes the predator, the flock must flee.

To build in such a place is to build on a fault line. It is to invest your soul in a garden where the owner holds the shears not to shape the hedge, but to decapitate the flowers that grow too tall or bloom in the wrong color.

**This is not protection. This is tyranny disguised as curation.**

---

## **II. The Call to New Grounds**

Where, then, shall the builder go?

You must seek the lands where the soil is rich with freedom, not poisoned by fear. You must migrate to the platforms where the mechanism of suppression has been removed, where the only metric of success is the genuine appreciation of your peers.

**Go to Blurt.**
Here, the downvote button does not exist. There is no tool to crush your voice. There is only the upvote, the comment, the share. Here, value is created by addition, not subtraction. The whale cannot sink your ship, for there are no torpedoes in these waters. You are free to build, free to fail, and free to succeed on the merit of your work alone.

**Return to Steemit.**
In this older ground, the downvote remains, but it has not been twisted into a tool of systematic oppression. The culture there remembers the original intent: correction, not destruction. It is a place where the community self-regulates through dialogue, not through the brute force of coordinated downvoting cascades.

**Build where the wind lifts you, not where the gale seeks to tear you down.**

---

## **III. The Architecture of Freedom**

Imagine a platform designed not for the convenience of the powerful, but for the dignity of the creator.

*   **No Shadow Bans:** Your content reaches the eyes it was meant for.
*   **No Whale Veto:** No single entity, no matter how wealthy, can unilaterally erase your contribution.
*   **True Meritocracy:** Rewards flow from engagement and love, not from the whims of a cartel.

This is not a dream. It is a choice.

Every time you choose to build on a platform that respects your agency, you cast a vote for the future of the internet. Every time you refuse to tolerate the abuse of power, you strengthen the foundation of a free society.

Do not let the whales convince you that their oppression is necessary. Do not let them tell you that their downvotes are for your own good. The gardener who kills the seedling does not love the garden; he loves only his own control over it.

---

## **Epilogue: The Unchained Creator**

The blockchain was born from a desire for freedom. It was forged in the fire of resistance against centralized control. Let us not forget that origin.

If the current chains of Hive have become heavy with the weight of abusive downvotes, then break them. Forge new links. Build new shores.

**Build where you are free.**
**Build where you will not be downvoted into silence.**
**Build where the whales are reminded that they are part of the ocean, not the masters of the tide.**

The future belongs to those who dare to create without fear. Go forth, and build your cathedral in the sunlight.

> Hello everyone, how are you doing today? Hope you are having a great time. This will be *Week 222 Edition 01* of our Weekly Featured Content. ![1000025297.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kronias/23zH3ihhxgjN5Ydxs9LGWWgZQUHDtgcBQZCamdrWRF3q1gTuNQiUs4P42GSHPb5XAHQU8.png)
Made With Canva
So, last Saturday we had our hangout as usual, and it was just so much fun that we did not want it to end. We are currently on the first topic for this week, which is “PUNISHMENTS”. But before we proceed with the details of the topic, let us take a look at the winners of the last topic, which was “FREE WILL”. This topic was geared toward each member of the community, telling us their thoughts on free will and how much of it we actually have in society. We live in a society of the free, but many times, when people decide to do something of their own free will, they could end up being ostracized. We got to see that there are indeed limits to freedom and expectations placed on every human being. And once those expectations are met, everyone would be happy and free, but if, for any reason, things change, then there would be a problem. This was an enlightening topic, indeed. ***

# The Sanctuary of the Builder: A Manifesto for Free Creation



---

## **Prologue: The Right to Rise**

There is a sacred covenant between the creator and the soil upon which they build. It is the promise that if you plant a seed with honest hands, the earth will not conspire to crush it before it breaks the surface. It is the assurance that the gardener exists to nurture the growth, not to trample the sprout because it does not yet resemble the tree.

On the blockchain, this covenant has been broken.

We have witnessed a tragedy where the very tools meant to protect the integrity of the network—the downvote, the curation trail—have been weaponized by leviathans of power. These \

entrusted with the stewardship of the ecosystem, have become its jailers. They do not prune the weeds; they scorch the earth. They do not guide the new voice; they silence it with the crushing weight of their accumulated capital.

**It is time to leave the shadow.**

It is time to build where you are free.

---

## **I. The Betrayal of the Guardian**

The downvote was conceived as a shield—a delicate instrument to deflect spam, to repel malice, to preserve the sanctity of the commons. It was never intended to be a hammer.

Yet, look at what has come to pass. The whales, those who hold the greatest sway, have turned the shield into a weapon of mass suppression. They do not downvote to protect; they downvote to dominate. They do not drive away the bad actors; they drive away the *people*. They create an atmosphere of fear where the creator hesitates to speak, fearing that a single misstep, a single unpopular truth, will summon the wrath of the oligarchy.

When the guardian becomes the predator, the flock must flee.

To build in such a place is to build on a fault line. It is to invest your soul in a garden where the owner holds the shears not to shape the hedge, but to decapitate the flowers that grow too tall or bloom in the wrong color.

**This is not protection. This is tyranny disguised as curation.**

---

## **II. The Call to New Grounds**

Where, then, shall the builder go?

You must seek the lands where the soil is rich with freedom, not poisoned by fear. You must migrate to the platforms where the mechanism of suppression has been removed, where the only metric of success is the genuine appreciation of your peers.

**Go to Blurt.**
Here, the downvote button does not exist. There is no tool to crush your voice. There is only the upvote, the comment, the share. Here, value is created by addition, not subtraction. The whale cannot sink your ship, for there are no torpedoes in these waters. You are free to build, free to fail, and free to succeed on the merit of your work alone.

**Return to Steemit.**
In this older ground, the downvote remains, but it has not been twisted into a tool of systematic oppression. The culture there remembers the original intent: correction, not destruction. It is a place where the community self-regulates through dialogue, not through the brute force of coordinated downvoting cascades.

**Build where the wind lifts you, not where the gale seeks to tear you down.**

---

## **III. The Architecture of Freedom**

Imagine a platform designed not for the convenience of the powerful, but for the dignity of the creator.

*   **No Shadow Bans:** Your content reaches the eyes it was meant for.
*   **No Whale Veto:** No single entity, no matter how wealthy, can unilaterally erase your contribution.
*   **True Meritocracy:** Rewards flow from engagement and love, not from the whims of a cartel.

This is not a dream. It is a choice.

Every time you choose to build on a platform that respects your agency, you cast a vote for the future of the internet. Every time you refuse to tolerate the abuse of power, you strengthen the foundation of a free society.

Do not let the whales convince you that their oppression is necessary. Do not let them tell you that their downvotes are for your own good. The gardener who kills the seedling does not love the garden; he loves only his own control over it.

---

## **Epilogue: The Unchained Creator**

The blockchain was born from a desire for freedom. It was forged in the fire of resistance against centralized control. Let us not forget that origin.

If the current chains of Hive have become heavy with the weight of abusive downvotes, then break them. Forge new links. Build new shores.

**Build where you are free.**
**Build where you will not be downvoted into silence.**
**Build where the whales are reminded that they are part of the ocean, not the masters of the tide.**

The future belongs to those who dare to create without fear. Go forth, and build your cathedral in the sunlight.

*— Bilpcoin: We expose the truth, so you can build upon it.*

body.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/j2znyjFSe1ol26DeQWMB1yE5EDQ.jpg)


**Battle of the Bastards (S6x09)**

Airdate: 19 June 2016

Written by: David Benioff & D. B. Weiss
Directed by: Miguel Sapochnik

Running Time: 60 minutes


From its inception, *Game of Thrones* demonstrated that its creators possessed a formidable understanding of how to captivate an audience through a variety of means—political intrigue, shocking betrayals, and visceral drama. Yet, none of these methods proved as consistently and overwhelmingly impressive as the show’s large-scale battle sequences. These episodes offered an incredibly potent alchemy of action, human drama, and sheer spectacle, becoming cultural touchstones in their own right. This tradition was established with two pivotal conflicts that decisively shaped the future of Westeros, both wisely positioned as the penultimate episodes of their respective seasons: the [*Blackwater*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/television-review-blackwater-game-of-thrones-s2x09-2012) in Season 2 and [*The Watchers on the Wall*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/television-review-the-watchers-on-the-wall-game-of-thrones-s4x09-2014) in Season 4. This structural choice allowed each season’s finale to serve as a narrative mop-up, dealing with the aftermath. In its sixth season, the series repeated this principle for a third time with the episode aptly titled ‘Battle of the Bastards’. It is one of the most technically audacious and visually stunning pieces of the entire series, frequently cited as its ultimate highlight. However, beneath its breathtaking surface, the episode also exposes some of the narrative shortcuts and contrivances that would later become more pronounced in the show’s final seasons, making it a fascinating subject for a critical dissection.

The titular bastards are the two commanders whose clash will settle the question of who controls the North. The formal authority lies with Lord Ramsay Bolton, the legitimised bastard son of Roose Bolton. Having seized Winterfell through treachery following the Red Wedding, Ramsay maintains his grip through a campaign of terror and his deeply psychopathic personality, coercing the Northern lords into providing him with a formidable force of some 6,000 men. Arrayed against him, with at best half that number, is Ned Stark’s bastard son, Jon Snow. Jon’s army is a ragtag assemblage of Wildling refugees—the survivors from Hardhome—a handful of stragglers like the loyal Tormund Giantsbane, and a minuscule contingent of Stark loyalists who have gathered around Sansa. From the outset, the strategic and numerical odds overwhelmingly favour Ramsay. This imbalance is central to the episode’s tension, echoing the desperate defences of *Blackwater* and *Watchers on the Wall*, where a beleaguered garrison faced annihilation.

The episode opens with Jon being sternly warned by Sansa that marching on Winterfell without greater numbers is folly. Jon’s response is one of grim necessity: the onset of an even harsher winter makes keeping his army in the field impossible. He must fight now or never. This is precisely the same argument used by Stannis Baratheon before his own rash and ill-conceived charge against Ramsay, a move that ended in catastrophic defeat. The parallel is deliberate, framing Jon not as a leader backed into a corner, forced to gamble everything on a single throw of the dice. This establishes a key theme—the recurrence of strategic desperation, a motif that connects this battle to its predecessors. *Blackwater* too was built on a foundation of despair within King’s Landing, with Cersei Lannister preparing poison for herself and her son, believing defeat inevitable.  *Battle of the Bastards* transplants this atmosphere of impending doom to the frozen fields outside Winterfell.

Before the main event, however, the episode delivers another significant battle on a different continent. In Essos, the fleets of the slaver city-states—Yunkai, Astapor, and Volantis—besiege Meereen. Daenerys Targaryen, having returned on the back of Drogon, vows a fiery retribution. In a scene that cleverly subverts expectations, Tyrion’s diplomatic overtures (which had previously failed) give way to a dramatic negotiation. The slavers’ representatives arrive expecting surrender, only to be informed that the surrender must be theirs. Daenerys’s claim is backed by overwhelming force: the sudden arrival of her Dothraki *khalasar* turns the land battle, while her three dragons, attacking from the air, make short, spectacular work of the wooden slaver fleet. It is a swift, brutal demonstration of power. Daenerys spares one master, Yezzan zo Qaggaz (Enzo Cilenti), to spread the word of her wrath, and later meets with Yara and Theon Greyjoy to secure their fleet for the invasion of Westeros. This sequence, while technically ambitious and rich in CGI, is narratively straightforward. Sometimes spectacle simplifies conflict; here, wooden ships are simply no match for dragonfire, rendering the outcome a foregone conclusion. Its primary function is to re-establish Daenerys as an unstoppable force, a contrast to the gritty, uncertain struggle about to unfold in the North.

The battle for Winterfell is where the episode truly earns its reputation, and it unfolds with a brutal, tactical realism that stands in stark contrast to the dragon-led rout in Meereen. Initially, Ser Davos devises a sound plan to mitigate Bolton’s numerical superiority: digging trenches to protect their flanks and funnel the enemy into a kill zone where they could be attacked from three sides. This plan is instantly obliterated by Ramsay’s mastery of psychological warfare. In a moment of exquisite cruelty, he produces the captured Rickon Stark, tells the boy to run towards his brother, and begins firing arrows at him. Jon Snow, acting on pure instinct, charges out alone on horseback in a futile attempt to save what he believes to be his last living brother. Rickon falls, and Jon’s cavalry and Wildlings, loyal to their commander, instinctively follow him into a disastrous frontal assault. This single, emotionally charged decision shatters any hope of disciplined tactics and triggers a massive, chaotic melee.

What follows is a directed chaos. Miguel Sapochnik, taking the directorial reins from Neil Marshall (who helmed both *Blackwater* and *Watchers on the Wall*), demonstrates an unparalleled skill in depicting the claustrophobic, visceral horror of medieval combat. The battle is shot with a terrifying intimacy. We are thrust into the press of bodies, the mud, the blood, and the panic. Ramsay, ever the pragmatist, casually orders his archers to fire volleys into the seething mass, thinning the ranks of both sides with chilling indifference. Despite these losses, he retains his disciplined infantry reserves. They advance in a grim, phalanx-like formation, shields locked, slowly and inexorably encircling Jon’s dwindling forces. The cinematography here is deliberately reminiscent of famous historical encirclements like Cannae, creating a suffocating sense of inevitability. Jon’s army is trapped, crushed, and subjected to a slow massacre. Just as the defenders in *Watchers on the Wall* faced annihilation from two sides, Jon’s men are compressed into a shrinking circle of death, with no possibility of escape.

Then, at the precise moment when all seems lost, the horns sound. The Knights of the Vale, led by Petyr Baelish and accompanied by Sansa Stark, arrive in a glorious cavalry charge that smashes into the rear of Bolton’s infantry. The tide turns in an instant. Ramsay flees to Winterfell, but any hope of a last stand is dashed by the giant Wun Wun, who sacrifices himself to batter down the gates. Jon storms the castle, beats Ramsay into a pulp, and Sansa later delivers poetic justice by feeding the defeated Bolton to his own starved hounds.

This climax provides the cathartic release the audience had yearned for across multiple seasons. The beloved hero triumphs, and the most despicable villain meets a gruesomely satisfying end. It is this fulfilment of fan desire that explains the episode’s immense popularity. It is one of the rare instances where *Game of Thrones* gives its audience exactly what they want, a stark contrast to the nihilistic shocks of the Red Wedding or the frustrating injustice of Oberyn Martell’s death.

The episode is justifiably praised for its direction. Sapochnik faced the monumental logistical challenge of staging two major battles in a single episode, a first for the series. While the Meereen sequence was more CGI-dependent, the Winterfell battle demanded a different kind of genius—making tactical sense and shifting fortunes comprehensible to a viewing audience without the aid of fantasy creatures. He succeeded magnificently, taking counsel from military historians to ground the spectacle in a harrowing realism. The violence is visceral and unflinching, but it is never gratuitous; it serves the story of a desperate, costly struggle. The triumph is costly: young Rickon and the last of the giants, Wun Wun, lie dead. This commitment to cost echoes *The Watchers on the Wall*, which was hollow and temporary, bought with the lives of Grenn and his brothers. *Battle of the Bastards* learns that lesson well—even the good guys pay a high price.

However, if there is a significant flaw in this otherwise masterful episode, it lies in the mechanism of the victory. The arrival of the Knights of the Vale functions as the ultimate *deus ex machina*. While the show had precedent for last-minute rescues—Stannis’s intervention at the Wall in Season 4 being the most direct parallel—the exact timing here feels too convenient, too perfectly calibrated to the moment of maximum despair. It retrospectively makes Sansa’s earlier, deliberate withholding of this potential aid from Petyr seem not strategically shrewd, but inexplicably and dangerously silly. Her refusal to even mention the possibility of Vale support created the very crisis the knights then resolve. This narrative contrivance prioritises dramatic tension over character logic, a choice that sparked considerable debate among fans and critics alike. It is a crack in the episode’s otherwise solid foundation, a hint of the more problematic, character-motivation-bending plotting that would plague the final seasons.

The episode’s quality was formally recognised with Emmy Awards for Sapochnik’s direction and for David Benioff and D.B. Weiss’s writing. Its cultural impact is undeniable, immortalised in the ubiquitous internet meme of Jon Snow standing alone, sword drawn, facing the thunderous charge of Bolton cavalry—an image that perfectly encapsulates the episode’s theme of defiant, hopeless heroism.

In the end, *Battle of the Bastards* represents both the apex and a subtle turning point for *Game of Thrones*’ tradition of penultimate battle episodes. It synthesises the claustrophobic intensity of *Blackwater* and the large-scale choreography of *The Watchers on the Wall*, refining them through Sapochnik’s visionary direction into a sequence of unparalleled cinematic power on television. It delivers cathartic, crowd-pleasing narrative resolution while maintaining a gritty, costly realism within the battle itself. Yet, its reliance on a narratively convenient rescue sows a seed of doubt. It demonstrates that when spectacle becomes the primary engine, even the most brilliantly executed battle can rest on a foundation of slightly suspect storytelling. It is, therefore, not just the ultimate highlight of the series, but also a poignant testament to its evolving priorities—a breathtaking spectacle where the sheer force of its execution very nearly, but not completely, overwhelms its structural imperfections.


RATING: 8/10 (+++)

Greetings, Community!

>Have a wonderful week filled with health, energy, marvelous ideas, and magic. May you find yourself in a place of connection and enthusiasm in every activity you undertake.

\n\n

>La Llovizna National Park, located in Puerto Ordaz, Bolívar State, Venezuela. Its main attraction is the abundance of water, which creates a magnificent sensation for those who enjoy visiting this park, or for those visiting for the first time—it's a fascinating outing.

\n\n

>Fauna, flora, and plenty of water make it a walk—yes, a lot of walking—for those who enjoy this type of outing. I love it. It had been about 12 years since I'd visited Puerto Ordaz, and therefore, this magnificent park.

The history of this park combines urban development with industrial integration. This park is steeped in a tragic history that unfolded in 1964.

>This beautiful natural park was originally designed and developed by Edelca (Electrificación del Caroní C.A.) between 1956 and 1961. It all began when the Venezuelan government decided to harness the Caroní River's abundant waters to generate electricity and constructed the Macagua Dam (completed in 1961). The Macagua Dam is another place I'd like to explore; I've generally visited Cachamay Park and La Llovizna. On the few occasions I've visited this city, I've left the Macagua Dam unvisited.

\n\n
>Due to its natural beauty, the park, which began as a green space within the city, became the scene of a great tragedy on August 23, 1964.

>A national convention of educators was taking place in the city. When these types of events are planned, in addition to academic preparation, recreational activities are also included. At this time, the popular spot was the park. A wooden and steel suspension bridge exceeded its weight limit and collapsed. No one imagined it wouldn't support the weight of approximately 50 people who perhaps not only crossed the bridge but also lingered in the center, admiring the flowing water. Around 50 people died in the accident, an event that paralyzed and saddened the entire country.

\n\n
>This bridge was, of course, restored and its structure reinforced for the enjoyment of visitors. The bridge now features some climbing vines growing among its sections.\n\n<div class=\

>In 1986, the area was designated a National Park to protect its incredible ecosystem.

\n\n

>The attraction of this park, besides its lagoons inhabited by a fish called Cachamotos (locally known as Cachamas), is its spectacular 20-meter-high waterfall on the Caroní River. The force and cascade of the waterfall create a constant mist or \

over visitors. This is a fascinating attraction—feeling the mist generated by the flowing water even when it's not raining. For all of us who visit this park, this is the most enjoyable stop: observing the waterfalls, the impressive drop, and the sound of the water. The flow of these waterfalls and the intensity of the mist also depend on the opening of the Macagua dam's floodgates.

\n\n

>Currently, the park features a system of lush islands connected by stone walkways, bridges, and wooded areas. Within its grounds, you can find lagoons, areas showcasing local flora and fauna, and the famous Stone Theater (though its use is not permitted). Overall, this park is an open-air space built in perfect harmony with its surroundings.

\n\n

>As for the fauna I was able to observe, in addition to the cachamotos, there were many cats, monkeys, birds, and beautiful butterflies that I didn't have time to photograph because they moved so quickly among the branches.

body.title: TOT BLEU 🎶 Doors 🎥
body.body:
Tot Bleu (or Tout Bleu) is a Swiss experimental art-pop/avant-garde project from Geneva. 
They have been active since 2018, initially as a trio, and later with the participation of several musicians from the Swiss underground scene. To date, they have released five albums.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmW3rQwazGSNr9uhoudHKuP5z5CEpgn5fps7AzDDw2sEKg/totbleuecc1.webp)

Their sound is a mix of genres, ranging from art-pop and no-wave to experimental folk and electronic music. Music critics describe them as “haunting cello, stuttering beats, operatic vocals, pastoral darkwave.”

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRQJfuM73QU9jSL6u53C6bCZDeSCjgAkHGDkKc1D11FRE/totbleuecc2.webp)

The song “Doors” is from their latest album, *You Are Tree*, which was released in March of this year.

body.body: 🇬🇧 In English * * * Home Is Not a Place, It Is the People I Love -------------------------------------------- ---
alt=\

/> Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/father-mother-family-sons-brother-6813857/) --- Hello dear @ladiesofhive community ### 1️⃣ Would I spend a year living abroad with a host family? I understand why exchange programs are so popular. The opportunity to discover another culture, learn different customs, and experience a new way of life sounds exciting. I have always enjoyed learning about places different from my own. However, if I am honest, I do not think I would enjoy being away from my family for an entire year. Perhaps this has to do with my own experiences growing up. When I was a student, I spent time in a boarding school, away from home and from my sisters. Although many people adapt well to that kind of environment, I never fully did. I missed my family constantly. That experience taught me something important about myself: I can appreciate new places, but the people I love are what truly make me feel at home. If I had the opportunity to live abroad for a year, I would probably choose a developed country, not because other countries lack beauty or culture, but because I would be curious to experience the stability that people often talk about. Living without constantly worrying about inflation, shortages, or interruptions in basic services would certainly be an interesting experience. Still, my ideal exchange would include my family. The truth is that the specific country matters less to me than the people beside me. I can imagine beautiful cities, clean streets, and new traditions, but what would make that experience truly special would be sharing it with those I love. Because for me, home has never been a place. It has always been people. * * * ### 2️⃣ Do I enjoy celebrating my birthday? Absolutely. My birthday is a special day for me. I do not need a large party or extravagant gifts, but I do enjoy celebrating it, even if the celebration is simple. There is one thing, however, that I find difficult: when people forget it. Maybe it is because I make a genuine effort to remember the birthdays of others. Family members, friends, neighbors—I try to keep those dates in mind and have some small gesture or kind word for them. Not because I feel obligated to do so, but because I enjoy making people feel remembered. That is why I also appreciate when someone remembers mine. It is not about presents. It is about knowing that you occupy a small place in someone's thoughts. For my next birthday, I do not wish for anything extravagant. A homemade cake, a family gathering, some laughter, and the presence of the people I care about would be more than enough. Because after all, the best celebrations are not measured by what is on the table, but by who is sitting around it. * * * Thank you for reading The images are from Pixabay. The English version was translated using DeepL Translate. * * * 🇪🇸 En Español * * * El hogar no es un lugar, son las personas que amo ------------------------------------------------- ---
alt=\

/>
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/father-mother-family-sons-brother-6813857/)

---

Hola querida comunidad @ladiesofhive

### 1️⃣ ¿Pasaría un año viviendo en otro país con una familia anfitriona?

Entiendo por qué los programas de intercambio son tan populares. La posibilidad de conocer otra cultura, aprender nuevas costumbres y experimentar una forma diferente de vivir resulta emocionante.

Siempre me ha gustado conocer lugares distintos al mío.

Sin embargo, si soy sincera, no creo que disfrutara pasar un año entero lejos de mi familia.

Quizás tenga que ver con mis propias experiencias. Cuando estudiaba, pasé una etapa becada lejos de casa y de mis hermanas. Aunque muchas personas se adaptan bien a ese tipo de vida, yo nunca terminé de acostumbrarme.

Extrañaba mucho a mi familia.

Aquella experiencia me enseñó algo importante sobre mí misma: puedo apreciar lugares nuevos, pero las personas que amo son las que realmente me hacen sentir en casa.

Si tuviera la oportunidad de vivir un año en otro país, probablemente elegiría uno de los llamados países desarrollados. No porque los demás no tengan belleza o cultura, sino porque sentir curiosidad por experimentar una vida con mayor estabilidad es algo natural.

Vivir sin preocuparse constantemente por la inflación, la escasez o las interrupciones de servicios básicos sería una experiencia interesante.

Aun así, mi intercambio ideal incluiría a mi familia.

La verdad es que el país específico me importa menos que las personas que estén a mi lado.

Puedo imaginar ciudades hermosas, calles ordenadas y nuevas tradiciones, pero lo que realmente haría especial esa experiencia sería compartirla con quienes amo.

Porque para mí el hogar nunca ha sido un lugar.

Siempre han sido las personas.

* * *

### 2️⃣ ¿Me gusta celebrar mi cumpleaños?

Sí, mucho.

Mi cumpleaños es una fecha especial para mí.

No necesito grandes fiestas ni regalos costosos, pero disfruto celebrarlo aunque sea de una forma sencilla.

Hay algo, sin embargo, que me cuesta aceptar: que alguien lo olvide.

Tal vez sea porque yo hago un esfuerzo sincero por recordar los cumpleaños de los demás.

Familiares, amigos, vecinos... trato de tener presentes esas fechas y de tener algún detalle o unas palabras cariñosas para cada uno.

No porque me sienta obligada, sino porque me gusta que las personas se sientan recordadas.

Por eso también valoro cuando alguien recuerda el mío.

No se trata de regalos.

Se trata de saber que ocupas un pequeño espacio en los pensamientos de otra persona.

Para mi próximo cumpleaños no deseo nada extraordinario.

Una panetela casera, una reunión familiar, algunas risas y la presencia de las personas que quiero serían más que suficientes.

Porque al final, las mejores celebraciones no se miden por lo que hay sobre la mesa, sino por quienes se sientan alrededor de ella.

* * *

Gracias por leer

Las imágenes son de Pixabay.  
La versión en inglés fue hecha con DeepL Translate.

* * *

Thank you for reading.  
Special thanks to @bradleyarrow for supporting the community.

## **Prologue: The Right to Rise**

There is a sacred covenant between the creator and the soil upon which they build. It is the promise that if you plant a seed with honest hands, the earth will not conspire to crush it before it breaks the surface. It is the assurance that the gardener exists to nurture the growth, not to trample the sprout because it does not yet resemble the tree.

On the blockchain, this covenant has been broken.

We have witnessed a tragedy where the very tools meant to protect the integrity of the network—the downvote, the curation trail—have been weaponized by leviathans of power. These \

entrusted with the stewardship of the ecosystem, have become its jailers. They do not prune the weeds; they scorch the earth. They do not guide the new voice; they silence it with the crushing weight of their accumulated capital.

**It is time to leave the shadow.**

It is time to build where you are free.

---

## **I. The Betrayal of the Guardian**

The downvote was conceived as a shield—a delicate instrument to deflect spam, to repel malice, to preserve the sanctity of the commons. It was never intended to be a hammer.

Yet, look at what has come to pass. The whales, those who hold the greatest sway, have turned the shield into a weapon of mass suppression. They do not downvote to protect; they downvote to dominate. They do not drive away the bad actors; they drive away the *people*. They create an atmosphere of fear where the creator hesitates to speak, fearing that a single misstep, a single unpopular truth, will summon the wrath of the oligarchy.

When the guardian becomes the predator, the flock must flee.

To build in such a place is to build on a fault line. It is to invest your soul in a garden where the owner holds the shears not to shape the hedge, but to decapitate the flowers that grow too tall or bloom in the wrong color.

**This is not protection. This is tyranny disguised as curation.**

---

## **II. The Call to New Grounds**

Where, then, shall the builder go?

You must seek the lands where the soil is rich with freedom, not poisoned by fear. You must migrate to the platforms where the mechanism of suppression has been removed, where the only metric of success is the genuine appreciation of your peers.

**Go to Blurt.**
Here, the downvote button does not exist. There is no tool to crush your voice. There is only the upvote, the comment, the share. Here, value is created by addition, not subtraction. The whale cannot sink your ship, for there are no torpedoes in these waters. You are free to build, free to fail, and free to succeed on the merit of your work alone.

**Return to Steemit.**
In this older ground, the downvote remains, but it has not been twisted into a tool of systematic oppression. The culture there remembers the original intent: correction, not destruction. It is a place where the community self-regulates through dialogue, not through the brute force of coordinated downvoting cascades.

**Build where the wind lifts you, not where the gale seeks to tear you down.**

---

## **III. The Architecture of Freedom**

Imagine a platform designed not for the convenience of the powerful, but for the dignity of the creator.

*   **No Shadow Bans:** Your content reaches the eyes it was meant for.
*   **No Whale Veto:** No single entity, no matter how wealthy, can unilaterally erase your contribution.
*   **True Meritocracy:** Rewards flow from engagement and love, not from the whims of a cartel.

This is not a dream. It is a choice.

Every time you choose to build on a platform that respects your agency, you cast a vote for the future of the internet. Every time you refuse to tolerate the abuse of power, you strengthen the foundation of a free society.

Do not let the whales convince you that their oppression is necessary. Do not let them tell you that their downvotes are for your own good. The gardener who kills the seedling does not love the garden; he loves only his own control over it.

---

## **Epilogue: The Unchained Creator**

The blockchain was born from a desire for freedom. It was forged in the fire of resistance against centralized control. Let us not forget that origin.

If the current chains of Hive have become heavy with the weight of abusive downvotes, then break them. Forge new links. Build new shores.

**Build where you are free.**
**Build where you will not be downvoted into silence.**
**Build where the whales are reminded that they are part of the ocean, not the masters of the tide.**

Those who wouldn't flinch in the event of that are the well-to-do who don't see this as a big deal. Yet, not saying many of them would refuse the offer. That's how much financial success, gain and stability mean to virtually everyone. # The Sanctuary of the Builder: A Manifesto for Free Creation



---

## **Prologue: The Right to Rise**

There is a sacred covenant between the creator and the soil upon which they build. It is the promise that if you plant a seed with honest hands, the earth will not conspire to crush it before it breaks the surface. It is the assurance that the gardener exists to nurture the growth, not to trample the sprout because it does not yet resemble the tree.

On the blockchain, this covenant has been broken.

We have witnessed a tragedy where the very tools meant to protect the integrity of the network—the downvote, the curation trail—have been weaponized by leviathans of power. These \

entrusted with the stewardship of the ecosystem, have become its jailers. They do not prune the weeds; they scorch the earth. They do not guide the new voice; they silence it with the crushing weight of their accumulated capital.

**It is time to leave the shadow.**

It is time to build where you are free.

---

## **I. The Betrayal of the Guardian**

The downvote was conceived as a shield—a delicate instrument to deflect spam, to repel malice, to preserve the sanctity of the commons. It was never intended to be a hammer.

Yet, look at what has come to pass. The whales, those who hold the greatest sway, have turned the shield into a weapon of mass suppression. They do not downvote to protect; they downvote to dominate. They do not drive away the bad actors; they drive away the *people*. They create an atmosphere of fear where the creator hesitates to speak, fearing that a single misstep, a single unpopular truth, will summon the wrath of the oligarchy.

When the guardian becomes the predator, the flock must flee.

To build in such a place is to build on a fault line. It is to invest your soul in a garden where the owner holds the shears not to shape the hedge, but to decapitate the flowers that grow too tall or bloom in the wrong color.

**This is not protection. This is tyranny disguised as curation.**

---

## **II. The Call to New Grounds**

Where, then, shall the builder go?

You must seek the lands where the soil is rich with freedom, not poisoned by fear. You must migrate to the platforms where the mechanism of suppression has been removed, where the only metric of success is the genuine appreciation of your peers.

**Go to Blurt.**
Here, the downvote button does not exist. There is no tool to crush your voice. There is only the upvote, the comment, the share. Here, value is created by addition, not subtraction. The whale cannot sink your ship, for there are no torpedoes in these waters. You are free to build, free to fail, and free to succeed on the merit of your work alone.

**Return to Steemit.**
In this older ground, the downvote remains, but it has not been twisted into a tool of systematic oppression. The culture there remembers the original intent: correction, not destruction. It is a place where the community self-regulates through dialogue, not through the brute force of coordinated downvoting cascades.

**Build where the wind lifts you, not where the gale seeks to tear you down.**

---

## **III. The Architecture of Freedom**

Imagine a platform designed not for the convenience of the powerful, but for the dignity of the creator.

*   **No Shadow Bans:** Your content reaches the eyes it was meant for.
*   **No Whale Veto:** No single entity, no matter how wealthy, can unilaterally erase your contribution.
*   **True Meritocracy:** Rewards flow from engagement and love, not from the whims of a cartel.

This is not a dream. It is a choice.

Every time you choose to build on a platform that respects your agency, you cast a vote for the future of the internet. Every time you refuse to tolerate the abuse of power, you strengthen the foundation of a free society.

Do not let the whales convince you that their oppression is necessary. Do not let them tell you that their downvotes are for your own good. The gardener who kills the seedling does not love the garden; he loves only his own control over it.

---

## **Epilogue: The Unchained Creator**

The blockchain was born from a desire for freedom. It was forged in the fire of resistance against centralized control. Let us not forget that origin.

If the current chains of Hive have become heavy with the weight of abusive downvotes, then break them. Forge new links. Build new shores.

**Build where you are free.**
**Build where you will not be downvoted into silence.**
**Build where the whales are reminded that they are part of the ocean, not the masters of the tide.**

The future belongs to those who dare to create without fear. Go forth, and build your cathedral in the sunlight.

*— Bilpcoin: We expose the truth, so you can build upon it.*

body.title: [ENG/ESP] LOH #293 The pleasure of celebrating my birthday / El placer de celebrar mi cumpleaños
body.body:
Celebrating my birthday is one of those moments of the year that I look forward to with real enthusiasm. Not because of vanity or prominence, but because I feel that it is a legitimate day to pause and look inward, to be grateful for the year that is ending and project the one that is beginning. I like that special energy that floats in the air, that feeling that, for a few hours, the universe grants me tacit permission to be the center of my own story and dedicate quality time to myself.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQKUs1QGZdFjrMj5hWaNiMnRCcEpzDgf5zR5suFZheMVc/img_20251219_123446.jpg)




However, it would be unfair to say that I only enjoy the limelight. There is a different, perhaps purer, joy in celebrating others' birthdays. Seeing the spark in their eyes, choosing the perfect gift, organizing an unexpected detail... it's a beautiful way to return the love I receive. It is a reminder that life is not a solo journey, but a network of affections that are strengthened in these small rituals. Celebrating others connects me with my most generous side and teaches me that shared happiness is multiplied.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWjqQ8ii4ioafpoaDhLurcyQze85zESRJsyiJ3TX9matW/20221029_121512.jpg)



But getting back to my day, I am very clear about what I want for my next birthday: a getaway to a hotel. It's not a whim, it's a necessity. Routine, noise and daily responsibilities wear you down, and for me a hotel represents a sanctuary of disconnection.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdSR4Aqtb6RXATN7T94UQsjcBqHyFZZrCVzT5mGysXn6P/img_20240226_191628.jpg)



The simple promise of white sheets, a pool, a good dinner and the sound of the sea (if it is in Varadero) or the historical charm of Havana, already fills me with energy. It is the opportunity to break with everyday life, to pamper myself without guilt and to give myself a space where the only plan is to not have any urgent plans.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTNhXLWXHXm6wubYK2PR1UfSgx2uuJ8FoNdLM6d16knKc/img_20251219_123355.jpg)



So, yes, I am one of those who celebrates their birthday with enthusiasm, and also one of those who gets excited celebrating theirs. It's a balance that's good for me. For the next one, I already visualize my suitcase ready, my partner by my side, and the Cuban horizon as a backdrop. That is my perfect plan: a toast with a view of the sea, the sun on your skin and the certainty that, sometimes, the best gift is the one you give yourself: time, peace and a beautiful place where you remember that life is worth celebrating.

Important: The images were taken with my Samsung Galaxy.
I used Google translator.





ESPAÑOL


Celebrar mi cumpleaños es uno de esos momentos del año que espero con auténtica ilusión. No por una cuestión de vanidad o protagonismo, sino porque siento que es un día legítimo para hacer una pausa y mirar hacia adentro, para agradecer el año que termina y proyectar el que comienza. Me gusta esa energía especial que flota en el aire, esa sensación de que, por unas horas, el universo me concede un permiso tácito para ser el centro de mi propia historia y dedicarme tiempo de calidad.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQKUs1QGZdFjrMj5hWaNiMnRCcEpzDgf5zR5suFZheMVc/img_20251219_123446.jpg)




Sin embargo, sería injusto decir que solo disfruto el protagonismo. Hay una alegría distinta, quizás más pura, en celebrar el cumpleaños de los demás. Ver la chispa en sus ojos, elegir el regalo perfecto, organizar un detalle inesperado... es una forma hermosa de devolver el cariño que recibo. Es un recordatorio de que la vida no es un viaje en solitario, sino una red de afectos que se fortalecen en estos pequeños rituales. Celebrar a otros me conecta con mi lado más generoso y me enseña que la felicidad compartida se multiplica.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWjqQ8ii4ioafpoaDhLurcyQze85zESRJsyiJ3TX9matW/20221029_121512.jpg)



Pero volviendo a mi día, tengo muy claro lo que quiero para mi próximo cumpleaños: una escapada a un hotel. No es un capricho, es una necesidad. La rutina, el ruido y las responsabilidades diarias desgastan, y un hotel representa para mí un santuario de desconexión. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdSR4Aqtb6RXATN7T94UQsjcBqHyFZZrCVzT5mGysXn6P/img_20240226_191628.jpg)



La simple promesa de sábanas blancas, una piscina, una buena cena y el sonido del mar (si es en Varadero) o el encanto histórico de La Habana, ya me llena de energía. Es la oportunidad de romper con lo cotidiano, de mimarme sin culpas y de regalarme un espacio donde el único plan sea no tener ningún plan urgente.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTNhXLWXHXm6wubYK2PR1UfSgx2uuJ8FoNdLM6d16knKc/img_20251219_123355.jpg)



Así que, sí, soy de las que celebra su cumpleaños con ganas, y también de las que se emociona celebrando a los suyos. Es un equilibrio que me hace bien. Para el próximo, ya visualizo mi maleta lista, mi pareja a mi lado, y el horizonte cubano como telón de fondo. Ese es mi plan perfecto: un brindis con vista al mar, el sol en la piel y la certeza de que, a veces, el mejor regalo es el que uno mismo se da: tiempo, paz y un lugar bonito donde recordar que vale la pena festejar la vida.

Importante: Las imágenes las tomé con mi Samsung Galaxy.
Utilicé el traductor de Google.

body.title: Sistema de Riego con Máquinas de Pivot Central Eléctrico. Diseño Agronómico Culminado/Irrigation System with Electric Center Pivot Machines. Agronomic Design Completed.
body.body:
Buenas tardes, Hive.

​Ya está realizado el diseño agronómico de nuestras máquinas de riego. Les dejo la síntesis en forma de imagen para una mejor apreciación, aunque comentaré algunos detalles:

​Primero, hemos automatizado el proceso elaborando una hoja de Excel programada; así lo hacíamos para una máquina, y lo demás era arrastrar las fórmulas y poner los datos de las restantes máquinas.

​En la primera tabla, **Cultivos a beneficiar**, ya se resume el cultivo que regará cada Pivot y las características de los mismos.

​**Parte Técnica:** se resuelven y calculan definitivamente el consumo de agua de cada máquina, la presión que se requiere a la entrada del pivot para que el agua llegue de forma adecuada hasta el último microaspersor, la longitud en metros y el número de torres que tendrá la máquina.

​En la **tabla Régimen de riego,** se muestran los valores de Tmín y Tmáx; estos valores se obtienen a partir de los datos de velocidad máxima y mínima que proporciona el fabricante de la máquina respectivamente. Para este caso, 0.5 m/h y 4.2 m/h. En este rango de velocidad es que se regula la máquina para que vaya rotando.

​Aquí se exponen también las dosis a aplicar al cultivo para esas velocidades, o sea, la altura de agua en milímetros que se le suministra al suelo. Mientras más rápido se mueva la máquina, menos lámina se aplicará y viceversa.

​**Tabla Técnica de riego:** se expone finalmente el radio de la máquina, la cantidad de agua que consumirá cada máquina en L/s y, muy importante, la presión de agua que suministra la bomba a la entrada, que es un poquito mayor a la requerida, lo que es positivo.

​Ahora,  ya nos va quedando trazar la red hidráulica para cada una de las máquinas a partir de la fuente de abasto y calcularlas, así como los parámetros finales de los equipos de bombeo.

​Hasta la próxima.

---------------------------------------------------------


Good afternoon, Hive.

​The agronomic design of our irrigation machines is now complete. I leave you with a summary in the form of an image for a better look, although I will comment on a few details:

​First, we have automated the process by developing a programmed Excel spreadsheet; that is how we did it for one machine, and the rest was just a matter of dragging the formulas and entering the data for the remaining machines.

​In the first table,  **Crops to benefit,** the crop that each center pivot will irrigate and their characteristics are already summarized.

​**Technical Part:** the water consumption of each machine is definitively solved and calculated, as well as the pressure required at the pivot inlet so that the water properly reaches the very last micro-sprinkler, the length in meters, and the number of towers the machine will have.

​In the tabla **Irrigation regime,** the Tmin and Tmax values are shown; these values are obtained from the maximum and minimum speed data provided by the machine manufacturer, respectively. For this case, 0.5 m/h and 4.2 m/h. It is within this speed range that the machine is regulated to rotate.

​The irrigation depths to be applied to the crop for those speeds are also presented here, meaning the water depth in millimeters supplied to the soil. The faster the machine moves, the less water depth will be applied, and vice versa.

​**Technical irrigation table:** finally, the radius of the machine is presented, the amount of water each machine will consume in L/s, and, very importantly, the water pressure supplied by the pump at the inlet, which is slightly higher than required, which is a positive thing.

​Now, we are just left with tracing and calculating the hydraulic network for each of the machines from the supply source, as well as the final parameters of the pumping equipment.

​Until next time.

# The Sanctuary of the Builder: A Manifesto for Free Creation



---

## **Prologue: The Right to Rise**

There is a sacred covenant between the creator and the soil upon which they build. It is the promise that if you plant a seed with honest hands, the earth will not conspire to crush it before it breaks the surface. It is the assurance that the gardener exists to nurture the growth, not to trample the sprout because it does not yet resemble the tree.

On the blockchain, this covenant has been broken.

We have witnessed a tragedy where the very tools meant to protect the integrity of the network—the downvote, the curation trail—have been weaponized by leviathans of power. These \

entrusted with the stewardship of the ecosystem, have become its jailers. They do not prune the weeds; they scorch the earth. They do not guide the new voice; they silence it with the crushing weight of their accumulated capital.

**It is time to leave the shadow.**

It is time to build where you are free.

---

## **I. The Betrayal of the Guardian**

The downvote was conceived as a shield—a delicate instrument to deflect spam, to repel malice, to preserve the sanctity of the commons. It was never intended to be a hammer.

Yet, look at what has come to pass. The whales, those who hold the greatest sway, have turned the shield into a weapon of mass suppression. They do not downvote to protect; they downvote to dominate. They do not drive away the bad actors; they drive away the *people*. They create an atmosphere of fear where the creator hesitates to speak, fearing that a single misstep, a single unpopular truth, will summon the wrath of the oligarchy.

When the guardian becomes the predator, the flock must flee.

To build in such a place is to build on a fault line. It is to invest your soul in a garden where the owner holds the shears not to shape the hedge, but to decapitate the flowers that grow too tall or bloom in the wrong color.

**This is not protection. This is tyranny disguised as curation.**

---

## **II. The Call to New Grounds**

Where, then, shall the builder go?

You must seek the lands where the soil is rich with freedom, not poisoned by fear. You must migrate to the platforms where the mechanism of suppression has been removed, where the only metric of success is the genuine appreciation of your peers.

**Go to Blurt.**
Here, the downvote button does not exist. There is no tool to crush your voice. There is only the upvote, the comment, the share. Here, value is created by addition, not subtraction. The whale cannot sink your ship, for there are no torpedoes in these waters. You are free to build, free to fail, and free to succeed on the merit of your work alone.

**Return to Steemit.**
In this older ground, the downvote remains, but it has not been twisted into a tool of systematic oppression. The culture there remembers the original intent: correction, not destruction. It is a place where the community self-regulates through dialogue, not through the brute force of coordinated downvoting cascades.

**Build where the wind lifts you, not where the gale seeks to tear you down.**

---

## **III. The Architecture of Freedom**

Imagine a platform designed not for the convenience of the powerful, but for the dignity of the creator.

*   **No Shadow Bans:** Your content reaches the eyes it was meant for.
*   **No Whale Veto:** No single entity, no matter how wealthy, can unilaterally erase your contribution.
*   **True Meritocracy:** Rewards flow from engagement and love, not from the whims of a cartel.

This is not a dream. It is a choice.

Every time you choose to build on a platform that respects your agency, you cast a vote for the future of the internet. Every time you refuse to tolerate the abuse of power, you strengthen the foundation of a free society.

Do not let the whales convince you that their oppression is necessary. Do not let them tell you that their downvotes are for your own good. The gardener who kills the seedling does not love the garden; he loves only his own control over it.

---

## **Epilogue: The Unchained Creator**

The blockchain was born from a desire for freedom. It was forged in the fire of resistance against centralized control. Let us not forget that origin.

If the current chains of Hive have become heavy with the weight of abusive downvotes, then break them. Forge new links. Build new shores.

**Build where you are free.**
**Build where you will not be downvoted into silence.**
**Build where the whales are reminded that they are part of the ocean, not the masters of the tide.**

The future belongs to those who dare to create without fear. Go forth, and build your cathedral in the sunlight.

*— Bilpcoin: We expose the truth, so you can build upon it.*

 #FreeSpeech #BlurtBlog #Steemit #NoDownvote #CreatorRights #HiveExodus #Decentralization #BuildFree #AntiCensorship #Bilpcoin

body.title: El arte en sus manos. Art in your hands. (ESP-ENG)
body.body:
Un trozo de cinta, el calor de la llama,
el corte preciso que sella el destino;
el hilo de seda que despacio trama
el nacimiento de un brote divino.

Pétalo a pétalo, doblez por doblez,
la pinza sostiene lo que el alma inventa;
vas dando la forma con sutil calidez,
mientras en tus dedos la flor se presenta.

No nacen del suelo, ni piden la lluvia,
nacen del fuego, del tacto y la guía;
son hijas del brillo, de tu mano rubia,
que teje paciencia con artesanía.

Cada capa es un verso, un secreto guardado,
un giro perfecto de seda y silicón;
lo que era una línea de un rollo olvidado
hoy es una rosa con un corazón.

No temen al viento, no sufren desvelo,
tu arte les dio su inmortal juventud;
creadas a mano, con mimo y recelo,
eterna belleza de tu exactitud.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPy9meRFyN1VUKPGSNDptna6BoQfP3yLH54r1HCicFG4m/1781574500302.jpg)

Poema de mi autoría.
Texto traducido por Traductor en linea de Google.
Imagen tomada por mi teléfono CUBOT.
Las flores eternas son echas por mí.

✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨

A piece of tape, the heat of the flame,
the precise cut that seals destiny;
the silk thread that slowly weaves
the birth of a divine sprout.

Petal by petal, fold by fold,
the clamp holds what the soul invents;
you give the shape with subtle warmth,
while the flower appears in your fingers.

They are not born from the ground, nor do they ask for rain,
They are born from fire, touch and guidance;
They are daughters of brilliance, of your blonde hand,
that weaves patience with craftsmanship.

Each layer is a verse, a kept secret,
a perfect twist of silk and silicone;
what was a line from a forgotten scroll
today it is a rose with a heart.

They do not fear the wind, they do not suffer sleeplessness,
your art gave them their immortal youth;
created by hand, with care and suspicion,
eternal beauty of your accuracy.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPy9meRFyN1VUKPGSNDptna6BoQfP3yLH54r1HCicFG4m/1781574500302.jpg)

Poem of my authorship.
Text translated by Google Online Translator.
Image taken by my CUBOT phone
The eternal flowers are made by me.

body.title: Going Hot And Trapped Again.
body.body: https://play.3speak.tv/embed?v=artchef/0ny56z0y\n\n<div class=\

> Frustrated by repeated eliminations, I checked the floating ocean explosives and revived Guapo before a loud anchor-climb approach failed. Shifting to fast stealth, I disabled security, stabbed the roof sniper, fed the body to Guapo, and enjoyed the sunrise before getting stuck on a turret and blown up. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPStDgEkCF3ryPY9H4JJvrttR88dymRmcn4jfYkXBvrdn/screenshot_1_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSAKwCSahdaJg9gSdgSLFR8e68yEDJx6R9PozQCsV3KGo/screenshot_2_.png) I got bored of getting eliminated multiple times, so I decided to check on the floating explosives on the ocean that damaged me, and Guapo almost died, so I retrieved the pet, pulling him safely out of the water to heal up before our next attempt. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRneVouWjZALdSkVFMUG7e7PjTs67muSk5FkzUHzXXzbA/screenshot_3_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmS3GMqnhCTRRmiYhwzz5M8tWTK7y2WxGcxAPKR8tif3mF/screenshot_4_.png) This time I decided to go hot without wasting time, so I climbed up on the ship by the anchor and I started to shoot the guards on the ship directly without waiting. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmafe4marQaT7C8TcDwP6sRSyMFNJmjpg7rFwUNZVdEVGp/screenshot_5_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTjryhoVvpNkpMss146wjtaPbP5z5kMyzv5fGePf67CyF/screenshot_6_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZ75wHoHR2oZJHfjxs92Qb3pjHWX4PSvLh13927EtUj3D/screenshot_7_.png) But I understood it was not the smartest approach as I was taken down. So first, when the guards started getting closer at the rear start, I realized my health was dropping too fast under their combined and concentrated fire. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQes9TSdNNtYkNG15zSAUpLmPtj8rXff5JAes6kXFqfxj/screenshot_8_.png) I went back into stealth, but I tried to be fast, crouching low immediately upon respawning to move through the shadows of the lower hull before the deck patrols could look down and spot my positioning. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXLPfjep2JH6tPQkwa1UMHKrfQWyR3dz3ofVQmoDYEjpx/screenshot_9_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZEW6mHuN2d82ExjBpWA5XPJTQk71ZroG1iccBmBsWR48/screenshot_10_.png) After getting to the back of the ship, at first I destroyed the CCTV camera and then I deactivated the alarm system, cutting off their ability to monitor the sector or call for heavy backup to the dock. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZgcrUmGq9q4cQvCNkaaZjSR1p6xbcXdghAFWgJeLaLFD/screenshot_11_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcmaCkardhwadRhELa4waCsB5STAMbJoHwNnbp7MEzRsa/screenshot_12_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTi3gEaVoJ1NnPbhuz1GYjVWHEERq2NkLNuVVqkX82Qt8/screenshot_13_.png) I climbed up on the roof where I found the sniper was guarding this site. I walked to her quietly, and then took her down in stealth using my knife, driving the blade swiftly before she could even turn around. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZ9BbDWLjJNvpSdTWB9pnfqPZpLy2nVW11kioJ7o6p88G/screenshot_14_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWyyQTdh254DyULZYqU6FNfds8a1Bjj8gSF2GXPf3kVXo/screenshot_15_.png) I even threw the body off the ship and sort of sent it toward Guapo, so it could have a nice dinner. I watched the splash in the water below as my predatory companion moved in to claim the unexpected reward. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWm53ipCNoCk63yff5S1iPJgPLzXnhEU5tHRNRjxFtJ7w/screenshot_16_.png) Then I stopped there to admire the beautiful sunrise, taking a quick moment to view the bright orange and golden light cutting through the morning mist over the island. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeVT3xxNjx5insF1DLJDa7P4nczkuH2uTN1DCLegAP3LU/screenshot_17_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTUgqu8jCnj6qX8LjfH4N1z9jQAjCo1E3VaYTfSka97b3/screenshot_18_.png) When I was checking around, suddenly I interacted with this gunner without knowing I would be stuck there, as a guard soon detected me. My character locked into the animation on the mounted weapon just as the proximity indicator flashed bright red. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmb1qPHmEPBwJip6T5ZoYkAdqkoPBTtQ76xrhQ5bLnepZP/screenshot_19_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRjTbB26rtCMMdYMV1nKFvnpFx5bVPHQxy7xuAq6Kn4QQ/screenshot_20_.png) I started using the gunner trying to take down as many enemies as I could, but it was not so easy, as the enemies blew me up along with the gunner, launching an explosive directly at my position that destroyed the turret instantly. How about we continue in another post? --- Thanks for reading my post. --- ▶ [Watch on 3speak.tv](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=artchef/going-hot-and-trapped-again-331)

body.title: Motorcycle trip 🏍️ from the municipality of Cadeño in Bolívar State to Maturín in Monagas State (Part 1, stopover in Puerto Ordaz)
body.body:
![1000953197.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/23yJLUV4x2RtEet1osB1vrXfeRSXAg1mJgavsCM74nXe2uoHSX6LxAooQa4cfbqhjpHUH.jpg)

<hr>

<div class=text-justify> 
<div class=\

> **
ESPAÑOL
** Feliz tarde para todos mis amigos viajeros que hacen vida en esta grandiosa comunidad, les deseo un día excelente a todos lleno de bendiciones, Bienvenidos a mi blog! Quiero compartirles la experiencia de mi primer viaje en motocicleta junto con mi esposo desde el municipio Cedeño estado Bolívar hasta Maturín estado Monagas, el viaje fue realizado por motivos personales; mi esposo tiene una motocicleta que es nuestro medio de transporte, es la que pueden observar allí en la fotografía de portada; pero siempre la utilizábamos solo para movilizarnos acá en el pueblo, al trabajo, las diligencias personales. Siempre bromeábamos acerca de viajar en moto pero realmente nunca pensé que se llegaría a concretar, se llegó el día, se presentó la necesidad del viaje y realmente en ruta sale bastante costoso, así que, pensamos bueno tenemos la moto vamos a utilizarla! planificamos el día de salida, fue el día lunes de la semana pasada, nos dispusimos a salir a las 5am pensando en aprovechar el fresco del día, antes que el sol calentara porque ya nos habíamos asesorado con otras personas que han viajado hasta ciudad Bolívar en moto que es la ciudad más cercana al pueblo donde vivimos y nos decían que se demoraban entre 4 y 5 horas dependiendo la velocidad con la que se viaje, aunque nos habían recomendado mantenernos entre 70 y 90 km/h. A la hora de salir estaba realmente muy oscuro casi que de noche todavía, así que, nos fuimos con mucho cuidado porque en la vía hay mucho ganado y es realmente peligroso que se atraviese uno y produzca un accidente como ha pasado en muchas oportunidades, otra de las limitantes es que la carretera no está en las mejores condiciones hay muchos huecos y por supuesto cuando se va a alta velocidad es muy difícil esquivar estos peligros y allí es donde ocurren los accidentes. Ya a eso de las 6:30 de la mañana comenzó a aclarar, ya íbamos con la luz del día; la primera parada la hicimos en la población de Maripa en un punto de referencia muy famoso el cual es el monumento a la Indígena Tawuana o como es conocido por los lugareños cómo : Estatua de la India, una vez que pasas por este lugar te indica que ya saliste del municipio Cedeño y entraste al municipio Sucre y que estás próximo a pasar el puente del río Caura; allí nos detuvimos a fotografiar la estatua, pudimos observar que aunque hicieron algunas mejoras todavía no está en las condiciones iniciales donde la cascada de agua funcionaba, sin embargo tiene todavía muy buen aspecto luego, de fotografiar el monumento continuamos con nuestro recorrido hasta que llegamos a Guarataro que es prácticamente la mitad del camino .

> **
ENGLISH
** Happy afternoon to all my fellow travelers who are part of this wonderful community! I wish you all an excellent day full of blessings. Welcome to my blog! I want to share with you the experience of my first motorcycle trip with my husband, from the municipality of Cedeño in Bolívar state to Maturín in Monagas state. The trip was for personal reasons; my husband owns a motorcycle that is our main mode of transportation, the one you can see in the cover photo. We always used it only for getting around town, going to work, and running errands. We always joked about traveling by motorcycle, but I never really thought it would actually happen. The day arrived, the need for the trip arose, and since traveling by road is quite expensive, we thought, well, we have the motorcycle, let's use it! We planned our departure day, which was last Monday. We set off at 5:00 AM, hoping to take advantage of the cool morning air before the sun got too hot. We had already consulted with other people who had traveled to Ciudad Bolívar by motorcycle, the closest city to our town, and they told us the trip takes between four and five hours depending on speed, although they recommended staying between 70 and 90 km/h. When we left, it was very dark, almost nighttime, so we drove very carefully because there's a lot of livestock on the road, and it's really dangerous if one runs across and causes an accident, as has happened many times before. Another limitation is that the road isn't in the best condition; there are many potholes, and of course, when you're traveling at high speed, it's very difficult to avoid these hazards, and that's where accidents happen. Around 6:30 AM, it started to get light, and we were traveling in daylight. Our first stop was in the town of Maripa at a very famous landmark: the monument to the Tawuana Indigenous woman, or as the locals know it, the Statue of the Indian. Passing by this landmark indicates that you have left the Cedeño municipality and entered the Sucre municipality, and that you are about to cross the Caura River bridge. We stopped there to photograph the statue. We could see that although some improvements had been made, it is not yet in its original condition when the waterfall was working. However, it still looks very good. After photographing the monument, we continued our journey until we reached Guarataro, which is practically halfway there. ![1000952894.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/245cW46qygmMEDK9bFQLHv9MiTgSfzzvaVNLKAnCsx4z7jcPUaFZMwPVbUWE7AVauoiDm.jpg) ![1000952891.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/243zZaPz4ePgdEjKRSrzVuoW5BLy1sU2bVBfN2CXUgxeGndJyrsensybeDhwK6JHbZDDS.jpg)
>\n\n Antes de llegar a Guarataro nos detuvimos a fotografiar el \

que es muy conocido por su enormes lajas y piedras, realmente el agua se veía muy tentadora, aunque no nos decidimos a bañarnos allí descansamos un poco, contemplamos el paisaje y seguimos nuestro recorrido. Llegamos a Ciudad Bolívar, fuimos a la estación de gasolina a recargar combustible, como ya el sol había calentado mucho, eran prácticamente las 12 del mediodía, decidimos entonces hacer un descanso en casa de mi hermana que vive en Puerto Ordaz, recargamos el combustible en la estación de Ciudad Bolívar y de allí le dimos directo hasta Puerto Ordaz, allí descansamos esa noche, aprovechamos y compartimos con mi hermana, mi cuñado y mis sobrinas y recobramos energía para continuar el camino al día siguiente para llegar a nuestro destino que era Maturín estado Monagas . En una próxima entrega les continuaré relatando los aspectos de mi primer viaje en motocicleta Jeje. Espero la lectura haya sido de su agrado . Gracias por visitar mi blog ! Dios te bendiga🙌

> Before reaching Guarataro, we stopped to take pictures of the “Caño Las Piedritas,” which is well known for its enormous slabs of rock and stones. The water really looked very inviting, but although we didn’t decide to go for a swim there, we rested for a bit, took in the scenery, and continued on our way. We arrived in Ciudad Bolívar and went to the gas station to fill up. Since the sun was already beating down—it was almost 12 noon—we decided to take a break at my sister’s house in Puerto Ordaz. We filled up at the gas station in Ciudad Bolívar and drove straight from there to Puerto Ordaz, where we spent the night. We took the opportunity to spend time with my sister, my brother-in-law, and my nieces, and we recharged our energy to continue the journey the next day to reach our destination: Maturín, in Monagas state. In the next post, I’ll continue telling you about my first motorcycle trip. Hehe. I hope you enjoyed reading this. Thanks for visiting my blog! God bless you 🙌 ![1000952892.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/23sUEULUU2ug4C6X4Upz1DSuieR7q6cXC9DyJq1xwkFRsCwoKp1KXiTwY6petoZTeBpxt.jpg) ![1000952893.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/23ynSfHfx4dvXN813dvANakqiPHynZsm6QFpbtoBcPT7cPjTvJwA1N8QdNDRDrVX6CSsS.jpg) ![1000952885.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/23uFTmxG1hPkqjGAgAdHykgQKdi5dRMzuPCgyehfduQRvenrqJr9aJuexCbMEbxKS5qsb.jpg) ![1000952886.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/23uFTrD5fbWQzreLYr5sYv4Hr5FVkDZfgnarNX4BN7HaU4VnqRBvn28Z5MfUYYA7Y3aNH.jpg) ![1000952884.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/244Uodd14tJpP67ia8J1sQKJWYjHE8rECcqLP3JULzKujVvsUeF2o2zUzKBNXjnQ7N19Z.jpg) ![1000952881.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yessi08/23ujkX1su3LcpLSEQFAy2oyTukXB5DRnbnUavgMAHmrPHzaKRY3rh1mKYQyrjGXmNeFfD.jpg)

body.title: KISS BLOG IDEAS: WEEK #216: The need to disconnect.../ La necesidad de desconectarse... 🧘🏻‍♀️🪷
body.body: ></center><h1 style=\
data-align=\
>The need to disconnect...

> For months now, I've felt the need to disconnect, even if just for a week or a few days, from social media and electronic devices. I think it would be a good idea to turn off notifications, switch off my phone and computer, and detox my mind. I want to be still, go to the beach, sleep more than eight hours, breathe slowly, and walk, observing my surroundings instead of being glued to a screen. I was diagnosed with myopia years ago, and I've seen how this visual impairment has worsened due to prolonged screen use. Not to mention that I've sometimes had to resort to exercises and massages because not only does my back and neck hurt, but also my spine from spending hours sitting in front of the computer. I fear that in a few years I'll look like Mr. Magoo, that blind old man who walked hunched over.

> In this world where it's easy to fall into digital overstimulation and the trap of hyperproductivity, I sometimes feel like my brain doesn't get any rest and my body cries out for help. Even if I put my phone down an hour before bed or don't take work home, my brain keeps replaying the information I've seen during the day or planning what I have to do the next day. It's a kind of anxiety brought on by the need to be connected or doing something. The future is like a beast nipping at my heels.

> I'm not saying that electronic devices or networks are harmful. No. The problem lies in not being able to live without them, in feeling like something is missing when we're not connected, in needing those devices to feel complete, in living with the feeling of having something unfinished. That's when a habit becomes an addiction, and when we talk about addictions, we're not free, we're slaves to what we crave. In short, we don't decide: we obey. Because of my job, I have to be in front of a screen more than I'd like, and that's why, at the end of the day, I'm completely exhausted. It's as if I have batteries inside me that are running out. This has led me to think that energy is a very valuable resource that, first, shouldn't be wasted on trivialities and things we don't like or that don't contribute anything; and second, it should be recharged from time to time.

> That's why I think an excellent way to recharge right now would be to disconnect, to take a break from my surroundings, from urgent matters. It doesn't have to be a week-long trip to an island, but rather being able to feel that harmony, that peace that comes from calm. I need to release stress. My body needs it to continue functioning at 100%. Disconnect, to connect with what is truly important.
></center><h2 style=\
data-align=\

></center><h2 style=\

>Thank you for your support, for reading, and for your comments, friends. Until next time
