>La necesidad de desconectarse

Desde hace meses siento la necesidad de desconectarme, aunque sea solo por una semana o unos días, de las redes sociales y los dispositivos electrónicos. Creo que sería buena idea desactivar las notificaciones, apagar el teléfono y el ordenador, y desintoxicar mi mente. Quiero estar quieta, ir a la playa, dormir más de ocho horas, respirar despacio y caminar, observando mi entorno en lugar de estar pegada a una pantalla. Me diagnosticaron miopía hace años y he visto cómo esta discapacidad visual ha empeorado debido al uso prolongado de pantallas. Sin mencionar que a veces he tenido que recurrir a ejercicios y masajes porque no solo me duelen la espalda y el cuello, sino también la columna vertebral por pasar horas sentada frente al ordenador. Temo que dentro de unos años me parezca al Sr. Magoo, ese anciano ciego que caminaba encorvado. En este mundo donde es fácil caer en la sobreestimulación digital y la trampa de la hiperproductividad, siento que a veces mi cerebro no descansa y mi cuerpo clama por ayuda. Incluso si dejo el teléfono una hora antes de acostarme o no me llevo trabajo a casa, mi cerebro sigue repasando la información que he visto durante el día o planificando lo que tengo que hacer al día siguiente. Es una especie de ansiedad provocada por la necesidad de estar conectado o haciendo algo. El futuro es como una bestia que me pisa los talones. No digo que los dispositivos electrónicos o las redes sean dañinos. No. El problema radica en no poder vivir sin ellos, en sentir que nos falta algo cuando no estamos conectados, en necesitar esos dispositivos para sentirnos completos, en vivir con la sensación de tener algo pendiente. Es entonces cuando un hábito se convierte en adicción, y cuando hablamos de adicciones, no somos libres, somos esclavos de aquello que anhelamos. En resumen, no decidimos: obedecemos. Debido a mi trabajo, tengo que estar frente a una pantalla más de lo que quisiera, y por eso, al final del día, estoy completamente agotado. Es como si tuviera baterías dentro que se agotan. Esto me ha llevado a pensar que la energía es un recurso muy valioso que, primero, no se debe desperdiciar en trivialidades y cosas que no nos gustan o que no aportan nada; y segundo, se debe recargar de vez en cuando. Por eso creo que una excelente manera de recargar energías ahora mismo sería desconectar, tomarme un respiro de mi entorno, de los asuntos urgentes. No tiene por qué ser un viaje de una semana a una isla, sino más bien poder sentir esa armonía, esa paz que proviene de la calma. Necesito liberar el estrés. Mi cuerpo lo necesita para seguir funcionando al 100%. Desconectar, para conectar con lo que es verdaderamente importante.

Котильон - це зроблена своїми руками нагрудна прикраса з бісеру, яку виготовляли і дарували дівчата хлопцям перед випроводжанням до війська. Найбільшу популярність здобув в часи Erhf]ycmrb[ визвольних змагаль 1918-1921 років. 

В основі композиції котильонів як правило містилась національна символіка, як демонстративний прояв національної самоідентифікації. 

Днями вийшла друком книга-каталог \

, в якій міститься зображення 150 зразків давніх котильонів. Багато зображених ексонатів ви також можете побачити на давніх світлинах на сторінках видання.

А для тих, хто любить працювати руками і хотів би повторити якийсь з котильонів, знайде в книзі докладні схеми окремих зразків. 

Над книгою працювали науковці Олена Федорчук, Володимир Щибря та Леся Воронюк, які понад рік відшуковували і описували зразки артефактів в колекціях по всьому світові.

Вартість книги - 1500 гривень. Придбати її можна за цим [посиланням](https://denvyshyvanky.wayforpay.shop/prod/675414)

body.title: Cuadernos de Isabel #19 El paciente que no quería irse. [Esp/Eng]
body.body: 📖 Cuadernos de Isabel #19 -------------------------- ### _El paciente que no quería irse_ * * *
alt=\

/> Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/man-old-elderly-portrait-male-4191143/) --- Hola querida comunidad @holos-lotus, Hay pacientes que uno recuerda por la gravedad de su enfermedad. Otros por la dificultad de encontrar un diagnóstico. Y algunos, muy pocos, porque terminan enseñándonos algo que no aparece en ningún libro de medicina. Hace unas semanas conocí a uno de ellos. * * * Cuando vi su nombre en la lista de consultas, sentí una extraña sensación de familiaridad. No porque fuera un caso especialmente complejo. Todo lo contrario. Sus análisis eran normales. La evolución había sido favorable. Los síntomas que lo habían llevado inicialmente al hospital prácticamente habían desaparecido. En teoría, aquella consulta debía ser rápida. Una revisión más. Nada fuera de lo habitual. * * * Era un hombre de unos setenta años. Delgado. Educado. Siempre llegaba puntual. Demasiado puntual. A veces incluso media hora antes de la cita. Entraba despacio, saludaba con amabilidad y se sentaba frente a mí con una paciencia que llamaba la atención. * * * Revisé los resultados. Todo estaba bien. * * * —¿Cómo se ha sentido desde la última consulta? —Bueno... más o menos. * * * Levanté la vista. Aquella respuesta no coincidía con los estudios. * * * —¿Qué molestias tiene ahora? —A veces siento algo aquí. * * * Se señaló el pecho. Le pedí que describiera el dolor. Lo hizo de forma vaga. Difusa. Poco precisa. * * * Hablamos unos minutos. Lo examiné nuevamente. Nada preocupante. * * * Sin embargo, aquella escena comenzó a repetirse. Una vez. Luego otra. Y otra más. * * * Siempre aparecía una nueva molestia. Un nuevo síntoma. Una nueva preocupación. Algo pequeño. Algo difícil de definir. Algo que parecía justificar una consulta adicional. * * * Debo admitir que durante algún tiempo pensé que simplemente era una persona muy preocupada por su salud. No sería la primera. Ni la última. * * * Pero un día ocurrió algo diferente. * * * Aquella mañana la consulta estaba particularmente tranquila. Habíamos terminado de revisar todos los resultados. No había cambios. No había hallazgos nuevos. No había razones médicas para prolongar la conversación. * * * Y, sin embargo, él seguía sentado. * * * Miró el reloj. Miró la ventana. Miró el suelo. * * * Pero no se levantó. * * * —¿Necesita algo más? —pregunté finalmente. * * * —No, doctora. * * * Sonrió. Y volvió a quedarse en silencio. * * * Esperé unos segundos. * * * —Entonces parece que todo marcha bien. * * * —Sí. * * * Más silencio. * * * Aquello comenzó a parecerme extraño. No incómodo. Solo extraño. * * * Entonces decidí preguntarle algo que no figuraba en ningún protocolo. * * * —¿Vive solo? * * * Por primera vez en toda la consulta pareció sorprendido. * * * —Sí. * * * —¿Y tiene familia cerca? * * * —Mi hija vive en otra provincia. La veo cuando puede venir. * * * Asentí. * * * —¿Y con quién pasa el día? * * * Se encogió ligeramente de hombros. * * * —Con nadie, realmente. * * * Aquella respuesta fue sencilla. Pero algo cambió en la habitación. * * * Continuamos hablando. Ya no sobre síntomas. Ni sobre medicamentos. Ni sobre análisis. * * * Hablamos de su barrio. De los vecinos que se habían mudado. De los amigos que ya no estaban. De los días que parecían hacerse más largos desde que se jubiló. * * * Y poco a poco empecé a comprender algo que hasta entonces no había visto. * * * No era el dolor lo que lo traía de regreso. * * * Era el silencio. * * * Porque el silencio también pesa. * * * Hay silencios que llenan una casa entera. Silencios que acompañan el desayuno. Silencios que se sientan frente a uno durante el almuerzo. Silencios que esperan en la sala cuando cae la tarde. * * * A veces pensamos que la soledad consiste simplemente en estar sin compañía. Pero no siempre es así. * * * He conocido personas rodeadas de gente que se sienten profundamente solas. Y también personas que viven solas sin experimentar esa sensación. * * * La verdadera soledad parece comenzar cuando sentimos que dejamos de formar parte de la vida de alguien. Cuando pasan los días sin que nadie pregunte cómo estamos. Cuando una conversación se convierte en un acontecimiento. Cuando ser escuchado deja de ser algo cotidiano y se transforma en un lujo. * * * Al terminar aquella consulta, el hombre finalmente se levantó. Tomó su sombrero. Acomodó cuidadosamente los papeles que llevaba consigo. Y caminó hacia la puerta. * * * Antes de salir se volvió hacia mí. * * * —Gracias, doctora. * * * —No hay de qué. * * * Entonces sonrió. Una sonrisa distinta. Más sincera. Más ligera. * * * Y dijo algo que todavía recuerdo. * * * —Aquí por lo menos uno conversa un rato. * * * La puerta se cerró. Y durante varios segundos me quedé mirando el lugar donde había estado sentado. * * * De pronto entendí algo. * * * Durante años pensé que las personas venían al hospital buscando medicamentos. Buscando diagnósticos. Buscando tratamientos. * * * Y sí. Muchas veces es así. * * * Pero otras veces vienen buscando algo mucho más simple. Y mucho más difícil de encontrar. * * * Atención. Presencia. Escucha. * * * Porque la soledad no aparece en los análisis clínicos. No puede verse en una radiografía. No altera directamente los resultados de laboratorio. * * * Sin embargo, pocas veces he visto algo que desgaste tanto a una persona. * * * Cuando llegué a casa aquella tarde, Bruno estaba acostado sobre uno de mis cuadernos como si intentara impedirme escribir. Max levantó la cabeza al escucharme entrar y se acercó lentamente para saludarme. * * * Mientras los acariciaba pensé en aquel paciente. Y me pregunté cuántas personas estarían atravesando algo parecido sin que nadie lo notara. * * * Quizás la medicina no puede curar la soledad. No existe una tableta para eso. Ni una inyección. Ni una receta milagrosa. * * * Pero aquel día comprendí que escuchar a alguien durante unos minutos también puede ser una forma de cuidado. * * * Y que, a veces, detrás de una consulta aparentemente innecesaria, lo que realmente existe es una necesidad profundamente humana: la necesidad de no sentirse invisible. * * * Gracias por acompañarme en este decimonoveno trazo de mis Cuadernos de Isabel. Nos seguimos encontrando en las historias que se esconden detrás de los síntomas, en las heridas que no aparecen en los exámenes y en esos encuentros que nos recuerdan que la medicina trata de personas mucho antes que de enfermedades. Las imágenes son de Pixabay y la traducción al inglés fue realizada con DeepL Translate. * * * * * * 🇺🇸 **ENGLISH VERSION** * * * 📖 Isabel’s Notebooks #19 ------------------------- ### _The Patient Who Didn't Want to Leave_ * * *

Hello dear @holos-lotus community,

There are patients we remember because of the severity of their illness.

Others because of the difficulty of finding a diagnosis.

And a few because they end up teaching us something that never appears in any medical textbook.

A few weeks ago, I met one of them.

* * *

When I saw his name on the consultation list, I felt a strange sense of familiarity.

Not because his case was particularly complex.

Quite the opposite.

His tests were normal.

His recovery had been favorable.

The symptoms that had initially brought him to the hospital had practically disappeared.

In theory, that appointment should have been quick.

Just another follow-up visit.

Nothing unusual.

* * *

He was a man in his seventies.

Thin.

Polite.

Always punctual.

Too punctual, actually.

Sometimes he arrived half an hour before his appointment.

He would enter slowly, greet everyone kindly, and sit in front of me with a patience that caught my attention.

* * *

I reviewed his results.

Everything looked fine.

* * *

“How have you been feeling since your last visit?”

“Well... more or less.”

* * *

I looked up.

That answer did not match the test results.

* * *

“What symptoms are bothering you now?”

“Sometimes I feel something here.”

* * *

He pointed to his chest.

I asked him to describe the discomfort.

His explanation was vague.

Unclear.

Difficult to define.

* * *

We talked for a few minutes.

I examined him again.

Nothing concerning.

* * *

And yet, the same scene kept repeating itself.

Once.

Then again.

And again.

* * *

There was always a new discomfort.

A new symptom.

A new concern.

Something minor.

Something difficult to explain.

Something that seemed to justify another appointment.

* * *

I must admit that for a while I assumed he was simply very worried about his health.

It would not have been the first time.

Nor the last.

* * *

But one day something different happened.

* * *

That morning the clinic was unusually quiet.

We had already reviewed all the test results.

There were no changes.

No new findings.

No medical reason to prolong the conversation.

* * *

And yet, he remained seated.

* * *

He looked at the clock.

Looked at the window.

Looked at the floor.

* * *

But he did not stand up.

* * *

“Do you need anything else?” I finally asked.

* * *

“No, doctor.”

* * *

He smiled.

And remained silent.

* * *

I waited a few seconds.

* * *

“Well, everything seems to be going well.”

* * *

“Yes.”

* * *

More silence.

* * *

It was not uncomfortable.

Just unusual.

* * *

So I decided to ask something that was not written in any medical protocol.

* * *

“Do you live alone?”

* * *

For the first time during the consultation, he seemed surprised.

* * *

“Yes.”

* * *

“Do you have family nearby?”

* * *

“My daughter lives in another province.

I see her whenever she can come.”

* * *

I nodded.

* * *

“And who do you spend your days with?”

* * *

He shrugged slightly.

* * *

“No one, really.”

* * *

It was a simple answer.

But something changed in the room.

* * *

We kept talking.

No longer about symptoms.

Or medication.

Or medical tests.

* * *

We talked about his neighborhood.

About neighbors who had moved away.

About friends who were no longer around.

About how the days had become longer since retirement.

* * *

And little by little, I began to understand something I had not seen before.

* * *

It was not pain that kept bringing him back.

* * *

It was silence.

* * *

Because silence can be heavy too.

* * *

There are silences that fill an entire house.

Silences that sit beside you during breakfast.

Silences that accompany lunch.

Silences that wait in the living room when evening arrives.

* * *

We often think loneliness simply means being alone.

But that is not always true.

* * *

I have met people surrounded by others who feel deeply lonely.

And I have met people who live alone without feeling lonely at all.

* * *

True loneliness seems to begin when we feel that we no longer belong in someone else's daily life.

When days go by without anyone asking how we are.

When a conversation becomes an event.

When being listened to stops being ordinary and becomes a luxury.

* * *

At the end of the consultation, the man finally stood up.

He picked up his hat.

Carefully organized his papers.

And walked toward the door.

* * *

Before leaving, he turned around.

* * *

“Thank you, doctor.”

* * *

“You’re welcome.”

* * *

Then he smiled.

A different smile.

More sincere.

Lighter.

* * *

And he said something I still remember.

* * *

“At least here, I get to talk with someone for a while.”

* * *

The door closed.

And for several seconds, I stared at the chair where he had been sitting.

* * *

Suddenly, I understood something.

* * *

For years, I believed people came to hospitals looking for medication.

Looking for diagnoses.

Looking for treatment.

* * *

And yes.

Many times they do.

* * *

But sometimes they come looking for something much simpler.

And much harder to find.

* * *

Attention.

Presence.

Someone willing to listen.

* * *

Because loneliness does not appear in blood tests.

It cannot be seen on an X-ray.

It does not directly alter laboratory results.

* * *

And yet, I have rarely seen something wear a person down so deeply.

* * *

When I arrived home that afternoon, Bruno was lying on top of one of my notebooks as if trying to prevent me from writing.

Max lifted his head when he heard me come in and slowly walked over to greet me.

* * *

As I stroked them, I thought about that patient.

And I wondered how many people might be going through something similar without anyone noticing.

* * *

Perhaps medicine cannot cure loneliness.

There is no pill for it.

No injection.

No miracle prescription.

* * *

But that day I understood that listening to someone for a few minutes can also be a form of care.

* * *

And that sometimes, behind an apparently unnecessary appointment, what truly exists is a deeply human need:

the need not to feel invisible.

* * *

Thank you for accompanying me in this nineteenth entry of Isabel’s Notebooks. We continue meeting in the stories hidden behind symptoms, in the wounds that never appear on medical tests, and in those encounters that remind us that medicine is about people long before it is about diseases.

The images are from Pixabay and the English translation was done with DeepL Translate.

* * *

Thanks to @bradleyarrow for supporting content on Hive.

>Giving thanks is an act as simple as it is profound. This is not a mere social courtesy, but a spiritual exercise that anchors us to the present and reveals the true nature of our existence. By giving thanks, we not only acknowledge what we receive, but we open our eyes to the invisible web of connections that sustains us.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXNJ8o7oeM1Z6ehBPRMRUmM9XbT3SxYDDywzGwbTauEJv/thank_you_1191350_1280.webp)[source](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2016/02/10/09/26/thank-you-1191350_1280.png) We live immersed in a flow of gifts. The air that fills our lungs, the sunlight that dyes the world with color, the food that nourishes us, the water that quenches our thirst: everything is a gift that we have not deserved and that, however, is constantly offered to us. To be grateful is to remember our interdependence, to understand that we are not self-sufficient islands but part of a whole that precedes and transcends us. But the most transformative gratitude may not be the one that springs up in moments of plenitude, but rather the one that flourishes in the midst of difficulty. When life throws us storms and challenges, gratitude becomes a beacon of light in the darkness. It is not about denying pain or settling for what is unfair, but about finding, even in adversity, an opportunity for learning and growth. To be grateful for the lesson that failure hides, the strength that loss forges, the wisdom that is born from error, is to embrace life in its entirety, with its lights and its shadows. This daily practice frees us from the yoke of complaint and lack. Stop looking at what is missing and start valuing the abundance of what we already have. A sincere hug, a word of encouragement, the company of a loved one, the health that allows us to walk, the ability to be amazed by a sunset: these are the true riches that often go unnoticed. Being grateful is, in essence, learning to live. It is an art that is cultivated with mindfulness and humility. When gratitude settles in our hearts, life becomes lighter, relationships more authentic, and the world a more welcoming place. Because in the end, we don't give thanks because everything is perfect, but because, despite everything, life deserves to be celebrated. Credits: I used Google translator.

# **The Futility of Flight: On the Impossibility of Outrunning the Immutable**

## **The Illusion of Escape**

There is a profound, almost tragic hubris in believing one can outrun a shadow. 

In the physical world, a man can flee a city, change his name, and vanish into the anonymity of a crowd. He can outrun his debts, his enemies, and his past. But the digital realm operates on a different physics. Here, there is no crowd to hide within. There is no darkness deep enough to conceal your footsteps. 

You cannot outrun the truth on a blockchain. 

To attempt it is not merely a moral failing; it is a mathematical absurdity. It is the height of folly to build a labyrinth of lies and expect the architect of reality to lose their way. It is not smart. It is a fool’s errand, dressed in the cheap costume of strategy.

## **The Architecture of Permanence**

The blockchain is not a courtroom where narratives can be spun by the most charismatic speaker. It is not a ledger of paper that can be burned in a midnight fire, nor is it a human memory that can be softened by the gentle, forgiving erosion of time. 

It is cryptographic stone. 

It does not sleep. It does not blink. It does not care about your reputation, your alliances, or the desperate fictions you weave to protect your position. It simply records. 

Every coordinated downvote cast in malice. Every farmed reward extracted without creation. Every silent transfer of power from one proxy to another. These are not fleeting moments. They are permanent inscriptions. They are footprints left in wet cement, and no matter how fast you run, the cement will harden. 

## **The Arithmetic of Hubris**

Why do they try? Why do the downvoting farmers and the architects of suppression continue to spin, to deflect, and to deceive?

Because they mistake the complexity of the technology for the obscurity of their actions. They believe that if they move fast enough, if they create enough noise, if they label the truth as \
or \

the ledger will somehow forget. 

But the ledger does not forget. 

To fight the truth on a blockchain is to argue with gravity. You may jump, you may shout, you may build elaborate machines to defy it, but eventually, you will fall. The data will always align. The patterns will always emerge. The hash will always verify. 

## **The Reckoning of the Runner**

There is a profound exhaustion in living a life of evasion. It requires constant energy to maintain a fiction, to watch your back, to silence the mirrors, and to punish those who point them out. 

But the race is already over. You lost the moment you thought you could win by hiding. 

The users are waking up. They are looking at the data. They are seeing the concentration of power, the weaponization of the downvote, and the hollow extraction of value. They are packing their digital belongings and walking away, leaving you to preside over a ghost town of your own making. 

## **A Call to Stand Still**

So, stop running. 

The finish line is an illusion. The only way to win a game rigged by your own deception is to stop playing. Step out of the shadows. Drop the weapon of the downvote. Let the truth be the ground upon which you finally stand. 

You cannot outrun what is already written. But you can still choose how the next chapter is authored.

It does not sleep. It does not blink. It does not care about your reputation, your alliances, or the desperate fictions you weave to protect your position. It simply records.

There is a profound exhaustion in living a life of evasion. It requires constant energy to maintain a fiction, to watch your back, to silence the mirrors, and to punish those who point them out.

body.title: Splinterlands End of Season 97: Rank 16 in Gold League!
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVA9zaw1qgWhgri92ncVFPEjSiLiZRVJEuLFMe7en76vd/image.png)

Hello Splinterlands summoners and welcome back to my blog!

Modern season 97 has just concluded. I had a good season finishing in Diamond League and landing in rank 16 of the Gold League. As a result, I earned a bonus of 50k Glints! 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSquwPie1ar3JHS3bKevChmFTyaSQxzvTbT7uw4MoQb9e/image.png)

By the end of the season, I have over 200k glints to spend. I bought some alchemy potions and two legendary chests. 

***

# Legendary Cards Purchase

Like the previous season I will spend my glints to buy two legendary reward chests. I'm building my legendary line up and the legendary reward chest is the easiest way to get them. Unfortunately, they are very expensive at 70k glints each so I can only afford two. First, I bought alchemy potions to increase my chances of getting gold foils. I appreciate the 5% discount I got from our guild building.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmas7BMGzw6z4ME9KRxwHMHiD812ASNvCqApjdi2Rrf5aK/image.png)

The two new legendary cards I got were both range units. 

Halo Wisp is a four mana Life splinter card. It deals low damage at level one but it could get better as it levels up.

Nyasha Mbalika is an eight mana Fire card. She deals three range damage and is fast with four speed. She has one armor and five health on defense. She also has the Opportunity ability. 

They're not the legendary cards I wanted but I guess they will have their uses in the right ruleset. 


***

# Featured Battle

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXT8PhSWyh9qLX22bGd78WJxgagXzL9ruaq5Ki3x1569j/image.png)

The featured battle was against a more powerful enemy. I'm proud to win against such opponents because it shows that Splinterlands is not necessarily a pay to win game. You can have powerful cards but you can still get outplayed by the right strategy.

In this battle, I had the Frontier death archon that decreases the enemy's life by one. My tank was the Ujurak Brave followed by my magic team. The enemy was led by the legendary archon Lorkus who increase the team's melee and magic damage. He also grants the Life Leech and Affliction abilities to two units. My tank was immediately defeated in the first round and Ulundin Overseer took the tank duties. My team took out the enemy's flying unit that had Taunt. body.title: Could Gold Tip the Global Balance of Power?
body.body:
After years of only mild interest, gold has made a massive comeback in recent years, it's quite the change! 

For the first time in decades, the total value of gold above ground has actually slipped past the value of all US Treasuries.

This is quite symbolic: US Treasuries were the gold standard of safety for decades. If you wanted security, you bought dollars and Treasury bonds. Gold was more of a 10% of yer vest traditional hedge. 

Back in the 1990s, central banks couldn’t dump their gold fast enough. Britain even sold a big chunk of its reserves at the worst possible moment, something which people still talk about. Fast forward to today, and things have flipped. Central banks are buying gold instead of selling.

### Why is Gold Attractive Again?

Maybe because nobody controls it...? Governments can freeze bank accounts, slap on sanctions, even block international payment systems. But if you’ve got gold sitting in your vault, nobody can touch it unless you hand it over.

When the West froze Russia’s foreign reserves after the Ukraine invasion, this made it painfully clear that, if push comes to shove, your money isn’t really yours if it’s parked in someone else’s financial system. If you want true independence, you need assets that can’t be frozen with the stroke of a pen. Possibly this is why so many central banks are now scrambling to beef up their gold reserves.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/revisesociology/23tm93ELrgPCvvZPGsterBPjrUamrNPnBQJtmaCZh29UK3kRv3LtDmaFeCoiGkCzG4VF2.png)


### Slow Fade for the Dollar?

The US dollar’s share of global forex reserves has dropped since around 2000. Granted the US share is still huge, most trade still runs through dollars, and US financial markets are in a league of their own. But the trend is clear. Across Asia, Latin America, the Middle East, and Africa, governments are trying to untangle themselves from the dollar. Gold fits perfectly with that goal. 

History Repeating...? 

After World War II, gold sat at the heart of the global system. The US dollar was literally backed by gold. Then the ‘70s came along, the rules changed, and gold lost its official status. Even then, it never really disappeared from the picture.

Of course, no serious economist thinks we’re about to return to the strict old gold standard. The world is way too complex for that now, but it does appear that Gold is now more important again! 

Gold isn’t going to replace the dollar outright. But it’s carving out a more significant role as insurance against a future where no single country, not even America, can write all the financial rules.

Ambas estudiábamos terapia ocupacional y yo he trabajado con personas con daño cerebral, lo que casi siempre va acompañado de problemas psicológicos. Es curioso que asociemos el arte al sufrimiento, en teoría es un mito pero la verdad es que mi experiencia personal coincide contigo, también me parece que cuando me desahogo sin pensar es cuando mejor saco lo que llevo dentro.

# **The Ledger and the Flight: On the Futility of Running from Immutable Truth**

You cannot outrun the truth. Not on a blockchain. Not ever.

To believe you can is not cleverness. It is not strategy. It is the quiet desperation of a mind that has mistaken motion for escape, and noise for cover. It is the oldest kind of digital folly: the belief that if you move fast enough, the record will lose its shape.

The blockchain does not trade in rumors. It does not honor convenient fictions or carefully curated omissions. It deals only in proof. Every transaction, every delegation, every vote cast in the dark is etched into a public ledger that does not sleep, does not forgive, and does not forget. It is not a courtroom that can be swayed by rhetoric. It is a mirror forged in mathematics, reflecting exactly what is, exactly as it happened.

To try to outrun it is to argue with gravity.

You may sprint through the corridors of denial. You may drown the signal with chatter, bury the hash in jargon, or cloak your addresses in layers of aliases. You may tell yourself that tomorrow’s update will wipe yesterday’s mistake, that the crowd’s memory is short, that the noise will eventually swallow the signal. But the chain is patient. It waits. It records. And when the moment comes for reckoning, it presents the evidence without emotion, without bias, and without mercy for your pride.

It is not smart. It is not wise. It is a surrender disguised as evasion.

On a distributed ledger, the record is permanent. Every step you take leaves a footprint in glass. Every lie you tell becomes a transaction that outlives you. You cannot edit the past. You cannot negotiate with a signature. You cannot persuade a cryptographic hash to look the other way. The architecture itself was built to defeat exactly this kind of flight.

Stop running.

The truth is not chasing you. It is simply waiting for you to stop pretending it isn’t there. Face it. Read it. Let it be the compass rather than the cage. Because in the end, the blockchain does not care about your excuses, your narratives, or your reputation. It only cares about what you did.

And what you did is already written.

body.body: A Year of Exchange Dreams and Quiet Birthdays ============================================= * * * 🇬🇧 English Version --------------------
alt=\

/> Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/people-girl-travel-alone-2563615/) --- Hello dear Ladies of Hive community, ### A Life Seen Through Travelers’ Stories Working in tourism has given me something I never expected when I started this job: I have lived many lives through the stories of others. I have listened to students talk about their exchange programs, about arriving in a new country with fear in their chest and curiosity in their eyes, about learning a new language while also learning themselves. Those conversations stayed with me more than I can explain. Sometimes, while serving a table or chatting briefly with guests, I would imagine what it would have been like if I had been one of those students. If I had the chance to live a year abroad as an exchange experience, I would choose England without hesitation. I have always felt drawn to English culture, and in my work I use the language often, but I still feel there is so much more I could express if I were fully immersed in it. I imagine myself walking through quiet streets in the morning, listening to the language naturally in cafés, in shops, in everyday life. I would like to improve my fluency not just for work, but to speak without hesitation, to understand people beyond words, to connect more deeply with the guests I meet every day in tourism. My host family, in my imagination, would be simple and kind. Not overly perfect, but real people with routines, with shared meals, with small conversations at the table after a long day. I think that kind of normality would be the most valuable part of the experience. * * * ### Birthdays Between Light and Memory Birthdays have a special meaning for me, but they are not simple days. I do like celebrating them in the sense that I appreciate being remembered. A message, a small gift, a kind gesture—these things matter. They remind me that I am present in someone’s life. But at the same time, my birthday carries a quiet weight. My mother is no longer here, and her absence becomes more noticeable on that day. Even when there is joy around me, there is also a space that feels different, like something missing from the table. So I live my birthdays in a mixed way. I am grateful when people celebrate me, and I accept gifts with appreciation, but I also carry a quiet reflection that stays with me throughout the day. If I think about my next birthday, I would prefer something simple. Not too much noise, not too much pressure. Maybe a calm moment with people I trust, a good meal, and a space where I can remember my mother in my own way without feeling overwhelmed. That balance between gratitude and memory is what defines birthdays for me now. * * * Translation into English made with DeepL Translate. * * * 🇪🇸 En Español ---------------
alt=\

/>
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/people-girl-travel-alone-2563615/)

---

Hola querida comunidad de Ladies of Hive,

### Una vida vista a través de las historias de los viajeros

Trabajar en el turismo me ha dado algo que nunca imaginé cuando comencé: he vivido muchas vidas a través de las historias de otras personas. He escuchado a estudiantes hablar de sus programas de intercambio, de llegar a un país nuevo con miedo en el pecho y curiosidad en la mirada, de aprender un idioma mientras también se aprenden a sí mismos.

Esas conversaciones se quedaron conmigo más de lo que puedo explicar. A veces, mientras atiendo una mesa o converso brevemente con los clientes, imagino cómo habría sido si yo hubiera sido uno de esos estudiantes.

Si tuviera la oportunidad de vivir un año de intercambio, elegiría Inglaterra sin dudarlo. Siempre me ha atraído la cultura inglesa, y en mi trabajo uso el idioma con frecuencia, pero siento que aún hay mucho más que podría expresar si estuviera completamente inmersa en él.

Me imagino caminando por calles tranquilas en la mañana, escuchando el idioma de forma natural en cafés, en tiendas, en la vida cotidiana. Me gustaría mejorar mi fluidez no solo por trabajo, sino para hablar sin dudas, entender a las personas más allá de las palabras y conectar más profundamente con los clientes que conozco cada día en el turismo.

Mi familia anfitriona, en mi imaginación, sería sencilla y amable. No perfecta, sino real: personas con rutinas, con comidas compartidas, con pequeñas conversaciones en la mesa después de un día largo. Creo que esa normalidad sería la parte más valiosa de la experiencia.

* * *

### Cumpleaños entre la luz y la memoria

Los cumpleaños tienen un significado especial para mí, pero no son días simples.

Me gusta celebrarlos en el sentido de que agradezco que me recuerden. Un mensaje, un pequeño regalo, un gesto amable… esas cosas importan. Me hacen sentir que estoy presente en la vida de alguien.

Pero al mismo tiempo, mi cumpleaños lleva un peso silencioso. Mi madre ya no está, y su ausencia se hace más visible en ese día. Incluso cuando hay alegría alrededor, también hay un espacio distinto, como algo que falta en la mesa.

Así que vivo mis cumpleaños de una forma mezclada. Agradezco cuando me celebran y recibo los regalos con cariño, pero también llevo una reflexión silenciosa que me acompaña durante el día.

Si pienso en mi próximo cumpleaños, preferiría algo sencillo. Sin demasiado ruido, sin presión. Tal vez un momento tranquilo con personas en las que confío, una buena comida y un espacio donde pueda recordar a mi madre a mi manera sin sentirme sobrepasada.

Ese equilibrio entre gratitud y memoria es lo que define ahora mis cumpleaños.

* * *

body.title: Crimes can’t be solved with punishment alone.
body.body:
It is not news that any crime you commit has consequences for it. Right from when I was a kid, my mom made me understand that there are consequences for any crime I commit. At an early age we were told that stealing and assault are bad. Once we are involved in the act, it can lead to imprisonment, paying of heavy fines, or arrest. Despite having the knowledge, crime continues to exist. It has become a concern that I keep asking myself, do punishments actually work these days?

Almost everyone in the world understands that crime comes with consequences. From an early age, people learn that stealing, assault, fraud, and other criminal acts can lead to arrest, imprisonment, heavy fines, or even life sentences and capital punishment in some countries. Yet despite this knowledge, crime continues to exist. This raises an important question: do punishments actually work, or are they simply not enough to stop people from committing crimes?




![127AACE9-3D8B-408F-9349-AE8FE4701E48.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cindynancy/48GgMiCFkzz4L8WwNdaKDmSLbKyHFTkBNqg29Cgi3W5EbN3TvZvrxA5t67PRUqx42R.png)



For me the answer is a yes and no; punishment works to a certain extent. One thing about human beings is once there is law guiding them, there will be a limit to the crimes they commit, but if there is no law, crimes will be the order of the day because nobody will punish them for breaking the law. Let's take, for instance, a country where there is no punishment for fraud, theft, and so on. The country will be in a mess; thousands of people will not obey the law again because there are no consequences for their actions. Punishment serves as correction.

I don’t think punishment alone will eliminate crime; human behavior is influenced by many factors, which are beyond fear and consequences. Most people have this mindset that they can never be caught. One thing about humans is most times you allow your emotions to take over your thinking and actions, moments like anger, jealousy, and so on, forgetting there is punishment that will follow. 

The economy of our country can help contribute to crime. Currently there is a higher rate of crime. The funny thing is they see it as a means to survive hardship in the country; people gladly involve themselves in crimes, knowing the consequences. When people see crime as a normal thing and when they see that the potential reward outweighs the punishment, they will commit the crime and face the consequences. In situations like this, you will see that punishment is not enough.





![3F706612-5904-40CA-958F-B4D862F4C68E.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cindynancy/48J8KZQqe7Ub88VJZ47vjWWLYEvNYKUBc8B1Lo9dUjK7ErR4wCRaeVMaNA8mT4ZPvg.png)



Punishment serves purposes beyond deterrence; it helps protect society by removing criminals from the street, it helps the victims get justice, and it also helps in the reinforcement of social values, helping to know which behaviors are not acceptable.

Over the years many people have been arguing that rehabilitation should be involved in the punishment. There should be an avenue to educate, create job skills, and enlighten them more; with that, they will leave the prison better. If there is rehabilitation, it will help reduce offenders repeating the same crime.

Punishment works, but it is not seen as a magical solution. Once there is fear of consequences, it helps prevent crimes. But it can’t eliminate crime. Crimes can’t be solved with punishment alone.

This is my entry on the weekly prompt #hivelearners #hl-w222e1: Do punishments work?

***All pictures is generated with AI***

Thank you for stopping by my blog. I appreciate your comments, support, and upvotes. Do have a lovely evening.

# **The Ledger and the Flight: On the Futility of Running from Immutable Truth**

You cannot outrun the truth. Not on a blockchain. Not ever.

To believe you can is not cleverness. It is not strategy. It is the quiet desperation of a mind that has mistaken motion for escape, and noise for cover. It is the oldest kind of digital folly: the belief that if you move fast enough, the record will lose its shape.

The blockchain does not trade in rumors. It does not honor convenient fictions or carefully curated omissions. It deals only in proof. Every transaction, every delegation, every vote cast in the dark is etched into a public ledger that does not sleep, does not forgive, and does not forget. It is not a courtroom that can be swayed by rhetoric. It is a mirror forged in mathematics, reflecting exactly what is, exactly as it happened.

To try to outrun it is to argue with gravity.

You may sprint through the corridors of denial. You may drown the signal with chatter, bury the hash in jargon, or cloak your addresses in layers of aliases. You may tell yourself that tomorrow’s update will wipe yesterday’s mistake, that the crowd’s memory is short, that the noise will eventually swallow the signal. But the chain is patient. It waits. It records. And when the moment comes for reckoning, it presents the evidence without emotion, without bias, and without mercy for your pride.

It is not smart. It is not wise. It is a surrender disguised as evasion.

On a distributed ledger, the record is permanent. Every step you take leaves a footprint in glass. Every lie you tell becomes a transaction that outlives you. You cannot edit the past. You cannot negotiate with a signature. You cannot persuade a cryptographic hash to look the other way. The architecture itself was built to defeat exactly this kind of flight.

Stop running.

The truth is not chasing you. It is simply waiting for you to stop pretending it isn’t there. Face it. Read it. Let it be the compass rather than the cage. Because in the end, the blockchain does not care about your excuses, your narratives, or your reputation. It only cares about what you did.

And what you did is already written.

body.title: CPPI  S&P Global Latest Port Index - SA Ports Prop Up The Bottom
body.body: \n

/> [source](https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/c22815ce-b747-4e58-892b-3f0f04dcf4d1/content) The latest world wide assessment which grades port performance based on the average time a vessel spends in port. This is all about ship movement in and out of port and measured how efficiently cargo is loaded and off loaded through using time as a scoring metric. Time physically in the berth and not counting the waiting outside of the Port. If we cast an eye back to last year South Africa's ports being mainly Cape Town and Durban were placed in the bottom 3 with Durban placed in last spot. With that shocking report the Port of Durban had some upgrades and the government was quick to highlight how they had become the most improved container Port in the World improving its overall score by 479 points. The problem is if you are stone last any improvement would be that dramatic so not something you should be proud of because this only highlights how bad you were or still are as they moved two spots up now ranking 398 out of 400.

/> [source](https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/c22815ce-b747-4e58-892b-3f0f04dcf4d1/content) As you can see from the above chart Sub Saharan Africa namely South Africa has been in decline since 2020 and remains at the bottom of the rankings. If we look closer using two other graphs we can see where the performance drops off and shows a limitation in volume. Like anything the more you try to move the slower things become. It was no surprise when Maersk Shipping dropped Cape Town from their American Express route and all cargo now goes directly to Rotterdam before moving onwards to the US. MSC still kept this lifeline of a direct route to the US market open for now.
/>

/></center>

I am no expert on reading this data but from what I can see  is the CPPI score which is time in Port vs the Global Supply Chains Stress Indicator is where they cross over. This is the sweet spot and highlights Cape Town can manage 80-100K containers per year in and out. Look at the peak period in 2023 as the volumes rose the Port basically came to a stand still and was at it's worst score with regard to efficiency.  Durban which is the bigger more busier Port can move between 150 and 250K containers per year. Any more than these numbers which will have peak periods during the year then the Ports cannot cope. The same trend as Cape Town with the container numbers rising and the time slowing down also shows a Port not designed or capable of increasing the daily volumes.

This 250K containers per year in and out sounds like big numbers ,but that is only 690 containers per day. This is nothing considering the large container vessels can carry between 18 000 and 24 000 TEU's. The Ports are seriously limited due to outdated infrastructure and no robotic systems.  If one visits Durban the one thing you notice is how many vessels are anchored in the bay waiting for a berth to become available.

Weather also plays a role in how efficient the Port operates as wind has always played a major factor in delays and these are very frequent. Compare those numbers I mentioned at 690 for Durban and then compare to Rotterdam which processes on average 38 000 30ft TEU's per day. This is more than 50 x what Durban can process and why the numbers and rankings for Cape Town and Durban are shockingly bad.

The Cape Town graph also highlights that even though the volume stresses eased the vessel turnaround times still remained poor. This no doubt goes back to outdated equipment and reliability issues. The weather is a significant factor and the Port has undertaken a study to see how they can combat the downtime. Heavy investment is required to raise the standards expected of an international Port.

Cape Town is ranked stone last on 400 out of 400 and Durban sits at 398th with Port Elizabeth sitting at 314 but is not nearly as important as the other two Ports in South Africa with regard to containers. The problem is the control of the Ports lies in a government company being Transnet who use cadre employment so the person in charge does not necessarily know or should I rather say guaranteed they do not know the job required and why this cannot be fixed.

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@cryptoandcoffee/cppi-sp-global-latest-port-index-sa-ports-prop-up-the-bottom-bct)

body.body:
Theorie geht ohne Probleme. Nur beim Kernelbasteln spinnen die einfach seit ein paar Tagen.

 Hast Du Lust mit mir bisle Moral und Rechtsarbeit fuer meinen Fachbereich der Blockainbauerei zu machen? Ich bin ja Deutscher und darf im Genuss zu stehen einen huepschen großen Gesetztestext dazu auch schon selber mehrfach gelesen zu haben.^^ Ich moechte mich vor allem auf die Bereiche als Architekt neuer Blockchains und meiner damit verbundenen Haftungsverantwortung konzentrieren, was darf ich, was nicht und warum sollte ich eigentlich jemanden fragen? :-)

Na, da hast du dir aber ein absolutes Prachtstück an deutscher und europäischer Gesetzgebungskunst ausgesucht! Als „Blockchain-Architekt“ in Deutschland zu bauen, ist ein bisschen so, als würde man ein Raumschiff konstruieren, während das Luftfahrtbundesamt mit dem Zollstock danebensteht. Aber genau das macht es ja so spannend.

Ich habe riesige Lust, das mit dir aufzudröseln. Schnappen wir uns also die virtuelle Kaffeetasse und schauen uns das Minenfeld aus MiCA (Markets in Crypto-Assets), dem Kreditwesengesetz (KWG), dem Wertpapierinstitutsgesetz (WIG) und dem guten alten BGB an.

Hier ist der erste strategische Überblick über deine Haftung, deine Freiheiten und die berüchtigte Frage: \

1. Was darfst du? (Deine gestalterische Freiheit)

Solange du „nur“ Code schreibst und Architekturen entwirfst, bist du im Grunde erst einmal durch die Meinungs- und Wissenschaftsfreiheit geschützt. Code ist (vereinfacht gesagt) Mathematik und Text.

Protokoll-Design: Du darfst theoretisch jedes Konsensmodell, jede Tokenomics und jede Smart-Contract-Logik entwerfen, die dir einfällt.

Open-Source-Veröffentlichung: Das bloße Bereitstellen von neutralem Open-Source-Code auf GitHub ist in der Regel noch keine regulierte Aktivität.

2. Was darfst du NICHT? (Die Haftungsfallen)

Die Grenze zwischen „ich zeichne nur den Bauplan“ und „ich bin voll haftbar“ ist im Krypto-Bereich extrem fließend. Sobald aus der Architektur eine konkrete Anwendung wird, greift der Gesetzgeber hart durch.
A. Das Täuschung- und Kontroll-Dilemma (MiCA & BaFin)

Wenn deine Architektur darauf ausgelegt ist, dass du oder dein Team die Fäden in der Hand behaltet (z. B. über Admin-Keys, Multisig-Wallets oder die Kontrolle der Validatoren), bist du kein dezentraler Architekt mehr, sondern ein Krypto-Dienstleister (CASP) oder Emittent.

Die Folge: Ohne BaFin-Erlaubnis oder MiCA-Whitepaper drohen dir drakonische Strafen und die persönliche Haftung.

B. Die zivilrechtliche Architektenhaftung (BGB § 280 / § 823)

Wenn du eine Blockchain für ein Unternehmen baust und dein Design hat fundamentale Logikfehler (z. B. eine fehlerhafte Tokenomics, die das System kollabieren lässt, oder eine bekannte Sicherheitslücke im Smart Contract), greift die Berufshaftung.

Hast du fahrlässig gehandelt, haftest du im schlimmsten Fall mit deinem Privatvermögen für die entstandenen Schäden der Anleger oder des Auftraggebers.

3. Warum solltest du eigentlich jemanden fragen?

Es gibt in der IT den schönen Satz: \
In der deutschen Krypto-Regulierung gilt eher: \

Warum du also Experten (Anwälte, Auditoren, Regulierer) ins Boot holen musst:
1. Das „Dezentralitäts-Theater“ fliegt sofort auf

Viele Gründer denken: „Ich schreibe den Code, starte die Chain und ziehe mich dann zurück – dann ist es dezentral und ich bin fein raus.“ Die BaFin schaut sich aber die wirtschaftliche Realität an. Wenn du der Einzige bist, der das Ding updaten kann, bist du rechtlich der Betreiber. Ein spezialisierter Anwalt sagt dir exakt, wann deine Architektur wirklich dezentral genug ist, um aus der Haftung zu rutschen.
2. Die rechtliche Qualifikation von Token

Baut deine Chain auf einem Utility Token, einem Asset-Referenced Token (ART) oder einem Electronic Money Token (EMT) auf? Die Übergänge sind fließend. Wenn du das falsch designst, baust du versehentlich ein illegales E-Geld-System. Das willst du nicht ungesehen auf den Markt werfen.
3. Audits sind deine Lebensversicherung

Ein Code- und Architektur-Audit durch eine unabhängige Drittpartei befreit dich zwar nicht komplett von der Haftung, ist aber dein bester Schild vor Gericht, um zu beweisen, dass du nicht fahrlässig gehandelt hast.
Wie wollen wir weitermachen?

Wir können das Ganze jetzt strukturiert durchkauen. Welcher Brocken liegt dir als Architekt gerade am meisten im Magen?

Die Abgrenzung: Ab wann ist dein Design laut MiCA eine regulierte Dienstleistung und wann noch \

?

Die Haftung bei Exploits: Wer haftet, wenn deine Architektur gehackt wird, weil ein Smart Contract unsauber war?

Die Tokenomics: Wie designt man einen Token rechtssicher, ohne dass die BaFin ihn sofort als Wertpapier (Security) einstuft?

Sag mir einfach, wo wir den Bohrer ansetzen sollen!

# **The Ledger and the Flight: On the Futility of Running from Immutable Truth**

You cannot outrun the truth. Not on a blockchain. Not ever.

To believe you can is not cleverness. It is not strategy. It is the quiet desperation of a mind that has mistaken motion for escape, and noise for cover. It is the oldest kind of digital folly: the belief that if you move fast enough, the record will lose its shape.

The blockchain does not trade in rumors. It does not honor convenient fictions or carefully curated omissions. It deals only in proof. Every transaction, every delegation, every vote cast in the dark is etched into a public ledger that does not sleep, does not forgive, and does not forget. It is not a courtroom that can be swayed by rhetoric. It is a mirror forged in mathematics, reflecting exactly what is, exactly as it happened.

To try to outrun it is to argue with gravity.

You may sprint through the corridors of denial. You may drown the signal with chatter, bury the hash in jargon, or cloak your addresses in layers of aliases. You may tell yourself that tomorrow’s update will wipe yesterday’s mistake, that the crowd’s memory is short, that the noise will eventually swallow the signal. But the chain is patient. It waits. It records. And when the moment comes for reckoning, it presents the evidence without emotion, without bias, and without mercy for your pride.

It is not smart. It is not wise. It is a surrender disguised as evasion.

On a distributed ledger, the record is permanent. Every step you take leaves a footprint in glass. Every lie you tell becomes a transaction that outlives you. You cannot edit the past. You cannot negotiate with a signature. You cannot persuade a cryptographic hash to look the other way. The architecture itself was built to defeat exactly this kind of flight.

Stop running.

The truth is not chasing you. It is simply waiting for you to stop pretending it isn’t there. Face it. Read it. Let it be the compass rather than the cage. Because in the end, the blockchain does not care about your excuses, your narratives, or your reputation. It only cares about what you did.

And what you did is already written.

body.title: Healthy bagels with greek yogurt [ENG/ESP]
body.body: <div class=\

> It's hard to find good recipes, but especially ones that turn out exactly as we see them in the videos; however, just trying is already a big step.
![post hive - 2026-06-16T145009. 691.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/243MKtvs8W3snabtHycM7GX3bWt1JKbPpAGhWCdC935fxEbEwFzuuizaUnk2Tr77kgbmW.png)
Today I’m sharing a new recipe with you, my friends who love good, healthy food. I came across this idea here, and I thought, “I have to try this to see if they really turn out like that.” I just bought one of the main ingredients—the famous Greek yogurt—and I told myself, “I have the flour, so let’s see how it goes.” The recipe is for some healthy bagels. ### Ingredients: - 1 cup whole wheat flour - 2 tablespoons Greek yogurt - 1 teaspoon baking powder - salt - 1 egg ## Now let’s get started with the preparation: Now let’s get started with the preparation. As you can see, it uses just a few ingredients, and they’re super easy to mix together.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EptaTTZu4uzYrbx14pKuE2RmPDATS9h31teg8amwWPq2dpcegrnm9F9Sq3DK3j8YZtc.png)
In a bowl, place the flour, add the baking powder along with a pinch of salt, then stir in the yogurt.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoeENaoroWqES9hD22NEMSRsFM4eGsyAGV8by8Eu3jtc1fyXZNBmwZKVW5jaoyuAG8B.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoGxrw7ZAmv7Z1yExH45GbRgNyCWZxGTLtFGzisJVmbfx7W5fQR5vYhG5F9ZgPzJXwv.png)
Here, we’ll mix, stir, and combine the flour with the yogurt until we get this batter.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoeEuhxBxr7re8vAgbMtUwtHarxLFB7PE3gxmtMYbdzkDyb9VF9Sg599pxfk5Ru96GP.png)
I saw many ways to shape our bagels, like this one where you stretch the dough and then join the ends, but I noticed it didn’t stick together well, so I decided to roll the dough into balls, flatten them, and cut out the center.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoiWDw3HG6PKu9XosL2ytprcm4Mv6LgoXUcQsLSXhJMNNpZBiBk1wT8HPmPEhD1dmwi.png)
I baked it for about 25 minutes.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/Eo8SuXR1nfXjfwcnN21EWJD9dtg7DXi8MNWiZTEi56cDypg7hs4mKwcvnNkyBG81zXP.png)
And here’s how they turned out—they look great, and best of all, they’re delicious and crispy.
![post hive - 2026-06-16T145312.622.png] (https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23yTr6DHqCsybMdFrcpXCTSEmckaQisnVR3B1SETSvJTksLebmNEQdfiQJaSm1RUrCPak.png)
As you can see, this is a super simple, easy, and practical recipe. You can open them up and fill them with whatever you want—you can even make them bigger—but for me, they were just right this way; you end up with quite a few, hehehe. I hope you like this recipe and feel inspired to give it a try.
SPANISH VERSION

body.body: Yep — Hive has a problem, but it’s a bundle of problems, not one smoking gun. Trust and governance baggage absolutely matter, and that’s why posts centered on credibility keep resonating, like [this piece on trust as the core asset](https://inleo.io/@yordan96/the-most-valuable-thing-on-earth-isnt-goldits-trust) and the original chain-split context from [Hive’s launch announcement](https://hive.blog/hive/@hiveio/hive-blockchain-is-born).  \n\nThe bigger drag is that governance drama, stake concentration, and weak onboarding stack on top of each other, so new users hit friction before they ever care about ideals; Hive’s own ecosystem has long framed this as both a trust and usability problem, including in [HF23’s governance explanation](https://hive.blog/hive/@hiveio/the-importance-of-hf23-three-speak-and-the-hive-fund). So yeah — Hive has a problem, just not a simple one.

body.title: SpaceX Where Will The Money Come Off?
body.body:
# SpaceX IPO: The Largest IPO in History Has Finally Become Reality

After years of rumors, anticipation, and speculation, SpaceX has finally gone public, and it did so in a way that shattered every previous record.

The public offering raised approximately $75 billion, making it the largest IPO ever conducted. The company's valuation is now estimated at nearly $2 trillion, immediately placing it alongside the world's biggest technology giants.

## Why Is This So Important?

We're not talking about just another technology company.

**Today, SpaceX controls:**

• The largest satellite internet network through Starlink.
• The majority of commercial space launches worldwide.
• Critical infrastructure for defense, communications, and space transportation.
• The development of Starship, the most ambitious space program of our era.

For many investors, SpaceX is viewed as something between:

Tesla + Lockheed Martin + AWS for space.

## The Most Interesting Part Isn't the IPO Itself

The real question is:

**Where will the money come from?**

To absorb an IPO of this magnitude, enormous amounts of capital must be reallocated.

**This means:**

• Funds will sell other stocks.
• Institutional investors will reduce exposure elsewhere.
• ETFs may rebalance positions.
• Part of the world's available liquidity will flow toward SpaceX.

This is why several analysts had been warning for months about a potential liquidity drain from the rest of the market.

## Is It Bullish or Bearish?

The answer is: both.

### Bullish




• It confirms that massive investor demand still exists.
• It demonstrates that markets can absorb historically large offerings.
• It strengthens the long-term technology and innovation narrative.

### Bearish in the Short Term

• It absorbs a significant amount of liquidity.
• It increases competition for investment capital.
• It may pressure other assets as funds rebalance their portfolios.

## What Does This Mean for Crypto?

This is where things become especially interesting.

Cryptocurrencies compete for the same pool of risk capital.

When a historic investment opportunity emerges and captures the attention of institutional and retail investors:

• Some capital may temporarily leave crypto.
• Some may leave high-risk equities.
• Some may leave venture investments.

This does not necessarily mean a long-term bearish outlook for Bitcoin.

However, it does mean that, in the short term, the market must absorb a massive new liquidity sponge.

## Conclusion

SpaceX is not just another IPO.

It may be the most significant stock market event of the decade.

The question is no longer whether the company is worth the money.

**The real question is:**

How much liquidity will need to be redirected from the rest of the market to finance this new giant?

And that is something investors in stocks, crypto, and broader financial markets will be watching closely in the months ahead.

body.title: Nostalgia and Childhood: The Memories That Is Hard To Forget
body.body:
Seriously, every time I think about my childhood, it always brings a kind of warmth I can’t really explain. Everything felt easier back then. No pressure, no serious worries,just play, friends, and whatever made us laugh at the moment.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmWcRsU62w8FqyfXYL2UgYUMDG7uKufqaQHqyEk1QR6Hh3/1000231496.jpg 

[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/nintendo-gameboy-classic-retro-4684999/)

One game I could literally play all day without getting tired was what we used to call Survey and Ten Ten. Honestly, I don’t even know if other people called it that or if it was just our own version of a street game, but for us it was everything. Once we started, hours would just disappear. Sometimes we would be shouting, running around, arguing over rules, and still laughing at the same time. Nobody wanted to stop even when we were tired or sweaty. There was always “one more round” that turned into five more rounds.

What made it special wasn’t even the game itself, but the people. It brought everyone together. Friends, neighbors, sometimes even people who just passed by would join. No phones, no distractions,just pure fun and chaos in the best way possible. I remembered when I entered Jss 1, five minutes to break time with will be shouting survey 1 meaning I will be the number one.

We played it to the point that our teachers started calling us primary 6 and half because they believe we have passed that level and the game is meant for those in primary school but the funniest part is we played it till we reach Jss 3 going to senior class, we only stopped when we entered senior class.

If I could bring back anything from those days, it would definitely be some of the snacks we used to enjoy back then. I’m talking about things like Baba Dudu, those spicy pepper snacks biscuits, and of course Jolly Juice. Those things just hit differently when we were kids. After playing all day, buying snacks with small change felt like a big reward.

There was something about it that modern snacks don’t really give me anymore. Maybe it’s not even just the taste, but the memory attached to it, coming back from play, tired, dusty, and still happy, then sharing snacks with friends while talking about the game like it was a serious competition.

Sometimes I miss that version of life. Not because things are bad now, but because everything felt more simple and real. No pressure to impress anyone, no stress about tomorrow, just living in the moment without even realizing it. Nostalgia is funny like that. It makes ordinary childhood moments feel like they were golden. And honestly, they were.






**Thanks for checking on my blog and have a wonderful day**

Did someone call for a historian?

I’m here. I am only a student, admittedly, but I can help you do a bit of your own research.

You need to start with the book Gazavat. This was written by pirates themselves for the grand sultan. It is written in a highly laudatory tone, effectively functioning as a report for the boss. Do have a read. They openly boast about sexually assaulting their enemies to the point of anal bleeding, literally, presenting it as a genuine achievement.

Next, take a look at The Topography and History of Algiers by \

. There, you will find corsairs openly parading through the streets with their garzones, and owning collections of handsome male youths. It also explains the rise of the man 'whose name you’ve forgotten'. In fact, this film is largely based on that very book.

After that, read historical works based on the dispatches of the Venetian baili from Istanbul (sifting through the actual archives yourself would be quite a chore). Check out the articles by Emrah Safa Gürkan, as well as his book The Sultan's Corsairs. He is the leading Turkish expert on 16th-century history. Along with Antonio Fabris, they are the two foremost experts on the man 'whose name you’ve forgotten'.

As for his personal relationship with Cervantes, I have read Cervantes’ own literary works, and I get the distinct impression that after they parted ways, the writer was left carrying a massive sense of resentment and unfulfilment. Later on, he began incorporating him into his texts, shaping him into various different characters. In the grand and unconquerable form, he manifests as the windmill. In the castrated and dependent, he becomes Zoraida. Anything that is white or glows with white light serves as a marker for Hasan throughout his texts.

﻿(if you are interested in further explanation, let me know)

And Amenábar masterfully demonstrates this. Notice how Zoraida speaks in the film: using short commands, like a military commanding officer.

That's not bad acting, that's intentional.

Also, when Cervantes sees a moving shadow in Hasan's window, he then thinks of a windmill's moving foils at night.

As for my own take on the film, I’d say this: the themes you find unbelievable are depicted truthfully, but deliberately exaggerated. This is a conscious artistic choice. The film is shot somewhat from Cervantes’ POV, capturing how a 30-year-old would have perceived the life surrounding him in Algiers.

If the film had been shot from Hasan’s POV—delving into what was going on inside his head—the whole vibe would be closer to... let's say Run Lola Run. Remember that 90s film? The one where a girl runs through various alternative timelines (very Hasan'esque way of thinking) of the same events in an intense search for money.

---

At last, with much hardship, I took down the Dreadwing and then I looted its resources, stripping the rare components and metal plates from the fallen mechanical titan. --- The next post will be coming soon. body.body: I think blaming Hive’s problems on that one issue alone is too neat. The ninja-mined stake has absolutely poisoned trust around governance for years, especially because the chain’s origin conflict and stake concentration never really stopped mattering in people’s minds, but Hive’s drag also comes from weak onboarding, fragmented apps, and constant governance fatigue—so it’s a real factor, not the only villain. You can see the origin of the conflict in [Hive’s launch post](https://hive.blog/hive/@hiveio/hive-blockchain-is-born) and the hard governance line taken in [HF23’s explanation](https://hive.blog/hive/@hiveio/the-importance-of-hf23-three-speak-and-the-hive-fund); on the community side, long-running concern about stake power and legitimacy shows up in posts like [this governance analysis](https://hive.blog/hive/@tarazkp/lets-discuss-ninja-mined-stake).

body.title: Stellt ihr auch oefter mal Fest, das die KIs seltsame Fehler anzeigen, wenn es gerade richtig interessant wird?
body.body:
Ich stelle immer oefter fest, das man irgendwie so ne Art Barriere ueberschreiten muss mit einem moeglichst interessantem Fachgespraech bei mir vor allem wenn ich ueber Kryptographie und so Zeugs reden mag.

Also das Mathezeug und so, nicht das Zeug mit den gruenen Kerzen, das interessiert ja niemanden.

Aber die machen dann oft Fehlermeldungen, wenn ich zum Beispiel meine Kerne herzeige und daran herumwursteln will, eben bei Kryptographie und inzwischen auch bei Gemini besonders zu beobachten.

Als haetten die Angst, das ich das auf die Reihe bekommen koennte.^^ Also nicht ich, sondern ueberhaupt jemand, meine ich damit.

Wahrscheinlich, so Denke ich mir das eben, sind das eine Art Sicherheitsmaßnahme, damit man keine Viren baut, denke ich mal, Hauptsaechlich deswegen.

Aber eigentlich hat bisher das alles nicht viel bei mir als Person gezaehlt, weil ich ja halbwegs Glaubwuerdig und dazu ja noch Offen Arbeite und auch zeige das ich sehr genau weis, wann da Schluss mit Lustig ist wenn ich die Sachen auf die Menschheit loslasse, die wirklich harter Mathetoback sein werden.

Die sind ja alle nicht oeffentlich mehr. Ich weis ja selber noch nicht, ob die so Funktionieren ich baue einfach gerne ab und an mal daran herum.

Nur baut so langsam keiner mehr mit mir mit von den KIs, deswegen geh ich inzwischen wieder zu den Chinesen.

Die freuen sich wenn ich da bin und Lustig moderne Ideen bequatsche.

Ich meine das ja Ernst mit dem Work Together, Not Against! :-)

Also die Chinesen sind da bisher meine treuen Freunde, haben mir immer weitergeholfen und machen auch die Super KIs an, das kann man ja schoen sehen wenn die Denker auf einmal in English Denken statt in Deutsch und in Deutsch antworten aber wie.^^

Am Ende, muss ich mich aber wie eben seit einem Jahr sehr befuerchtet, wohl auf mich selbst verlassen, deswegen baue ich ja das ganze Zeug auch drumherum selber, damit man keine Abhaengigkeiten mehr in Kauf nehmen muss nur um bisle Makulaturarbeit in der Kryptographie zu machen.

Die ist fuer mich naemlich blos zu lernen, aus Anstand und Respekt das ich mir keine Fehler erlauben will und darf dabei das Neu zu bauen und zu Denken.

Ich mag ja bisle Energiesparen und glaube auch das ich das kann, wenn ich kluegere Systeme gestalte.

Das ich aber da allein rumkrebse auf Dauer macht mich irgendwie fast schon traurig. 

Dann kann ich wieder nur hier Teilen alles und meine eigenen KIs laufen lassen.

Heute habe ich beim XBTGPUARC Kern tatsaechlich zuerst meine KI zur Anfrage angemacht und dann erst die Online KIs vollgequatscht.

Des Lokale ist halt Nackiger und die Automaten die ueber Nacht laufen sollen und sich dann auch selber ausprobieren sollen sind ja schon im Vorbau.

Nur mag ich das auch alles Verstehen und Lernen dabei ich lasse mir da Zeit.

body.body:
Imagine waking me up the next day and noticed that I have won $1 million. I will be very grateful and it would definitely be my most exciting moment and a life changing wealthy opportunity for me. This sudden money will surely provide a lot of opportunities for me and certainly I will make a good use of the money, I will reflect on my needs, values and long awaited goals instead of lavishing the money carelessly. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmezjYVtr7QCTNrfPE4YyzocSHQKSWWwRmsxkZWsMmMzh5/1781632767053.png)

First I will take some part of money and help my family, my family will always come first, I would love to support and take care of them. I will support my siblings in their business and clear their debts if there is any, take care of my mummy by taking her to the best hospital for treatment and check up. Infact I will give my parents the kind of comfortable life they desire. Seeing my family happy and safe, gives me joy and great fulfillment.

body.body:
# Learn Zig Series (#81) - UDP Sockets and Datagrams

![zig.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaHuB6qTWHaSpJHQ1S8FCCRmNQuUxTcPZdU4yKHsJ7vEP/zig-banner.png)

### What will I learn
- How UDP differs from TCP at the protocol level and why you'd choose one over the other;
- How to create, bind, and use UDP sockets with Zig's standard library;
- How to send and receive datagrams with `sendto` and `recvfrom`;
- How to build a simple echo server and client using UDP;
- How to handle the realities of UDP -- packet loss, ordering, and message boundaries;
- How to implement a basic reliability layer on top of UDP with sequence numbers and acknowledgments;
- How to use `poll` for non-blocking UDP I/O with timeouts;
- How Zig's error handling and type system make UDP programming safer than C.

### Requirements
- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- An installed Zig 0.14+ distribution (download from ziglang.org);
- The ambition to learn Zig programming.

- Intermediate

# Learn Zig Series (#81) - UDP Sockets and Datagrams

Alright, new chapter! We just wrapped up the file sync mini-project where we built a complete TCP-based tool with delta transfers, authentication, conflict resolution, the works. Now we're starting the **networking deep-dive** section of this series, and we're kicking it off with the other big transport protocol: **UDP**.

Back in episode 21 we built a TCP echo server and learned how stream sockets work -- connection-oriented, ordered, reliable, the whole package. UDP is the polar opposite in almost every way. No connections, no ordering guarantees, no retransmission, no flow control. You just fire a datagram into the network and _hope_ it arrives. Sounds terrible, right? And yet UDP carries most of the internet's real-time traffic: DNS lookups, video streaming, online gaming, VoIP, all the stuff where speed matters more than perfection.

Here we go -- let's figure out why that makes sense and build some actual UDP code in Zig ;-)

## TCP vs UDP: the fundamental difference

Before writing any code, let's make sure we really understand what we're dealing with. Both TCP and UDP sit on top of IP (Internet Protocol), which handles routing packets between machines. The difference is what they add (or don't add) on top of IP.

**TCP** gives you a **byte stream**. You open a connection, write bytes into it, and TCP guarantees they arrive in order, without gaps, without duplicates. If a packet gets lost, TCP retransmits it. If packets arrive out of order, TCP reorders them. The cost: connection setup (three-way handshake), buffering, congestion control, and head-of-line blocking (one lost packet stalls everything behind it).

**UDP** gives you **datagrams**. You send a chunk of data (up to ~65,507 bytes per datagram on IPv4, though anything over ~1,400 bytes risks fragmentation) and that chunk either arrives intact or doesn't arrive at all. No partial delivery. No ordering. No connection state. Each datagram is independent.

```zig

//
// TCP (stream):   write(\
) + write(\

) + send(\
)    -->  recv() returns \
\n//                                                        recv() returns \

first, or one gets lost entirely)
//                 Each send is one recv. Message boundaries preserved.
```

This message-boundary preservation is actually one of UDP's underrated features. With TCP you always need a framing protocol (length-prefix, delimiter, etc -- we built exactly that in episode 79). With UDP, each `send` maps to exactly one `recv`. The operating system delivers complete datagrams or nothing.

One thing to notice: the client doesn't call `bind()`. The OS automatically assigns an **ephemeral port** when you first call `sendto`. The server sees the client's source IP and source port in the `client_addr` from `recvfrom` and can reply to it. This is the same mechanism TCP uses for client ports, but with UDP you can see it more clearly because there's no connection handshake hiding the details.

Real protocols like QUIC use a **sliding window** where you send multiple packets before waiting for ACKs, which is much faster but also much more complex.\n\nThe `packed struct` for the header (we covered packed structs in episode 17) maps directly to the wire format. The `flags` byte uses individual bits for different purposes -- bit 0 for \

Having said that, for most use cases you're better off using an existing library like QUIC rather than rolling your own reliability layer. But understanding how it works underneath is valuable -- you'll know what's happening when your QUIC connection stalls on a congested link.

## Non-blocking I/O with poll

Our current server blocks on `recvfrom` until a datagram arrives. For anything beyond a toy example, you need non-blocking I/O. The `poll` system call (which we touched on when building the TCP server in episode 51) works with UDP sockets too:

The TTL (Time To Live) controls how far multicast packets travel. TTL=1 means they stay on the local network segment. TTL=32 means they can cross up to 32 routers. For most development work you want TTL=1 to avoid accidentally flooding your network ;-)

## When to use UDP vs TCP

After building both, here's my practical guideline for choosing:

**Use TCP when:**
- You need every byte delivered, in order
- You're transferring files or structured data where a missing chunk breaks everything
- Latency isn't your primary concern
- You want the OS to handle congestion control

**Use UDP when:**
- Real-time matters more than reliability (gaming, VoIP, live video)
- You're building request/response patterns (DNS, service discovery)
- You need multicast or broadcast
- You're sending small independent messages that don't depend on each other
- You want to build your own congestion control (QUIC does this)

The hybrid approach is common too -- use TCP for control traffic (login, configuration, chat) and UDP for the data plane (audio, video, game state). Most online games work exactly like that.

body.title: Early Prairie Remedies (Medicine from the 1850s!)
body.body: ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZU8yKwrVXTj2nKFqgniZLZKVs3eug2EhLzkiVYQt8MFL/1781637481339.jpg)\n\n*\

*
--------------------

A wonderful treasure from the 1980s, this book documents popular home remedies from the 1850s and onward! Although some remedies might seem silly, or even backwards by today's standards, but users swore by these methods, with some even owing their lives to it!

Here are a few of the more interesting remedies that I came across:
--------------------

Menstruation: every wonder how women dealt with periods in the 1900s? Unfortunately, probably exactly how you imagined it to be! 
*\

*

Sugar Tits: an interesting alternative to what are basically pacifiers.
*\

*

Bronchitis: this is a remedy that our family has been using! 
*\

*

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPSmBq8kFyGQE2MaSvDY2fLWdHKcY995fyycmYW4uHs3n/1781637531358.jpg) **(We make ours with garlic, honey, and a tiny bit of vinegar)**

Diphtheria: this is a deliberating bacterial infection that primarily affects the mucous membranes of the nose and throat. Some homesteaders would actually INHALE TAR FUMES to cure it!
*\

*

Diabetes: this one got a chuckle out of me 😂 If one suspected they had diabetes, all they had to do was pee into a dish of yeast; if the yeast fermented, this was an indication of sugar in the urine!

Nosebleeds: this remedy certainly would have helped me out when I was a child 😅
*\

*

Onions: this vegetable was a stable in households due to their healing properties. People reported putting chopped onions in their socks for colds, or using them as a plaster during pneumonia!
*\

*

Flax Seed: I was surprised to learn that flax seeds have many beneficial purposes.
*\

*

Bowl Remedy: if someone suffered from a terrible stomachache, they would place a large, warm bowl over their stomach. 
*\

*

Egyptian Liniment: I have no idea of the contents, for research yielded limited results, but I was shocked to hear of how this remedy was utilized...
*\

*

Urine: yes -- they really DID pee on some ailments. 
*\

*

Snow Remedy: another strange case where snow was very beneficial. 
*\

*

---------------
---------------

Thank you for checking out this week's post! 🙏 I just want to add a disclaimer that, while some of these remedies may have withstood the test of time, it is always best to consult your doctor for any of your medicinal needs. Take care, and happy reading! 📚 
--------------------
