links.title: Lock Away Baggage
links.body:
>

I had an interesting conversation with a psychotherapist the other day about emotional baggage and whether we actually need to dive into it or not. In her opinion, yes, it is necessary - but I myself am not so sure. It is not that I don't think it can't be useful, more that I think it can lead down an endless rabbit hole of issues that will keep putting barriers up to making changes for the future. 

> Where does the trauma end?

---


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23wXEE2q21G754tewLhRzSY8CPYGNRYHLxdDJSrwiUzPmKLxXDgntFaYgJ8PNAFd41HQD.png)


---

Conversely, I also don't think it is good to just bury everything without discernment, because some of that baggage may contain something that really needs to be dealt with before moving on. But, just because something needs to be dealt with, it doesn't mean everything needs to be dealt with, because the work it takes might not be worth the difference it makes.

I am a proponent of emotional management, not denial of emotions. For me, they provide an indicator that can point to an issue, but that doesn't mean they need to be acted upon. Nor does it mean that the emotions are justified in the first. An emotional reaction to a misheard word still feels valid, even though it is based on an error in understanding. Acting on emotions as if they validate behaviour, *is poor behaviour* and will be met with a lot of unnecessary conflict and harm. 

But as the therapist said, it is also possible that even if we lock away our emotional baggage, it can find ways to leak out. For instance, prior to the stroke, I hadn't really felt any sense of physical stress based on work volume, because before it ever got to that point, I had strategies to prepare for and cope with for instance, the volume of work. This saved me from feeling that pressure that people describe when getting burned out. But, after the stroke I lost connection to both the early warning signs that would trigger my strategies, and the strategies themselves. But, even though I don't consciously feel stressed in my head, I get the physical reactions in my body. 

If I hadn't have developed the strategies earlier, I likely would have burned out from various stressful periods throughout life which often came layered on top of one another. But, since I learned about various aspects when young, I built strategies *before* I ever got to that point. Unfortunately, this isn't the way most people prepare for stress, because while they aren't stressed, they feel they are able to cope. But once the stress starts, they make an assumption it is because the stress level is too high, not that they never actually built a robust strategy. 

I think an easy way to consider this is like going to the gym to train muscle strength prior to actually needing to use the muscles under duress. Being strong *before* having to lift a heavy weight obviously means that the task is easier to deal with. But, if the muscles aren't developed until after the need arises, it becomes an impossible task.

And through my own observations, a lot of people get stressed by the \

situations they face, despite people next to them facing the same situation, can manage. But they don't ask themselves why that is the case, because they are stressed and focusing on their own suffering. 

When stressed is not the time to start building strategies to cope with stress, as it is like turning up to centre court at Wimbledon as a place to start to practice serving. The work has to be done before, the skills developed before, the muscles strengthened, strategies repeated *before* being needed. And that is what a lot of childhood and young experience does for us, as it gives us opportunities and exposure to lower level stressors that we can learn to deal with. But, if in childhood our approach is to avoid difficult situations, we do not develop the tools we require to face higher level stresses in the future as an adult. 

For example, one of my clients today was saying about her divorce several years ago, that she is ironically now in a place where she would be okay in that relationship. That is part of the experience though, isn't it? It seems ironic at times, but it speaks to the progression and growth we make as an individual to deal with our world, and how we learn from our experience to face our future. We can't go back to the past, but we can make better choices going forward. 

And this is why I wonder how useful digging into the baggage of the past is all the time, because there might not be that much to learn from it that is useful for us now. Yes, it might bring in some kind of emotional safety or relief, but does it help us improve? And then, is the improvement worth the energy from looking back, or could that same energy have more impact working forward? 

Everyone these days seems to be looking for \
and keep on finding trends and gimmicks to follow. But, is the energy usage to follow these actually making it efficient? For example, a lot of people sit down in front of a screen to \

from the day, but is that actually the best way to unwind? Is an hour in front of a streaming service as impactful as an hour of meditation? If meditation is too difficult and the mind won't settle, why is that the case?

Of course, we each have to find our way through the life and my answers aren't your answers, but I do think that a lot of the personal strategies we believe to be robust and effective, are actually comfort mechanisms that do not have the effect we think they do. They are our defaults, and we tell ourselves a story that they are working, like all the people who say they are good at handling stress, *when they aren't stressed.* And when they are stressed, it is because what they face is so stressful, everyone would be stressed. 

> But that is nonsense.

We all have different levels of coping strategies that we employ to manage our lives, and just like managers in the workplace, there can be a very large variation in effectivity. We might believe we are a good manager, but we might actually be the one that is tearing the team (of ourselves) apart. Trying to micro-manage, focusing on the wrong tasks, unable to prioritise, causing friction. But, because we have always been in the management position, we think that time-in makes us capable. Time is not a good measure of skill, experience is. And if in our experience we avoid dealing with difficult situations and stresses as they arise when young, it is likely we are going to be stressed when we are older. 

>\

And with so many ways to turn our attention to something else, we can keep creating an impression of a smooth sea, rather than facing the swells and learning to ride the smaller waves, preparing ourselves to surf the *fifty-year storm.* And it is when we avoid dealing with what we face at a daily level, that the baggage starts to build up and weigh us down. And eventually, when it starts to break the hinges and tumble out of the hold, we still don't have the skills and strategies to deal with the fallout. That's great, very admirable even, to be honest. I, on the other hand, am one of those who get discouraged quickly by anything; I need some extra motivation or a clear objective to do something or get somewhere. I've wanted to do many things in my life, but in the end I get discouraged by every mistake or failure I make. 🥴

That's why I really admire people like you, who regardless of setbacks, mistakes, or terrible results, keep going and try again. You're a role model in that sense, really. And yes, there are good projects on Hive that curate or do their job very well. I happen to know one that I've been attending for over a year now, and it has helped me tremendously to grow, improve, and meet amazing people. 

Coincidentally, the community's name is \

and it's very small. The owner of the community is the user to whom I delegate part of my HP because I greatly appreciate the mocking selection of content and curations he has. He is also a moderator of a community that supports and helps people with autism, etc.

But enough with the self-promotion, that wasn't really my main goal. I just wanted to open up a bit to you, and I hope this has been helpful or provided some guidance for what you're looking for. links.title: Dino Crisis [Let's Play] - 06
links.body:
*Another encounter with T-Rex, as Dr. Kirk takes the opportunity to escape again. Also, our Helicopter crashed so...*

-----

**Dino Crisis** is a survival panic game developed by the same team behind Resident Evil. It swaps out zombies for dinosaurs. The game follows Regina, a special agent sent to investigate a mysterious island facility after an experiment for a new energy source went horribly wrong!

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQz7BtVkjKVHjdCHxokMKPfzanNQgqy9vfSB5dZeEnFZe/VeniceAI_vFc26C8_@2x.webp


The first **Dino Crisis** game first released on PS1 and features real-time 3D environments with dynamic camera movement. The dinosaurs serve mostly as a background threat as Regina explores the facility and learns more about the 3rd Energy Project!

***This playthrough uses the ReBirth Mod on top of the GoG version of the game.***

I played Dino Crisis during my teenage years. I already played the first hours of Dino Crisis 2 at the time, and with my little English knowledge, Dino Crisis 1 felt complicated in comparison... I didn't know where to go 2 hours into the game. Finally finishing the game now with the GoG version felt incredibly satisfying.

Despite the clunky controls, the game still holds up surprisingly well. With its tense atmosphere and the constant threat of raptors lurking around every corner. The story adds some interesting sci-fi elements, though the the time travel aspect turned out to be more a plot device to introduce the Dinosaurs, rather than the actual main plotline.

While I'd recommend this game to survival horror fans, I did run into some technical issues... FMVs kept skipping themselves which broke some of the cinematic flow. The game features huge amounts of backtracking, especially near the end, so much that I kept a guide open so I figure out what I was missing. Still, the ending was satisfying and worth the journey. links.title: Another Year Older: Celebrate or Keep It Low-Key?
links.body: > I’ve always been the kind of person that would always go all out for the people that I care about. I really don’t care about the money or the energy I’m going to have to put in doing that. Just seeing the smiles on the faces of those I care for is enough to make me feel fulfilled. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS5iHUinbRgWQK8msD7yrfF46XYbpzgkr1bMNTDS1obFR/160a1a4b_1202_4086_8c93_dd0857fae0cf.jpeg) Over the years, I’ve come to realize that I’m that one friend that is always in for the fun. Anything that makes me happy, count me in. And you know what brings joy, it’s birthdays. We all have birthdays running throughout the year. But our thing about these birthdays is that it’s just a day. And I believe you might as well spend it well since it’s just one day in a year you can celebrate your birthday. But when you think deeper into it, you can actually celebrate your birthday on any day you want, because you have free will. Growing up, my parents always made sure I celebrated my birthday with my friends and family. But life made me realize that not everyone had it the way I did. I’ve met people who have never received even a birthday cake before. Then there’s me whose friends throw a surprise party for on my birthday. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUYx5yMrtWetPKDTy6PBiG4Zpw4PQoab2xhYyDYH1pUcx/df2b530c_eb53_4fdc_9324_db858dab4001.jpeg) As I get older, I yearn for more quieter birthdays and the occasions surprises. But when it comes to my friend’s birthdays, I try to go all out for them because they do deserve it. I celebrated my birthday a month ago and it was a very quiet one. In fact , quieter than I imagined. But it was a good one. I gained some clarity and the peace of mind to think through my life. Thinking about it now, I think I’d like to go big for my next birthday. Probably host some friends or go on a solo trip. Something to awaken my inner adventurer. If I get to celebrate my birthday once a year, I might as well spend it in grand style because it is a day to be grateful for. - - - Images belong to me. - - - ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXuSJ2V9NneWQW9Jxgobw7BtKvMb3UBPdxv3jaAhx5vpA/f40b32ec_5287_4867_ae7e_9fa77d7f679b.png)

links.title: My Splinterlands Season Recap: Rankings, Rewards, and New Challenges
links.body:
Hello Splinterlands players how are you I hope your last season went well mine was okay I could not play that much because I did not get that much time In the next season I will try to play as many battles as possible and improve my ranking Right now my ranking is not that good. You can see my ranking in Frontier is around 1400 and in Modern my ranking has reached Bronze 1st. Mehmood I hope my next season will be better than the last season and I will be able to do more battles and share with you all some of the best battles. So this season has just started so best of luck to all of you and I hope you will find out how it goes well and you will be able to collect a lot of good rewards this season so thank you till the end.



![reacap.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bhattg/23uQk8RHadyCgfxKnHGenhXCn3QEheGACMc6GiiWhgqN5DVXPfVRmiXQ4XQ1nbk9GTwcV.png)


[ImgSrc](ChatGpt.com)




## Season rewards -: 


You can see below the season and rewards. My take on Splinterlands has made a lot of changes to its website in the last few years. If you play regularly, you must have experienced this. A lot of updates have been made and the website is looking more interesting. It is a bit difficult to adjust but overall the interface looks quite good. You also get a lot of options. In the first season and you might not have seen such results but now you can see that a lot of changes will be made due to which you can see all these things easily.



<center>
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bhattg/EoCbr46SKymZMx2edY4uBW8wwCkHg4p9bbmgEgoKRPDk8AX65v8SHM6qqJhw9GhgNin.png)
</center>




## Glint Shopping -:


See, this season did not go that well for me because I collected very few rewards. Prasad, I had some words left from the previous season as well which I decided to spend as soon as this season ended and I bought chests for about 20 minutes. And let's cut it this time, they did not come out well but still you can see below which cards I received them from and I hope that my next season will be good, I don't know how many records I will be able to select but still I hope that we do even better next season, let's see what happens.


<center>
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bhattg/23swfwJLGyqEfi1g8Eeqke8SxKV2DNjBYTPVn2QYRDtZdwdHY79EPoyLVoDDCox9yvyTQ.png)
</center>


## Rewards -: 


If I talk about rewards, they were about 0.5 USD. It wasn't that much, but whatever you get for free is good, and I hope this season will be good for me. Whatever I make here, I'm investing it here. For now, the value has fallen significantly, so there's no point in withdrawing right now.


<center>
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bhattg/23tkp4NEAwwKQb2x6oWEVV7xA6kmYg6uphAcKrc7YwEE9WTRB4tLUoKPoLzBvnk85aa3Q.png)
</center>


I just keep playing in the hope that someday the value of the cards will increase and then I will get a good profit, let's see what happens. If I talk about SPS particularly, its value has also fallen a lot and many people are taking it as an opportunity and are making a good investment as well. I am also not in the mood to invest right now, due to which I am not making any kind of investment right now, let's see what happens.

That's all for today, I will meet you soon with a very amazing battle, till then you also keep battling, thank you.

links.title: Steamed Egg with Tofu and Shrimp
links.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmckPKpBsyrLQM1DTv5vbe5HHREHa1TeL87kuybhah8t2F/1781629142757.png)

Hi bloggers and food lovers, how are you all doing? Today I’m going to share an easy, simple, and healthy recipe—it’s not fried, similar to cawan mushi but not quite as smooth. Just mix everything together and steam it. This dish is packed with protein thanks to the tofu, eggs, and shrimp. These measurements are for 2 servings. Okay, let’s get started

**Ingredients:**

- 1 block of silken tofu
- 2 eggs 
- 150 ml water
- 2 shrimp
- a pinch of pepper
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 2 tbs soy sauce
- 2 tbsp cooking oil
- a sprinkle of chili flakes 
- seaweed strips

**Steps:**

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaqaChd3tmc191jdp1Hi5h7GyWT7siznpFEJu2mB2joxV/1781628590924.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQ1LsJFXxHERaXXNeaVhkzBe8XBtzFw13Rni6iuk4uR8L/1781628591175.jpg)

- Prepare the silken tofu and cut it into pieces like this

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTnnmB3AZUwFmp7LtAtvYbVfMgKKnmSTR7PZc5Wq2XBKJ/1781628620043.jpg)

- Place the tofu in a heat-resistant container

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQCJbhFt3mVpJ92ZUGXHfzEWX6bk7Pv19QQFYc1hNNmHX/1781628642019.jpg)

- Crack the eggs into a bowl 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRF15YPaH6mKmdPESHvTQSorbHSnJtBsgcuAAtzYA9UCX/1781628660104.jpg)

- Add salt to the bowl 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXp7rePrx5CURP9SCYBpiHoJPStkmttohBDYMFeuSdcsi/1781628678989.jpg)

- Add water to the eggs

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSWyPj8GFSLmkrUvKEN41emfybyYty78dEo2GEQWDgGWJ/1781628700835.jpg)

- Whisk the eggs and water until well combined 

- Skim off any foam from the egg mixture

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUzsf3PxYTGQFTKpizjn2uHudVb8t3p1XYL9oPhev6APu/1781628738163.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXTStdt3TpgjfJkPm8hTMSRaP6SfYVCFjJZKfswkMQhRa/1781628738370.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme9zvuar4vGzjGcxonbR6AijiLaLyHmvdDN3wRCJCLvnt/1781628738536.jpg)

- Pour the egg mixture over the tofu until the tofu is completely submerged

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeZc5hE9H7gQ1ismwa2XVpcfWbyNmcdt5eU3yrhyrNbdf/1781628738702.jpg)

- Make sure there are no foam or bubbles on the surface of the egg mixture, then place the tofu and egg mixture in a steamer

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXqcVKvcCxbEAFpq8kJ6ZfLFJo5dfqBpnnTvkYe4j7EQS/1781628782414.jpg)

- Steam until the eggs are cooked through, about 10 minutes 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU9vYbQeX3FNiJYA6rVTNfbLqh4g2yjpyb8vJP5Pi6S1F/1781628846964.jpg)

- After 10 minutes, add the seasoned shrimp with pepper and salt on top

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfFRGSsYxhRYdPeiTtaz93CoC6FCac89sgNEz3Q6Da1CZ/1781628874378.jpg)

- Steam again for 20 minutes until the shrimp are cooked

- Remove and let cool briefly 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmP3W5zdi2iAwCwnMAWxKxVdT26Hy6nKiS1HQSKNLotn9g/1781628901885.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTcbBv3qp6HZ9A9sdjCK6NTLfdGLSVwzWW29CNT6p445t/1781628902054.jpg)

- Drizzle soy sauce over the steamed tofu, egg, and shrimp

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYXn9HhzhwsThzYDj1wgEK8DvWGr878mraZLm968JyDyh/1781628921520.jpg)

- Add seewed/nori strips

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVDPpdfRrb2mHTTjXj6pQwHEHb5qZ5VDrg68xTMxnp8Lz/1781628951173.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQNesstChdqJwFxd5VvWLRK6SpJQPEPQvRgqJoBMxFYEL/1781628951364.jpg)

- Add 1 tbsp of hot cooking oil for each steamed tofu 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdEQ4JXM3yVs5fZ9MgnjKmYvteUbRDuGEtdx9SMVc5oAv/1781629049310.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeg9UP1afVK8x9QysYUaETqc1yjy2S6FAvsUH5g5xfUSF/1781629049941.jpg)

- Sprinkle sesame seeds and chili powder on top 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWZ8irXLHvRPGqMtEUxYCfmpaZFvxoGdesWhe9yHmpJGQ/1781629077034.jpg)

- Steamed Egg with Tofu and Shrimp dish is ready to serve

links.title: The end - monomad - eng/esp
links.body:
She always stays until the end. She takes advantage of every second of the safari. When I was about to gather my things, I noticed her sitting on the wall behind me. It was well worth postponing for a few seconds disassembling everything, and giving that time to our dear Wendy, against the columns battered by time and the mindless graffiti.
***
*Ella siempre se queda hasta el final. Aprovecha cada segundo del safari. Cuando yo estaba por recoger mis cosas, la noté sentada en el muro detrás mío. Bien valía la pena posponer unos segundos el desarmarlo todo, y darle ese tiempo a nuestra querida Wendy, contra las columnas maltratadas por el tiempo y los grafitis descerebrados.*

links.body: (English version) A Perlenbacher Can from Lidl Cheers, dear members of the #BEER community! This is the first time that I post to this community, so wish me good luck! There are cheap beers that you wouldn’t drink even if you got them for free. Perlenbacher is not one of them.

/> When I visited a local Lidl store the other day, I was attracted by Perlenbacher’s low price, like all things Lidl. The thing is that paying a low price doesn’t automatically mean that you want to get low quality, as well. I hadn’t tried it before, so I decided to give a go. In my opinion, I think it has a fairly refreshing taste and pairs well with light meat dishes, which is what I wanted. Another way that I enjoy drinking beer is without food, and Perlenbacher also did well in this field. At the end of the day, for its price, you get a decent quality pils that you can cherish regularly. As I found out through online searching, Perlenbacher has also received an award from World Beer Awards, which makes it an even more appealing choice. Well, the weather starts getting hotter by the day, so I guess I'll open plenty of Perlenbacher cans over the summer. (This post was translated from English into German with Google Translate) (Deutsche version) Hallo, liebe Mitglieder der Bier-Community! Ich poste zum ersten Mal hier, also drückt mir die Daumen! Es gibt billige Biere, die man selbst geschenkt nicht trinken würde. Perlenbacher gehört nicht dazu.

/>

Als ich neulich in meinem Lidl war, fiel mir – wie bei Lidl üblich – der niedrige Preis von Perlenbacher sofort ins Auge.

Niedriger Preis bedeutet ja nicht automatisch schlechte Qualität.

Ich hatte es vorher noch nie probiert und beschloss, es einfach mal zu testen.

Meiner Meinung nach schmeckt es recht erfrischend und passt gut zu leichten Fleischgerichten – genau das, was ich gesucht hatte.

Ich trinke Bier auch gerne mal ohne Essen, und auch da hat Perlenbacher überzeugt.

Letztendlich bekommt man für den Preis ein ordentliches Pils, das man regelmäßig genießen kann.

Wie ich bei meiner Online-Recherche herausfand, wurde Perlenbacher sogar mit einem World Beer Award ausgezeichnet, was es noch attraktiver macht.

Nun ja, das Wetter wird von Tag zu Tag wärmer, also werde ich wohl im Sommer viele Perlenbacher-Dosen öffnen.

Greetings!

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZQ1FKS8eVXJM9KUwrnpWJy3xNfeBqxsdmwNsS99wbG1b/1781628908489.jpg)

This life has taught me a series of lessons and I will not argue with anyone that says, \

I have experienced a series of events in this little time I have spent in this world. Although I might be young, but the circumstances of life have dealt with me, I have once been disappointed and also, I have been cheated and defrauded.

However, one of the lessons this life has taught me is not to give up in the face of challenges. Losing someone so dearly to me was the major lesson of my life and this has really redefined my life  from what it supposed to be to what it is right now. Then, before the demise of my mum, I have always wanted to learn a skill as she would be like,

\

I replied.

Although, I sounded as if I have heard and agreed to her advice, but deep inside me, I have never thought of doing what she had wanted me to do as I was enjoying myself in my field of learning, not only that, I was also enjoying the support of my mum who have made everything available for me despite the fact that I have not yet hearken to my mum's advice.

After a while, I lost my mum who had always been my pillar of support. When the news of her death came to me at school, it was like the world had come to an end, but there's little I could do regarding her death as life goes on.

However, the reality of life dawned on me a little while after her death and it was then I realized that she meant so much to me while she was alive. It's like my support system was shut down when she was no more and all the pieces of advice that she used to dish out to me was no more.

Life began to happen to me when all those who promised me  could not meet up with their promises. Even family members who had called me to a corner during her burial and promised me saying, \
Could not even make do with their promises. That's when I realized how thoughtful the saying that says, \

After I had realized the authenticity of this saying, I began to live my life without expecting anything from anybody, but life would have been so kind to me has it been that I have heeded to my mother's advice of learning a skill as I would have fall back on the skills when I could not further with my educational degree journey due to lack of funds.

I dropped out of school with the hope of coming back after working sometimes to raise funds for myself in order to progress.
I started to live on my own and for survival as there's no one for me. I went to a construction company to work there as a laborer and it was at that company that I started a monthly contribution with my co-worker. After six months of the contribution, everything scattered and I could not get my own share of the contribution. I was down and devastated as the money had been penned down for my return to the four walks of the classroom. 

I took the matter to the Manager of the company and he tried to interfere in the matter. He told me saying, 
\

I replied.

However, the more he tried to help me out , the more the matter was getting messier. It was then he decided to help me on his own, he asked me,

\

I replied.

That how this man saw me out of my university education, however, seeing how difficult the situation I have found myself after the death of my mum, I enrolled for a skill while I was returned back to school as I would not want to waste another golden opportunity that has presented itself to me and thank God I was able to learn fast. It's the skill I learnt that I fall back upon when there's no job for me after school and that's what I'm still eating till today. My painting skill has never let me down even when the whole world has.

Till today, the contribution saga has not been resolved but I thank God for sending a timely angel in the person of the manager to me.

Thanks for reading.

links.title: When consequences are Certain
links.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXc7DoHdU253N2shRExn9oMggsbDsi9NZpvVcN6eCKLfh/1781628391991.jpg)

Whenever the topic of justice and punishment comes up, I find myself standing somewhere between opinions.

After all, every criminal knows there are consequences. A thief knows stealing is against the law. A fraudster knows prison awaits if they are caught. A corrupt politician knows that embezzling public funds is a crime. Yet these things continue to happen every day.

If punishment alone worked, crime would have disappeared long ago. But then, if punishment did not matter at all, why do many people avoid crime despite having opportunities to commit it?

The answer, I think, lies in certainty.
Human beings are strange creatures. We often gamble when we believe the odds are in our favour. Imagine a road where there is a sign that says, \

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZKQECYdkQLKfRMKSbNstGMom9e3xaGnNbwHF2b4EA8ch/1781628610034.webp)

That sounds terrifying, but if drivers know there is almost no chance of getting caught, many will still speed. 

Now imagine another road where the fine is only ten thousand naira, but cameras monitor every metre and offenders are punished without exception. Most people would slow down. The certainty of punishment often matters more than the severity of it. 

That said, there are crimes that leave me deeply troubled. Corruption is probably top on the list.

Whenever I see hospitals without equipment, schools with leaking roofs, roads that become death traps after a few months, I cannot help but wonder where the allocated funds went.

Somewhere, someone signed papers. Somewhere, someone approved payments. Somewhere, someone became richer while ordinary citizens paid the price.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZKQECYdkQLKfRMKSbNstGMom9e3xaGnNbwHF2b4EA8ch/1781628610034.webp)

In my opinion, leaders found guilty of corruption should face swift and uncompromising justice because public office is a sacred trust. When someone steals public funds, they are not simply stealing money. They are stealing opportunities, healthcare, education and sometimes even lives.

Likewise, I feel strongly about violent criminals who terrorize communities.

In a country where banditry has caused so much suffering, entire villages have lived in fear. Families have been displaced. Children have lost parents. Parents have lost children.

The pain is difficult to describe. My anger sometimes tempts me to wish for punishments so severe that no one would ever dare commit such crimes again.

>  It's too gore for me to describe here.

But when I calm down, I remind myself that justice must remain justice. A society ruled by anger eventually becomes as dangerous as the criminals it seeks to punish.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZKQECYdkQLKfRMKSbNstGMom9e3xaGnNbwHF2b4EA8ch/1781628610034.webp)

What I truly want is not cruelty. What I want is accountability. I want corrupt leaders to know they cannot hide behind power because in my country they really do hide behind power. 

Last week, I heard someone embezzled Trillions and guess what the Senate dismissed his arrest, you have no idea how pained I was. Yet a Cyber criminal will be prosecuted and thrown in jail, I'm not saying that's not how it's supposed to be but Justice should be justice irrespective of who is involved. 

I also want violent criminals to know they will be arrested, prosecuted, and sentenced according to the law. I want justice to be swift, fair, and certain. Because perhaps that is where the real power of punishment lies.

Not in how horrifying it is. Not in how loudly it is announced. But in the simple fact that everyone knows it will happen. When people believe consequences are unavoidable, many think twice before crossing the line.

And if enough people think twice, perhaps we can build a society where fewer crimes are committed in the first place. That, to me, is the kind of punishment that truly works.

links.title: Incline Chest-Supported Row - Hidden Gem
links.body:
https://play.3speak.tv/embed?v=stevenson7/fdz1l6xa

It’s exam week for me, so I’ve decided to skip the gym and use this week as a deload. I’ve noticed my CNS fatigue has been pretty high lately, especially since I’ve been going all-out on my new routine.

Interestingly, about 43% of my workout on Thursday was focused on back training, and my back was definitely feeling it afterward. From Friday through Sunday, my back muscles were sore, particularly my mid-back.

One of the new exercises in my routine is the incline chest-supported row. Depending on your hand position, it can effectively target your rhomboids, traps, lats, and even your rear delts.

One of the main reasons I’d absolutely recommend adding this exercise to your routine is that it takes the strain off your lower back and allows you to really focus on isolating your back muscles. I usually do a lot of bent-over row variationslandmine rows, barbell rows, single-arm dumbbell rows, and so on. While they’re all great exercises, one disadvantage is the stress they can place on the lower back. With the incline chest-supported row, everything feels much more comfortable and controlled, making it both effective and safer.

Highly recommended.

If you watch the video, you’ll notice I was trying to find my balance a bit. That’s because I was already fatigued from the previous exercises, and this was actually my third set by the time I remembered to film. The bench also wasn’t the most comfortable.

The key is getting the setup right. Keep your feet planted firmly on the floor with your heels slightly elevated, keep your eyes focused on the bench, drive your elbows back, squeeze at the top, and get a good stretch at the bottom.

So, tell me, what’s your go-to routine for back day?

Thank you for reading. Till next time, enjoy the gains.

God bless.

links.title: The Economy of Abundance
links.body:
AI is breaking the old moats.

It can build apps.
Automate workflows.
Generate content.

That creates an uncomfortable question:

**What happens to businesses built on the idea that these things are hard?**

For a long time, the internet rewarded scarcity.

Private data.
Closed platforms.
Proprietary software.

That was the moat.

Build something useful.
Protect it.
Keep others out.

That made sense when software was hard to build.

But AI is changing the game.

The old question was:

**“How do I stop others from copying me?”**

But maybe that is no longer the right question.

The better question is:

**“How can I benefit when they do?”**

That is the economy of abundance.

## Bitcoin Showed the Way

Bitcoin’s code is open.

Anyone can copy it.

But Bitcoin is not valuable because nobody can see how it works.

It is valuable because everyone can.

The more people run Bitcoin nodes, build shared tools, accept Bitcoin, and trust Bitcoin, the more useful the network becomes for everyone involved.

That is the shift.

This is the new moat.

## Can This Business Model Work Beyond Bitcoin?



![2026-06-11 Abundance 5x3.png](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/2c5e10441a6d6aa6a049409a5181851c6e4e01ffc1f92e5bbfbcf6d22dbb6c28)



Take coffee.

In the old Web2 model, every coffee-loving community builds its own silo.

A Vancouver coffee community has a map of unique cafés.
A Portland roaster community has coffee brand ratings.
A Seattle coffee club has cool contests.

Each project lives its own life.

Knowledge is split.
Users are split.
Rewards are split.

Everyone builds a useful little island.

Then everyone builds a wall around it.

But AI is tearing those walls down.

## What an Abundance Model Looks Like

Now imagine those projects are built on the same open foundation.

The **Open Data Layer** has information about cafés, roasters, products, recipes, and brewing equipment.

The **Open Social Layer** has user accounts, ratings, reviews, recommendations, and community activity.

The **Open Business Layer** has contests, giveaways, rewards, service offers, and sponsor opportunities.

Now projects can tap into this shared foundation.

And contribute back to it.

The open layers are not controlled by one company.

No gatekeepers.
No central authority.
No permission required.

Everyone can safely build on them.

The foundation cannot be pulled out from under your feet.

## Competition Becomes Joint Success

The network effect benefits everyone.

More cafés, roasters, and products means better choice.
More users means more content and social connections.
More businesses means more rewards and contests.

The success of one project can strengthen all the others.

Projects benefit.
Users benefit.
Businesses benefit.

A new coffee guide can tap into an extended knowledge base.

A local roaster can reach coffee lovers across many projects.

A giveaway can travel beyond one website’s audience.

In the old model, each project fragments value.

In the abundance model, each project expands the shared network.

## Your Worst Nightmare Becomes the Strategy

In the scarcity model, being copied is the nightmare.

Someone saw your idea.
Someone built a similar site.
Someone is coming for your users.

So you defend.

You close the system.
You protect the data.
You lock in the users.

But in the abundance model, the logic flips.

You want others to copy the idea.

Openly.

You want more local coffee guides.
More roaster communities.
More reward-driven discovery projects.

Because if they build on the same open foundation, their success strengthens the network you are part of.

Their users add activity.
Their businesses create more opportunities.
Their sponsors make the ecosystem more attractive.

What used to be your worst nightmare becomes your greatest advantage.

Being copied is no longer the thing you fear.

It becomes the thing you design for.

## The New Moat

This is why scarcity-based models become fragile in the AI era.

If your advantage is only software, AI can build it.
If your advantage is only workflow, AI can replicate it.
If your advantage is only content, AI can create it.

The walls get thinner.
The tools get cheaper.
The copies get better.

But open layers are different.

They become more valuable as more people use them.

Open data.
Open social.
Open business.

These networks compound.

All projects built on the open foundation are lifted by the same tide.

You are welcome to join us.

links.title: Cat sleeping on the bike seat.
links.body:
> ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdG44JS3bAp1cdjpeCYzMgfc4AXV6ah39191cprZonpoT/1781627997599.jpg) In the busy life around us, hundreds of scenes escape our eyes every day. But there are some scenes that suddenly bring a strange peace to our tired minds. One such wonderful moment is captured in the picture. A Hero motorbike seat is parked in a corner of a busy road or garage. And on that black leather seat, a sweet cat is sleeping peacefully with its eyes closed. This white cat has light brown and yellow highlights on its head and tail. In the picture, it is seen sitting with its four legs folded into a perfect circle, which cat lovers affectionately call Cat Loaf. A bright red helmet is placed right next to the cat. The color combination of the black bike, red helmet, and white cat makes the whole picture very attractive. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRxm7F4ftZ6QUWnFtxudFiHKYAJpsb8rE8y8BfYTgaBva/1781627997776.jpg) What's interesting is that the cat is resting its head on the helmet as if it were a comfortable pillow. The bike owner may have parked the bike after finishing his work. And it is on that occasion that this little four-legged creature has chosen the most comfortable place for its afternoon or afternoon nap. Cats have this strange ability. Cats can adapt to any hard, uneven, or strange place and sleep. The cat in the picture is no exception. In this mechanical city where people are constantly running, they are struggling for a little rest. There, this cat's sleep reminds us peace is not in external splendor, but in inner peace. This beautiful picture teaches us how to find joy and peace even in the smallest things. If you're a cat lover or a biker, this scene is bound to put a smile on your face.

This game is built on the Solona blockchain. Simply connect your Solona wallet (ex. Phantom) to the game and get started playing this game in the browser. We need to hold 1000 KINS tokens (worth around 13.5$), so we are able to start playing this game.

**In-game Economy**

*   **Gold:** In-game currency, it's used for buying cosmetics, items from the shop, trading with players, and completing quests.

links.title: A new excursion through the forest, river and mountain of Los Maleteros - Venezuela / Una nueva excursión por el bosque, el río y la montaña de Los Maleteros - Venezuela
links.body:
A couple of years ago I went to this place for the first time and it was an incredible experience. Some friends who own a plot of land there invited me, and I didn't miss the opportunity.

>*Hace un par de años fui por primera vez a este lugar y fue una experiencia increíble. Me invitaron unos amigos que tienen una parcela allí, y no desaproveché la oportunidad.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_074035.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/Epdggxd4HqRTxtL8aJtUeZp9dHzP32wjNxHK1wG9fSso1cgkXxk6omAeCbwEbRY9sXs.jpg)</center>

My sister was invited that time too, but she didn't feel like going. Later, she saw my photos and regretted it, so recently, when they invited us again, she didn't hesitate to go and see this beautiful place.

>*Aquella vez mi hermana también estaba invitada, pero no se animío a ir. Luego vio mis fotos y lo lamentó, así que hace poco, cuando ellos nos volvieron a invitar, no dudó en ir a conocer este bello lugar.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_074014.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/Ep1Vzu6R5Lcb7c1tWCzrwappL4YSGvy6G1vau8KfXW1x8NUw1wGvbAeXjghRfBkHDer.jpg)</center>

Located at the end of Los Maleteros neighborhood in La Victoria, Aragua state (Venezuela), this natural area features a forest, a river, a small waterfall, and mountains. Several fields, primarily belonging to the local residents, can also be seen.

>*Ubicado al final del barrio Los Maleteros de La Victoria, estado Aragua (Venezuela), esta zona natural posee bosque, río, una pequeña cascada y montañas. Se pueden ver también varios sembradíos, que pertenecen principalmente a la gente que vive por aquí.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_074318.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/Ep5mdLaJBzVqaStC4uLYVvTLUA4UwrKpXMtpysYLBZ3VFo4YWkRBGRPTN5CpSwHYSC8.jpg)</center>

<center>![IMG_20260409_074541.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/244xsF4isDHuduKk37U73qtdhy1NsvdbsvtuVDf8prPQKycEgP3q6jZZYynBWJfyFNPhJ.jpg)</center>

We arrived at the place shortly after 7:00 am, and after stopping for coffee at the house of Joan's parents, Betty's husband, who are the friends who invited us, we went into nature.

>*Llegamos al lugar poco después de las 7:00 am, y luego de pasar a tomar café por la casa de los padres de Joan, el esposo de Betty, que son los amigos que nos invitaron, nos adentramos en la naturaleza.*

<center>![DSC00289.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23z77V2ZoPBMvYBFaqvnTbh6Qkg3wFyze8NMnWPWaAhXodTtH4unNNbU489RhAJC9AmHF.JPG)</center>

<center><sub>Photo by @gatubela / Foto de @gatubela</sub></center>

<hr>

<center>![DSC00290.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EoiVh7xLNLR8wDXcLXUMPZf3Rf8MYz9NbtvJCTctbrAYP8xYrjQswD442AWDMdRAx6W.JPG)</center>

<center><sub>With Betty and Joan - Photo by @gatubela / Con Betty y Joan - Foto de @gatubela</sub></center>

<hr>

We walked through the forest and a few minutes later we arrived at the most well-known point of this trail, La Pared waterfall.

>*Caminamos por el bosque, y unos minutos después llegamos al  punto más conocido de este sendero: la cascada La Pared.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_074932.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23uFVbX9G23V9tpED8Akx68L72dj5HcZ4h7eckijU5DB14sR5a1adxg3LVTYGTDPBK4u2.jpg)</center>

<center>![IMG_20260409_075241.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23vsL5f2cp7x6LKg6rxNcL5kx5fqdr1hBATKSCMeNm3i9UaUS7RYhHJzXLinz3XHxdCUh.jpg)</center>

Since the rains hadn't arrived yet when we went, the well levels were low. Years ago, the water from this river was diverted by the owners of a farm in the area, which is why you can see old pipes in the ground.

>*Como aún no habían llegado las lluvias cuando fuimos, el nivel de los pozos estaba bajo. Hace años, el agua de este río fue canalizado por los propietarios de una hacienda que había en la zona, por eso se pueden ver viejas tuberías en el suelo.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_075331.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23vi3sNKngXWi9Dterv5hfR5krQE1sk5BWaRFb6WhbMc9sCDjBa8PFbg1639DKMJL3FZA.jpg)</center>

<center>![IMG_20260409_075409.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EogMmnSPpepWduq8xRCAM8AcWPnuJEmvMh2drjvArpLRbwV4UrNDS7WFndDqXLtdXbQ.jpg)</center>

The waterfall was also altered by human hands; the wall it has is made of cement, although due to the years and the action of water and vegetation, it now looks natural.

>*La cascada también fue intervenida por la mano humana; el muro que tiene es de cemento, aunque por los años y la acción del agua y la vegetación, ya parece natural.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_075525.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23u62xjkhWoxQVTdkU7dQLnEpgrJuGFvZ185EaAW7txV9r5eCrz1ttGiKg8KFQ1suzssZ.jpg)</center>

Since we were going to our friends' plot, we decided to save our enjoyment of the waterfall for the return trip. The scenery along this trail is fabulous, with several river crossings and beautiful vegetation.

>*Como íbamos a la parcela de nuestros amigos, dejamos el disfrute en la cascada para el regreso. Los paisajes de este sendero son fabulosos, hay varios pasos de río y bella vegetación.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_075822.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23x15Eh87dEQuUAGt7KhZjRLUZJsgYJAE2SiUceJ8XtL1UQ7hdRxhoD2vLvCoUKwzL6UX.jpg)</center>

<center>![IMG_20260409_080108.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/Eoc75wsmERbPHW8HxgFr4BLqnroooWs1n44tWsWJQvJh66wjVgJNX7HRhjj2ZuhijxY.jpg)</center>

<center>![IMG_20260409_080323.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/244UjGdSEXNGs3rvPzU5HSHusQumV35vWLELHhME7ad35cG91Nv9uGwxHaqtB8XqQdUZN.jpg)</center>

<center>![IMG_20260409_080810.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23x16oD4y33tdbwDjTzo85ngL76m6W2wCEmx3QUf6xDiGnG5qy5q6hJgJ2YjKvAPd4H8c.jpg)</center>

Moreover, the aromas of some flowers, like the one you see in the photo above, were divine. The sun was already peeking out and the heat would soon arrive, so we continued our hike up the mountain.

>*Además, los aromas de algunas flores, como la que ven en la foto de arriba, eran divinos. Ya el sol se asomaba y pronto vendría el calor, así que seguimos nuestra ruta montaña arriba.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_081555.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EnYQ1FgT6tyRXTi1qvJ4kDTJSAbokFC6FF7YEDrQJ1qNTSuLNrrRDWsm8g4omSAkCXd.jpg)</center>

<center>![IMG_20260409_082946.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23xehws4DQR3TRpp1zucKrMrypgqBcrLdciNA81RmcNx6ZhkKbXcmasJLbHf456HAfxq9.jpg)</center>

About 15 minutes later we arrived at the plot. The idea was to help our friends clean a little, water the plants and pick some fruits. Excellent plan, don't you think? 😉

>*Unos 15 minutos después llegamos a la parcela. La idea era ayudar a nuestros amigos a limpiar un poco, regar las plantas y recoger algunos frutos. Excelente plan, ¿no creen? 😉*

<center>![IMG_20260409_083100.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23sUCw1saKofwetfkYTUMd1USqoRtLdNi3Q9Mwq1DMgUK7Y9j3DHwLANtFZe2hL7DuEqV.jpg)</center>

They have several plants there, such as coffee, citrus fruits, papaya, bananas, yucca, plantains, sweet peppers, passion fruit, and more that I don't remember 😃.

>*Ellos tienen varias plantas allí, como café, cítricos, lechoza (papaya), cambur (bananas), yuca, plátano, ají, parchita, y más que no recuerdo 😃.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_083029.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23u652orFRRiVVugLogtEPkuk4XZ3TqbZTjs74rpRRMBgEviQXuiQY6RzgPiwc5meBqN1.jpg)</center>

There are crops they can't plant, like pumpkin or tubers, because the animals that live there, like peccaries, eat them 😂.

>*Hay rubros que no pueden sembrar, como por ejemplo auyama o tubérculos, porque los animales que viven allí, como los báquiros, se los comen 😂.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_083142.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EnWHWip6GTFokf7qBceR8jwKja6zLrg1BbMGhJGc6BtCwgAUtSKZiYJ7Vz9ZB3CZB2g.jpg)</center>

As for irrigation water, fortunately it flows down from the mountain, and they've installed a tank and a hose, so they can water without any problems. This was the task we did most during our visit, because since it hadn't rained, many plants were thirsty.

>*En cuanto al agua para el riego, afortunadamente baja de la montaña, y ellos han puesto un tanque y una manguera y con eso pueden regar sin problemas. Esta tarea fue la que más hicimos en nuestra visita, porque como no había llovido, muchas plantas estaban sedientas.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_083656.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/2432HWFASSKFBY4v9WvEMknfvcKrWw6CErX6b83k7Q2VZqrFDqx5EsdSgxxL9GWbo9dn5.jpg)</center>

But we also had some leisure time; chatting, eating and taking photos.

>*Pero también tuvimos ratos de esparcimiento; conversando, comiendo y tomando fotos.*

<center>![DSC00306.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/Eoc8R4AELUb6nN1LzmP1g1rm5jDp7UuPeiwwv5qKL2cA4EXuWHECv7Jw6D4o3Ps227o.JPG)</center>

<center><sub>Photo by @gatubela / Foto de @gatubela</sub></center>

<hr>

As I mentioned at the beginning, the mountains of Los Maleteros are beautiful. No wonder Betty and Joan dream of building a little house here to escape the city from time to time.

>*Como comenté al principio, las montañas de Los Maleteros son una belleza. Con razón Betty y Joan sueñan con construir una casita aquí para escapar de la ciudad de vez en cuando.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_083758.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EqQMhkdCRnizx6FJRGp7oqyNbVVebYPp9JHsxj4BkdkUGVJZaTEBxUJA3iMjNSvkqoX.jpg)</center>

<center>![IMG_20260409_084127.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23wMf2KLv539bc4sNqwEezunAjznfkSKPQcyVo6gbezvGuXeyC3TPE7LgMCVrzQrcGw1q.jpg)</center>

<center>![IMG_20260409_085829.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23tmFdxqAs3vEWiQcY8i8koeP2ZyCXpwiULQXFpLJ55mpc6Wu4SfgnUEmsa8poHVL1Zv4.jpg)</center>

My sister @gatubela was fascinated by the place, and by the task of watering. She grabbed the hose and watered every plant she found 😄.

>*Mi hermana @gatubela estaba fascinada con el lugar, y con la tarea de regar. Agarró la manguera y le echó agua a toda planta que encontró 😄.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_091254.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/242Nh2kwvS5dZAbPZfwjdm5mPqW83MxA6wNK2SUSkHBLfwnc5MsCTJd13prpgVBPh1NoJ.jpg)</center>

Look at the thorns on these mandarin trees, it's a shame they didn't have any fruit yet.

>*Miren las espinas en estas plantas de mandarina, lástima que aún no tenían frutos.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_091918.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/Eo4B1v5iGxzUXXcDx6L6qANanzZZNE9yf382jyiddwM5DPbupnyrgJajJJ2K4ozcmCm.jpg)</center>

<center>![IMG_20260409_094144.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23wgMvF1pHBuSAnhxeATa6qUECYPD1Xj9aHu89yoB72nKgqSTQq2oNTRdTxTB1T25aNb4.jpg)</center>

After we finished watering, we harvested the crop. There were green papayas, perfect for making sweet, and plantains too. Our friends gave us a few kilos of these fruits ❤️.

>*Después de terminar de regar, recogimos la cosecha. Había lechozas verdes, ideales para hacer dulce, y también plátanos. Nuestros amigos nos regalaron unos cuantos kilos de estos frutos ❤️.*

<center>![IMG_20260409_094637.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EowFZbqgw7XHcN55LrCHJGpTjc4ReQeWZsVGMam1KNUh2s2BesBuvVKNBMiB9HTXkJo.jpg)</center>

<div class=\

> ![IMG_20260409_100618.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23w2exd1ZmMTgEwjdk6MizkE5WvNhgH4nYtV9Au9FHeP1DcCUHc2DSZDBS3Q4pnCx46d2.jpg) It was about 10:30 in the morning when we finished our work on the plot and started back. >*Ya eran como las 10:30 de la mañana cuando terminamos las labores en la parcela y emprendimos el regreso.*
![DSC00320.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23zGYDT4UNUH4VanvRpNbNhC2cEQa6GEaTd1Z4NVjEt2h99MwH8Bu9fcUm5P5vgDnX7nS.JPG)
Photo by @gatubela / Foto de @gatubela
Look at the trunk of this tree, a gift from the forest that I couldn't help but photograph 😊. >*Observen el tronco de este árbol, un regalo del bosque que no pude dejar de fotografiar 😊.*
![IMG_20260409_103547.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23xedizcPEY8VqNxMeYtM67kGV7KEjvD97FzduWZUe5gNC8b5NFYccgcF3xhssEm7Ff4E.jpg)
We went back to the waterfall and stopped there to cool off. Although I didn't go in the water this time because I didn't bring a change of clothes, I did take off my shoes to dip my feet in the water. Betty was the only one who went under the waterfall, and she stayed there for about an hour, she didn't want to come out 😄. >*Volvimos a la cascada y allí hicimos una parada para refrescarnos. Aunque esta vez no me bañé porque no llevé cambio de ropa, sí me quité los zapatos para meter los pies en el agua. Betty fue la única que se metió bajo la cascada, y allí estuvo como una hora, no se quería salir 😄.*
![IMG_20260409_105641.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23xARb3aVz3Ps8DogdqrA2KLmfUVNPEya5Xus79gDUG9RGhkk4vk6cd2RtrrnpBFxhFcC.jpg)
![DSC00329.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23vhuagxZh1282NcdCpZQ9ZzmNez6SpUUiLoGiPGCoK9Z4GU7Jrgr7CXa2CcX9vjFKwac.JPG)
Photo by @gatubela / Foto de @gatubela
![IMG_20260409_105934.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/EoGxV7YPG1Dei74pAVbbvrzCL5AryJGp77i3CNKpJro9kBswNKySVnRLkB7EXqXnvuJ.jpg)
And that's how this little adventure came to an end. One of the most amazing things about Venezuela is that in any town or city, you can find beautiful natural spots nearby that take you away from your daily routine, and you can visit them for very little or no cost at all. >*Y así terminó esta pequeña aventura. Una de las cosas más increíbles de Venezuela es que en cualquier pueblo o ciudad puedes encontrar cerca bellos lugares naturales que te sacan de la rutina y a los que puedes ir gastando muy poco o gratis.*
![IMG_20260409_110939.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23vsNPf4yToDdxyS4xBxAvpTeUQW3pTc9HjRWmG4MURScFMFzxxN87aqu5R2ugZg7mrPr.jpg)
![IMG_20260409_110946.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23xp6h19Ph8SrwDzLft63dU2prRX6t1bdo3FNp3msoZ1w9iNKNaBWBbXrXQsapsje4rwA.jpg)
![IMG_20260409_111100.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sofathana/23wqgaJ987bxHa6ooZUpzLRqSCwHMJMPh8weg6wW2R2uavvGvRGqiJeXhRamHmuTGvxTX.jpg)

**THANKS FOR VISITING MY BLOG! / ¡GRACIAS POR VISITAR MI BLOG!**

body.title: El Patico [Also in English]
body.body:
![Junio.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/germanandradeg/23u5bKD1U2cfmq64FTeJ7fZP61BK58U1cmczAwPSCG7ybLgwXw2Jj9rYToiN16wAcAebP.jpg)


<div class=\

> Si llegases a conocer a mi prima Yolimar, lo primero que dirías sería que está bien buena. A sus más de cincuenta años conserva un cuerpo que muchas muchachas de veinte quisieran tener. Pero eso sería apenas la primera impresión. Después descubrirías que es una mujer bondadosa, empática, un paquetico de amor. Paquetico porque apenas mide 1,57 metros. Mi papá y mi tío siempre fueron muy unidos, y esa unión terminó por trasladarse a sus hijos. Mis primas eran mi familia; las hermanas que nunca tuve. Cuando viajo a mi niñez, siempre encuentro a mis primas jugando conmigo, pero Yolimar ocupa el papel principal. Tal vez porque teníamos casi la misma edad. Jugó conmigo a los vaqueros, a la guerra, al Monopolio y con los Lego. Y yo, sin protestar, me convertía en el papá de sus muñecas, cocinaba en la cocinita y vivía dentro de aquellas casitas improvisadas con sábanas. Fue una infancia sana, llena de cariño y de unión. Yo nunca fui de tener amigos y hasta con mis hermanos jugaba poco. Pero con Yolimar era distinto. Con ella me sentía cómodo. Éramos gemelos nacidos de vientres diferentes. No sé por qué, pero donde hay mucha luz siempre termina apareciendo algo oscuro. Una mañana estábamos en casa del tío. Como de costumbre, jugábamos por todos lados. Aquella casa era inmensa y el patio todavía más grande. Allí convivían perros, gatos, gallinas, patos y, durante un tiempo, hasta una vaca. Esa vaca debimos habérnosla comido en algún momento, porque nunca más la volví a ver. Pero aquella mañana ocurrió algo fuera de lo normal. En la casa también había un pozo. Era territorio prohibido para todos los muchachos. No tenía cerca, pero bastaba con acercarse unos metros para que, como por arte de magia, se escuchara un grito del tío o de la tía. Era como si la zona tuviera un sensor de movimiento. O quizás éramos nosotros los que llevábamos algún chip incorporado y nunca lo supimos. Aunque lo dudo. Que yo sepa, en aquellos tiempos esos dispositivos ni existían. Y si existían, debían ser tan grandes como un brazalete. Pero volvamos a la parte oscura. Ese día Yolimar me preguntó: —¿Quieres hacer algo que jamás hemos hecho? La expresión de su cara me cagó, pero también despertó mi curiosidad. Respondí con un sí rotundo. —Vamos a perseguir las gallinas y los patos. Le dije que eso no era buena idea, que podían atacarnos y hacernos daño. —No vamos contra los grandes —respondió—. Vamos por los pollitos y los paticos. Ellos no hacen nada. Tenía razón. Aquellos pequeñines eran tan confiados que siempre se acercaban a nosotros con total curiosidad. Y comenzó la persecución. Corrimos por todo el patio. Ella, por un lado. Yo, por el otro. A veces chocábamos entre nosotros y terminábamos muertos de la risa. ¡Qué vaina tan buena! Nos divertíamos de lo lindo. En un momento me dieron ganas de hacer pipí y le dije que iba al baño. —Aquí te espero —respondió. Cuando regresé, lo que vi me pasmó. Yolimar había cruzado la frontera prohibida. Ella me miró. Yo la miré. Su expresión no era normal. Parecía otra persona. Ahora que lo recuerdo, tenía la cara de una poseída. Los calcetines que no llevaba puestos se me arrugaron y las esféricas se me subieron hasta las amígdalas. Con aquella cara de loca me hizo señas para que me acercara. Yo le respondí en voz baja, procurando que nadie nos oyera: —No podemos estar ahí. Pero insistió. —Ven para que veas esto. No te lo puedes perder. Como siempre, pudo más mi curiosidad y di el primer paso. Al llegar al pozo, me llamó la atención que nadie hubiera gritado. Ni el tío ni la tía. Aquello me dio confianza. Yolimar sostenía una cuerda entre las manos. —Mira. Entonces la jaló. Al final de la cuerda había un patico amarrado por el cuello. Sí, en lugar de fabricar un papagayo con papel y palitos, decidió convertir al pobre animal en uno. Solo que, como no podía hacerlo volar, se le ocurrió lanzarlo al pozo una y otra vez. Yo me convertí en su cómplice; no dije nada. Éramos dos desquiciados. Pero aquello todavía no era lo peor. La verdadera crueldad antinatural (unnatural cruelty) llegó cuando sacó al patico del pozo, me tomó de la mano y salimos corriendo hasta el baño de la casa. Frente a la poceta lanzó al patico y bajó la cadena. Eso sí era crueldad antinatural. El agua no logró llevárselo. El pobre animal permanecía allí, aterrado. Esperó a que el tanque volviera a llenarse. Bajó otra vez la cadena. Y lanzó nuevamente al patico. Esta vez con mucha fuerza. Esta vez desapareció junto con la cuerda. Ahora entienden por qué no estoy muy bien de la cabeza. El lado oscuro de Yolimar era de un negro aterrador. Yolimar no está presa, es linda, pero lo mejor es estar lejos de ella. Por si acaso. Hasta aquí mis cinco minutos.

La imagen fue editada con [CANVA](https://www.canva.com/). *Es mi responsabilidad compartir con ustedes que, como hispanohablante, he tenido que recurrir al traductor [Yandex Translate](https://translate.yandex.com/?source_lang=es&target_lang=en) para llevar mi contenido original en español al idioma inglés. También hago constar que he utilizado la herramienta de revisión gramatical [Grammarly](https://app.grammarly.com/). `16 de junio de 2026` --- # English # The Little Duck

> If you ever got to meet my cousin Yolimar, the first thing you’d say is that she is drop-dead gorgeous. In her early fifties, she still has a body that many twenty-year-old girls would kill for. But that would be just the first impression. Later, you’d discover that she is a kind, empathetic woman—a little bundle of love. A little bundle because she barely stands at 5 feet 2. My dad and my uncle were always very close, and that bond naturally passed down to their children. My cousins were my family, the sisters I never had. When I travel back to my childhood, I always find my cousins playing with me, but Yolimar plays the leading role. Maybe because we were almost the same age. She played cowboys, war, Monopoly, and Legos with me. And I, without a single complaint, would become the dad to her dolls, cook in her play-kitchen, and live inside those makeshift houses made of bedsheets. It was a wholesome childhood, full of affection and togetherness. I was never one to have friends, and I barely even played with my own brothers. But with Yolimar, it was different. With her, I felt comfortable. We were twins born from different wombs. I don’t know why, but where there is too much light, something dark always ends up creeping in. One morning, we were at my uncle’s house. As usual, we were playing all over the place. That house was huge, and the backyard was even bigger. Dogs, cats, chickens, ducks, and, for a while, even a cow lived together back there. We must have eaten that cow at some point, because I never saw it again. But that morning, something out of the ordinary happened. There was also a well on the property. It was forbidden territory for all us kids. It didn’t have a fence, but all it took was stepping within a few meters of it for a shout from my uncle or aunt to ring out, as if by magic. It was like the area had a motion sensor. Or maybe it was us who had some kind of chip embedded in us, and we never knew it. Though I doubt it. As far as I know, back in those days, those devices didn’t even exist. And if they did, they must have been as big as a bracelet. But let’s get back to the dark part. That day, Yolimar asked me: —Do you want to do something we’ve never done before? The expression on her face scared the shit out of me, but it also sparked my curiosity. I replied with a resounding yes. —Let’s chase the chickens and the ducks. I told her that wasn’t a good idea, that they could attack us and hurt us. —We’re not going after the big ones —she replied. Let’s go for the chicks and the little ducks. They don’t do anything. She was right. Those little guys were so trusting that they always approached us with pure curiosity. And so, the chase began. We ran all over the yard. Her, on one side. Me, on the other. Sometimes we would crash into each other and end up dying of laughter. Man, what a damn good time! We were having the time of our lives. At one point, I needed to pee and told her I was going to the bathroom. —I’ll wait for you here —she replied. When I came back, what I saw froze me solid. Yolimar had crossed the forbidden border. She looked at me. I looked at her. Her expression wasn’t normal. She looked like a different person. Now that I think back on it, she had the face of someone possessed. The socks I wasn’t even wearing shriveled up, and my spheres climbed all the way up to my tonsils. With that crazy face, she motioned for me to come closer. I answered in a low voice, making sure no one could hear us: —We can’t be over there. But she insisted. —Come see this. You can’t miss it. As always, my curiosity got the better of me, and I took the first step. When I reached the well, it caught my attention that no one had shouted. Not my uncle, not my aunt. That gave me confidence. Yolimar was holding a rope in her hands. —Look. Then she pulled it. At the end of the rope was a little duck, tied by the neck. Yes, instead of making a kite out of paper and sticks, she decided to turn the poor animal into one. Only, since she couldn't make it fly, it occurred to her to throw it into the well over and over again. And I became her accomplice just by witnessing it and saying nothing. We were two maniacs. But that still wasn’t the worst part. The true unnatural cruelty came when she pulled the little duck out of the well, grabbed my hand, and we ran to the house's bathroom. Right in front of the toilet bowl, she threw the little duck in and flushed. Now that was unnatural cruelty. The water didn't manage to take it down. The poor animal stayed there, terrified. She waited for the tank to fill up again. She flushed the chain a second time. And she threw the little duck down again. This time with a lot of force. This time, it disappeared along with the rope. Now you understand why I’m not quite right in the head. Yolimar’s dark side was of a terrifying pitch-black. Yolimar isn't in prison; she is beautiful, but it’s best to stay far away from her. Just in case. That’s my five minutes.

body.title: Are Laws Truly For Everyone?
body.body: alt=\

/>

I grew up hearing that law is for everyone. That nobody is above the law. We were taught in school, our parents told us and our politicians say it every election season. And for a long time many of us believed it.

Well maybe it's actually truly in other countries, but I don't think it is so in Nigeria. I live in Nigeria and I watch things happen here every single that made that phrase \

sound like a joke .

I have heard and seen a young man get arrested and spend months in jail just because he couldn't afford bail. No conviction, No proper hearing, just waiting, rotting because poverty made him invisible to the system that was supposed to protect him.

And then I have watched men who stole money that was meant for roads, hospitals, schools walk around free. Giving speeches, attending events, smiling for the cameras. There cases filed somewhere, pending indefinitely. And it got me wondering \

?**

A poor man caught stealing bread to feed his family would receive jungle justice and can spend months in pretrial detention, while a wealthy man who steals money through fraudulent contract will hire 10 lawyers, file twenty motions and be seen at the dinner party before his case is even assigned a hearing date.

This is the part people don't talk about enough. Laws did not fall from sky. Somebody wrote them and I believe that person was not a poor person. They feel that the people who made the law are wealthy. They're connected . We all know this , even if we do not say it, in our society the same offence do not carry the same weight for everyone. It solely depends on who commits it.. A young man from a poor background would likely be harassed, searched and even arrested on suspicion. But someone driving an expensive car through the same road would wave and move on.

It's sad that we have a system that talks about equality loudly while quietly serving the people at the top. The law that supposed to be for everyone has now become one more thing that happened to us instead of for us.

body.title: La autonomía en la vejez comienza en la juventud
body.body:
<div class='text-justify'>

Hablar de autonomía es algo que no muchas veces se hace, porque de cierta manera hay una tendencia a creer que siempre lo seremos, o tal vez sea que se asume de manera irrefutable que cuando seamos adultos mayores o, personas de tercera edad, las limitaciones llegarán si o si, y que la independencia es una especie de sueño. Y quizás, dentro de las opciones también está el hecho de que ni se piensa en eso, porque en la juventud plena sencillamente se centra la atención en otra cosa y la vejez se ve como algo sumamente lejano. 

La amiga @damarysvibra nos ha compartido un [post](https://hive.blog/hive-131951/@damarysvibra/proyeccion-y-autonomiaororforward-looking-and-self-reliance)donds nos habla de esa realidad por la que todos pasaremos, que tiene que ver con llegar a una edad en la que nuestro cuerpo ya no responderá de igual manera desde el punto físico a como cuando teníamos 20 años, pero eso no quiere decir que no tengamos independencia ni que necesariamente debamos perder autonomía, esta es **la etapa de la vejez**.



<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdEPo4LdVkRxZKHWLaVaEY8h616CKAcBuP4GVtjgwP63K/image.png)
</center>
<center>[Imagen de Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/vejez-juventud-mano-abuela-ni%C3%B1o-360714/)</center>

Quiero centrar esta publicación en algo muy importante, definitivamente algo **indispensable** a considerar desde temprana edad, y es el cuidado de nuestro cuerpo, porque si desde la juventud no tenemos cuidados básicos hacia el, no podremos disfrutar de una vejez con libertad de movimiento, de elección, de decisión, y pienso que en general, la mayoría de nosotros los que estamos en los 30, incluso quienes están en los 40, aspiran llegar a la edad que la vida les permita llegar con salud, con un cuerpo que les permita seguir teniendo un rango de autonomía. 

Teniendo una capacidad total de valernos por nosotros mismos, siendo jóvenes, el concepto de *\

* no parece tener una gran relevancia, pero dejaré un concepto que nos comparte la universidad de Internaciones: [La autonomía en la vejez es la capacidad que tiene el adulto mayor de valerse por sí mismo. Es decir, puede tomar decisiones que influyen en su bienestar](https://uni.edu.gt/noticias/dignidad-autonomia-vejez/), cómo se puede ver, damos por hecho que siempre eso de tomar las decisiones de nuestra vida, de todo lo que determina nuestro bienestar dependerá de lo que deseamos hacer, pero no siempre es así y, lamentablemente, cuando llegamos a cierto nivel de edad, puede ocurrir que seamos totalmente dependientes, y no creo que nadie quiera llegar a eso.
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaqiZz8np6uKSnTTkZQcsKA5Zwyg2AVpqsFDgmwypm6m4/image.png)
[Imagen de Gaspartacus | Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/mayor-jubilado-mar-viejo-gente-5125979/)
Quiero dejar por aquí algunas recomendaciones que pienso son básicas, pero importantísimas para tener muchas más posibilidades de alcanzar una edad avanzada con salud, y que esta nos permita tener autonomía y, a pesar de formar parte de la tercera edad, seguir teniendo esa autonomía de la que hoy hablamos: 1- Hay que priorizar las proteínas en la alimentación, no importa si te inclinas por las proteínas vegetales o las de origen animal, pero nuestra dieta no debe centrarse en los carbohidratos, y no quiero decir con esto que debamos eliminarlos, no, solo que de un plato no deben ser lo principal, y hablo de carbohidratos complejos, como verduras y hortalizas, y no digo que no podamos comer pasta o arroz, pero que no sea esto lo que predomine en nuestro plato.
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPMKMKayFhWt2dRVLuvoMWHWabzDM48n57VDxggYvyQFe/image.png)
[Imagen de stevepb | Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/ensalada-nuevo-org%C3%A1nico-comida-374173/)
2- Evitemos al máximo lo que son las frituras y los productos ultraprocesados, esto es lo que está generando el mayor daño a la salud a nivel global, porque son productos, **no son alimentos**, y no nos nutren. Y en cuanto a lo que respecta a frituras, al uso de aceites vegetales, **elimínalos de tu vida**, en este punto si soy bastante radical, porque no generan ningún beneficio, son altamente inflamatorios, son la causa principal de problemas arteriales y cardíacos, y considerando que las enfermedades coronarias son la principal causa de muerte en el mundo, *¿entonces para que consumirlo?*. 3- Muévete, es decir, has ejercicios, caminar hace bien, pero hacer pesas es muy importante. Después de los 35 años ya nuestro cuerpo empieza con un proceso de pérdida muscular, y la manera de evitar que esto ocurra, y de mantener nuestra masa muscular que nos permitirá gozar de buena movilidad en la adultez es ejercitarnos. Lo mejor es empezar a temprana edad, pero no quiere decir que, si alguien tiene 40 o 60 años no pueda empezar, en realidad, nunca es tarde.
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbZTUHSpWHLrf3WCxmvwo14KjhUL92hABPrxrE55CQVQD/image.png)
[Imagen de Surprising_Media | Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/ni%C3%B1a-extensi%C3%B3n-aptitud-f%C3%ADsica-7217972/)
4- Por otro lado, y de suma importancia, y esto va como resultado de la aplicación de lo anterior, **mantén un peso adecuado**, esto evitará el desgaste de nuestras articulaciones, incluyendo las de la columna, rodillas, pie, etc, y esto nos dará más chance de movilidad cuando tengamos edades más avanzadas. Son recomendaciones básicas, fáciles de llevar, y no hablo de no darnos un gusto de vez en cuando, sino de que no nos excedamos, porque lo que hoy no parece hacer daño, termina sumándose y dejándonos para el futuro muchas limitaciones. Nada de lo que les he compartido es extremo, y la salud lo vale todo, porque podríamos tener mucho dinero, pero si no gozamos de buena salud, de nada nos serviría porque no podríamos disfrutarlo. Y dejo aquí mi publicación, esperando que sea de mucha utilidad este sencillo mensaje. Que tengan un bonito día.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTXJ83kY9BN2p9LYSbwXSBXReBLDTGBc5YnFKLLf4e4ke/image.png)

body.body:

Hello Asean Hive Community

On Valentine I ordered a Pizza and it was quite scammy. I made a post about that here: https://ecency.com/@dewabrata/i-got-pizza-scam-on . Actually that was not my first experience in getting a \

pizza, I had several experience before. So I decided not to get any Pizza for some weeks after that valentine night pizza case lol.

However last month before I had my medical surgery, I decided to get some pizza again. There were some promos from mid May 2026 and I thought I should not miss that chance. So then I ordered a promo from a famous Pizza chain here in Indonesia, and I ordered one of their signature pizza and got another free pizza.

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/Eoc82T9yW7BkdXQY4bK86rG66VQc1Bxzv1h3AcN1nfK99muByG5wiBZi9tn5M779zu8.jpg

This was a cheesy bites pizza, it was my last ex Girl Friend favorite. The edge of the pizza was like a small butter roll with stuffed cheese inside.

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/23xAVKRLrh3WYbmuRXiSftQjwXRBgWccyCszRHPX4t9CFDueB1oZ5Zwe9U7CRpa2fNkKE.jpg

And this was the extra free pizza I got from their promo. A Meatza Pizza, which was a pizza with a meat only toppings. When I took this shot, my mother already snatched a slice of the cheesy bites there, so you could notice there was a slice missing there lol.

**So how come they were part of the scammy promo too?**

That's the real question here, I believed these promo pizzas were a scam too. The first reason, I did not have to tell a lot here, was the toppings. For the cheesy bites, you could see that the edge of the pizza or the cornicione was bigger than the middle part which had the toppings. lol WTF was that, they tried some optical illusion or some eye trick?

For the meat only toppings, you could see there wasn't any pepperoni there, no some minced beef or anything. The meat were beef sausage, beef meatball and chicken sausage. Those were cheap you know lol.

The second reason why they became scammy was the size.

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/23wqkoCeH1U3cKi9GWpDcWtM76UyLzzvLuGUgZxjp5zurk7A4jWpjgW6VuTe3oNKTetU8.jpg

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/23uQrpUwpmZ5LnD4e4c91rGpGeycXTk4Vt2JQJxW29Ngu2iE6Q4t1f8MnxXLNRy1DhB5L.jpg

Seriously they were small! I am a 5' 6\
, maybe around 8\

. They even said those weren't personal pan pizza lol.

Ok the last one and I save it as the last because it is the good part. Did they use cheap Ingredients? I would be honest here, they did not do that thing. I believed those pizza were made by good ingredients, because their taste was very good. I could not say they were great, because I had them before years ago, that time it was a lot better. If their taste had declined, mostlikely because they used less toppings than what they used to use before.

Ok that's my last bad Pizza experience before. I hope you do not have the same experience as me.
