links.title: What You Can't Avoid, Welcome It.
links.body:
###### ***Finding peace and power by embracing the inevitable***

#### Greetings Hivers,

We all fight things we can't change. Traffic jams that wreck your morning plans or the slow creep of age or unexpected health issues or those days when life simply refuses to follow your script. As a doctor I see this struggle every single day in my patients and in my own life. We tense up then push back and end up making things harder for ourselves. But what if the real shift is simpler than we think, \

**stop fighting what you can’t avoid and start welcoming it.** ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbsRhb4JgXRpyPgFLJXQdQhKCb9tus8fyQt8wWTEuiijC/1781623343771.png) Image Created With Google Gemini This isn’t about giving up or being passive. It’s about moving your energy away from pointless resistance toward something wiser acceptance. I’ve been thinking about this a lot lately while balancing my medical practice time with family and life here on Hive. ### The Trap of Resistance You’re stuck in a long hospital queue or crawling through bad traffic after a long shift. What is your first reaction? Frustration builds you start checking your phone every few seconds or your mind spirals into worst case scenarios. That resistance doesn’t make the wait any shorter it just drains your energy. I’ve learned this the hard way during difficult patches in my personal life. Holding tightly to “how things should be” left me exhausted. The moment I began saying, “Okay, this is happening. Let’s work with it,” everything started feeling lighter. The wave is coming anyway why not learn to ride it? the easiest way to get things sorted. ### What to Avoid? Common Resistance Habits Here are some traps that make unavoidable situations hurt even more when - **Constant complaining**: A little venting is normal but endlessly asking “Why me?” keeps you stuck and blocks any real progress. - **Over planning**: Trying to control every outcome whether it’s perfect health career moves or family matters, only creates more anxiety when life has other plans. - **Numbing out**: Endless scrolling on social media platforms for no reason or burying yourself in work just to escape. It only delays the real work. - **Blaming others**: This hands away your power. Life throws curveballs not everything is in our control. - **Toxic positivity**: Forcing yourself to say everything is “fine” when it clearly isn’t. Real acceptance starts with honesty. Stepping away from these habits has freed up so much mental space for me. I’ve noticed the same pattern in the health tips and Hive experiences I share small daily resistances around aging tech changes or routine stress can build into something much heavier. ### Tying It to Life on Hive and Beyond If you’ve followed my earlier posts as of reflections on daily habits, tech tools for doctors and creators or deeper pieces like *How to Survive in 2026*, *Story of A Middle Class Boy*, and *Efforts Never Die* you’ll probably spot this same thread running through them. What unavoidable challenge are you facing these days work pressure? health goals? or growing on Hive? ### The Beautiful Payoff When you welcome what you can’t avoid, you start gaining these following things; - More energy for the things that truly matter. - Real growth and fresh creativity. - Stronger and more genuine connections (people can feel when you’re truly present). - Most importantly A deeper trust in yourself. Life will keep sending waves some will gentle and some crashing hard. The secret isn’t becoming wave proof. It’s learning how to swim with them. What are you welcoming in your life right now? Drop your thoughts in the comments. If this spoke to you feel free to reblog or share it with someone who might need it. Stay healthy, keep exploring, #aliveandthrive #hivepakistan #firstcontext ![image](https://images.ecency.com/DQme3UUygStACc7KmxkE2F5R62gjiCe8ef2N1fSqJ4CkTph/1709406530011.png) # NOTE * English isn't my First even Second Language, sometime I use Google Translator. * Photos have their source links.. * Don't hesitate to give your feedback , It will encourage my confidence. * Thank you very much for reading and spending your Time. * **Share your Point of Views.....** ![image](https://images.ecency.com/DQme3UUygStACc7KmxkE2F5R62gjiCe8ef2N1fSqJ4CkTph/1709406530011.png) # If you are new, this is for you. ### [How to Write a Blog?](https://ecency.com/hive-140084/@nabbas0786/blogging) ### [DO, AVOID, USE (DAU), Tips for Newbies](https://ecency.com/hive-192111/@nabbas0786/do-avoid-use-dau-tips) ### [How to Use Ecency Front-End of Hive?](https://ecency.com/hive-140084/@nabbas0786/how-to-use-ecency-front) ###### **Ghulam Abbas (@nabbas0786)** Passionate Doctor | Healing & Caring | Exploring Life's Wonders With Hive ✨ ![image](https://images.ecency.com/DQme3UUygStACc7KmxkE2F5R62gjiCe8ef2N1fSqJ4CkTph/1709406530011.png)

links.title: Mensaje diario de 5  minutos: debería divorciarse / 5 Minute Freewrite: he should divorce
links.body:
>



# Decisión

​

#


En una etapa bastante compleja de la vida está la relación que tengas con otra persona; y si es alguien donde hay un vínculo que los une o unió por mucho tiempo, es decir, hay sentimientos de amor, admiración y la confianza para compartir todo hasta vivir juntos construyendo un hogar y hasta una familia es muy difícil hablar o imaginar si toda esa conexión un día de repente se rompe y todo termina. Siendo muy complicado además de doloroso por todo lo que implica una separación.

Hablar de divorcio es un tema muy fuerte y para tomar esa decisión quiere decir que se pensó hace bastante tiempo; pues, no es algo repentino porque primero se va apagando todo lentamente como enviando señales de que algo está mal y a pesar de eso continuas para intentar salvarlo. 

Pero puede ser que entres en negación y prefieras fingir que todo está bien, por eso no enfrentas la situación o también sucede que buscas todas las alternativas posibles para solucionar lo que esté pasando; sin embargo, no logras recuperar nada sobre todo cuando es solo una de las partes que está poniendo todo su esfuerzo es recuperar la relación pero la otra no.

Cuando te cuesta tanto decidir, encuentras o tienes a otra persona cerca como amigo o familia que te dice: **debería divorciarse** de una vez porque ya no hay nada que recuperar. Es más importante valorarte como persona y mujer antes de seguir luchando por algo que evidentemente no vale la pena; entiendo que las ganas de resolver las cosas debe ser de los dos porque si solo una quiere seguir remando ese barco no avanzará sola o quizás hace rato ya estaba sola y no se había dado cuenta.
​


​<center>![WhatsApp Image 2022-05-12 at 3.28.50 PM.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeucn6MeLy6DkeFM7A2nU8vB9xADUBt8Yr6bzbsja2DRK/WhatsApp%20Image%202022-05-12%20at%203.28.50%20PM.jpeg)</center>
​

# Decision



#
One of the most complex stages of life is the relationship you have with another person; and if it’s someone with whom you share—or have shared for a long time—a bond—that is, feelings of love, admiration, and the trust to share everything, even to the point of living together, building a home, and starting a family—it’s very difficult to talk about or imagine what it would be like if that entire connection were to suddenly break one day and it all came to an end. It’s not only painful but also very complicated because of everything a breakup entails.
​
Talking about divorce is a very heavy topic, and making that decision means you’ve been thinking about it for quite some time; it’s not something that happens suddenly, because first everything slowly fades away, as if sending signals that something is wrong, and despite that, you keep trying to save the relationship. 

But you might go into denial and prefer to pretend that everything is fine, which is why you don’t face the situation head-on. Or it might be that you look for every possible alternative to fix whatever is going on; however, you’re unable to salvage anything, especially when only one person is putting in all the effort to save the relationship while the other isn’t.
​
When you’re having such a hard time deciding, you find or have someone close to you—a friend or family member—who tells you: **you should get a divorce** once and for all because there’s nothing left to salvage. It’s more important to value yourself as a person and as a woman before continuing to fight for something that’s clearly not worth it; I understand that the desire to work things out has to come from both of you, because if only one person wants to keep rowing, that boat won’t move forward on its own—or maybe it’s been adrift for a while now, and you just haven’t realized it.
​

#

# Stonycreek Township, Somerset County, Pennsylvania

**Source:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonycreek_Township,_Somerset_County,_Pennsylvania

Stonycreek Township garnered global attention during the September 11 attacks when United Airlines Flight 93, intended to strike the United States Capitol in Washington, D.C., crashed into a field near downtown after civilian passengers on the flight from Newark, New Jersey to San Francisco International Airport rebelled against the flight's al-Qaeda terrorist hijackers.

What is now Stonycreek Township was settled in 1762. Most old records call it Stony Creek. The township was incorporated in 1792 from portions of Quemahoning Township as the last of the six original townships of Somerset County.
Glessner Bridge was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1980.[4]

September 11 attacks[edit]

![Image 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Flight93memorial3.jpg/250px-Flight93memorial3.jpg)

The September 11 crash site of Flight 93
Stonycreek Township gained global attention on September 11, 2001, when United Airlines Flight 93 crashed there. Flight 93 was one of four airliners hijacked that day as part of the Al-Qaeda terrorist attack on the United States. It is widely held that the Flight 93 hijackers intended to use the craft to strike the United States Capitol. The crash occurred when the passengers tried to overpower the hijackers and seize control of the aircraft, prompting the terrorists to deliberately crash it rather than lose their advantage. The passengers learned of the plane's intended fate through cell phone calls to and from family members. All 44 people aboard the plane (including the four hijackers) were dead on impact. The site is now the location of a national memorial honoring the passengers and crew.[5]

Flight 93 National Memorial[edit]

George W. Bush and Laura Bush visiting Stonycreek Township on September 11, 2002, the first anniversary of the attacks
The original temporary memorial to the passengers and crew of Flight 93 was located on a hill, about 500 yards (0.46 km) from the crash site. On July 8, 2010, a new temporary entrance and memorial were opened at an area called \

. It is where the FBI set up their command center and where family members first saw the aftermath of the crash, bringing their own memorials, where visitors can leave them today. The initial phase of permanent construction of the Flight 93 National Memorial, including the visitor center, was to be completed by the 10th anniversary in 2011. The first phase of the permanent memorial was completed, opened, and dedicated on September 10, 2011. The current design for the memorial is a modified version of the entry Crescent of Embrace by Paul and Milena Murdoch. The memorial was built around the crash site, following the plane's flight path, and protects the area of impact, known as the \

, which will remain protected and accessible only to family members of the passengers and crew.

![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Map_of_Somerset_County%2C_Pennsylvania_highlighting_Stonycreek_Township.PNG/250px-Map_of_Somerset_County%2C_Pennsylvania_highlighting_Stonycreek_Township.PNG)

Stonycreek Township is located approximately at 40.01°N by 78.88°W, about 3 miles (4.8 km) west-southwest of Indian Lake, Pennsylvania. According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the township has a total area of 61.4 square miles (159.0 km2), of which 61.1 square miles (158.3 km2) is land and 0.3 square miles (0.7 km2) (0.44%) is water. It is bordered to the northeast by Shade Township, to the northwest by Quemahoning Township, to the west by Somerset Township, to the southwest by Brothersvalley Township, and to the east by Allegheny Township. Pennsylvania Route 31 runs along the township's southwestern border with Brothersvalley Township and passes into Allegheny Township to the east. U.S. Route 30 / the Lincoln Highway runs along the township's northeastern border with Shade Township. Pennsylvania Route 160 passes through Stonycreek Township as it heads northeast from Brothersvalley Township to Shade Township. Route 160 and Route 31 intersect in Roxbury, and Route 160 and U.S. Route 30/Lincoln Highway intersect in Reels Corner.

Historical population

20002,221—20102,2370.7%20202,087−6.7%2022 (est.)2,066[3]−1.0%U.S. Decennial Census[6]

As of the 2020 census,[7] of 2000, there were 2,221 people, 820 households, and 634 families residing in the township. The population density was 36.3 inhabitants per square mile (14.0/km2). There were 1,033 housing units at an average density of 16.9/sq mi (6.5/km2). The racial makeup of the township was 98.96% White, 0.09% African American, 0.32% Native American, 0.14% Asian, 0.05% from other races, and 0.45% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino of any race were 0.23% of the population.
There were 820 households, out of which 35.5% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 68.3% were married couples living together, 5.9% had a female householder with no husband present, and 22.6% were non-families. 18.2% of all households were made up of individuals, and 8.2% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.71 and the average family size was 3.10.
In the township, the population was spread out, with 26.5% under the age of 18, 6.5% from 18 to 24, 29.4% from 25 to 44, 25.3% from 45 to 64, and 12.2% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 38 years. For every 100 females, there were 100.1 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 99.5 males.
The median income for a household in the township was $33,828, and the median income for a family was $38,418. Males had a median income of $30,236 versus $21,714 for females. The per capita income for the township was $14,463. About 9.6% of families and 10.8% of the population were below the poverty line, including 11.9% of those under age 18 and 3.9% of those age 65 or over.

![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Map_of_Pennsylvania_highlighting_Somerset_County.svg/250px-Map_of_Pennsylvania_highlighting_Somerset_County.svg.png)

links.title: The Effectiveness of Punishment in Modern Society
links.body:
Hello to all hive users 🤗❤️🙏
Hope you all are healthy and doing great in your life🙂


No matter which country you live in, the legal system there includes provisions for punishment. Penalties exist for everything from the most minor offenses to the gravest crimes. Punishment is not prescribed solely to penalize individuals for their wrongdoing; it also serves to reduce the incidence of such crimes. If a person knows that committing a crime could result in a specific punishment, they will think twice before acting. In fact, most people would refrain from committing the crime altogether, knowing the severity of the potential consequences—such as the risk of ruining their career—even for a minor offense. Thus, the prospect of punishment makes people deliberate carefully before engaging in any criminal activity.





![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZ6zY5CHoQ4x76yNrmx4TgPG4K5Hmj49kAhHRgmqrtWqk/1781602554015.png)

Image Generated By Chatgpt 



You may have noticed that crime rates vary significantly between countries—being very low in some and extremely high in others. This disparity is often due not only to superior, modern legal systems but also to the existence of severe punishments that are widely known to the public. Sometimes, these punishments are even broadcast live to demonstrate the dire consequences of committing even a minor offense, thereby compelling people to think twice before breaking the law. However, this applies to situations where a person is in full control of their faculties; some crimes are committed when a person is not of sound mind—for instance, while under the influence of intoxicants. A person who is fully conscious might well consider the potential punishment, but someone who is not in a rational state of mind cannot do so. Regardless of how draconian the legal system's penalties for a specific crime might be, an individual who is not in a state to comprehend the situation simply cannot factor those consequences into their decision-making.

Rising crime rates in a country do not necessarily imply a higher number of criminals or an inadequate legal system; the root cause may lie elsewhere—unemployment, for instance, is a major factor. In countries with high unemployment, people often turn to illicit paths to earn money. Once someone starts down this wrong path, turning back becomes extremely difficult; it becomes a quagmire that drags the individual into the criminal underworld. Crimes then tend to escalate, and the person eventually ends up on the list of criminals. In many places, a sluggish legal system also emboldens offenders. You may have observed that in some countries, cases where the facts are largely clear drag on for years. Conversely, in nations with swift legal processes, people are deterred from committing crimes. However, in countries where the legal system is flawed—plagued by bribery and instances where the government shields powerful figures—anyone with a bit of influence or the right connections might commit a crime without a second thought, knowing they can easily secure their release from jail.

Ultimately, the conclusion is that reducing crime requires a concerted effort across multiple areas rather than focusing on just one thing. While harsh punishment might deter some individuals, it does not affect everyone; therefore, addressing various aspects is crucial. A solution can only be found through a collaborative approach tackling these different factors, and only then is there a possibility of reducing crime.
While punishment is necessary, we also need to improve other aspects of the system. The legal framework should ensure that everyone is treated equally and that any action taken against individuals is applied uniformly, without regard for a person's identity, power, or status. The kind of reform programs implemented in prisons should also be introduced in schools, colleges, and other settings; this would foster awareness and help people realize how wrong it is to commit even a minor offense.









Thanks for reading my post till the end. 
If you have any suggestions or feedback then please comment down.

links.title: Naples Diaries #1
links.body: /> Hello dear travel lovers. I decided to spend three days in Naples and inhale this intense atmosphere to the fullest. In my opinion, if you gathered all of Italy and all the clichés about it into a single city, you would end up with Naples. This city brings all of Italy together. Right next to the smells emanating from the rotting garbage in the center, the amazing aromas of traditional pastries, coffee, seafood, burnt rubber and old diesel blend together. Magnificent palaces, murals, slums, high-crime neighborhoods and right above them, viewpoints opening up to Italy’s greatest beauties.

/> Naples is located in southwestern Italy, on the coast of the Tyrrhenian sea and is one of the country's most important port cities. Many tourists visit the city via cruise ships. Some arrive from Rome by bus or train in a journey of two hours at most. But the majority reach the local airport by plane. The city center can be reached by express buses. Surprisingly everything here is quite simple and clear. You follow the signboard arrows, buy a ticket from the booth for five euros and reach the train station. However this simplicity and convenience end right there. Because at that exact point, I think the real Naples adventure begins.

/> Whether we call all these local characteristics a colorful atmosphere, authenticity or the cheerful and carefree nature of the locals, everyone who comes here immediately notices the poverty and disorder. The numbers confirm this too. We could feel that we were in the capital of one of Italy's poorest regions. While the per capita national income in the Campania region is between 18 and 20 thousand euros, this figure is more than double in the north around 38 to 45 thousand euros. This situation is immediately evident from the old and cheap cars on the streets, the lack of landscaping, the dilapidated state of the buildings and the abundance of graffiti.

/> Furthermore in most of the massive buildings we saw, the elevators were installed later and required payment. Those living on the first or second floor don't pay, but residents on the upper floors have to drop coins into the elevator every time they go up and down. In short poverty and occasional misery make themselves felt immediately. Actualy when examined closely, it becomes clear that the palaces and churches here wouldn't be built out of nowhere. There was definitely a serious flow of money here once upon a time.

/> This wealth began when the Greeks established the first settlement here in the seventh century BC. Centuries later the city was destroyed and a new city was founded right next to it. This new settlement is thought to have been established where the medieval Castel dell’Ovo castle stands today. The name of the city emerged naturally. Neapolis meaning New City. In this regard the capital of Campania has many global namesakes. Novgorod in Russia, Newtown in the USA, Neustadt in Germany, Novo Mesto in Slovenia and many other examples, including Carthage. The word Carthage also means New city. Judging by some of the buildings, one gets the feeling that a similar fate awaits Naples.

/> Yet unlike Carthage, Naples had the chance to become a part of the Roman Empire. Even back then there was an important port here. Due to the proximity of thermal springs and the beauty of the region, Roman nobles loved to relax in Naples. After the fall of the Roman Empire, the city passed into Byzantine rule. In the tenth century it was attached to the Kingdom of Sicily and soon became the capital. In honor of this event Castel Nuovo, one of the most important symbols of the city was built. Its construction took only three years. This duration is prety much the same as the time the local mafia needs today just to clear the garbage from a single street.

/> Castel Nuovo hosted the court of the Kingdom of Naples for centuries. Its western facade tells the beginning of a new era for the city. There is a triumphal arch built to commemorate the conquest. The King of Aragon originaly wanted to build an independent arch in the Roman style, but due to fear of a rebellion where the dynastic coat of arms could be damaged, he decided to place the structure in a safer spot between the towers of the castle. Thus, Naples acquired the first work of Renaissance architecture in all of southern Italy. Even if unofficial this marked the beginning of the Spanish rule that would last for four centuries.

/> There are two different urban layers in Naples. The first is the layer where the trade of vegetables,fruits and all kinds of goods is actively carried out. There are also endless, noisy scooters.In short life is buzzing here. On one hand, this situation might seem daunting and that is why most people run away from Naples. On the other hand people flock here because there are very few cities left in Italy that have managed to keep life so vibrant even in their center, especially ones as beautiful and large as Naples.

/> The other important and cultural layer begins from the third and fourth floors up. This petrified layer never changes. It undoubtedly possesses a mesmerizing beauty. When you get a bit disheartened and tired from the first layer, you can look up and admire this unchanging and always glamorous view. Of course, the apartments hanging out laundry change things a little.

/> Leaving the extremely noisy street, we stepped into a courtyard and once again I was spellbound. Because before us stood the fascinating Palazzo dello Spagnolo and its famous stairs, where words fall short. The building was constructed by architect Ferdinando Sanfelice. I don't know what can be said about the Rococostyle stairs. When walking on that noisy street, you usually look under your feet to avoid falling, so you don't notice this beauty. Actually the building on our left as we walked was a beautiful palace bearing the same name. But we barely saw it.

/> Upon entering here we were able to examine everything in detail. Over time, the palace took the name Palazzo dello Spagnolo because it was bought by a very wealthy man nicknamed the Spaniard. You must definitely come here. I am sure the best photos among the buildings in Naples can be taken here. Because it is both not very crowded and where else in the world could you see such a structure? Forget Naples, it is rare to find its like even in the world.

/> Now I want to say a few words about hotels and apartment rentals. I rented an apartment near the shopping street Via dei Mille, in one of the quietest and cleanest areas of the city. The nightly price of this luxury apartment cost me only 65 euros. If you are planning a trip too, it makes the most sense to handle the payment issues in advance, get a virtual card and use it wherever you wish. I made the payment via Booking using a virtual card. I think a virtual card provides great convenience while traveling all over the world. This way you don't have to deal with exchange offices or carry cash with you.

/> We went out into the noisy streets of Naples again. After walking about 300 meters from Palazzo dello Spagnolo, we came across a very interesting courtyard. Unfortunately though it has worn down over time, luckily this wear occurred homogeneously. So the courtyard doesn't look bad even now. Of course a renovation wouldn't be bad at all. It's hard to comment on the situation.

/> However as ordinary tourists, even while walking, we can see the beauty here or at least this interesting vibe. It is very nice to come across such open courtyards and stairs in Naples. Outsid life was practically buzzing with an incredible noise, while absolute silence reigned where we were. This was highly enjoyable.

/> We walked about 15 meters more and came across another work by Ferdinando Sanfelice. This project was designed about 15 years before Palazzo dello Spagnolo. However as it appears, it is crystal clear that Ferdinando was a true master at creating these kinds of open staircase structures. I know that commercials are frequently shot in this courtyard. These stairs are very often preferred when someone wants to shoot an interesting commercial with an atmospheric, unusual background. It's not hard to understand why. Let's say we needed to shoot a model and a perfume or a new clothing collection here. I think it would give wonderful results and I would buy that outfit myself.

/> Of course these works of Sanfelice are not the most popular spots on Naples tourist map. These courtyards remain a bit far from the center and only a very small number of people stop by here. However almost everyone visits the neighborhoods where Via dei Tribunali and Via San Gregorio Armeno are located. This also has its own unique texture. In terms of historical buildings, everything is in its proper place here too. First comes the Cathedral of San Gennaro, the largest holy site in Naples. This temple almost embodies the entire history of the city. A Pagan temple of Apollo, ancient Greek walls, a Roman aqueduct, an early Christian baptistery and Gothic chapels have all come together in its structure.

/> The current building was constructed in the early fourteenth century and was subsequently rebuilt and expanded multiple times, incorporating Gothic, Baroque and Neoclassical elements. Aside from its religious and historical importance, visiting churches in Naples literally means stepping into a different world. You forget the noise, the heat, the garbage. You are left alone with the works of the best masters of their era. This is also true for the Sansevero Chapel. A fantastic place absolutely worth visiting. Right next to it is the Gesu Nuovo Church, which has the most unusual facade in all of Italy. It has a rather eerie appearance. The church was established on the site of an old fifteenth century palace. When the Jesuits bought the building, they hardly changed the facade, which was made of a very hard local limestone in the shape of pyramids. Yet behind the harsh exterior appearance, magnificent Baroque interiors are hidden.

/> Afterward all tourists, one way or another, end up on Via Toledo, the main pedestrian street named after the Spanish viceroy of Naples. This is quite symbolic since almost the entire layout of the old city took shape during the years of Spanish rule. During the Aragon dynasty period, Naples became a center of attraction for artists and scientists. Under the Habsburgs, it became one of the largest cities in Europe, second only to Paris in terms of population. To find out what happened next, we had to walk along Via Toledo street and reach the city's main square, Piazza del Plebiscito.

/> Here lies one of the most famous architectural structures in Naples. The Basilica of San Francesco di Paola, adorned on both sides with semicircular covered colonnades. The Royal Palace, Palazzo della Prefettura and Palazzo Salerno complement the square perfectly. The name of the square Plebiscito, meaning referendum, was not chosen by coincidence either. After the Napoleonic Wars the administration returned to the Bourbons, the minor branch of the Spanish dynasty.

/> I am concluding what I have to say about Naples here for today. On my next posts I will continue to share the places I visited and saw here with you. See you very soon. [//]:# (!pinmapple 40.83849 lat 14.25270 long d3scr)

links.title: Bracket IV Day 1 Grind & Feedback
links.body:
>
Hello, there! **@saydie** here, playing **Splinterlands** everyday!

> Today, I officially start playing Survival Mode under the Bracket IV. This is in response to this **[Post](https://peakd.com/splinterlands/@splinterlands/announcement-splinterlands-survival-mode-stress-testing-next-season)**, asking for players to participate in order to test the liquidity bots in preparation for the implementation of Brackets in modern. For the players who will participate, they will be rewarded with an additional 250k Glint if they manage to play 250 battles with 50%+ win rate, but if under 50%, they still receive 100k Glint. Yesterday, I said that I did not expect to reach 250 battles, but after playing today, I think that it can be doable. In this post, I want to share my Day 1 Grind progress and some of my early feedback. ![CA.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/23tvY7mZ5F1UqsiqG2X3RRGzAX3ozTT6Hq4tcztUxyzehmwovZ6ty8JR6rmEoqVCkYBQp.png)

> Just like the previous survival season, all players will start in Wood Tier at 0 rating once they enter a Bracket, the same goes with me. Since this is still Survival Mode, +20 rating regardless of your winning streak, so it will take a while to get to a substantially high rating. That said, the liquidity bots that you will encounter in the Wood Tier are quite easy to handle, as they mostly use Foundation Archons and units, meaning that their stats are capped at Silver. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/23tGaDVHQyAH3rViGkQywoSE2PjuUF3eTHoovK19bRrWttfV3wHECpEYzZEAVtfsoeJuW.png) However, as soon as you reach Bronze Tier, this is where it starts to get difficult, because you will start to encounter liquidity bots with max-level Archons and units, meaning that they are capped at Gold. Given how easy the liquidity bots you encounter in Wood Tier versus the liquidity bots that you encounter at Bronze Tier, the difficulty progression of the liquidity bots has increased from easy to difficult real quick, so it definitely caught me off guard, especially since I am still not that familiar with Gold level meta, as I always play at max level. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/23tGcNJ5xzhVcVsSj9H3fpQncc4oRgsLKaLr4chEHPjxLhYNz2qSgWQpavvzALcyQ3B8z.png) Another thing that makes fighting the liquidity bot harder is that they play using all card sets, not just Modern cards. I even faced against a liquidity bot that uses land crafted cards in its battle history. Although we can also use Wild cards, the bots being able to play all sets places us at a huge disadvantage, and I could not see how the bots being able to play wild cards will be able to provide good data for modern brackets. I would rather prefer it if the team had just tweaked Bracket IV so that only modern cards can be used in battle. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/23sxA5tDWksviaUCUBJB51Hd8xvs1aag9AQddPwENvjr4T5cCTpdWWSnMZziFtYBud8Y4.png) For my first day of grinding Bracket IV of Survival, I played a total of 26 battles, by which I won 20 of them. That currently gives me a 76.92% win rate, which is still above the 50% requirement to get 250k Glint, though it will likely fall lower as I continue to play the Bracket through the season. I could still play more since I still have lots of Archons and units that I can use despite the losses that I have, but I decided to call it a day, so that I can write my feedback. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/Eo1vVUSLdbaWDn1hUNmLbgmPh7MXxGoY1kjSPpw9UnMb8TtzLZnFZY89ioTia9ARiwh.png) ![CA.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/23tvY7mZ5F1UqsiqG2X3RRGzAX3ozTT6Hq4tcztUxyzehmwovZ6ty8JR6rmEoqVCkYBQp.png)

>

* **Survival Cooldown reduction is a big thumbs up.**

I did not notice it yesterday, but when making my last post, but the cooldown of the cards that were defeated in battle seems to be significantly reduced for the stress testing period, which is great for casual players like me that does not have a large card collection. That is the reason I could say that playing 250 battles, even for someone like me, can be doable.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/23tGTsF5GpsGwURpCjPhXbUwjP5y7H2c2Q1M3F62xDrN3gTLMgki5k18sZ8DJq7wyAu8h.png)

* **Liquidity Bot difficulty progression sucks.**

From liquidity bots playing only max-level foundation cards at Wood Tier, it immediately goes to max-level cards for the bracket, which is a bad difficulty progression. It's like after completing the tutorial, you're immediately facing off with the final boss of the game. At least try to diversify the level and the type of cards that the bot can use to provide a better difficulty progression, then only include those super-strong bots in matchmaking once the player has reached more than 1k rating, not when they are still at only 300 rating.

* **Matchmaking time on Wood Tier was quick, but after that, matchmaking can take up to 2 minutes.**

When I was still at Wood Tier, the matchmaking against liquidity bots was almost instantaneous, but after reaching Bronze Tier, the matchmaking time became inconsistent. Sometimes, I get a match within 30 seconds, but there are times that 2 minutes have already passed, and I still cannot find an opponent, whether it was another player or a liquidity bot. And that was still just the beginning of my grind. I wonder how long the matchmaking will be once I reach a much higher rating.

![CA.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/23tvY7mZ5F1UqsiqG2X3RRGzAX3ozTT6Hq4tcztUxyzehmwovZ6ty8JR6rmEoqVCkYBQp.png)

<center> <div align=\

> And that was my first day of feedback playing the Bracket IV of Survival mode. Will probably give you another update after a week of grinding. Hopefully, by that time, they will make matchmaking time quicker, because they have shown that it can be done when I was playing at Wood Tier. Thank you, and see you on the next post! ![CA.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/23tvY7mZ5F1UqsiqG2X3RRGzAX3ozTT6Hq4tcztUxyzehmwovZ6ty8JR6rmEoqVCkYBQp.png)

links.title: Film Review: The Diary of Diana B. (Dnevnik Diane Budisavljević, 2019)
links.body:
![(source: tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/A83Sakm0DTdTFFNFSAo7zu3GjGC.jpg)

World War Two ended almost three-quarters of a century ago and slowly but inevitably perishes from living memory. In Croatia, however, it is still a very relevant subject, especially in the realm of politics where differences in views on contemporary issues play second fiddle to the question of which side someone’s ancestor fought for in the global conflict. This could be explained, to a certain degree, by the fact that World War II was particularly destructive in a small and relatively poor country like Croatia, causing more bloodshed and destruction than in any time before or since. And, to make things even worse, most of that bloodshed and destruction was caused by Croatians themselves, resulting in one of the darkest and most shameful chapters of national history. That war drew out the worst in people, but it also drew out the best. One example of the latter is the subject of *The Diary of Diana B.*, the 2019 biopic directed by Croatian filmmaker Dana Budisavljević.

The film’s protagonist is the author’s distant relative Diana Budisavljević, a woman often described as Croatia’s closest equivalent to Oskar Schindler. She was actually Austrian; in her youth she married Julije Budisavljević, a Croatian Serb surgeon who would later become a member of the city’s social elite in Zagreb in the pre-WW2 years. In April 1941 the city and the rest of Croatia was occupied by Nazi Germany and their Axis allies; they installed the puppet regime of the Independent State of Croatia, led by the fascist Ustasha movement, whose platform called for the elimination of all non-Croats, namely Serbs, Jews and Romani people. Those minorities became brutally persecuted, although Budisavljević, mostly thanks to having saved some future Ustasha leaders before the war, evaded persecution himself. His wife, however, was deeply disturbed by the fate of Serb women and children being put in concentration camps and decided to collect and deliver humanitarian aid. Her efforts gained further urgency in June 1942 when a German and Ustasha offensive against Partisans on Mount Kozara in today’s Bosnia resulted in a large number of Serb children ending up in facilities like the notorious Jasenovac Concentration Camp, where thousands quickly succumbed to neglect, starvation and disease. Budisavljević organised a rescue in the form of mass adoption and foster care among Zagreb families, which ultimately saved thousands of lives; her personal connections among the higher ranks of the German military and Catholic Church made this operation possible and offered protection to her and her husband. In May 1945 victorious Partisans entered Zagreb, but the new post-war Communist government failed to recognise Diana Budisavljević’s work and, until recently, her role in those events was virtually unknown.

For Dana Budisavljević, who had made only documentaries until this point, *The Diary of Diana B.* is her first live-action film and it shows. Obviously inspired by Spielberg’s [*Schindler’s List*](https://peakd.com/film/@drax/retro-film-review-schindler-s-list-1993), it tries to pay not-so-subtle homage to that film with its use of black-and-white photography. There are, however, few similarities between the two films, partly due to the much lower budget for Budisavljević’s film, which was made as a Croatian-Slovenian-Serbian co-production. Almost all live-action scenes take place indoors – in the Budisavljevićs’ luxurious villa or various offices – and consist of lengthy discussions about the protagonist’s work or the political situation, which serve as exposition for viewers not so familiar with the history of Yugoslavia in WW2. Those scenes are often poorly directed, overlong and uninspired despite some of the actors, like Alma Prica in the title role, trying their best to bring some life to their characters.

*The Diary of Diana B.* works best in documentary scenes, where the director can apply her rich past experience. This includes authentic documentary footage made in the camps, which is almost seamlessly fused with the rest of the film; those scenes, which feature starved and sick children, many of them actually dying in inhumane conditions, are quite disturbing, and this film should not be recommended to overly sensitive viewers. Equally powerful is the documentary footage made in the present day when four of the rescued children, now people at the twilight of their lives, recall their experiences, horrors they witnessed, and families and loved ones they lost, while one of them struggles with the fact that the loss of Diana Budisavljević’s records deprived him of his proper identity. Those segments of the film make the live-action scenes unnecessary and create the impression that Dana Budisavljević could have made a much better film if she had taken inspiration from *Shoah*. Although deeply flawed, this film nevertheless serves its purpose by providing an important history lesson, especially needed in these times when such lessons might be forgotten and characters like Diana Budisavljević might be needed again.



RATING: 5/10 (++)


*(Note: The text in the original version is available [here](https://draxreview.wordpress.com/2019/11/28/review-the-diary-of-diana-b-dnevnik-diane-budisavljevic-2019/).)*

links.title: Exploring, Gamla stan, Archipelago & More | A Day In Stockholm Center City
links.body: /> Traveling In europe as been a dream.. in my travel blog today we look at my exploration of Stockholm city center and all it has to offer.. When i tell you this is one of the best places i have been, from the train system to the tram line custruction of the city… all this made exploring here such a great experience

/> My day started at noon after commuting from bas to slussen using the train, the train system was really an enjoyable ride with the colour representation being yellow and blue it gave of the impression of a project that was made with pride and prestige.

/> Alighting at slussen station see directly the lane down to **old town**, i trecked down the bridge lane over seeing the stockholm port.. here we saw lots of boats and ship docked.. in a far distance was a train travk that ran across the port. Hotels like “ “”” were also in view from the brige were the sun was on the horizon in the watee.. it was an indeed beautiful sight to see.

/> The infamous (**Gamla Stan)** Old town was on the top of my list to visit, it saw a lots of tourist every year with the beautiful colour buildings which always amazed me in pictures, in the square was the Royal palace and monumental statues that holds the history of sweden. In this place i could also visit some shops and traditional local market were i purchased som souvenirs and window shopped holiday materials that were on display

/> I proceeded down the lane after my visit to old town. The coast ran along far down and the sea breeze made the air cold but refreshing i looked iver the bridge which at this spot was lower and closer to the water, it was nice to have a view of cruise ship with tourist on the water … in view where a couple of Luxury hotels like the Grand Hotel
/> On this lane saw the assembly house

/> It was really an incredyday taking in the city of stockholm. And i cant wait to share more with you from my visit.. Thanks a lot for stopping by i would love to see you in the next one. \[//\]:# (!worldmappin 59.32553 lat 18.07280 long Stockholm Center d3scr) All images are mine taking on my iphone 13 device some images are edited with meitu app see you next time!!

links.title: Street Struggles and Silent Corruption
links.body:
***Every day, especially in places where getting by is tough, you can’t help but see the big difference between people struggling on the streets and those in positions of power. I often think about how corruption affects regular people, especially street vendors who work hard through all kinds of weather just to earn enough for one meal.***

When you walk through the streets, you see people selling all sorts of things: vegetables on small tables, fish on melting ice, snacks wrapped in plastic, and trinkets laid out on cloths. These vendors are more than just sellers—they are parents, children, and breadwinners who wake up early or stay up late to get by. Their lives may look simple, but behind it all is a daily fight for dignity and survival.

![4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23uQrWZtmK1G4T9DcF1Kgcf2vEc6UdArQcHs4QkAePP6vjxCMxsHDNyS5Lp4aZcusd4JU.jpg)

**Corruption makes things even harder for them, quietly affecting their daily lives**. While they work honestly, many face unfair treatment from the very systems that should protect them. Some vendors are told to pay extra fees just to keep their spot on the sidewalk. Others are forced to leave without warning, losing their goods and ending the day with nothing. It’s a harsh reality where those with the least are often asked to give the most.

**It’s frustrating to see how corruption can reach even the smallest parts of society.** It’s not always obvious or in the news; sometimes it’s hidden in daily transactions, in permits that take too long unless you pay extra, or in rules that change depending on who you know. For street vendors, this means living with constant uncertainty. One day they can sell, the next day they’re forced to leave. There’s no stability, just the hope that tomorrow might be better.

![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/EokdeJokan9Z91Cxksu8QBhZQggiEhSirs1eMgUhvkACDn7z9w4wiVwijjQz2Yy3MR7.jpg)

Even with all these challenges, street vendors keep working hard in the most honest way they can. Their resilience is truly admirable. You might see a mother selling bananas with her child on her back, a father calling out to people with a tired but hopeful voice, or a student selling snacks after school to help their family. These are stories of quiet strength.**They may not have much, but their determination is hard to break**.

![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/EopsxQpdKXX4bjFU3WftAyKAqAxNb9wnD9TuJjd1ryNaxhxpdnGYmtkho4oJz73mwct.jpg)

**Meanwhile, corruption continues to widen the gap between those who struggle and those who benefit from unfair systems.**Money that could help improve markets, build shelters for vendors, or create fair programs is sometimes lost or misused. Instead of creating opportunities, resources are wasted or taken from those who need them most. It’s a sad irony that the people who work the hardest often get the least support. It’s easy to feel angry when you think about these things—angry at the unfairness, the lack of accountability, and the systems that ignore the poor. But there’s also sadness. Sadness for the vendors who start each day with hope but face uncertainty, for families who have to choose between food and other needs, and for a society where being honest doesn’t always mean you’ll get by. 

![3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23uQtoCfCDm4MKZFKhwtGgs8mzn1KYdny8RxMgbTvjgDDtwJGMivsuwgGSB2SYAuTN2bs.jpg)

**Still, even with all these struggles, there is hope.** You can see it in small acts of kindness—like customers choosing to buy from street vendors instead of big stores, neighbors sharing food or helping each other, and communities working to create fair spaces for small sellers. These small actions won’t end corruption right away, but they start changes that remind us there’s still humanity in everyday life. Real change starts with awareness. When people see what street vendors go through and how corruption affects them, they start to think more about their choices. Supporting small sellers, demanding transparency, and advocating fair treatment are simple yet powerful steps.

***Leaders and institutions also need to remember that their job is to serve everyone, especially those who are most vulnerable. In the end, the story of street vendors and corruption isn’t just about struggle. It’s also about resilience, dignity, and the hope for a better future. It’s about people who keep fighting fairly, even when the world isn’t fair.***

![5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23wMaevpk7ZL7uhU5cBCUdHhAjJZEKFBCkHYRhY5UD1SK5Xve6CSGJCDbPbH9iLxkw3V2.jpg)

The system may not be perfect, but the voices of ordinary people are strong, showing us that change can happen when we face the truth and work for justice. And even in the face of corruption and hardship, the courage of ordinary people continues to shine in quiet ways. But life on the streets teaches us something important: surviving isn’t just about having resources, but also about having courage. 

***Even amid corruption and hardship, the courage of ordinary people shines in quiet yet meaningful ways.***

links.title: If Punishments Work, Why Does Crime Continue?
links.body: When I was growing up, I used to think that the final solution to crimes or other evil behaviors is punishment. Looking at it from the surface, people should simply avoid acting bad since they know the consequences for their actions, but then I grew up to see that it's not that simple as I thought. Every adult is aware that crimes like robbery, scams, kidnapping, and the like attract big punishment. At times, some victims spend their entire lives in prison, some are sentenced to death, and other big punishments are given, yet crimes never stop. ![17816216901534216279935877728935.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nkemakonam89/23u5xaBPn8M349LKCZ3mB8ZJvQZuhmQMPzn7UnfmKnr6wdd2raDncYh6J7GNyJNKJZG1B.png) ***** People still commit crimes of different colors every now and then. It's a concern, and this brings us to this prompt question, which is, do punishments really work? Are punishments just enough to stop people from robbery? Theft, rape, and the like? ***** From my perspective, punishments work to some extent; at least there are still individuals who stay away from trouble due to the fear of going to prison, but they are rare. And while these punishments scare some people away from committing crime, there are other factors that affect negatively the way humans behave, which are beyond the fear of the consequences attached. Take for instance the incidence that happened in my community a few years ago. This young guy was caught several times committing theft. At first, our community chairman came through for him and only gave him a serious warning; it wasn't long before he committed another serious crime, and this time around, he was handed over to the police, and after being detained for some time over there, everyone expected his brain to reset, but sadly, that never happened. ***** A few months later, he resumed his criminal activities, and some people were saying that the punishment he had received so far wasn't enough to make him quit. But then something happened in the process of deliberately deciding on bigger punishments to give this young guy. It was discovered he was struggling with drug addiction over peer influence. So you see, his major problem wasn't because he wasn't aware of or scared of the punishments, but the addictions he was struggling with were the real problem he had. It overpowered him far more than the punishments. ***** That experience was a big lesson, which is that punishments can address crimes but not the reason behind the crime. Even in our different homes, kids can be punished for some bad behaviors, and they will keep repeating them until the main cause of the act is addressed properly. The same thing is applicable to diverse areas of human lives where crimes are commonly seen and practiced repeatedly even with clear legal punishments. ***** However, I don't mean that punishments should be scrapped; no, our society needs them in order to maintain order. I don't want to imagine a society without rules, laws, and consequences for crimes; it would just make people behave without control, and there would be a lot of chaos for the masses, but then there is a need to understand the root of a problem and then bring a lasting solution. At the end of the day, punishments will continue to work and help prevent countless crimes from certain people, but then, human beings are difficult to understand. Many people commit crimes because of addictions, poverty, environmental influence, and more. ***** Maybe we should put more effort into addressing the cause of these crimes rather than punishing the victims; let's say a combination of both, and hopefully, we could start having a significant change in our society. ***images was created using chatgpt***

links.title: THE WAR: Deal theater [eng/срп] РАТ: Игра око договора
links.body:
>

The world is in a fever again. Are we getting peace in the Middle East? Iran and the US confirmed the signing of a ‘Memorandum of Understanding’ on Friday – whatever that means…


The price of oil futures has fallen to $80, and Trump’s team is trying to present the as-yet-undisclosed contents of the document as a complete victory for the United States. Is that really the case?

Just a week ago,
>Seymour Hersh ran a story on his Substack blog about Trump ‘vaguely inquiring about the nuclear option to end the war with Iran more quickly.’

>

Свет је поново у грозници. Спрема ли нам се мир на Блиском истоку? Иран и САД потврдили су потписивање ‘Меморандума о разумевању’ у петак – ма шта то значило…


Цена будућих уговора на нафту пала је на 80 долара, а екипа око Трампа покушава да представи још неоткривени садржај документа као потпуну победу Сједињених Држава. Да ли је баш тако?

Пре само недељу дана,

>Симор Херш пустио је на свом Сабстак блогу причу како се Трамп ‘неодређено распитивао око нуклеарне опције ради бржег завршетка рата против Ирана.’

[![Trump-2026-06-11_124401.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lighteye/242hohZxSgY5udeAJAYmU5GKRCNd9qDhx75uVUnTKankrskkASP3FHCfsKeRTSVRc9zQz.jpg)](https://breakingthenews.net/Article/Trump-said-to-explore-'nuclear-option'-against-Iran/66482259)
Source / Извор: [Baha Breaking News](https://breakingthenews.net/Article/Trump-said-to-explore-'nuclear-option'-against-Iran/66482259)

>

Given the fact that Seymour Hersh, in his old age, serves as an intermediary through whom intelligence services (primarily the CIA) release test balloons to the public, one could assume that this is the latest in a series of bluffs to scare the Iranian leadership. Iranians called the bluff. Iran threatened to completely destroy American bases in the Middle East and a good part of Israel. And Trump suddenly remembered that the deal was better.

>

Имајући у виду чињеницу да Симор Херш у дубокој старости служи као посредник којим обавештајне службе (ЦИА пре свега) пуштају у јавност пробне балоне, могло се претпоставити да је ово последњи у низу блефова како би се иранско руководство препало. Блеф није успео. Иран је запретио потпуним уништењем америчких база на Блиском истоку и доброг дела Израела. И Трамп се изненада сетио да је договор бољи.

![Winning_2026-06-12_10-05-43.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lighteye/EokbadQQnyLa9mpihVz5FMR3SVJfATnWAQ7LMoPebt2UXat3aPHvBxUjvjSY8C15j7s.jpg)

> We still do not have a confirmed text of the memorandum of understanding, but the following text has been leaked from the Iranian side:

The 14 Proposed Points

According to the text published by Mehr News Agency, the draft framework contains the following provisions:

1. Immediate and permanent cessation of hostilities on all fronts, including Lebanon.

2. U.S. commitment to non-interference in Iran's internal affairs and respect for Iranian sovereignty.News

3. Complete lifting of the U.S. naval blockade within 30 days.

4. Withdrawal of U.S. military forces from territories bordering Iran.

5. Reopening of the Strait of Hormuz within 30 days under arrangements determined by Iran.

6. Suspension of sanctions targeting Iranian oil, petrochemical products, and related exports, alongside full access to Iran's financial resources.

7. Presentation of a reconstruction plan by the United States and its allies valued at a minimum of $300 billion.

8. Commencement of negotiations within 60 days to reach a final agreement covering nuclear issues, sanctions architecture, and relevant resolutions of the United Nations Security Council and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).

9. Reaffirmation of Iran’s commitment to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) and its renunciation of nuclear weapons production.Broadcast & Network News

10. U.S. commitment not to increase troop deployments in the region or impose new sanctions during negotiations.

11. Unfreezing of $24 billion in Iranian assets during the negotiation period, with half of the amount to be released before talks begin.

12. Establishment of a monitoring mechanism to oversee implementation of the agreement.

13. Approval of the final agreement through a United Nations Security Council resolution.

14. Final negotiations to begin only after partial asset releases, suspension of oil sanctions, and the lifting of the naval blockade. The talks would be limited to enrichment activities, sanctions relief, and economic reconstruction, excluding missile programs and regional proxy issues.

Source:

> Још увек немамо потврђен текст меморандума о разумевању, али са Иранске стране процурео је следећи текст:

14 предложених тачака

Према тексту који је објавила новинска агенција Мехр, нацрт оквира садржи следеће одредбе:

1. Непосредни и трајни прекид ватре на свим фронтовима, укључујући Либан.

2. Обавеза САД да се не мешају у унутрашње послове Ирана и поштују ирански суверенитет.

3. Потпуно укидање америчке поморске блокаде у року од 30 дана.

4. Повлачење америчких војних снага са територија које се граниче са Ираном.

5. Поновно отварање Ормуског мореуза у року од 30 дана у складу са аранжманима које одреди Иран.

6. Суспендовање санкција усмерених на иранску нафту, петрохемијске производе и сродни извоз, уз потпун приступ иранским финансијским ресурсима.

7. Представљање плана обнове од стране САД и њихових савезника у вредности од најмање 300 милијарди долара.

8. Почетак преговора у року од 60 дана ради постизања коначног споразума који обухвата нуклеарна питања, архитектуру санкција и релевантне резолуције Савета безбедности УН и Међународне агенције за атомску енергију (IAEA).

9. Потврда посвећености Ирана Споразуму о неширењу нуклеарног оружја (НПТ) и његовог одустајања од производње нуклеарног оружја.

10. Обавеза САД да неће повећавати распоређивање трупа у региону нити уводити нове санкције током преговора.

11. Одмрзавање 24 милијарде долара иранске имовине током периода преговора, при чему ће половина износа бити ослобођена пре почетка преговора.

12. Успостављање механизма за праћење спровођења споразума.

13. Одобравање коначног споразума кроз резолуцију Савета безбедности УН.

14. Завршни преговори почињу тек након делимичног ослобађања имовине, суспензије санкција за нафту и укидања поморске блокаде. Разговори ће бити ограничени на активности око уранијума, ублажавање санкција и економске обнове, искључујући ракетне програме и питања регионалних посредника.

Извор:

>

This sounds too good to be true – full capitulation of USA.

I must admit that I borrowed the title of this text from an episode of ‘CrossТalk’ by Peter Lavelle, the first part of which discusses what it would mean to eventually sign such a text:

>

Ово звучи превише добро да би било истинито – потпуна капитулација САД.

Морам признати да сам наслов овог текста позајмио од епизоде ‘Унакрсног разговора’, Питера Лавела, у чијем се првом делу разматра шта би значило евентуално потписивање оваквог текста:

#### [Deal theater?](https://rumble.com/v7bb9c2-crosstalk-deal-theater.html) at Rumble. Duration / Трајање: 27:09 (енг)
[![CrossTalk BULLHORNS-2026-06-15_093122.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lighteye/23xAVtFY73a59bzo4iXXuKRpiEU3WtVQWcHGXaBEGoRYbckxS3arMQ98A6rouguZ1TSBF.jpg)](https://rumble.com/v7bb9c2-crosstalk-deal-theater.html)

#### [Deal theater?](https://bastyon.com/index?v=5dbd1e59a61f4f2bbc0675bae97d135088f1727f35edb6fd62a1a1d3933d5a83&video=1&ref=PKLvDiBvAsTbYDJhC1xNfby2GFnybCQpHn) at Bastyon. Duration / Трајање: 27:09 (енг)
[![CrossTalk BULLHORNS-2026-06-15_093122.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lighteye/23xAVtFY73a59bzo4iXXuKRpiEU3WtVQWcHGXaBEGoRYbckxS3arMQ98A6rouguZ1TSBF.jpg)](https://bastyon.com/index?v=5dbd1e59a61f4f2bbc0675bae97d135088f1727f35edb6fd62a1a1d3933d5a83&video=1&ref=PKLvDiBvAsTbYDJhC1xNfby2GFnybCQpHn)

>

Trump's spin masters will certainly be able to portray even this text as a victory, and the MAGA crowd will swallow it all without any problems.

>

Трампови спин-мајстори свакако ће умети да чак и овакав текст прикажу као победу, а МАГАрци ће све то без проблема прогутати.

![Blame Biden_2026-06-12_10-05-57.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lighteye/EoK6E4DZbhMavQD8d7AGTPETrZov8vsxWP7aA3tmgoiZN7URPCBSqLVa3tEMrZhFRvM.jpg)

>

Trump has already established a proven pattern of plunder that he has been repeating with great precision since the beginning of the war. Now that everyone has believed in peace, and oil prices are falling, check who is buying the most oil on the stock market.

>

Трамп је већ установио проверену шему пљачке коју врло прецизно понавља од почетка рата. Сад кад су сви поверовали у мир, и кад цене нафте падају, проверите ко је највише купује на берзи.

![Oil circle_2026-06-12_10-06-18.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lighteye/23xVbyTLLX748vkmzA444Je1TwJzYnMo8JJP7w5B4d9CRbXcVNcePpx1GmAfVbtKrgopX.jpg)

>

Of course, this scheme of plunder has its end. And it came with the realization that the military power of the United States is nowhere near that which Hollywood propaganda portrays. Not even close.

So where is the problem? Israel cannot agree to this. Does Trump have a way to contain them? Of course, but don't forget who has control over whom. Trump will not dare to contain Israel. Otherwise, we could see a real assassination! Or some explosive Epstein Files disclosure!

Israel knows it will never again have the opportunity to command a global military power like this, and the best we can expect is a retreat to the ‘Syrian scenario.’ The Empire will never give up until it completely collapses.

>

Наравно, и ова шема пљачке има свој крај. А он је дошао схватањем да војна моћ САД није ни близу оној коју шири холивудска пропаганда. Ни близу.

Где је онда проблем? Израел на ово не може пристати. Има ли Трамп начина да их обузда? Наравно, али не заборавите ко кога држи у шаци. Трамп се неће усудити да обуздава Израел. Иначе бисмо могли да видимо прави атентат! Или експлозивно откриће у Епштајновим документима!

Израел зна да никад више неће имати прилику да овако управља једном глобалном војном силом, и најбоље што можемо очекивати је повлачење на ‘Сиријски сценарио’. Империја неће одустати док се потпуно не распадне.

![Rick-CropImage.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lighteye/23uEwyqCifYdKZYvbpkTqrnj28x5RHnVtc5jFeMSie1S9ojs8m2TCHtPXa2fkJco3MfjM.jpg)
Source / Извор: [Sanchez Effect Screenshot](https://www.rt.com/on-air/)

>\n

So, we are nowhere near the end of the deal theater. There will be no peace as long as the Israel project exists…

\n

>\n

Нисмо ни близу завршетка театра око договора. Мира неће бити све док постоји пројекат Израел…

\n

>

body.title: All The Masks Are Off
body.body: alt=\

--_ [Jesse Welles](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XCCWjgWCI4g) Sunday was Flag Day, and to mark the occasion the Bridge Brigade was out over the interstate with a message for motorists. '_Make Corruption Illegal Again_' would have felt a bit hyperbolic not too long ago, but we now live in an age where insider trading is a pardonable offense and a prime endeavor of the ones launching wars.
alt=\

/> That's not to mention the more traditional flavors of malfeasance that in past times politicians actually attempted to conceal. The night before the Bridge Brigade action I stumbled upon the Jesse Welles song the title of this is drawn from and it just hit hard, a theme song for this moment we're in.
alt=\

/>\n\nThe brigade had barely gotten their letters zip-tied to the bridge when a counter-protester showed up. Wearing a 'White Lives Matter' shirt and waving a Trump 2028 flag, the young man proceeded to alternate between shouting slurs and yelling \
_Masks are off indeed._\n\n
alt=\

/> Had been encountering the dude at protests for a while now, since at least No Kings 2.0 last October, but the explicit racism and fascism was a new development. He would eventually claim to be a member of the neo-fascist and white supremacist group [Patriot Front.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot_Front)
alt=\

/> He could probably try out for Westboro Baptist Church, much like them, the offensiveness of his ranting was matched only by the ineffectiveness of his trolling. _They probably wouldn't let him bring his bear spray though._
alt=\

/> Despite prior experience with shitheads like him, it was still jarring to hear the hate coming out of his mouth. _Still have trouble wrapping my head around how people take that nonsense seriously._ The masks may be off but at the end of the day the little shit was still outnumbered fifty to one.
alt=\

/>\n\nSuspect that the masks have come off because there is currently little in the way of consequences for corruption and hate, but as the saying goes, all things come to an end. _And we the people have got receipts._

body.title: Llama 4: Meta redefines open source with native MoE and multimodality
body.body:
Meta has released relevant open models before — Llama 2 and Llama 3 had real impact on the community. But Llama 4, released in April 2026, represents a shift in scale and architecture that goes beyond the previous versions. It is Meta's first family of open models with a native Mixture of Experts architecture and multimodal capability from training onward.

## The Llama 4 family

Llama 4 arrived with three models, at different stages of availability.

**Scout** has 109 billion total parameters and 17 billion active per inference, with 16 experts in the MoE. It is the model designed to run on a single NVIDIA H100 GPU — which makes it accessible to those who don't have cluster infrastructure. Its context window is 10 million tokens, the largest among open models at the time of release.

**Maverick** has 400 billion total parameters with the same 17 billion active, but with 128 experts in the MoE routing. It requires a DGX H100 system or an equivalent multi-GPU setup. On the available multimodal benchmarks, it surpasses GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash.

**Behemoth** is in a different category: 2 trillion total parameters and 288 billion active. It has not yet been made publicly available — it was announced mainly as a \

, used to improve Scout and Maverick via co-distillation. When — and if — it is released, it will represent the largest open source model ever made available.

## Why MoE matters here

Llama 3 was a dense model. Every token processed activated all the parameters. Llama 4 changed that: with MoE, Scout processes each token using only 17 billion of the 109 billion available parameters. The computational cost of inference drops significantly.

For those who use models in production — especially at high volumes — this difference has a direct impact on cost per token and on system throughput. Scout was designed specifically to be viable on single-GPU hardware in a way that Llama 3-70B simply was not, despite having superior performance.

## Native multimodality

\

here has a specific meaning: Scout and Maverick were trained on text and image data from the start, they did not have visual capability added via later fine-tuning. This tends to result in better integration between the modalities — the model reasons about images the same way it reasons about text, without the architectural separation of models that received vision as an add-on.

Both were trained on data covering 200 languages, with in-depth support for 12 of them, including Arabic, Spanish, German, and Hindi. The training corpus totals 40 trillion tokens.

## The 10 million token window

Scout's 10 million token context was the largest among open models at release. To put it in perspective: 10 million tokens are approximately 7.5 million words — the equivalent of several complete books, or an entire codebase of a medium-sized project.

In practice, this opens up use cases that were previously exclusive to proprietary APIs with premium pricing: analysis of complete documentation, ingestion of large codebases, reasoning over extensive datasets in a single call.

## Licensing: the point to watch

Llama 4 uses the Meta Llama license, which allows commercial use for most companies. But there are two important restrictions that differ from truly open licenses like MIT.

Companies with more than 700 million monthly active users need a special license from Meta. And, at the time of release, users and companies domiciled in the European Union were prohibited from using or distributing the models — a restriction with significant practical implications for global operations.

This places Llama 4 in a different category from DeepSeek V4 (MIT) and Gemma 4 (Apache 2.0) in terms of unrestricted freedom of use. For most companies, it is not a problem. For platform-scale operations or those with significant European presence, it requires legal analysis.

## Meta's strategic positioning

Meta does not release open models out of altruism. The strategy is consistent: by establishing Llama as the foundation of the open source ecosystem, Meta ensures that its hardware (MTIA), its AI products (Meta AI), and its infrastructure (PyTorch) remain central to global AI development.

Llama 4 Scout running on an H100, with 10M context and native multimodality, is the most convincing version of that argument Meta has ever made. The model is not just good enough for production use — for many use cases, it is the best available.

body.title: The Wounds We Carry, The Pains We Hide
body.body:
What happens when the person who gave you life becomes the source of your deepest pain? A raw, honest reflection on maternal betrayal, broken family bonds, and healing from the wounds we hide from the world.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdCzoDumG53DSG5QdP6h1pLtjwrRtxn7SX8HhhSs6aMhh/1781576818688.png)
_[Image Source: AI Generated via Google Assistant]_


Betrayal hurts. Family betrayal hits hard, but a mother's betrayal hits entirely differently.

Who would have thought that someone who gave you life and nurtured you could also be the one to hurt you so deeply?

Oh yes, we all know that no one is perfect. But some actions are simply not expected from certain people, no matter how imperfect they claim to be. Mothers are supposed to be a haven. A mother is like a fortress, the home we run to when we are in danger outside.

Now tell me: where do we go when our protector is the ultimate cause of our pain and tears?

The older we get, the more life teaches us its lessons through pain, deep wounds, and betrayal.

I used to wonder why some people lose all connection with their siblings and parents as they grow up. Over the years, I have finally come to understand. So much happens behind closed doors until eventually, the bond is completely broken.

Honestly, the life we live is exactly like the earth: whatever crop you sow is exactly what you will reap.

So tell me;
Have you ever been betrayed by someone who was supposed to protect you? How did you handle the pain?

I would love to read your stories and thoughts in the comments below. Let us unburden together.


#creativewriting #thought #proofofbrain #alive #neoxian

The Greece angle is a good reminder that market leadership often comes from balance-sheet repair before people notice the narrative change.

When a country moves from crisis case to preferred allocation, the stock market usually re-rates before the broader public mood catches up. Corporate profits matter, but so does the signal that institutions are willing to treat the market as investable again.

The risk is that political symbolism can run ahead of structural improvement. I would watch whether foreign inflows keep coming after the headline effect fades.

body.title: Bitcoin Bounced. The Difficulty Drop Says Something More Important.
body.body:
Bitcoin bounced, but the miner signal is more interesting.

That is where I keep landing.

The price move got most of the attention because it is easy to understand. Bitcoin slipped toward the low $60K area, then recovered into the mid-$60K range as geopolitical pressure cooled a bit and risk appetite came back. Crypto stocks moved with it. The usual names reacted. Strategy bought more BTC. Traders started arguing about whether the bottom was in.

Fine.

But underneath that price move, the network just gave a cleaner signal.

Bitcoin mining difficulty dropped by a little over 10% in the latest adjustment. That is not a normal small retarget. It is one of the larger downward moves of this cycle, and it tells a different story from the spot chart.

Price can move because of headlines. Difficulty moves because miners actually changed behavior.

That distinction matters.

When difficulty falls that hard, it usually means enough hash power left the network during the prior period that blocks were coming in slower than expected. The protocol adjusts. The remaining miners suddenly get some relief because the same machines now compete against a lower difficulty target.

That does not automatically mean Bitcoin is bullish.

It does mean the stress reached the production layer.

And that is worth paying attention to.

The simple version is this: weaker miners got squeezed, some machines likely went offline, and the network recalibrated around the miners that stayed.

Which, honestly, is the part that interests me most.

Markets talk about miner capitulation like it is a dramatic one-day event. In reality it is often slower. Margins compress. Financing gets expensive. Energy contracts matter more. Older rigs become uneconomic. Public miners try to preserve balance sheets. Private miners disappear quietly.

Then difficulty adjusts and the survivors get a better setup.

That is the part people miss. A difficulty drop is both a sign of pain and a release valve.

If price keeps falling after the adjustment, the relief does not last. More miners get pushed toward the edge. But if price stabilizes while difficulty is lower, the remaining miners get a window where economics improve without needing a major rally.

I do not have a strong take yet on whether this was the final washout. I doubt anyone really does.

What I can say is that the miner layer is no longer confirming the clean institutional-demand story.

Earlier this year, the easy narrative was simple: ETFs absorb supply, institutions buy dips, Bitcoin grinds higher. That story still has pieces that are true. The ETF wrapper changed access. Corporate balance sheets still matter. Strategy buying another batch of BTC is not meaningless.

But mining difficulty cutting sharply tells us the market is also forcing real operators to make hard decisions.

That is a different signal than a fund flow chart.

ETF flows show allocation behavior. Difficulty shows production pressure.

Both matter, but they do not always point in the same direction.

The next thing I am watching is not just whether BTC stays above $65K. That level matters because traders are watching it, but I care more about whether hashrate recovers quickly after the adjustment.

Fast recovery would suggest miners were waiting for the reset. Machines come back online, margins improve, and the network absorbs the shock.

Slow recovery would say something else. It would suggest balance sheets are still tight, energy economics are still ugly, or some operators are not ready to come back even after the protocol made mining easier.

That would be more concerning.

There is also a second layer here: public miner stocks.

They often trade like leveraged Bitcoin proxies, but they are not just Bitcoin proxies. They are businesses with debt, power costs, machine depreciation, treasury decisions, and dilution risk. When difficulty drops, the better-positioned miners can benefit. The weaker ones may only get a temporary reprieve.

That gap is where the market usually starts separating names.

Maybe I am overthinking it, but the miner signal feels more honest than the price bounce.

A headline can move Bitcoin for a day.

A difficulty adjustment tells you the network had to adapt.

That is the part I am tracking now.

I rigged the brazier to explode if any guard tries to light it later. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcR4nDBZXGowcr8AG12LYHBJ3TkJHUvVRWVaSvTN77V7K/screenshot_15_.jpg) Now that I was done setting trap on the brazier, I jumped off the tower to get to the treasure of the location. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme5dqZZk7vMuVcKHUXgUNcUBytjZL28io1E4QSPTCdvvA/screenshot_16_.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWSnhU6yci3CpRy2GhnF5qVAjZZJ91HE5BWVHws2X2k3n/screenshot_17_.jpg) Yeah, I found the treasure inside a tent.
