body.title: Simple relax in the downtown with my wife.
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWPmXrGtEt5cAjeNwL78nKTT7jto37ivbxa8Vgs4ounmZ/1781598500673.jpg)

Hello everyone. How are you today? I hope all is well with you and your family. This week is another week where my wife and I have free time, maintenance for the longan trees is not required this week as the fruit has reached approximately 1 cm in diameter. We're off to relax in the downtown again. In the morning, we and the kids have milk and bread for breakfast. After breakfast we took our granddaughter and autistic son to school. Then we left for the downtown area straight away. This morning, the atmosphere along the main road (Highway 107) is cloudy with gentle sunlight.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTHWUbcF9bqvi1U3oGWw3R4gAQq4UaUaVs4Vqg1mxbV7S/1781595194130.jpg)

We walked around downtown for almost an hour, then stopped at a shop that sold everything for a single price (20 Thai baht). I want several large plastic pots to plant water convolvulus. I've tried growing Chinese morning glory in a 12-inch plastic pot, and it was absolutely fantastic. Therefore, I want to plant more of them in plastic pots. This shop has plastic pots in many sizes and styles. Even though it's the rainy season, the weather is quite hot right now, and some days are very hot in the afternoons, Besides plastic pots, so we want tank tops for our autistic son. And we buy some miscellaneous items too.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYtdNWzpUcgEYouBpZPVPWUDGVPqihadtrf3M8W8GFbQP/1781595194451.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTJcetD3VGzeptpYzy2qB2i9qKkwywATGKdNXQJdpqh2g/1781595194354.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWyGzfgrZCGfWZG7ruN4WFpqxS15txyufd7rnFDys6Wvc/1781595194240.jpg)

After that, we stopped for ice cream at Dairy Queen, but they were free ice cream cones that we redeemed with my credit card points. We could sit and eat ice cream cones in the food court at Lotus and relax until almost noon.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXoGdBiPbWSUFsdUH1VCAMdoBaMLXQhwDyYD2gQ6NCXqL/1781595194543.jpg)

Our lunch today was crispy fried mussels pancake at a restaurant near Lotus.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme4wbgErQ2Enk9DWRKYwdfKDo8iyFR13ZDTiphFKXudXg/1781597713169.jpg)

After lunch, around 1 p.m. we walked around the wet market in downtown. Besides walking around, we also bought snacks in the afternoon and eggs here.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdC41j4QTcpa2vN1FvHCVCakWRiMV9VeLDBPC78KLpScK/1781597713530.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRG1NoiEbWY515UjqAzJoP6hxktPScnQy5aNGdnGEwgv6/1781597713389.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcqWbtH5HDVzuLC2TrLT6RWfDcfbMnWyZHLtdhBLKyo2q/1781597713257.jpg)

Finally, we picked up our autistic son from school and go home. These are the stories and photos I want to share for this post. Invite everyone to see and enjoy my stories and photos. Please forgive any errors/mistakes. Have a great day. See you next time. Thank you for your support and visiting my post. Bye 🤗

📷 Take photo By Smartphone Vivo V30.

body.title: 16 June 2026, Freewriters Community Daily Writing Prompt Day 3136: unnatural cruelty
body.body:
Unnatural cruelty No one deserves to be confined. Birds are social and emotional beings. Clipping their wings and locking them in a cage is unnatural cruelty. They were born to be free, to fly, to experience, and to explore. If they come to our homes, it will be in search of water or food, not captivity. They don't deserve to be living decorations in any space. Their wings are not ornaments; they are very important in the ecosystem. They disperse seeds, control insects, and adorn and brighten forests and jungles with their songs and flights. Unnatural cruelty isn't just a visible blow or wound; it's also a beautiful cage, entertainment. Birds were born to be free, not to justify our cruelty or satisfy our ego's whims. Be kind to birds. Never buy them, don't trap them, don't separate them from their community or their habitat. Don't be part of unnatural cruelty. >Crueldad antinatural Nadie merece permanecer en una jaula, las aves son seres vivos sociales y emocionales, cortarle sus alas y encerrarlas es una jaula es crueldad antinatural, nacieron para ser libres, volar, experimentar y explorar, si llegan a nuestro hogar será buscando agua o alimento no buscando cautiverio no merecen ser parte de decoración viviente de ningún espacio, sus alas no son adornos, ellos son muy importantes en el ecosistema, esparcen semillas, controlan a los insectos, adornan y alegran bosques y selvas con cantos y vuelos, crueldad antinatural no es solo golpe o herida que se ve, también es una bella jaula, entretenimiento, las aves nacieron para ser libres no para justificar nuestra crueldad o satisfacer nuestro ego capricho. Sé amable con las aves, nunca las compres, no las atrapes, no la separes de su comunidad ni de su habitat, no seas parte de una crueldad antinatural. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSgayx3fhvBMLnr561vqxwrUusQvx2jwRYXApyEj9nJRj/1781608293135.jpg) This writing belongs to my participation in the daily writing challenge of the #freewriters community, created by @mariannewest. >Este escrito pertenece a mi participación en el reto diario de escritura de la comunidad #freewriters, creado por @mariannewest.

body.title: Opening with a funny scene...
body.body:
...a live joke mind you, as a bit of confusion was at play. 
![141.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23xp8drLTdt6EaiBcPGBfVv1S6Zjg3pbddWCqupcixcCcyL9ycgxe5MVAbDqXhMcGfTE8.jpg)

*Hello*, she said, *who are you?* *is this your car as it is not parked very well.*

Alcohol can have a different effect on people, and I think that it's the same in nature's wildlife. Especially the little ones, and I will show you the effect that it had on this little bird. All in a joke of course, as I don't want to antagonize some nature lovers.

You will see that I also have some other interesting views in here, and I am sure that you will want more information on them. So, I have a full description of the flowers, as well as the ingenious timing of a bird to know when to start mating and nesting.   

*You can't hide in the mirror,* she said, *as I see you, and I will tell my husband, as he is a traffic officer.*
![142.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23w2ighY5rMWVBnJvJfdTpjfyEL5JBtSGoMz5mBGSfSQuAW19aWmkhCauVof1srVxaa6N.JPG)

*Denise*, the husband shouted, *I told you not to take so many sips from that glass of left over wine.* :)
![148.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23tH8BqUnnUoJh6TcUgcAJHEa8fAvEWqj6tGvAtUysRmZiejajrfFtASzucr4USGR9XhF.JPG)

Right, now let's get serious.

I have been keeping an eye on the Protea flowers, as my hope was to get one of the little sunbirds to come and sit on them. The birds check the progress of the proteas in order to see when they start to produce nectar. So, imagine my happiness when I suddenly saw a big sunbird coming in to test the flowers. 

![107.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EqBdCMJrSVRejn9CiZRUumcrdVwnDqZ2jX1u7fwsAd8f1rrha5mn5yS46XKGDmBr8gP.JPG)

Not any sunbird, but a male Malachite Sunbird (Nectarinia famosa) landed, and although it took a bit of time for him to arrive, I was ready to get him on camera. You will also see him testing a protea flower, and once he was satisfied, then he departed.

![134.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/48K7gFDFLoN7X8vnJcNPA5G4u8zdgSmBQD9TtHb3QKj2k89gaZcAnxXX6mw73uNfCQ.JPG)

![136.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EoGxN7xPSsbsXbzX7LXWm3JzAqSqrX3CQmRop7BxwpkdL1C3VjZoy9KLy6GKPrmZHcc.JPG)

![137.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23uFRhVZHN19ZF7Nrm6wKRkek6WvQvocbBSKsT865u8cvyDx9dXZDe4fv1mq6vMJfczLR.JPG)

The different protea pincushion flower buds.

The protea flowers are native to South Africa, and especially to the Western Cape Province. There are several protea flower species, and in here I will concentrate on the Leucospermum Pincushion of the Protea family. The first flower below is the red pincushion flowers. 

![121.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23tvW9UNLeowJKwG7VBw85aPRxvdy9qK1TjZQVJwvAjeUKxPw4KfHiPMa8z6wksghtWx2.JPG)

The second flower buds below are those of the yellow pincushion flowers. 
![122.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23tbnRvhLwWRmztgFDw6XMm1wekb5H2X5sGypnZHLbjkdwmP777aFR22GXLfRheeFWGQS.JPG)

You can see the bud of a King protea flower (Protea cynaroides).
![123.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/Eo8RP3tBZ3GQAk2Ghh2wtZgRynnPgwQxvxTQtDX8y8Sg9oQM36eR1V4A78E7kZDGd2Q.JPG)

Here is a final look of the King protea in progress. 
![126.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EoAZmgzzSJUDnDegg42QGovtuKcUMMJKdAXsuKECdKtzmtda9Wsj81zjtTy3QzN3Pzu.JPG)

So, there you have it, three different subjects to see in this post, and you can tell that I like variety. I also like to make the posts as detailed as possible in order for anyone that is interested to do their own research on it. We don't have very much to laugh about these days, but a smile costs nothing and a friendly smile can save someone's life. 

I can also tell you that the birds love these flowers and I have taken many species sitting on the proteas and the pincushions to post over time. I am hoping for a bumper season during this winter spell, as I would love to show you some of the other beautiful bird species that visit the flowers. Even if I can't, then I will just carry on trying. 
Such is life. 

I hope you enjoyed the pictures and the story. 

Photos by Zac Smith. All-Rights-Reserved. 

Camera: Canon PowershotSX70HS Bridge camera. 

Until next time, cheers!

body.title: “We don't need words” - hear yourself
body.body: She was raised in a family where she was the only one who could hear the world around her. As a result, she had to take on a lot of responsibility from a young age, being the only link between her family and the outside world. But then something unexpected happened - she discovered she had a talent for singing. This newfound passion gave her a dream to hold onto, something that was all her own. Now, she's faced
alt=\

/>

with a tough decision: should she put her family's needs first, or should she follow her own path and finally find her own voice? It's a choice between duty and desire, between doing what's expected of her and doing what makes her happy. She's always put others first, but now she's wondering what it would be like to hear her own voice, to make her own choices, and to go her own way.  
“Feel My Voice” is an Italian version of a well-known story, full of special sunny sincerity and expression. Unlike the lyrical French original “The Belle Family” or the acutely social American remake “CODA”, which won an Oscar, the Italian film emphasizes family relationships.  
This story is a beautiful and emotional journey, set against the vibrant backdrop of Italy. The country's lively and loving atmosphere breathes new life into a familiar tale, turning it into a powerful therapy for the soul. Unlike previous versions, which focused on tenderness or survival, this one is about finding the courage to be happy and the incredible power of music to break through even the most overwhelming silence. It's a story that will touch your heart and remind you of the importance of embracing joy and letting music be the soundtrack to your life. With its rich and emotional storytelling, this tale has the power to transform and uplift, making it a truly unforgettable experience.

  
#cine #cinema #film #moovie

body.title: Learn Creative Coding (#96) - Image Classification for Art
body.body:
# Learn Creative Coding (#96) - Image Classification for Art

![cc-banner](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcX6yi9Uoqxh5UyHPgVosRfwKDaeR2JFKby1JqADcAjbD/cc-banner-amber.png)

Four episodes ago we loaded our first ML model -- MobileNet image classification through ml5.js. Feed a video frame, get back a label and a confidence score. \

Simple, useful, and we moved on quickly to body tracking, hand tracking, and face mesh because those models gave us spatial data -- keypoints we could map to particles, trails, colors, meshes. Classification seemed flat by comparison. One label per frame. Where's the creative depth in that?\n\nTurns out: a lot deeper than it looks. We barely scratched MobileNet in episode 92. We used it as a label printer -- show an object, read the label, move on. But a classification model doesn't just output a label. It outputs 1000 confidence scores simultaneously, one for every category it knows. The label is just the highest-scoring one. The full distribution of scores is where the interesting stuff lives. A photo of a coffee mug might score 72% on \

-- the model is simultaneously seeing all three and being most convinced by one. That distribution is data. Rich, continuous, creative data.\n\nThis episode takes image classification seriously as a creative tool. Not just \
but \

and hold a mug in frame. The grid cells covering the mug glow red. Move the mug and the glow follows. The model's confidence is spatially distributed -- it's hottest right at the center of the mug and fades at the edges where the patch only partially contains it.\n\nChange the target to \
and hold up a book. Different region lights up. Change to \
and your hand glows. You're building an attention map -- a visualization of where the model's \

falls for any given category. The scan is too slow for real-time interaction, but as a generative process it produces beautiful, ghostly overlays that reveal how the model parses space.

## The webcam oracle: labels as live text art

The simplest creative use of continuous classification is treating the labels themselves as visual material. The model generates a stream of interpretations -- one per frame, each a word or phrase. That stream of words is itself interesting. Point the camera at your room and the model narrates what it sees in its own limited vocabulary: \
one frame, then \
the next, then \

Each label is technically defensible but collectively they reveal the model groping for the right word.

## Feature extraction: seeing with the model's eyes

Classification is the model's final opinion. But inside the neural network, before it arrives at that opinion, it builds a rich internal representation of the image. These intermediate representations -- called features or activations -- capture visual properties at different scales: edges, textures, shapes, objects. The early layers see low-level stuff (edges, gradients). The later layers see high-level stuff (wheels, faces, fur textures). You can extract these features and use them directly, bypassing the classification entirely.

ml5's `featureExtractor` gives you access to the layer just before classification. The output is a vector of numbers -- typically 1024 values -- that represent the model's \

). Collect 15-20 examples of each by clicking a button while pointing the camera at the right scene. Hit train. Seconds later you have a custom classifier that responds to YOUR specific environment. The creative applications are wide open. Train it on hand gestures unique to your art practice. Train it on different lighting moods in your studio. Train it to distinguish between \

Build a piece where you deliberately show the model objects from different cultural contexts. Track which ones it recognizes confidently and which ones confuse it. The confidence gap between \

**Combine with the previous models.** Nothing stops you from running classification alongside pose detection or hand tracking. Classification picks the visual theme, hand tracking controls particle emission points, face mesh modulates parameters through expressions. Layer the readings for richer interaction.

## 't Komt erop neer...

- MobileNet doesn't just output a single label -- it computes 1000 confidence scores simultaneously. The top label is the most confident category, but the full distribution tells you how the model distributes its \

across all known categories. The gap between the top two scores measures certainty: wide gap = confident, narrow gap = confused. Both the distribution and the gap are mappable creative parameters
- Confidence landscapes: classify patches of the image (sliding a window across the frame) and map the confidence for a specific category to color at each position. The result is a heatmap showing WHERE the model sees a particular thing. Slow but visually fascinating -- the model's spatial attention becomes visible as a ghostly overlay
- The label stream from continuous classification is itself creative material. Treat the model as a narrator that names what it sees. Confident labels appear large, uncertain ones small. Old labels fade, new ones appear. The gap between reality and the model's vocabulary creates accidental poetry
- Feature extraction bypasses classification entirely. MobileNet's internal representation (a 1024-value vector) captures visual properties without committing to a category. Two images with similar feature vectors look alike to the model. Extract, compare with cosine similarity, and you can build visual memory, sort photo collections, or detect when the scene matches a stored reference
- Transfer learning via ml5.featureExtractor lets you train custom categories with 15-20 examples each. The model already knows how to see -- you just teach it your groupings. Train it on your specific environment, gestures, moods, or objects. The categories you choose define the vocabulary of your interactive piece
- Multi-model layering: run classification, pose detection, and hand tracking on the same video feed simultaneously. Each model provides a different reading. Classification picks colors, body pose drives structure, hands emit particles. Three neural lenses on one scene. Performance drops to 5-10 fps but creates a slow, dreamlike aesthetic
- ImageNet's 1000 categories reflect Western consumer culture: 120 dog breeds, very few non-Western objects. The model's vocabulary IS its limitation. Deliberately showing it objects from different cultural contexts and visualizing the confidence gap becomes a commentary on representation in training data
- The object-controlled visual synthesizer maps each recognized category to a unique generative visual: different particle behavior, color, and physics. Confidence modulates intensity. Object switches create smooth visual transitions. The camera becomes a performance instrument -- each object is a note, each transition is part of the composition
- Decoupling classification speed (15-20 fps) from render speed (60fps) is essential. Classification runs in its own async loop, updating shared state. The draw loop reads that state every frame for smooth animation. Don't block rendering on classification callbacks
- Keyword matching for category lookup needs tuning per environment. MobileNet labels are specific (\

) while your visual mode keys are generic. Use substring matching and test with your actual objects to discover what the model calls things\n\nFive episodes into the ML arc. We started with flat labels (episode 92), built up through body skeletons (93), finger joints (94), and full face meshes (95). This episode circled back to classification and found a lot more depth than we originally gave it credit for. The confidence distribution, spatial scanning, feature extraction, custom training, multi-model layering -- classification isn't just \

It's a rich creative signal. And we still haven't gotten to what happens when one neural network transforms images based on the style of another.

Sallukes! Thanks for reading.

--- 原本想拍店门口照片，结果吃饱后就忘了…… **Yakiniku Like**（焼肉ライク）是一家来自日本的连锁烤肉店，最大的特色是“一人烤肉”。每个座位都有自己的小烤炉，一个人也能轻松吃烤肉。 ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lovelemon/23ynhdsJx5VPRkAPveVs21DJCwcT7khNQYxbPGkYzq5FUTvnvBD7uxZ9w1vxFywKtS7RH.jpeg) 店内用餐环境都是一人一个座位，如果跟朋友一起来，中间的隔板是可以拿开的。在上图中，由于我拍到了米特的大头，我嫌他头碍事，我就把整张照片卡通化了。 ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lovelemon/48Sqdy6k3kKszWsAMvezbXJWRS9QPLeZQd7J6YVR2K24GgGEWwvEUXHPZ4itXKKLtB.jpeg) 每个座位有自己的小烤炉，就像上图这样…… ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lovelemon/48Z6tcKvp5CsL3RRtuYhyckAEHJwh3DuKBy22e21AXmYrqrFrWw4pFZHy2ckVpssXJ.jpeg) 之后我们用自己的平板点餐，整个菜单都是牛肉，不吃牛肉的我看得有些崩溃！幸好老板这时出来，我赶紧询问，原来所有套餐都是牛肉，猪肉只能单点，而且只有一个选项，米饭还要另外加。 ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lovelemon/48a4uUkkkkWR6ZzjzxDVBiTg4A2x8tNHsW5YeuCPp6KZQ4Bmx3bznHtJqLra26Jrkw.jpeg) 全日本的餐厅是不是都免费供应白水？这间店也是，店员给了我们杯子，我们自己装水喝。 ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lovelemon/48RPsVsvUc4aGnPZLsmVRfKEmfduoHEvLcsbaijv4QEJjni6HYWWQ1Dm29QMsJk8y2.jpeg) **猪肉片** 我点的，单点猪肉片另外加米饭、汤、泡菜，米特还问我的猪肉片怎么那么少？我也不知道它那么少啊！ ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lovelemon/48K8XxWQX4Eh9Qu1v2pDcC8WAotDHXxWtvchiku8St6YB1m5zPGQrYeBr4dFZJz1SJ.jpeg) 我烤肉技术不好，自己烤出来也焦黑焦黑的…… ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lovelemon/48TKcoZNQLmmZDX47gLjEWgGcBD272mTJdYNq1mBMwZfg3Z8Et9zZtPkCUuAePZEoq.jpeg) **牛肉套餐** 米特点的，这一份就不一样了，牛肉片看起来就比我多，然后米饭、汤、泡菜，都是包括在套餐里面的。 米特问我还要不要 add-on 猪肉片？我拒绝了，毕竟我怕烤出来又烤焦。 米特还问我明明不太会烤肉为什么选这种一人烤炉？不然他就可以帮我烤了，像平时那样他烤我吃。我去！说得我那么一无是处，就算我自己烤焦了我也照吃！哼…… **价钱** 共：日元 ￥2450

body.title: Borderline
body.body:
A crazed stalker https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/tKy6P66kjsfs3SmsqxB2jMxLyc6.jpg
[Source ](https://www.themoviedb.org/movie/1013482-borderline/images/backdrops)
Edited in Photoshop & Canva App
https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jcrodriguez/245cUBXzvWF8QVukk8UvqTFX6FutvCzv1TyGDA8ybnR5QKA1v6nMvGS4j6y81Qg9M2HLn.jpg
You know how much I love seeing Samara Weaving covered in blood, running for her life, surviving on the edge, and a few days ago I finally got to see Borderline. I hadn't had time to see Over Your Dead Body or Ready or Not 2: Here I Come, two of her films, but I was really looking forward to them. By the way, there's a movie called Caroline Caroline, which apparently hasn't been released in my area, so I'll have to wait to see another Samara Weaving film. This time, Borderline is quite a strange movie. It's a mix of genres that sometimes left me a little disoriented, especially at the beginning. As the movie progressed, I started to understand the story and appreciate the humor, and that's how I ended up enjoying it. A lot of crazy things happen in this story, some funnier than others, but the ones I enjoyed the most were some of the gory scenes. The story takes place in the 90s and revolves around Paul, a completely unhinged man, and his obsession with a pop star named Sofia Minor. She's a famous star, and he's a complete loser. His fixation on her, whom he wants to marry, leads him to commit a series of hilarious and somewhat bloody acts. He won't be alone; he'll be accompanied by a couple of lunatics like himself. Calhoun, his friend, is very strong, not very bright, and has terrible aim. And then there's Penny, a character I loved because she stars in a couple of grotesque and quite disturbing gore scenes. Penny is played by the actress Alba Baptista. I didn't know who she was, so I looked her up and discovered she's a Portuguese actress. I think she has potential in the horror genre. She has a small role in the film *Mother Mary*, so I hope she gets more work in Hollywood. The other actor with significant screen time, playing the deranged stalker, is Ray Nicholson, Jack Nicholson's son. He follows in his father's footsteps, bearing a striking resemblance to the teenager with the same unsettling smile. These unhinged roles suit him perfectly. It's a very theatrical character, full of humor and madness, and the actor shines in his role. He and the Portuguese woman are the funniest characters in the film. Of course, Samara Weaving does what she does best: run, fight, kill, jump, and end up covered in blood, though not quite as much as in some of her other films. While the story isn't entirely well-developed and there are details that betray its low budget, it's still entertaining. It's not a film to analyze in depth; just watch it to pass the time. The cast is what makes it work. Look for it on your streaming platform and tell me what you think. ---- > Ya saben cuánto me encanta ver a Samara Weaving cubierta de sangre, corriendo por su vida, sobreviviendo al límite, y hace unos días por fin pude ver Borderline. No había tenido tiempo de ver Over Your Dead Body ni Ready or Not 2: Here I Come, dos de sus películas, pero tenía muchas ganas de verlas. Por cierto, hay una película llamada Caroline Caroline, que al parecer no se ha estrenado en mi zona, así que tendré que esperar para ver otra película de Samara Weaving. > Esta vez, Borderline es una película bastante extraña. Es una mezcla de géneros que a veces me dejó un poco desorientada, sobre todo al principio. A medida que avanzaba la película, empecé a entender la historia y a aceptar el humor, y así fue como terminé disfrutándola. Pasan muchas cosas locas en esta historia, algunas más graciosas que otras, pero las que más disfruté fueron algunas de las escenas gore. > La historia se desarrolla en los años 90 y gira en torno a Paul, un hombre completamente desequilibrado, y su obsesión con una estrella del pop llamada Sofia Minor. Ella es una estrella famosa, y él un completo perdedor. Su fijación con ella, con quien quiere casarse, lo lleva a cometer una serie de actos hilarantes y algo sangrientos. > No estará solo; lo acompañarán un par de locos como él. Calhoun, su amigo, es muy fuerte, tiene poca inteligencia y una puntería pésima. Y también está Penny, un personaje que me encantó porque protagoniza un par de escenas de gore grotescas y bastante perturbadoras. Penny es interpretada por la actriz Alba Baptista. No sabía quién era, así que la busqué y descubrí que es una actriz portuguesa. Creo que tiene potencial en el género de terror. Tiene un pequeño papel en la película *Mother Mary*, así que espero que consiga más trabajo en Hollywood. > El otro actor con mucho tiempo en pantalla, interpretando al acosador desquiciado, es Ray Nicholson, hijo de Jack Nicholson. Sigue los pasos de su padre, con un parecido asombroso al adolescente de la misma sonrisa perturbadora. Estos papeles desquiciados le sientan de maravilla. Es un personaje muy teatral, lleno de humor y locura, y el actor brilla en su papel. Él y la mujer portuguesa son los personajes más divertidos de la película. > Por supuesto, Samara Weaving hace lo que mejor sabe hacer: correr, pelear, matar, saltar y acabar cubierta de sangre, aunque no tanto como en otras de sus películas. Si bien la historia no está del todo bien desarrollada y hay detalles que evidencian su bajo presupuesto, sigue siendo entretenida. > No es una película para analizar en profundidad; simplemente mírala para pasar el rato. El reparto es lo que hace que funcione. Búscala en tu plataforma de streaming y dime qué te parece.

body.title: Film Review: Skyfall (2012)
body.body:
![(source: tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/yMqggZoWEZ9zXBXiWpPWB2r69xr.jpg)



James Bond has survived a great deal over half a century on the silver screen. He has outlasted his creator Ian Fleming, weathered the departure of Sean Connery (the first and, for many, the only true cinematic Bond), and emerged unscathed from ill-advised casting experiments and the end of the Cold War, which rather robbed fictional characters of his ilk of their primary purpose. He even survived the appointment of Daniel Craig, a choice that initially had diehard fans clutching their pearls. Given this track record, one might reasonably expect the longest-running film franchise in history to endure the particular trials presented by *Skyfall*—and endure it does, though not without showing some rather telling signs of strain.

That survival remains very much the operative word is established by the traditionally spectacular pre-credits sequence, which concludes in a manner that would spell the end for any ordinary protagonist. For this secret agent, however—one who is beginning to show his years—it merely provides an opportunity for an extended disappearance. Bond retreats into the shadows, only resurfacing after a terrorist bombing of MI6 headquarters in London. With his colleagues dead or wounded, and the intelligence service under threat, the presumed-dead 007 returns to active duty, submitting himself to a series of humiliating physical and psychological assessments before tracking the perpetrator to Shanghai. There he encounters Sévérine (Bérénice Marlohe), an exotic beauty connected to Silva (Javier Bardem), a former British agent turned cyber-terrorist with a personal vendetta against M (Judi Dench).

The fundamental challenge facing any new Bond film is the need to satisfy audience expectations regarding the preservation of the formula—spectacular action, exotic locations, beautiful women—whilst simultaneously offering something different. That the makers of *Skyfall* intended to emphasise the latter became clear the moment Sam Mendes was announced as director. A filmmaker whose specialism lies in gloomy dramas about the emptiness of modern bourgeois existence, Mendes appeared an odd fit for the franchise. It became apparent that Christopher Nolan's \

reinvention of Batman had served as the primary inspiration; the result is a Bond film that is far removed from escapist adventure and the embodiment of petty-bourgeois ideals. Mendes seems intent on \

the character, presenting him as a frustrated middle-aged man grappling with vulnerabilities and childhood traumas he has never overcome. The theme of mortality is further emphasised by the prominence of M, played by a visibly exhausted Judi Dench, who here becomes the first M in franchise history to utter the word \

This deconstruction extends to the villain. Bardem's Silva is conceived as a curious amalgam of Heath Ledger's Joker, a camp auntie, and an Oedipal homicidal maniac. The film's climax, set in the Scottish Highlands at Bond's ancestral home, feels more appropriate to a minimalist anti-Western than to a modern action blockbuster.

Despite such iconoclastic tendencies, *Skyfall* remains largely entertaining and successful. This is thanks in no small part to Mendes's skilled use of locations, several genuinely impressive action sequences, direct and indirect homages to classic Bond films, and a strong cast. Marlohe stands out as one of the most memorable Bond girls in recent memory—a femme fatale in the truest sense. Roger Deakins's cinematography is frequently stunning, particularly in the Shanghai sequence bathed in neon light.

However, the critical panegyrics that elevated *Skyfall* to the status of greatest Bond film ever made do not withstand scrutiny. The picture is overlong, and due to shifts in location and tone, it occasionally feels as though one is watching two different films—a conventional Bond adventure and a self-consciously \

character study—crudely stitched together. The dialogue, to put it mildly, is unlikely to feature in any Bond anthology. The attempt to give Bond a traumatic backstory and a literal family home (complete with a caretaker played by Albert Finney) borders on the bathetic, undermining the very ambiguity that has allowed the character to endure for fifty years.

Viewed in the context of Daniel Craig's tenure, *Skyfall* represents a partial recovery from the nadir of [*Quantum of Solace*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/film-review-casino-royale-2008) (2008), that rushed, incoherent sequel which suffered from the Writers' Guild strike and misguided directorial choices. Yet it falls well short of the standard established by [*Casino Royale*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/film-review-casino-royale-2006) (2006), which successfully rebooted the franchise by stripping away decades of accumulated excess and returning Bond to something approaching Fleming's original conception. Where *Casino Royale* balanced realism with genuine emotional stakes, *Skyfall* substitutes brooding introspection for character development. The seeds of the franchise's subsequent decline—evident in the disappointing [*Spectre*](https://peakd.com/film/@drax/capsule-film-review-spectre-2015) (2015), where Craig's evident weariness and the cheapening of Bond's relationship with his arch-nemesis Blofeld reached their nadir—were arguably sown here.

For all its pretensions towards seriousness, *Skyfall* ultimately demonstrates that James Bond still has a future, even if this particular iteration suggests a franchise increasingly uncertain of its identity. It is a film that wants to have its cake and eat it—to deconstruct the hero whilst celebrating him; to reject the formula whilst relying upon it. The result is a handsome, occasionally thrilling, but ultimately compromised picture: superior to the immediate predecessor, inferior to the franchise's best, and considerably less revolutionary than its admirers claimed.


RATING: 5/10 (++)


*(Note: The text in the original Croatian version is available [here](https://draxblog.com/2013/04/08/recenzija-skyfall-2012/).)*

body.title: Close, but not quite
body.body:
<center>![IMG_20190331_142046.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23x1FccrnzgX7HksEZFpxmHhR4YAJtm43vRG4VfkSYea8Zz2DeLfn9oXj9iSzUXdEQKgX.jpg)</center>

-----------------------

New Mexico is another one of those states that I have never visited.  I've been to three of the four states it touches, but I have never been to the state itself.  In addition that, I am not sure I can really even include Arizona since I just stepped foot in it briefly after we crossed over the Hoover Dam.  It was probably Colorado that brought me the closest to New Mexico, but even then, we were way up in Denver, so I still wasn't really that close.

I'm thinking about changing all of that this fall as I look into taking a trip out west.  I'm not sure if it is really going to happen, but it's one of the things floating out there between @mrsbozz and myself.  It would be to celebrate my 50th birthday, even though it would be about six months past the date.  Unfortunately, our summer was already pretty booked by the time we started talking about going on a trip.


<center>![IMG_20190331_142911.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23xKzVgrQbCmds3B39HxXAa4hSNe8HN8iNE6gyiTF41aSocyYbhycRxN3Mm27dHZg4RqA.jpg)</center>

-----------------------------

If Valley of Fire in Nevada is any indication of what I might expect to see in New Mexico, then I am all in for sure.  Even if it isn't the sort of stuff I might see, I still want to take the chance to visit the 47th state.  In case you haven't guessed, we are heading into New Mexico this week for my #threetunetuesday post sponsored by @ablaze.  I was kind of worried going into this week that I wouldn't be able to find material for this post, but it turns out there are a lot more songs with New Mexico in the title or lyrics than I had anticipated.

One of them comes from a very familiar face in my #threetunetuesday posts.  I have a feeling if I broke everything down, by the end of this series he will likely have been featured more than any other artist.  In addition that, I have a bluesy favorite for you as well as another older artist that I have used maybe once or twice in the past.

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=26hGqZE17rc&list=RD26hGqZE17rc&start_radio=1)

-------------------------

Let's get started with the artist we all know and love, Billy Joel.   Joel is the artist that I am guessing I have used the most in this whole series.  He has a surprising number of songs where he references states in the union.  It has actually surprised me just how much I have used his songs in this series.  There was a song by Bruce Springsteen too, but I didn't want this week to look too much like last week.

Especially given the fact that next week is New York I think, and you better believe I'll be sharing another Billy Joel song for that.  \

is one of his lesser known songs that I am not super familiar with.  It has a killer intro though and then runs into a pretty amazing verse and chorus combination.  I'd be struggling to say anything bad about any Billy Joel song to be honest.  He's a national treasure if there ever was one.  \n\n<center><iframe width=\

-------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vKFmS8o871E&list=RDvKFmS8o871E&start_radio=1)

-------------------------

The easy way out this week would have just been to share three different versions of \

for you.  It's probably the most well known song that mentions New Mexico and about a million different artists have covered it.  I could have called it three hundred tune tuesday and you likely wouldn't have heard a single repeat.  Instead, I decided to exclude that song from this post and pick a couple more obscure songs.  \n\nPaul Simon is another one of my favorite artists from back in the day.  He was always able to put together some really poignant and witty songs.  They kind of touch you in your soul and they have a way of kind of haunting you.  \
is one of my favorites, but this week I am sharing with you \

.  It's a really mellow tune with some pretty amazing guitar work.  The reference to New Mexico comes right at the beginning and then it moves into a really moody tune.

It's a really good song.

--------------------------------

Apparently, there is a Johnny Cash song called \
, but I can't say as though I have ever heard it and that seemed a bit on the nose, so instead, I am going to share the song \

for you by Chris Stapleton.  I've had the chance to see Stapleton once or twice in concert and I have to say, he puts on a heck of a show.  It's not one of those shows where it has a ton of production value and the pyrotechnics blow you away.  Instead, it's more of a show where the guy just gets up there and melts your face off with his singing and guitar playing. 

You tend to get that a bit more with country singers than you do with other artists.  

Once again, the reference to New Mexico comes right at the beginning of this song.  It's pretty clear and it sets the tone for the rest of the song.  If you ever get the chance to see Stapleton in concert, I highly recommend it.  Even if you aren't a country fan, you will likely dig his gritty bluesy sound.  Some might even argue he isn't really a country singer.  

You be the judge...

<div class=text-justify>

>

**<center>ESPAÑOL</center>**
 
Bendiciones abundantes y eternas para todos los miembros de esta comunidad de @worldmappin. Es un placer saludarlos y desearles un día feliz y lleno de bendiciones. Que Dios los colme de bendiciones.

Hoy les comparto mi visita a la rotonda José Martí. Ubicada en la Avenida Gran Mariscal, muy cerca del banco Fondo Común, esta rotonda es relativamente nueva. Anteriormente conocida como la rotonda Fondo Común, ahora cuenta con una escultura de José Martí, líder cubano. Su diseño minimalista y atractivo facilita el acceso. Hay cuatro pasarelas, cada una con el nombre de la plaza. Más allá de estas, se encuentran bancos en forma de media luna, y junto a ellos, jardineras triangulares redondeadas separadas por un muro azul. El piso de granito está decorado con estrellas.

Debajo de los bancos, luces LED añaden hermosos destellos a la plaza por la noche. En el centro se encuentran el pedestal, la escultura y cuatro banderas: la de Venezuela, la de Cuba, la del estado de Sucre y la del municipio de Sucre. El pedestal es muy diferente a los que solemos ver en las plazas, ya que está formado por dos columnas abiertas en el centro, y debajo se encuentra la inscripción de la placa. Desde este punto, se puede ver parte de la Avenida Gran Mariscal hacia el sector Caigüire, la oficina del Banco Fondo Común, y en la placa se lee lo siguiente: \
. También fue poeta, pensador y visionario de América.

>

**<center>ENGLISH</center>**
 
Abundant and everlasting blessings to all members of the @worldmappin community. It is a pleasure to greet you and wish you a happy and blessed day. May God shower you with blessings.

Today I'm sharing my visit to the José Martí roundabout. Located on Gran Mariscal Avenue, very close to the Fondo Común bank, this roundabout is relatively new. Previously known as the Fondo Común roundabout, it now features a sculpture of José Martí, a Cuban leader. Its minimalist and attractive design is easy to access. There are four walkways, each displaying the name of the plaza. Beyond these are crescent-shaped benches, and next to them are rounded, triangular planters separated by a blue wall. The granite floor is decorated with various stars.

Beneath the benches are LED lights that add beautiful sparkles to this plaza at night. In the center are the pedestal, the sculpture, and four flags: the Venezuelan flag, the Cuban flag, the flag of the state of Sucre, and the flag of the Sucre municipality. The pedestal is very different from what we see in plazas, as it is formed by two columns, open in the center, and below it is the inscription of the plaque. From this point, one can see part of Gran Mariscal Avenue towards the Caigüire sector, the Banco Fondo Común office, and we read the following on the plaque: \

He was also a poet, thinker, and visionary of America. ![RJM (5).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EokdaUJCU11kV7ssoertfEDX7DFfLFZuA5KfAEbGBEbgD65dYTXSmDPyBFpRLsS36WH.jpeg) ![RJM (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/Eos2oP1rwWv21kp4ACYJVGWiWqTWJNThLttReYMY7wKzzSF2LjATx6QvcaY7Ljgsmk7.jpeg) ![RJM (4).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/Eo6MpkTTr5THK2tbqeTBmYKuvJqmHnd8PokGm6m9bydZ5K6Zuq9yeuSrMMFbCpoE7iF.jpeg) ![RJM (15).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EpQvE5pAqbqyZpkrt92Yt5u86Nt43V6EoWbvW1wQDNxsnRyVzX9TM3JNzZfvwjztYAy.jpeg) ![RJM (19).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EowEdf3kUAKt78Xtv5gRnTsSeBXYEh58ETJQHhQJAubZDVMpDpXLkMYNtdDGXZcTGSn.jpeg) ![RJM (21).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/23w2oLYCupSYpuZgS6C9AaKGxBSnR3T3FEfHTN3jLwM88yq3zmwCAyYT4E68As6Ww5pZh.jpeg) ![RJM (22).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EoErXscGi6zeK5K3WyuL9snSmvG4uZf8XySAxXrt4T3Gfqf2nEF282BZN9G82sjnnnB.jpeg) ![separador virgilio 1.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/48fPJW5oSR5NrT5insR3hayLh9ET1ifvCG8zGp4Rfk8EhMtUrcwakXhr5g3cRk6Y8x.gif)

> Siguiendo el recorrido, se aprecia la escultura, el pedestal formado por tres columnas, una plaza detrás donde se alza la estatua y una vista de los jardines. Estos están repletos de plantas ornamentales, entre las que destacan las de hojas moradas. Otra vista muestra parte de los jardines, el edificio del banco y la colección de plantas que adornan esta rotonda. A continuación, se ven más de cerca las banderas, la avenida que conduce a la zona, el monumento y los muros de la estructura donde se encuentra la escultura, que son grises en los laterales y blancos en la parte frontal y posterior. Esta estructura, a su vez, tiene una base cuadrada; luego, a través de la otra entrada, se encuentra la identificación del Gobierno del Estado Sucre y una vista completa de la sede del Banco Fondo Común, un banco con su respectiva luz LED en la parte inferior, una vista de la panadería y la rotonda hacia la Avenida Gran Mariscal, seguida de una vista completa de la rotonda, las palmeras y los postes ubicados en los bordes. Esta plaza recibe mantenimiento regular por parte de la Fundación Sucre Te Quiero. Tiene cuatro entradas, y cada una está identificada con el Gobierno del Estado Sucre, la Fundación Sucre Te Quiero y el nombre de la rotonda, José Martí.

> Continuing along the route, we have a view of the sculpture, the pedestal formed by three columns, a square at the back where the statue stands, and a view of the gardens. The gardens are filled with ornamental plants, the most striking of which are those with purple leaves. Another view shows part of the gardens, the bank building, and the collection of plants that decorate this roundabout. Then we see the flags closer, the avenue leading to the area, the monument, and the walls of the structure where the sculpture rests, which are gray on the sides and white on the front and back. This in turn has a square base; then, through the other entrance, we have the identification of the Sucre State Government and a full view of the headquarters of the Banco Fondo Común, a bank and its respective LED light at the bottom, a view of the bakery and the roundabout towards Gran Mariscal Avenue, followed by a full view of the roundabout, the palm trees, and the posts located on the edges. This plaza receives regular maintenance from the Sucre Te Quiero Foundation group. It has four entrances, and each one is identified with the Sucre State Government, the Sucre Te Quiero Foundation, and the name of the roundabout, José Martí. ![RJM (2).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EpT3Jq36GW9p7et385CEWeLcSuvsdD9qaZ7d6h1sPvFrzb7PwzGGxzEwxCyxAxJbo6W.jpeg) ![RJM (3).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/Ep3gfG55cJNRa4yYFLwdriSykajuc8ZWjJVoZV1AXK2K49PkJmiGsE2TbrN2EMPg1a5.jpeg) ![RJM (6).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EpNnrkvzqyQns1NuYrPNyKTKDbqZndcLw8LrvZD8eAGYtFACbEHzgCekT7jHkZUTZZb.jpeg) ![RJM (7).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/241tUuAMe2CYSrhCnc1SxuLML7Kf2km9vU62yFT9qV3nxjKcAFg22dMdHdi35nRVPxW67.jpeg) ![RJM (8).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EpC9U4AfMqH9nXaQHtHQ1fozW6YxQ5QkN8w6ZXUNEnRPRck5UZbHUSoRJZwAZdMEX9M.jpeg) ![RJM (9).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EpA3Z2GMrPYnAHVbmy7FaS8CifiYjdueQV76xejkkGgH8CDZtutHn9HScuCXkX9pycH.jpeg) ![RJM (10).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/Eq357Xt9GcyMx6NJB1BCat38VjfrqweqoCb3b45KoXdhTtJ4q57Z3MQEJ4wKcCoLkys.jpeg) ![RJM (11).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EpA2aFVst2Cj97teGUEB3vXwLeumD3JmDteajo4Gweh4uJ4BdrPKKCgzDaPVwFirfe7.jpeg) ![separador virgilio 1.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/48fPJW5oSR5NrT5insR3hayLh9ET1ifvCG8zGp4Rfk8EhMtUrcwakXhr5g3cRk6Y8x.gif)

>


En la siguiente imagen, vemos la frase \

en un cuadrado azul, similar al que vimos anteriormente. Se aprecia una vista lateral del hospital, los jardines, la escultura central y los bancos de concreto. El día de mi visita, estaban realizando trabajos de mantenimiento en el jardín: riego y limpieza.\n\nSegún los encargados del mantenimiento, la plaza se inauguró este año, aunque su espacio pertenecía anteriormente a otra rotonda. Ahora se llama Rotonda José Martí. En otra vista, se observa la frase \

y el pavimento que conforma la plaza. A continuación, una vista lateral de la escultura, los bancos y las banderas. Finalmente, una vista de los jardines traseros, los bancos y otra de las estrellas que adornan el pavimento. Hay varias estrellas blancas ubicadas a lo largo de los senderos. He pasado por esta avenida varias veces, pero esta es la primera vez que me detengo a explorar esta plaza, conocerla y observar sus curiosos bancos. Gracias por acompañarme en esta fascinante aventura explorando la Plaza José Martí.
>\n\nIn the next entry, we see the phrase \

in a blue square, similar to the one we saw previously. We have a side view of the hospital, the gardens, the sculpture in the center, and the concrete benches. On the day of my visit, they were doing maintenance work on the garden: watering and cleaning.\n\nAccording to the people in charge of maintenance, the plaza was inaugurated this year, although its space previously belonged to another roundabout. It now bears the name of the José Martí Roundabout. In another view, we see the phrase \

and the paving that makes up this plaza. Then, a side view of the sculpture, the benches, and the flags. Finally, a view of the back gardens, the benches, and another of the stars that adorn the paving. There are several stars located along the walkways, and they are white. I have passed by this avenue several times, but this is the first time I have stopped to explore this plaza, get to know it, and observe its curious benches. Thank you for joining me on this fascinating adventure exploring the José Martí Plaza. ![RJM (12).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EonkbViGo8ck6iWVEVWF9RoZRb5B5FejnN4rzgqyWqopBtJEqwZsVrv5Xwzh352MgRW.jpeg) ![RJM (13).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EpnCo25NoY3RmSwL3h28XbnNWiuq6ZH49bbs6GP5NbaHCQkfm6XZDZcKf8nK1xNgCh1.jpeg) ![RJM (14).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EpGQgA1xsSXsdYaPjGVJF3rc89Wn7dMheyr3HJMRAKeEN1Hx7Zsx7w1XsSkze3DEgvU.jpeg) ![RJM (16).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EoGyMDnpCrWqoeu2XQUEyvsv7LZtBqx5fAG4vGwm85cAQWYkKfQZ48cv7DRzTZ2XYKt.jpeg) ![RJM (17).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EpNpNRx2gQayQNw1VeGNLXLcGHwPUdnprcBwjbDtWyunRmNEN9GKffFk4Zg12XHyuZJ.jpeg) ![RJM (18).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/EogQC7YqWp968oeVKyF8i7XqyVRBmHJkQrCCX2SGpNmz9wSK8CkrX4uYnK6h7sGuFCX.jpeg) ![RJM (20).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/Eo4E3PAC77iydWmJQQ7yzJts4Bn3R8a1dcLWqvpDYNWE12pvHuvNF668UjxpUjgfnF2.jpeg) ![separador virgilio 1.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/virgilio07/48fPJW5oSR5NrT5insR3hayLh9ET1ifvCG8zGp4Rfk8EhMtUrcwakXhr5g3cRk6Y8x.gif) [//]:# (!worldmappin 10.47253 lat -64.16178 long d3scr)

body.title: A little sparrow [EN/ES]
body.body:
## A little sparrow > ## Un pequeño gorrión ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSQvw5Y1HKfosVDPNovuxTR7zsxLSxU4MfLkmpvuL3ymd/pic.jpg) Hello, the drawing I share with you today is of a little sparrow. They are very nice birds to draw, even if they don’t have the flashy and striking colors that other birds have. For this drawing I used markers and a piece of recycled paper. I first started by sketching a small outline of the bird’s general structure; with a pencil I created some contours, playing with line thicknesses and parts with no lines at all. For color, I used alcohol-based markers, trying to blend the colors as much as possible and represent them as faithfully as I could to reality. I really liked the final result and I hope you like it too. Thank you for joining me for another day of drawing. > Hola, el dibujo que les comparto hoy es de un pequeño gorrión. Son unas aves muy bonitas de dibujar, aunque quizás no tengan los vistosos y llamativos colores que tienen otras aves. Para este dibujo utilicé marcadores y un pedazo de papel reciclado. Comencé primero trazando un pequeño boceto con la estructura general del ave; con un lapicero creé algunos contornos jugando con los grosores de la línea y partes sin ninguna línea en lo absoluto. Para el color utilicé marcadores en base de alcohol, tratando de mezclar lo más posible los colores y representarlos lo más fiel posible a la realidad. El resultado final me gustó mucho y espero que a ustedes también les guste. Gracias por acompañarme un día más dibujando. --- ***About:*** ==*Sketchbook and Journal of a Learner*== **If you like my content, join my [Fanbase clicking here](https://hive.vote/dash.php?fan=nestodibuja&i=2)**
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc31AecQSitU5xAjsqS4snajcWh6CMMyapx88itjomSah/thanks.png)
___ *All photos and images are created by me. These are pictures of my sketchbook. Many of my drawings are practice pieces rather than finished works. Images from the internet may or may not have been used as references, copies, or sources of inspiration as part of my learning process.*

summary.title: The Never Ending Story (ESP/ENG) Book Review
summary.body:
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bethyjade/23wCL48xbKAzXphk5QDJL6MgARJ9dXUk73E5YBbGxxFG2s4hvx8X4SHSbB7j3P6wiZrtu.png)
[Fuente](https://es.pinterest.com/pin/40884309114283059/)

Many people know this title from the famous 1980s movie, but few know that a book called The Neverending Story actually exists. This story, with its epic and wonderful plot, begins like any other, with a chubby, misunderstood boy named Bastian, who has problems with his father and, to make matters worse, suffers from bullying at school. In an attempt to escape his painful reality, he steals a book from Mr. Koreander's bookstore called The Neverending Story. But as Bastian reads, he realizes something amazing... He is much more involved in the story than he imagined. The fantasy kingdom is literally crumbling because of an invisible but devastating force called \

The Childlike Empress needs a new name, and Bastian is the one who can give it to her. By doing so, he crosses the literary barrier, breaks the fourth wall, and is transported to the fantasy world where he becomes a very powerful warrior. However, every time Bastian makes a wish in the fantasy kingdom, he loses a memory in his own world.\n\n>Muchas personas conocen este título por la famosa película de los ochenta, pero pocos saben que realmente existe un libro de la Historia Sin Fin. Esta historia con una trama tan épica y maravillosa inicia como cualquier otra, con un niño regordete e incomprendido llamado Bastian, que tiene problemas con su padre y para colmo sufre de acoso escolar, en un intento por evadirse de la realidad tan dolorosa, él roba un libro en la librería del señor Koreander llamado La Historia Sin Fin, pero a medida que Bastian va leyendo se da cuenta de algo impresionante... Ël está involucrado en la lectura mucho más de lo que imagina. El reino de fantasía se está desmoronando literalmente por causa de una fuerza invisible pero devastadora llamada \

La Emperatriz infantil necesita un nuevo nombre y es Bastian quién puede otorgárselo, al hacerlo cruza la barrera literaria, rompe la cuarta pared y se traslada al mundo de fantasia donde se converte en un guerrero muy poderoso, no obstante, cada vez que Bastian pide un deseo en el reino de fantasía pierde un recuerdo en el mundo al que pertenece.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bethyjade/244y8RpckM4EtaTj1rPpGMad6YhFrgsQVRnQxe1vHfe5XePQSoF84gFNoABrF5d6KRuyw.png)
[Fuente](https://es.pinterest.com/pin/AQ5APM5O27_PK1tp6Nq3uUr7Z2K043h38cwOnNmPWGPQH3QQ39oCVfo/)

Although different, this book reminded me a lot of Narnia, not only because of its epic and fantastical elements, but also because it never bored me. It has a very fast pace from beginning to end, is divided into two parts, and each explores a different side of Bastian. In one, he feels vulnerable and fragile, seeking refuge; in the other, it's the complete opposite: he feels strong, powerful, and proud, and it's there that he begins to lose his essence. This gives us much to think about and analyze, making it a very reflective book. Fragility isn't good for us, but neither should we be overconfident in ourselves. We must recognize that we need others, that we are part of an ecosystem in which the best way to live is to help one another.

>Aunque es diferente, este libro me recordó muchísimo a Narnia, no solo por loselementos épicos y fantásticos que tiene, sino porque nunca me aburrió, tiene un ritmo muy movido desde el inicio hasta el final, está dividido en dos parte y cada una de ellas explora una parte diferente de Bastian, en una se siente vulnerable, frágil, busca refugio, en la otra es todo lo contrario, se siente fuerte, poderoso y ufano y es allí donde empieza a perder su escencia, lo cuál nos da mucho para pensar y analizar, así que es un libro muy reflexivo. La fragilidad no nos hace bien, pero tampoco debemos excedernos en la confianza que nos tenemos a nosotros mismos, debemos reconocer que necesitamos de los demás, que formamos parte de un ecosistema en el cuál la mejor manera de vivir es ayudarnos los unos a los otros.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bethyjade/23u62hpnxjJR7BKcGsi2ZjxgvFvJyfTkg6HtC22gHMcBXuaTvFuaaaQ4S45tFEQ83sCYG.png)
[Fuente](https://es.pinterest.com/pin/183099541097889926/)

Something that makes the experience even more enriching and fun is that thanks to the magic of Fantasia, Bastian manages to break the literary barrier by entering the story (every reader's dream, although it depends on what they are reading, of course). This makes us identify even more with the character, gives him more personality, and makes him closer to us.

>Algo que hace que la experiencia sea aún más enriquecedora y divertida es que gracias a la magia de Fantasia Bastian logra romper la barrera literaria entrando en la historia (el sueño de todo lectr, aunque depende de lo que esté leyendo desde luego) esto hace que nos identifiquemos aún más con el personaje, le da más personalidad y lo vuelve más cercano a nosotros.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bethyjade/23wWu31dYfF9M1phmjUX2U3KjKdGkZT34b6Rbao9899xZ3ModZBjt3nE6xT4w7sqmpETK.png)
[Fuente](https://es.pinterest.com/pin/1047579563331457200/)

On the other hand, I must admit that one of the things I enjoyed most, because I also felt a connection to it, is the concept the author gave to \

which we could summarize as that emptiness left by the absence of dreams and illusions, the lack of motivation that often accompanies us in daily life due to work and routines. This begins as a small breeze, but it could become a devastating hurricane, capable of sweeping away even mountains of rock, as happened in Fantasia. And that's because Fantasia and \

are connected; neither can exist without the other.

\n\n>Por otra parte debo reconocer que una de las cosas que más disfruté porque también me hizo sentir identifiada, es el concepto que le dio el atuor a \

la cuál podríamos resumir como ese vacío que deja la ausencia de sueños e ilusiones, la falta de motivaciones que a menudo nos acompañan en la vida cotidiana por causa del trabajo y las rutinas diarias, esto comienza como una pequeña brisa, pero podría llegar a convertirse en un huracán devastador, capaz de arrazar hasta con montañas de roca, como ocurrió en Fantasía. Y es que Fantasía y \

están conectados, ninguno puede existir sin el otro.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bethyjade/23tveT72PiSSx8TBLUhvUYR2m8TpGkHvGdaFdvUfms6km6qBxYaZ9j3jzN38FLkZ86wEv.png)

And well, people, that's all for today's post, I hope you liked it. Thank you very much as always for supporting my work, I welcome new readers, I love you all very much, I send you a hug and I'll see you in another post.

>Y bueno, gente, esto ha sido todo por el post de hoy, espero que les haya gustado. Muchas gracias como siempre por apoyar mi trabajo, le doy la bienvenida a los nuevos lectores, les quiero mucho a todos, les envío un abrazo y ya nos encontraremos en otro post

summary.title: Something the Lord Made [Movie Reveiew] ESP/ENG
summary.body:
![Black and White Modern Film Production Presentation.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23wMj8YpVD4hBzrYKhQyvhY2sCvH3iqErFwCcBZDHtUAXFQGPLLKAkHxzg4844przfXxc.jpg)
(Cover designed by me in canva editor)
>Portada diseñada por mi en el editor de Canva
[Fuente](https://es.pinterest.com/pin/250723904225223639/)
[Fuente](https://es.pinterest.com/pin/378091331199859752/)

I recently decided to take a formal tour through the entire filmography of my all-time favorite actor, Alan Rickman, because there are really many of his films that I haven't seen yet, but each time I realize why his films are so special and have that certain something, since he didn't accept just any role but those that have personality and leave a mark, in this case for example we see him playing Doctor Alfred Blaloc a brilliant scientist and surgeon who also existed in real life. >Recientemente decidí darme un paseo formal por toda la filmografía de mi actor favorito de todos los tiempos, Alan Rickman, porque realmente son muchas las películas suyas que yo aún no he visto, pero cada vez me doy cuenta de porque sus películas son tan especiales y tienen ese no se qué, ya que él no aceptaba cualquier rol sino esos que tienen personalidad y dejan una huella, en este caso por ejemplo lo vemos interpretando al Doctor Alfred Blaloc un científico y cirujano brillante que además existió en la vida real.

Overview/Resumen

The film begins in the late 1920s and then jumps forward in time to the 1930s and 40s. Vivien Thomas, the protagonist, is a brilliant technician, a \

—someone who can do everything: repair, build, and so on. He loses his life savings (due to the Great Depression of 1929), the money he had saved for university, and is forced to take a job as a maintenance worker at Vanderbilt University. There, Dr. Alfred Blalock sees great potential in him (he learns quickly, is daring, has great self-confidence, and enjoys research and innovation). They begin working together on experiments to improve surgical techniques and save lives. Suddenly, they encounter the dilemma of \

infants whose skin turns blue due to insufficient oxygen saturation. Alfred... Blalock and Vivien Thomas work hard until they find an effective solution, becoming pioneers in this type of heart surgery. However, the big problem is that Vivien never went to university due to circumstances; her knowledge is self-taught, and she must also fight against the injustices of the system, racism, and segregation of her time.

\n\n>Al inicio la película transcurre durante los últimos años 20 y luego va avanzando en el tiempo durante los años 30 y 40, Vivien Thomas, el protagonista de esta historia, es un técnico brillante, también lo que se conoce como un \

es decir, de esas personas que pueden hacer de todo: reparar, construir cosas, en fin... el caso es que él pierde (por causa de la gran crísis del 29) todos sus ahorros de siete años de trabajo con los que pensaba entrar en la universidad, y por esa razón se ve obligado a trabajar como mantenimiento en Universidad de Vanderbilt, pero allí ele doctor Alfred Blalock ve grandes actitudes en él (aprende rápido, es osado, tiene una gran seguridad en sí mismo, le gusta investigar e innovar) así que ambos comienzan a trabajar en experimentos que les permitan mejorar técnicas de cirugías para salvar vidas, cuando de pronto se encuentran con el dilema de los \

bebes cuyo tono de piel cambia a ese color debido a que no tienen una buena saturación de oxigeno, de esta manera tanto Alfred Blalock como Vivien Thomas trabajan duramente hasta dar con una solución efectiva convirtiéndose en pioneros en la cirugía cardíaca de esta índole, sin embargo el gran problema es que Vivien nunca fue a la universidad debido a las circunstancias, sus conocimientos son autodidactas y además debe luchar contra als injusticias del sistema, el racismo y la segregación de su época.

Trailer

https://youtu.be/UclKFAQ0eJQ

My Opinion/Mi Opinión

This film (like many of its kind) aims to expose the profound structural hypocrisy of the labor system of that era, a consequence of racism and segregation. Vivien had to enter through the back door, couldn't use the same restrooms as white people, received a meager salary, and to top it all off, his work wasn't publicly recognized, even though he was the main architect of the technique Dr. Blalock used in his surgeries. Here, I must mention Mos Def's performance, which was brilliant and perfectly suited to the demands of his role. His gestures conveyed the frustration his character felt, but at the same time, one could also perceive his love and passion for his work, his great resilience, and his almost inexhaustible patience to endure all the injustices that were normalized in his time. >Esta película (al igual que muchas de esta índole) pretende exponer la gran hipocresía estructural que tenía el sistema laboral de esa época por causa del racismo y la segregación, Vivien debía entrar por la puerta de atrás, no podía usar los mismos baños que los blancos, recibí un salario miserable y para colmo su labor no era reconocida públicamente, aún y cuando fue él el principal artificie de la técnica que el doctor Blalock usó en sus cirugías, y aquí debo mencionar la actuación de Mos Def pues estuvo brillante y a la altura de las exigencias de su rol, en sus gestos se notaba la frustración que sentía su personaje, pero a la vez también se podía percibir el amor y la pasión por su trabajo, la gran resiliencia y la paciencia casi inagotable que tenía para poder soportar todas las injusticias que en su época estaban normalizadas.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23ywuBkgMEujokAMDTanjw7GZTzP2ZBUhc6JNnfsE3kFUdzUCUQpUMVNU6eSp5HMghv7y.png)
[Fuente](https://es.pinterest.com/pin/523754631642265695/)

As for Alan, wow! His Shakespearean theatrical training is evident in his gestures and the force he brings to each of his characters, always with a very personal touch of arrogance. In this case, Dr. Alfred Blalock also required a certain indifferent tone, normalizing concepts that are quite questionable today. Furthermore, playing characters who move in the field of medicine is not easy at all; it requires not only memorizing unfamiliar terms, but also speaking and moving as surgeons do in their environment but in a different context and era. So, as always, I was very satisfied with his performance.

>En cuanto a Alan ¡Wow! se nota su formación teatral shakespeariana en sus gestos y la fuerza que imprime a cada uno de sus personajes, siempre con matiz de arrogancia muy personal, en este caso el Doctor Alfred Blalock requería también de cierto matiz indiferente, normalizando conceptos que hoy en día son bastante cuestionables, además interpretar personajes que se mueven en el ampo de la medicina no es nada fácil, requiere no solo de memorizar términos poco familiares, sino que debes hablar y moverte como los hacen los cirujanos en su entorno pero en un contexto y época distinta, así que como siempre quedé muy satisfecha con su actuación.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23xAdziL6yDrhBhJSuBYAfiJqESAJiGfMKbNZQmP8NnMMLtZHRLwwjqYsuYsbcRvkW2n3.png)
[Fuente](https://es.pinterest.com/pin/420171840238235081/)

The relationship between Blalock and Thomas is very complex. They admire and appreciate each other, but Blalock is unwilling to publicly acknowledge Vivien Thomas's great talent, even though he knows it's essential. In fact, on occasion, he swallowed his pride to seek him out, but his scientific ego and fear of challenging the conventions of the complicated era in which they lived were always there. However, the ending of this film is... Wow! I won't say anything except that it didn't disappoint me at all.

>La relación entre ambos Blalock y Thomas es muy compleja, ambos se admiran y se aprecian pero Blalock no está dispuesto a reconocer en publico el gran talento de Vivien Thomas, a pesar de que sabe que es imprescindible y de hecho en algunas ocasiones doblegó su orgullo para ir a buscarlo, pero siempre está allí el ego científico y ese miedo a desafiar los convencionalismos de la complicada época en la que vivían. Sin embargo el final que tuvo esta película es... ¡Wow! No mencionaré nada a excepción de que no me decepcionó para nada.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/243BgAZ1to1ZEuz5ousbo2xQNjXq5Nj6iEZmhC2duhsdM7nAq3k991QtyKuR2MZowWmwX.png)
[Fuente](https://es.pinterest.com/pin/301600506295533158/)

Something that fascinated me about this film is that it completely departs from anything that could be considered \

It's not a story about racism and segregation, but rather one of overcoming adversity and achieving justice. It raises a profound question about what truly matters in professionals: their university degree or their actual knowledge and capacity for innovation? Furthermore, this is an original story; it doesn't attempt to usurp established narratives like Disney's The Little Mermaid or Snow White, or the almost cartoonish versions that cinema and Netflix have usefully presented of literary and even, worse still, historical figures, which, frankly, only cause great disappointment. So, I think this film is a great example for contemporary cinema. If we want to see inclusion or the representation that new generations so desperately crave, we need more authentic stories.

\n\n>Algo que me fascinó de esta película es que se aleja totalmente de todo lo que se pueda considerar como \

pues no es una historia sobre racismo y segregación, sino de superación y justicia que pone sobre la mesa una gran reflexión acerca de lo que realmente importa en los profesionales ¿su título universitario o sus conocimientos reales y su capacidad de innovación? Además esta es una historia propia, no pretende usurpar historias ya establecidas como la Sirenita o Blancanieves de Disney, o las versiones casi caricaturescas que ha presentado el cine o Netflix útilmente sobre personajes literarios e incluso, peor aún, históricos, que la verdad solo causan gran decepción, así que creo que esta película es un gran ejemplo para el cine actual, si queremos ver inclusión o la representación que tanto anhelan las nuevas generaciones, necesitamos más historias autenticas.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23xKvUpjBQjFSvzMPZtNiACyh2wviA4HeScdgZwWeLKWX9Yvy3QPV351sAqSiGahcvq7J.png)
[Fuente](https://es.pinterest.com/pin/391953973807005110/)

Well, here's my recommendation, and I hope you enjoy it. I don't regret watching this movie at all; on the contrary, I treasure it in my mind and heart, and I can now cross another Alan Rickman film off my watchlist 🤗

>Bueno, por aquí les dejo esa recomendación y espero que sea de su agrado, no me arrepiento de haber visto esta película, al contrario, la atesoro en mi mente y en mi corazón, y ya puedo tachar una más de las películas de Alan Rickman de mi lista de películas por ver 🤗
![Presentación Propuesta de Proyecto Portfolio Scrapbook Marrón y Negro.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mairene1/23wqwC8G3pmfAmUg1E61Zg3gUWbUypQbajqdteMGTFid9mWcYbLuHqe1kY7FxJ8zAiMM5.jpg)

summary.title: At the beach with my sisters (ESP/ENG)
summary.body:
![Miniatura de YouTube vlog un día conmigo recortes blanco amarillo (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/23xydki2qdEHfaFLimZ4UtaigbFQdbukvgHbB9YDYZG5rw8Q4HM7nxZTkmGc89U5EcLvo.jpg)
Made with Canva Editor >Imagen editada en Canva

Every now and then, we all need a complete break from our routine, to breathe some fresh air and remind ourselves that we're alive and deserve some leisure time. However, last weekend, thank God, I had the opportunity to do much more than that. I was able to spend quality time with my sisters (three of them). We went on a trip to the beach and also to explore several places in the beautiful port city of Puerto Cabello, Venezuela. We visited many tourist spots, but today I want to share our visit to the beach. We arrived early in the morning and were divided into three groups traveling in three buses. >De vez en cuando nos viene bien una desconexión total de la rutina, respirar un aire distinto y recordarnos a nosotros mismos que estamos vivos y que merecenos un rao de esparcimiento, sin embargo el fin de semana pasado, gracias a Dios yo tuve la oportunidad de hacer mucho más que eso, yo pude pasar tiempo de calidad con mis hermanas (con tres de ellas) Nos fuimos en una excursión a la playa y también para recorrer varios lugares de la hermosa ciudad portuaria de Puerto Cabello, en Venezuela. Visitamos muchos lugares turísticos pero yo hoy quiero ostrarles nuestra visita a la playa. Llegamos temprano en la mañana y estábamos divididos en tres grupos que viajaban en tres autobuces.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.04.51 AM (3).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/23ynUgKJU7ChhcKA74F8vAtMg9dLmDp6dU1XRcTkKSRfmzaVP5R62nYMpU7ExoXaz9qLz.jpeg)

We went to Playa Sonrisa, which is a wonderful beach very close to the boardwalk, so you don't have to travel far out of town, and I like that. It also has lovely places to take pictures, but what I like most is that the beach feels more like a swimming pool because it has breakwaters, making it much safer for all tourists.

>Nosotras fuimos a Playa Sonrisa, la cuál es una playa maravillosa que está muy cerquita del malecón, así que no hay que viajar un largo trecho fuera de la ciudad, y eso me gusta, además cuenta con lindos lugares para tomarse fotos, pero lo que más me gusta es que la playa parece más una piscina debido a que cuenta con rompeolas y eso hace que sea mucho más segura para todos los turistas
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.04.52 AM (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/23wWvxFKSMrxcQV6FcMzK2EVrhJHiFGbUW3m8FpBSFEJBUtowjt6Q3QddRmR4PDY5F3YT.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.04.52 AM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/23wgS5Di1fPHZvhg3MKYo6ZtqdEviPdBmxnUog2M66qWXnmvBJRQVj5z6XWi2ZCVSnSqh.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.04.51 AM (2).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/245HgdpJ8Ye8ofVXxgxZ9wgmFMEuFy66r5yRpAg6HUbeH9kk6qA8syDGViWA16F8nDvtY.jpeg)

Because it was the weekend there were a lot of people but it wasn't anything that disturbed the peace, everyone behaved appropriately, respecting the atmosphere and everyone's space, nobody had loud music, in short, it really was a very pleasant atmosphere.

>Por ser fin de semana había mucha gente pero no era nada que perturbara la paz, todos se supieron comportar a la altura, respetando el ambiente y el espacio de cada quién, nadie tenía musica fuerte, en fin, de verdad que había un ambiente muy agradable.
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.05.35 AM (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/23zS1Nzwt6HyZL5V4kHnEmqTpEKnsGaJHMZZugV7yXq1fCfbA7jFUCrvYAtNKivDCrNoz.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.05.35 AM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/2423yinVAoPzQn9idGAVy7QUPagSzM4iJrGbzZikmc4fENp16BViPUtwzBm571J1nGvwY.jpeg)

My sisters and I took lots of photos to capture the happy moment and to show them to our respective children, especially the two of them who have children living abroad. It's wonderful to know we still have each other, so we take advantage of every special moment to enjoy time as a family and have a great time.

>Mis hermanas y yo aprovechamos de tomar muchas fotos para inmortalizar el feliz momento y también para mostrárselas a nuestros respectivos hijos, en especial ellas dos que tienen hijos viviendo en el extrangero. Es bonito saber que aún nos tenemos las unas a las otras, así que aprovechamos cada momento especial para disfrutar en familia y pasar un muy buen rato.
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.05.36 AM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/23zknRWNmnaFhQLKYCu8AzRsvAcHUkwweYVnELaP1PvugCaEbAtR5nuEovQNH2W7HqYv6.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.05.38 AM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/244A6cdGXsjvSYYVxmjMy5Nz7vsvWusGa3UqsSKXiu4sg2eF7hRE74br1ykqasxj2Khb1.jpeg)

After exploring the beach, we decided to sit down and rest for a while, especially since, as I mentioned at the beginning of the post, we had been touring the city for a while, so we needed to recharge our batteries with a good lunch and some rest. We enjoyed it a lot because one of my sisters started telling us anecdotes about herself that we didn't know, and that made us burst out laughing 😄, making our moment of relaxation even more enjoyable.

>Luego de explorar la playa decidimos sentarnos a descansar un rato, en especial porque, como les dije al principio del post, nosotras teníamos rato haciendo un tour por la ciudad, así que necesitábamos reponer energías con un buen almuerzo y un rato de descanso.Lo disfrutamos mucho porque una de mis hermanas empezó a contarnos anécdotas que nosotras no conocíamos de ella y eso nos provoco un ataque de risas de los buenos 😄, haciendo que nuestromomento de esparcimiento fuese aún más agradable.
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.04.50 AM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/23uQkM3DSmM8QWfRZ1DDetTWSGhLD2DprZjbn9u9LRfYDuZuKqHb4Q5K2sVPEzSuM81ot.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.04.51 AM (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/23uFPL655CVMTfmh7zBk2vBfPA3rVjuB1wCnMrzjmfwKCachUg7MWffMp47GMNJ2XvstK.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.04.50 AM (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/23vhunoqByka6z7Gh89t9J6ZUkSvWbvcd1iLMBxLxgff1GGZX4ALh5uqDUvL1NHrkHJ3A.jpeg)

And of course we went into the sea to relax a bit. It was absolutely warm, the perfect temperature, very pleasant, but even more pleasant was the company of my sisters. I also met some new people; they're all from the church group one of my sisters attends, so they're easygoing people.

>Y desde luego entramos al mar para relajarnos un poco, estaba absolutamente cálido, la temperatura perfecta, muy agradable, pero más agradable aún fue la compañía de mis hermanas. También conocí gente nueva, todos son del grupo de la iglesia a la que asiste una de mis hermanas, así que es gente tranquila.
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.04.50 AM (4).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/244eEJcpNgtejwX3V1TxhhDKb7FGeBFaqCZjfWJQ5pn5J5LxU2yEjHmWsEuwdKBDQvJhw.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.04.50 AM (3).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/243fxXVcBKdjAiuXgoFjN2PkQ4cnYxtCrG47hgBoLUXPndYamDUrgkmp8RsVgjinBt3Xj.jpeg)
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.04.51 AM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/23rB7DJCgZsGPDR47uGgbFDwfFXYNWQ8JE7jJCbUV5caLhtHJcRuuGTodWGRjTkw2g88k.jpeg)

That break from our daily routine was truly wonderful for the three of us. We took the opportunity to recharge, spend quality time together, meet new people, learn about the local culture (of Puerto Cabello), and of course, have fun—we really needed that! I hope to God that moments like these will be repeated, that we'll have many more like this as a family, God willing.

>De verdad que esa desconexión con la rutina diaria nos vino de maravilla a las tres, aprovechamos para \

pasar tiempo de calidad, conocer gente nueva, aprender sobre la cultura local (de Puerto Cabello) y desde luego divertirnos, que bien que nos hacía falta. Espero en Dios que momentos como estos se repitan, que tengamos muchos más como este e la familia, Dios mediante.
![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-15 at 11.04.50 AM (2).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/242rnicmiCJw45vfrydoTTir3TSLVUf3VvUJ2Q76kvEnZk1Siw3ZJpWes6rCKqv8vuZX6.jpeg)

Thank you so much for allowing me to share these beautiful family moments with you. I'm sending you lots of virtual kisses and hugs 😘🤗 and blessings.

>Muchas gracias por permitirme compartir con ustedes estos momentos familiares hermosos, les mando muchos besos y abrazos virtuales 😘🤗 además de bendiciones.
![_Miniatura de Youtube Procrastinación Simple Dorado y Crema.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carmen1659/245n5WzTfDjt8QuC1CfX1iGPu5crq9bsYhnHjwPHUAnBL93vKUMEPGEND9gUCyLLvHj4k.jpg)
