summary.title: Feathered Friends Show Me A Photo Contest Round 275 \
summary.body:
![3 3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pranavgtd/23wCL4WNLakfdVcnkvEXgWHxzJJCJChiBWCNPNE4Kt7Tg3Ak5iTmmz2tvErp4gtQcU2mH.jpg)

Hello Hive Community.

I hope you all are fine. I am also fine here. Today's post is on Feathered Friends. The topic of today's post is free theme. The photograph presented here beautifully depicts the Sirkir Malkoha, one of the most distinctive and attractive birds found in the Indian subcontinent. As can be seen in the photograph above, this bird, perched on dry ground amidst grass and bushes, looks alert and active while searching for food. The Sirkir Malkoha's graceful posture, long tail and unique facial features make it a remarkable subject for birdwatchers and nature photographers. Although it does not have bright colors like the peacock or the kingfisher, the Sirkir Malkoha bird has a quiet beauty that blends in perfectly with its natural environment.


![2 2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pranavgtd/23viAchb9GqPYLEGPSgYRaDtFMGG47E9krAq6E2sXSU8DEXAo34jTnpz2KxyN2qFLVTbx.jpg)

The Sirkir Malkoha is a medium-sized bird of the cuckoo family. As can be seen in the photograph above, this bird's slender body and exceptionally long tail clearly give it a beautiful appearance. The feathers of this bird are mostly grayish brown. This grayish-brown color helps this bird blend in with the dry grasslands and scrub forests it lives in. This natural shade protects it from predators and allows it to move around unnoticed while searching for food.


![1 1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pranavgtd/23wMmCcqddb5SwdXKHgLJtoGvaBrX5vGvA6SxxcugtEjjzAVgCBhK1auX9vXzKV7xXAUb.jpg)

One of the most striking features of the Sirkir Malkoha bird is the bright red skin around its beak and face, as can be seen in the photograph above. This splash of colour contrasts beautifully with the otherwise earthy tone of its body. The bird's beak is also slightly curved, which is perfect for catching insects and other small creatures. Its strong legs and feet enable it to move quickly on the ground and through dense vegetation. The habitat, as can be seen in the photograph here, reflects the typical environment preferred by the Sirkir Malkoha. Dry soil, sparse grasses, thorny bushes and open scrub provide ideal conditions for this bird. Unlike many birds that spend most of their time in the upper branches of trees, the Sirkir Malkoha often spends its time close to the ground.



![4 4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pranavgtd/23vsbM945jZKpaLDZgojd3qpHR3NPtpQL1av3yvpfn9BMi6kggswLkPLhgA6yBEBUmV2k.jpg)


As seen in the photograph above, this bird has been captured in a natural and undisturbed environment. The dry grass in the background creates a soft and natural frame around the subject. The lighting highlights the subtle shades of brown and grey in the bird’s feathers. While the red facial skin stands out vividly. The long tail that spreads behind the bird adds grandeur to the composition and emphasizes one of the species’ most recognizable characteristics. This photograph not only documents the bird but also tells the story of life in the dry grasslands where the Sirkir Malkoha thrives.

I believe that the Sirkir Malkoha is a remarkable bird. This bird combines beauty, adaptability and ecological importance. Like other birds, this bird, which lives peacefully among dry forests and shrubs, plays a valuable role in controlling pests and maintaining the balance of nature.

I hope that my post will accept the Show Me A Photo Contest Round 275.

I sincerely thank you for visiting and reading my post.

summary.title: Sie Ruboh: A Traditional Acehnese Dish
summary.body: <div class=\
> <div class=\

> ![20260611_124215.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wqthxwcrrWtGHZQKGYTeePWf3geT4ZbxvgqzZj517fzBf4eMxgUuthZR1corfUXyiNt.jpg)
Hello, foodies! Today I’m going to show you how to cook beef at home. Unlike usual, today I’m preparing a traditional dish that really piqued my curiosity.
Sie Ruboh Soup
![20260611_124319.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wX5R2c59ttTrCroZnWJYNVAoRV7i8Crjvkh1Eh1TB7g6qbcoW1vAfxwZD4ecWjsdtoC.jpg) Sie ruboh is a beef dish that’s quite popular in our region. This dish is a traditional specialty originating from the Aceh Besar region of Indonesia. It’s typically served during major events like weddings, welcome parties, and other large celebrations. “Sie Ruboh” is the Acehnese name for this dish, but in Indonesian it’s called “daging rebus” (boiled beef). It’s similar to gulai, but this particular soup doesn’t use coconut milk—it relies solely on spices and natural ingredients from nature. The essential ingredient is palm sap vinegar, as that is what gives it its extraordinary flavor. Palm sap vinegar is made from palm sap that is typically harvested naturally directly from the palm tree; in Aceh, it is usually sold fresh at traditional markets. Honestly, this is the first time I’ve made this soup. I hope I can make it just as well as the one cooked by the expert at my mother’s house yesterday
Ingredients

>
**Main ingredients**
![20260611_115532.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/EpQxfBnGkpjfHk6udaQUkh8NXTGfboRzNTSygc5tnv2u5FPrEvchuMEz7dqS3SVmujd.jpg)
300 grams of beef offal and meat 1 stalk of lemongrass 20 grams of galangal 1 pandan leaf 1 clove of shallot 2 bay leaves 1 curry leaf 50 ml of palm vinegar

>
**Spice Paste**
![20260611_114008.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/Eq7PNQBUaxTyaZmYVpGUXpWaXSMgckP4huedkbeAU1uLhfPHYvsGafRAWUe6XfjYDFa.jpg)
2 cloves of shallot 2 cloves of garlic 3 cm of turmeric 5 red chili peppers 5 dried red chili peppers 6 bird’s eye chili peppers
Preparation
Season the meat and offal with salt and lime juice to taste; I add about ½ teaspoon of salt plus 2 tablespoons of lime juice, then marinate briefly. Blend the spices in a blender until completely smooth.

> ![20260611_114338.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23tmQStEtfNvaJPVeY28scGgCi1qwiBuU5tiVQdybNSCdt2UWR8jCmYkQ4wx6KBjPaqsA.jpg) ![20260611_114510.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23uFTcru1nz4E516eXDpLzodWnDoTWZFDBndiCbv2XjKV7U8gQyPfwHJf4p9hrNk4gvkP.jpg)

> ![20260611_114518.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23wqgbEcDbaaDwe77fJQTPy7hZn9iR54iGZDAAVEYqKHEN5o2i4zsds4qD6gSdTF4QnEN.jpg) ![20260611_114446.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23tc3HNJ2vz5U8eSiaECuFny4BuxLejCRGE4PEuwxy1qcJE5Qtrw9Kf8Z5U5CdvzRe7rU.jpg)
Add the ground spices to a cooking pan, then add the meat that has been marinated with salt and lime juice.
> ![20260611_114610.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xVFDFRhS4Kgw8R3dr4XkroHwaopnevukNfNp32kBcdLQFztyrh2p4AfkxzhTUM5BxVG.jpg)

> ![20260611_115537.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23uQmsDqv98m5c7KWz45RrfGHdCaGziBkHJU6Am7spWm6Xudc34dad2Qow9jWDv8k5BJ5.jpg)
Stir and add the aromatic ingredients: lemongrass, pandan leaves, curry leaves, bay leaves, and sliced shallots. Turn on the stove and begin cooking.

> ![20260611_115601.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23vsNfe9Y5rc1G4CGvG97mVDvwgwR6BNj3odZX5Ja5bkStS2to6MRtX2xPU2aSH58LQD7.jpg) ![20260611_115610.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23xAXpzaaDBFPJoLKcWXWH39tCAjGjrtKNceMfhP1QxLcYVnjrBXJSvLnVeZy1fxugw2p.jpg)

> ![20260611_115741.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23tbsLNbqyuj8voCheRaK5KbJve5GvF8vJFUkf6ZToKhFD7qd9YvaL4XgNzE4jF8buXY5.jpg) ![20260611_120300.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23uFTYXdFH23AhsRNAbwLpnLM43kEyEZW9THkJLfhmy7gEtVyFhXUWMYAWDBZMBCt2MuM.jpg)
Grate the galangal and add it to the pot, stirring until evenly distributed. Don’t forget to add palm vinegar, and then add salt if the flavor isn’t quite right after tasting. Cook until the meat is tender—it takes a while, but the result is incredibly appetizing.

> ![20260611_115716.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23u5vaaLwoQfJgbKK5phyL1QmruDGhWR8CPxTUfWyhJ6YwcfFuuwxBstrjZZdjEgAsKtY.jpg) ![20260611_120309.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23u69FDDSgvgkg1xGMHih8W559DSZD8ERvJjEi4C6dS5N4c6cbFAV6QgxmtkKBSJ9Y3gD.jpg)

> ![20260611_120316.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23uFRv23SBUAoJZxmx9LnigPKyA9qSqJUa1tL3j3VeZ6t7RhqzoeqMDkx4io1Hgp93X6R.jpg) ![20260611_120900.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23tviSvY2DdGHS5icvDinYkoYhSZtDscss1QC6ZrUi5UoK7xeLnLZrFdXzVeTYZGd1S3X.jpg)
Serving Suggestions
![20260611_124348.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/EogQmsaNCTiYRtadqn7PUscu4kBoLiJdjT3WwdBHfsxxsbksiLjobUcE4yxYy6V9bkH.jpg) Serve in a serving bowl, then enjoy with white rice—it tastes incredibly fresh and delicious. You’ll make this recipe over and over again because it’s that good. If you don’t like offal, you can just cook the meat on its own, and it’s still delicious. This dish is truly special; even though it was my first time making it, I was thrilled that the flavors turned out just right.
| ![20260611_124354.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/244KgK7TqqQisSZMCynAUc9NEPNmwKEZEboihpunxV3V1oNheK4Xdq9YSEDqueCuehdkL.jpg) | ![20260611_124312.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/244AHHW6XJwAPSthvhaqksFxjLeTJNwGzNwiGcyvVKNnoLBRuW3MnjQYJBZg9KkPHDbvA.jpg) | ![20260611_124303.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/244V4pLHQg4thvMYHUKufapzzVhBGqJZaCo2FVrppNCgfcNkR1fFixJAbhEtPt93m5vxo.jpg) | |-|-|-|
The savory, natural sweetness, and slight tang from the palm vinegar make it even more fantastic. The level of spiciness is just right on the palate when paired with rice—it’s all truly satisfying.
![20230506_212938_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nurfay/23yTv75jgyP5CSod1jCZoAPbPAnA7mSYtNJUa33KmuA4GgtmxGNNUyyxR9bq8gsiGS8qF.png)

今天普普通通的就过去了，待会有一节公选课，最后一节公选课了，记得两个月前老师要给我们一人一套MIDI Keyboard，辅助我们学习编曲，但是数量有限，当时我还害怕我分不到，着急去抢了一份，结果拿回来拆开试过一次，发现不会使，并且我不通任何乐理，就一直放着了。当时生怕自己没有，如今到手了却置之不理，我总是这样。当初发试卷的时候也是，发的时候生怕轮不到自己，发到到手后自己又懒得写最后抄的答案，我就是这么的双标。
 
今天的雨下得好漂亮啊，中午去图书馆睡了一个午觉，被哗啦哩啪啦的下雨声吵醒的，下得很壮观啊，每个雨滴大到连我的手机镜头都能捕捉到，我没带伞，要带的话真想举着伞去雨幕里挥霍一番。
 
等我出来后已经不下雨了，有些遗憾，期末了，最后的英语大作业大家商量着今天下午一起做完了，随随便便地应付过去了没花太多时间。
 
这个下午被打散了，我干脆回宿舍收拾了一下零碎物件，收拾完也就该上课去了，平平淡淡悠悠然然就过去了。收拾宿舍的时候发现我不知不觉间买了好多书回来，还没看完几本，实在没出息，而且意外地发现有本书我竟然买过两次，但我完全没印象了，怪哉怪哉。既然翻出来了待会我就看完吧，其实我不是很喜欢这本书，但它有些许意思，把玩一下还是不错的。

我很想看之前的电视剧《半妖倾城》，现在看来这部剧还是很潮流很新颖的，当时就很迷我，现在也是，昨晚看了第一集，没开倍速但时间很快就过去了，虽然有些地方傻乎乎的，但总体还是不错的，比现在的剧强多了。

summary.body:

It was a long day. She just arrived at the house, after spending an hour in traffic. She was used to it. But, she lost patience quickly, as she just finished a really busy day at work. She achieved some of her year's goals and met deadlines of that day. It was not just perfect, as it was in the cost of adding extra hour and a half of her time to accomplish all of that.

As soon as she entered home, everything vanished. She walked straight to that room, as if she was programmed to do that. There was no hello at the door, and she did not even notice that. The only thing she saw was the blue and pink room, as soon as she open the room's door. She tossed the toy elephant from the chair and sat next to the crib. She was looking at it, as if she was seeing someone in there. As if her baby is still asleep. The crib was empty. The room was quiet. It was the quietness that strikes more than anything else. She said while talking in a soft voice to herself, \

. She held the crib's edge and looked into the empty crib. The memories were going through the times she prayed that he was given more time. She stayed silent as she always do. But, the words within her were saying, \
. # PT

>

Foi um dia longo. Ela acabara de chegar em casa, depois de passar uma hora no trânsito. Estava acostumada. Mas perdeu a paciência rapidamente, pois tinha acabado de terminar um dia de trabalho muito corrido. Alcançou algumas de suas metas do ano e cumpriu os prazos do dia. Não foi perfeito, pois custou uma hora e meia a mais do seu tempo para dar conta de tudo.

Assim que entrou em casa, tudo desapareceu. Caminhou direto para aquele quarto, como se estivesse programada para fazer isso. Não houve um \

na porta, e ela nem percebeu. A única coisa que viu foi o quarto azul e rosa, assim que abriu a porta. Jogou o elefante de brinquedo da cadeira e sentou-se ao lado do berço. Ficou olhando para ele, como se estivesse vendo alguém lá dentro. Como se seu bebê ainda estivesse dormindo. O berço estava vazio. O quarto estava silencioso. Era o silêncio que mais a impressionava. Ela disse, falando baixinho consigo mesma: \

. Segurou a borda do berço e olhou para o berço vazio. As lembranças a invadiram, relembrando os momentos em que rezava para que ele tivesse mais tempo. Permaneceu em silêncio, como sempre. Mas as palavras dentro dela diziam: \
.\n\nPosted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@ronnie10/enpt-i-hold-your-hand-hp9)

summary.title: Tuesday, a sunrise walk near Cisco breweries restaurant
summary.body:
# a sunrise walk near Cisco breweries restaurant Today I will share some shots from a walk I took one morning recently and focusing on the views around the Cisco Breweries restaurant. I actually walked there this morning but have not got those photos off my camera as yet. Davy's Locker was an iconic seafood restaurant on New Bedford's waterfront for nearly 50 years which closed in 2014. I believe there was another restaurant there for a short period and then Cisco opened there in 2021 Before getting to the photos, today was been a frustrating start. Overnight, our AC unit froze up, so I have it off at the moment and will check it out once all the ice defrosts, a bit frustrating as we just had it served recently, so hoping it isnt a big issue. Then I decided to head to Fort Tabor beach this morning, but when I got there the gates were locked, first time I have seen that in ages, so I ended up on the Harbor walk and walking in the area I will share shots of today. Starting with this shot of the Entrance from the car park they have there, I thought the tractor was a cool touch, not sure if it is always there, or it related to some event they are having
![sunrise by cisco.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23zastd3zfETUnPyb9rTyHLt31bmE2GiwqJEF3FXubp5DRMWQzuQQU8ebxo78p1yvrZ24.jpg) **Sony A7iv 27mm F11 1 Sec ISO 100** **[Click here to view larger](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23zastd3zfETUnPyb9rTyHLt31bmE2GiwqJEF3FXubp5DRMWQzuQQU8ebxo78p1yvrZ24.jpg)**

They have built up the place nicely, plenty of outdoor seating, inside seating and an upstairs deck, a stage for musicians to play and it does good business This next and the rest of the shots are focusing more on the view over the water, most of the people who go to eat or drink there, do not see, well they do see the water view but of course not the sunrise colors This is on a walkway they have they goes around the restaurant
![sunrise by cisco-2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/243fiATAptreWnYvrzSwzdX78UEjzvT8ipLyxN92rtvpUMehB9Lxk4sCDW7zeycDx9K4B.jpg) **Sony A7iv 20mm F11 1/8 Sec ISO 100** **[Click here to view larger](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/243fiATAptreWnYvrzSwzdX78UEjzvT8ipLyxN92rtvpUMehB9Lxk4sCDW7zeycDx9K4B.jpg)**

The restaurant is behind me as I took this shot,
![sunrise by cisco-3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/242riLxn4BVGeoVPtxmyvP3tG25fFiDXWthYxpRPt9qHtUixu8GThw32n5W4d1u3Tsru7.jpg) **Sony A7iv 17mm F11 1/10 Sec ISO 100** **[Click here to view larger](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/242riLxn4BVGeoVPtxmyvP3tG25fFiDXWthYxpRPt9qHtUixu8GThw32n5W4d1u3Tsru7.jpg)**

Love the cloud reflections in these last couple of shots, this dock is behind the restaurant and in the warmer months, they have a boat that goes out and picks up people from their yachts or pleasure craft to bring them into the restaurant
![sunrise by cisco-4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23yTUHUWAKjzutLtQY2qHWRmwsSdep9Vyvk7mpMpZGiJJ1kvfwKjqYLvYppAzz1mkq7V6.jpg) **Sony A7iv 17mm F11 1/8 Sec ISO 100** **[Click here to view larger](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23yTUHUWAKjzutLtQY2qHWRmwsSdep9Vyvk7mpMpZGiJJ1kvfwKjqYLvYppAzz1mkq7V6.jpg)**

summary.title: If Only I Could Bring Them Back
summary.body:
Childhood days are ones filled with so many memories that can not be trade for anything. They lasts forever in ones head either it's good and the opposite. 

![1000155813.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/afrikens/1000155813.jpg)

The joy of being able to freely play around when you are been permitted by your parents or even when they are out and not around to seal you in the room like the fishes in a Titus sandine. That's the most free moment I love to have cos those are the times I know that even if my playing ends up in crying when I get hurt, I don't get beaten by mum for hurting myself (only God knows why those mothers do like that, lol. You would even be happy that the beating is forgotten when she's treating you first, only to get beaten after you're treated).

The numerous games we would always do keeps flashing back now and all it does to me is bring some beautiful smile to my face. From playing under the rain with pants alone, to drawing a 12 square box on the floor, either it's on sand or a cemented floor known as Suwe, skipping rope game, monini monini modeji modeji game (has to do with legs counting), ten-ten game, daddy mummy and children play, (the sweetest ones are when our parents are not home and we can get their food stuffs to cook food for our family play, lol. 

One of the games I would love to bring back is the tinko tinko tinkololo tinko game, lol. My God lol
It's not like this game is kind of more special than the rest but the fact that you're doing multiple things together at the same time and also involves IQ makes it interesting to me. 

![1000155819.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/afrikens/1000155819.jpg)

In this game, you're making use of your two palms with another competitor and these palms are to be swinging in and out, up and down, tapping or clapping and all that. It requires reasoning and strength at the same time because you just not mistake a next step for another and the more the number increases, the more the pace at which the palm swings. So brain and strength must be intact to do this game cos you wouldn't wanna lose out.

As a child, I wasn't really a fan of junks and I could only relate with a few candy sweets so I don't really have any snacks coming to my head right now.

My childhood was full of fun and one of the best moment I missed was staying awake almost through the night because I was looking at my hanged ready-made bob gown that I was to wear to our school end of the year/term party the next morning, lol.

I'll be dropping my 🖊️ here on the Scifi Multiverse Prompt 

Thanks for reading through 🤗 

All images are Mine

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@afrikens/if-only-i-could-bring-them-back-dwd)

근래 계속 늦잠을 자던 탓인지, 오랜만에 맞이한 이른 아침은 유난히 졸렸다.
그래도 첫 출근 날. 지각만은 하고 싶지 않아 무거운 몸을 일으켜 출근 준비를 했다.

낯선 출근길.
타고, 걷고, 다시 타고, 또 걸으며 조금 긴장한 마음으로 회사에 도착했다.
다행히 늦지는 않았다.

막연히 상상했던 모습과는 조금 다르기도 했고, 또 생각보다 비슷하기도 했다.

오전에는 오리엔테이션을 듣고,
오후에는 팀에 자리를 배정받은 뒤 다시 영상 오리엔테이션이 이어졌다.
회사마다 다 비슷할 거라 생각했는데, 막상 와보니 또 저마다의 분위기가 있었다.
익숙한 듯 낯설고, 낯선 듯 익숙한 공기.

긴장과 설렘, 그리고 조금의 걱정까지.
여러 감정이 뒤섞인 채 정신없이 하루가 흘러갔고, 어느새 첫 출근이 끝났다.

아직은 모든 게 어색하지만,
오늘의 이 낯섦도 언젠가는 익숙한 일상이 되겠지.

일단은… 정말 피곤하다.

summary.title: Introvert Talks - The Trip I Almost Didn't Take
summary.body:
<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23zkiCWQf2pr3JgZZzwZGSBrXCtsv3sYNtC7BerYKVvUpM5rYqGK3LMwuA6yG2ubTv5TQ.png)</center>

\

is meant to be a new initiative or theme, where I myself as an introvert, just talk about reflections and thoughts about my life, or maybe share more personal stuff. :)\n\nThis is my weekly post under this \

theme and let's see where it takes me and us.

***
**For a moment, I actually wondered if I should call off my trip.**

**But I am glad that I went for it.**

I fell and injured my knee a few weeks ago in Seoul, South Korea (you can read more about it [here](https://peakd.com/hive-126152/@relf87/introvert-talks-a-fall-a-pause-a-reminder)), and the timing was quite bad because I had a trip that followed closely after.

I was still in recovery mode and I could walk but not too much, and when the day of the flight came, I did think if I should go ahead and the thought of risking another fall or worsening my injury did cross my mind. Also, I wasn't sure if I was in the right mental state to \
given my condition. In fact, I was feeling down that I wouldn't be able to \

the holiday because my travel itinerary had to be adjusted significantly, depending how much I could walk eventually.

Ultimately, I decided to go for it. After all, recovery takes time and cannot be rushed and life needs to go on.

And having returned from the trip, I am just glad that I overcame my negative thoughts and quite enjoyed myself over the 5 days in Bangkok, Thailand. And this reinforced the thinking that actually we have control of many things in our life. In this instance, it's my thoughts and mindset. I could have continued to feel depressed throughout the trip, but I chose to enjoy myself as much as possible with my limitation.

One of more enjoyable activities this time happened to be aromatherapy massages. I am not a huge fan of massages, but it's just something that tourists to Bangkok go for, but after this trip, I realised it was one of the best activities for me. No walking and just pure relax. As for my injury, I could tell the therapists to avoid the affected area and they would understand. So no issues at all. As such, I felt that I had a lot of rest and relaxed a lot during this trip, which was different from the usual sightseeing itinerary, i.e. ticking places off the checklist.

Another activity that I enjoyed more compared to my previous trips would be the food. Because I had to rest more, having long meals at restaurants or sitting at cafes became a must whenever I visited the shopping malls. And I could people watch and soak in the views sometimes.

If this experience has taught me anything, it would be the importance of the mindset and also taking time to slow down the pace of life occasionally. It really feels different, when one takes their time and live more in the present. Hopefully the next time when I visit Bangkok, I could venture out more, but for now, I am grateful that I had a great trip, thanks to the 5 star hospitality of the Thais too!

Ending off with a photo taken from high floor cafe/lounge!

![20260610_102947.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/Ep7tAqfuapiYKM1JTogJajWr7U3PDijD3vfQGZGdzXYRkmbB4sjDRGJXShSfdcWEPCP.jpg)

All just for owning BBH. There are two ways you can get BBH. First you can buy them from the open market. I use TribalDex myself.

Or they can be tipped to you. The great part about BBH tipping is that when you tip a token to someone else you do not loose any of your own. There is a central pool that supplies them.

And a third way to get BBH would be people gift them to you. There was an update to the tipping bot. If you now tip 1 BBH you get 1 BBH also. How facking awesome is that.

Wood heating is always the way... but inside apartments or wooden-made houses, a menace.

15L is HUGE mate! That's almost like a normal oven. I don't need that big one unless you want to go for a turkey or something like that, but because I also have a normal oven, this is more for quick and fine stuff. But maybe you don't have a oven, so that would make more sense to me.

I have this one, https://ninjakitchen.co.nz/collections/grills/products/ninja-foodi-smart-xl-grill-air-fryer-ag551 (right now, and getting quite old...) 

I am Portuguese, so it's everything grilled if possible. LOL Wooden grilled makes everything totally memorable. The juices dropping into the charcoals and then blasting all that smell into the product. Hummmm, there is no substitute so far for me.

Cooking bread at 220-250C is very hard indeed, not enough temperature to raise the dough fast enough. You need tricks, like a ceramic/metal pot (which retains heat for longer periods of time and together with the humidity of the bread increases both pressure and temperature, then after 40-45 min, I usually uncover the pot, and let it cook for another 30 min to create that crunchy crust.

This last one hack is mostly for normal ovens... but if you are on a normal good +300C things (can be electric/gas but wood-based beats it always)... You can make bread like normal bakers... and my dad still has a handmade stone wood oven in Portugal, where we used to bake all sorts of food. Lots of memories...

summary.title: Lamp Post Fixed
summary.body:
<center>![IMG_2707.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/coinjoe/23wWtnUyYAYraxgYugQqRTsSLWkxB9VRwrUUhKsAjPVgSyav1mb5334Dh9ogGyss9bgds.jpeg)</center><center><sub>New weather proof socket.</sub></center>

One of the sockets on our outdoor lamp posts went bad. We have two that sit on each side of the driveway. Seems moisture made its way into one of them and caused corrosion. Stopped working completely.

Not much of an electrician, but I know enough to make me dangerous to myself. So I purchased some weatherproof sockets on Amazon. Replaced the bad one yesterday. It took me some time. Only because I kept connecting wires before attaching the lamp hood pieces correctly. Had to unwire and rewire several times. Rerun wire through the hood pieces and so on. Finally got it right.

<center>![IMG_2706.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/coinjoe/23tc1iEC6BYgucFkkcasH5sMrCUithGmRYMbHrJFzGfuSgkz9faZkfxqGB9DYRaRiSWsH.jpeg)</center><center><sub>The repaired lamp post.</sub></center>

By the time I was done, I was exhausted. Sun was out and I was directly in it. Just sucked the life out of me. Had to actually take a couple breaks just to get through it. I intended to go ahead and replace the other lamp's socket as well. Just to have it done and replaced with the new weatherproof kind. Preventative maintenance you know. But I was too exhausted. It will have to wait till another time. Or until it goes out. Whichever comes first.

In the meantime, back to the garage. Always another project. Always something that needs done. You knock one out and two more are waiting. That's just how it goes.

But I'm happy to be feeling up to doing some small projects and little chores outside now. There was a time not too long ago when I couldn't. When I spent most of my days in the recliner watching winter pass by through the window.

This is better. Even if the sun kicks my ass and I have to take breaks. I'm out there. I'm doing things. I'm moving.

That's progress.

![HiveDivider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/coinjoe/EoGvX4Va6X4ZfjnYkvBhFi2bqZsCrwoqpWhwgmGDPKVDS9eeZ4zF8foqAfcm44mn84d.png)
Thanks for reading,
Joe

summary.body:
https://youtu.be/PC9wjZh-kyg?si=nzACnA4J3678K1lQ

When people fail to nurture their family, they often feel hopeless. This is why we must honor, protect and invest in our families the same way Jesus did.

A good example is David, who, even while fleeing from King Saul, remained deeply concerned for his family's safety. Even in the midst of danger and uncertainty, David made sure his parents were protected.

Like Jesus, he demonstrated that true strength comes with responsibility and care for family. So we must endeavour to appreciate God for fathers and for the family system He designed to sustain us. We must never at any time take our family for granted because God cherishes family.

summary.title: The punishment that came after every Sega game.
summary.body: <div class=\

> ## Hello, everyone. I welcome you to my blog. Trust me when I say that childhood was one of the best things that happened to us as individuals, especially some of us who, despite having very strict parents, still found a way to enjoy our childhood and then serve the punishment that followed it. I think childhood is one of the few times in our lives where we are genuinely happy and our every smile is not faked but rather very genuine, and then every cry and tear is also genuine until adulthood comes and things completely change, and now we wear a smile on our faces but are very sad on the inside. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdHSMFYce7rw5ifmJ7xYPYVPHiGeHMiEFH3QQwG88LSW2/1781605142614.jpg) [Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-video-game-system-sitting-on-top-of-a-wooden-floor-pXLWVAW4f7A) There are many memories I still have about childhood that I still remember, and I find myself smiling sheepishly maybe because of what I did, a friend did, my siblings did, or something we did as a group. Many of the things we did as kids always had consequences, but trust me, most of the time we preferred to suffer the consequences rather than not do those things at all, and sometimes as an adult I am glad I did because I would not have had any story to share if I did not do those things despite knowing the consequences. Sometimes all that you need to enjoy your childhood is just to do those things that will attract those punishments, especially when you enjoy those things. Growing up in a neighborhood where we lived as one big family, you were free and welcome to your neighbors' houses like they were yours. That even helped us offend our parents more because there were houses your parents might not have wanted you to get into, but because the family welcomed you and was not hostile, you found it difficult to pay attention to your parents' instructions. I had a friend, but for reasons best known to my mom, she asked us to stop going to their house, but then they came to our house, and we could not help but find ourselves following them to theirs, and no matter how hard we tried, it was something we could not resist. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNP6u3HW3yuhpsnxdiHGMNSeK4LKxWjVeqsuiosdPH9o9/1781605142545.jpg) [Source](https://unsplash.com/photos/two-boys-are-playing-a-video-game-on-the-television-nVk581BTI_U) My mom will scold us, and sometimes she flogs us, but then things got worse when my friend's dad now bought them this TV game called SEGA. Then, it was something that every child wanted to have then, even though the graphics then were poor, but we enjoyed it like our lives depended on it. You can play Contra 4, Sonic, Mortal Kombat, and a very slow football game on this Sega. Once we start playing that game, we don't even remember we have a house to go back to; we will be inside, and before you know it, everywhere is dark, and we start thinking about how to go back home and face our parents. That game caused me more trouble than it actually brought me joy, but I feel like the trouble it brought my way was actually worth it; I can go hours playing Sega without ever getting tired. We go from Sonic to football to Mortal Kombat and even wrestling.

In this meeting, I return to this beloved community to share some images featuring a small species of spider I found on my plantation.

This spider is not an insect and is not considered a pest. Unbeknownst to us, this spider can play a role in controlling and predatoring insects, earning it the nickname \

Spiders also have three hunting methods: web-spinning, hunting, and jumping spiders. Like the one I encountered in this meeting, I believe the small spider was a jumping spider. When I approached, it immediately jumped away from me, disappearing among the small leaves. Spider species also have morphological characteristics consisting of four pairs of legs and three segments. Spiders also have multiple eyeballs depending on the species, so the spider's eyes can be used as a reference in determining morphological taxonomy. summary.title: Promenade between luxury and nature - the English promenade in Nice, a walk by the sea (and more)
summary.body:
Dear Hivers, in the desire to convey my tour of Nice to you as authentically as possible, I thought for a long time about which approach to writing a post to apply and how to put everything I saw into one post.
Not at all.
So that you (like me) could conclude what it is like to stay in Nice, I will present the visit to this city in three separate posts.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfSMSXhgtGgkWrvxrneguABcCK6LR511n2EUdAHxb7nLW/1781604592642.jpg)

I will write to you about a walk by the sea on the famous English promenade, a walk in the old town and especially, a walk in the park on the Colline du Château hill.

The English Promenade, a popular promenade in Nice (Promenade des Anglais) is exactly 7 kilometers long.
​It stretches along the Bay of Angels (Baie des Anges), connecting the airport to the west and the Colline du Château to the east.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQBujxPg2VrgN3iiKuEGtBFYmCP7ZZvHQEP9w3kxTtAuH/1781603307399.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmebJJ13rW5K5Ehsfq1ZmJyDSjoh6ptuCchCvv4e8SM3gq/1781603307512.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNngU9ZWs3fpjUc3jAhJTMAFo9FS4xhTy6gwo4PSKnYFz/1781603307587.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcXyDtXGdkMHtFREaZHSApoWXU2pEm4ZRgXzf633n8ER2/1781603307655.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmT7i5HDwLwYUc4pXtvf3E4ZW94VBFr7qBScGEmyCFRyk2/1781603307715.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma1rK2F9ymaN2P7z723aWYazXLCsC5MVcEpRzvyUAHUL8/1781603248319.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmanxHPvUVDrvfebi31KV7dGp9phhURJMj62SV2tNjjPU5/1781603248432.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmY3GTCEwHJPxorV9mLw1Xbog3HA74kpgiKWEWhfJY85KD/1781603248510.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXjRCJwbxoRX8PWSULgzEBrqNJdx9oBroaMig5DP1br8d/1781603248593.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmY1rPF7cid1WxJxNkuXoexrgawg1AsM3iBZWKP77uKExU/1781603248686.jpg)

Along its entire length, on one side is the beautiful sea, the color of which gave this coast its epithet - Azure, while on the other side there are houses, villas of famous and wealthy residents of Nice, hotels, parks.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmefgDTkqm6dTxwf4wTX3fzj4esH3VLKg4jWpkUHjpkaFp/1781603359099.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXx43gqRpWq2HQ5Fi3AHSSf9UkYiaHdNA7dyqodGTzBoY/1781603359203.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX1ZngwrhTNZSGBMyDiSeK4f8xKh7RyJjSi7zkBf46sU3/1781603359269.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWcFDNeAypK91gYHAMPo3iQYHPDJxHwhCeRWEEwSWQu4F/1781603359361.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRRFxMcydrf5jJHnjDVbYrVc13fUJUfPzTCZdb3Y4N62D/1781603359449.jpg)

One of the most famous hotels in the world, and certainly a symbol of the city of Nice, the Hotel Le  Negresco, is located on this promenade.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdP48umUbQK3SvbkzU5gSFufnFJYHUfQDqo79jMxtAQgz/1781599460902.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmadao9jaHXx5x8brzkHhNE5HW292LrFvTsnwkHeTWuptc/1781599460964.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmb8DZczNuu4KCkg5fXkZz2dwBKFkvWMeBLQHAgWjfoKkn/1781599461031.jpg)

The history of the hotel is fascinating.
Built and opened just before the first World War in January 1913 , owned by the rich Romanian Henry Negrescu.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUk5oCvMDriBfZHmM7zY3wam1AUnkPAdbnWFdPn8kWK3d/1781603439981.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTWgofvbdSfzC4px5aB2EEU5yAZbgdSKWr8z9dtQCoDEg/1781603440155.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWs7qG5Qz8hb2u1W2WEgKZefFmp7AT8CuPQ2pFnRgX9ds/1781603440230.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmePpt6fLd6RKQQ9XgUW5Nn4A2aThjdcjjzJzoUiF5trRs/1781599518977.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUjHfDdEtuzRbhu66N8hyzjEiK37GG3cfEogZ25hsn8x4/1781599519043.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmd9vY3G2BE2E1oDbsufBCjUsb2CFbkoFQ88CUrxQPZWs7/1781599519095.jpg)

The architect of the hotel was Édouard-Jean Niermans, and the hotel was designed and built as a hotel that brought a revolution in luxury and enjoyment.
Each room had its own bathroom, heating system, mail delivery.
The glass dome of the Royal Salon, which I did not have the opportunity to see, was designed by Gustave Eiffel himself.
After the start of the First World War, Henry Negresco showed his generosity and turned the hotel into a military hospital.
Without a rich clientele, he spent his fortune during the war and died as a bankrupt businessman in 1920.
Then, until 1957, the hotel was owned by a Belgian company, and in 1957 it was bought by the Mesnage family. 
According to the story, they chose this hotel because it was the only one in Nice that had an elevator that could accommodate wheelchairs. Mrs. Mesnage.
The further fate of the hotel is like in a fairy tale.
The management of the hotel is taken over by their daughter, Jeanne Augier, and over the following decades, the hotel is turned into a museum and gallery.

Over the following decades, Jeanne transformed the hotel into a living gallery, filling it with over five centuries of French art—from Louis XV-style furniture to contemporary works by Salvador Dali, Jean Chagall, Henri Matisse and Niki de Saint Phalle.

During all that time, she managed to resist the offers of hotel chains and to this day, even after her death in 2019, it remains the only independent hotel in Nice, which is managed by an independent foundation that Jean started during her lifetime.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVUhEgTNmisH5YQw8VUgYHT6qm34777zgyvr8zkGNWTLt/1781599641788.jpg)

I didn't have a chance to peek inside the hotel, judging by the room rental prices, they probably have a strict policy on entering the hotel, so I photographed it from the outside from all sides.

Right next to the Hotel Le Negresco there is another interesting object, the Massena Palace Museum.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmadJQSHAGFHs84CrZMK9AZYE7gAwrrewgCxmgvNqaz2pt/1781599665857.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPYAVJknrSs9UDjCT7cUpMpmF4FJQuetSJucjPiw6BWQe/1781599665943.jpg)

Built at the beginning of the 20th century as a villa, it served as the winter residence of the Massena family, to be sold to the city of Nice in 1918, for a symbolic sum with the condition that it be turned into a museum of local history open to the public, free of charge and accessible to all visitors.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXjqkoX8DWBCDTCZDSiqLxcMmUJg25bLNLWdWMVSuBMeZ/1781599751819.jpg)

Entrance to the museum is not free today, but it is possible to take a walk through the beautiful garden of the villa.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPREuxaJ7VppPLAKyewRcnzsBkc6WfaihFZyNsYA4qiu4/1781599859514.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfYFPR7WKSffjsf2C3eEQRof1Kjn6VAtCdF4wLiE1YgWi/1781599859614.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYwtjkCmXPVGxgrpszvnBfq455qbk9h7VPq5AqtATxFbm/1781599859692.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbNxh3YSja91YMD7dxJ21vu6grcwCdmeWenarGwKtMq5i/1781599859759.jpg)

In one corner of the garden, there is a section dedicated to the victims of the terrorist attack in 2016, when, in celebration of the fall of the Bastille, a truck was driven into the promenade by a terrorist and killed 86 people.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbmB9NnVap1jwRLW4eAscSm39QqHCF51LE7c9Y1jkfogH/1781603837126.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRgLPK25u6GkNKucaGiNCAj6em3VtfcvvL7v4RuiqkscW/1781599900688.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTBfZCr3aWs9j5YcQAVz4Ma9Sbt3ZGPaekj48jbBGkBnw/1781599900760.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdomn15jMnGqA5PKvFk6Jzn2MffduUKgEFQbMsrbc5Lf4/1781599900831.jpg)

This monument on the promenade is a memorial to these victims.
Since that horrific attack, the promenade has been fenced off with pillars, so that no large motor vehicle can enter the footpath.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSAhrzqwuMnrgsDMyfqwiZs82Pudx4zvJHRMZwZXQTb8i/1781600013853.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWAj1NHXc7GbaxWC7o78ZYGHPpypC9yhdqXUWYHY8RZSm/1781600013933.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWcFDNeAypK91gYHAMPo3iQYHPDJxHwhCeRWEEwSWQu4F/1781600014007.jpg)

Unlike the sculpture that was erected in memory of the victims of the terrorist act, there is another monument on the promenade, erected in 2012 on the fiftieth anniversary of the return of a large number of Algeian citizens to France. Since 1830, when the French conquest of Algiers began, after France finally lost the war in 1962, over 10,000 families whose ancestors went to conquer Algiers were forced to return to France.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNngU9ZWs3fpjUc3jAhJTMAFo9FS4xhTy6gwo4PSKnYFz/1781600041975.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc71evfkA7pyPkPGaKiPwdqWwqvbef2FurTduzZcx8pzh/1781603978408.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUxg9E7GwUbgfth2FFrFauVCdYywAKw8pauwoaNkN8HPk/1781600042218.jpg)

The broken plate with the footprints symbolizes the departure and breaking of the vwz and contact with that other world.

Real enjoyment is the moment of a break in the walk, when you can take a break on the blue chairs, with your feet up on the fence, while observing the open Mediterranean sea.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmedK9F6AtxVrQt1DZTSGR3Vgi7CTUzE6iJ8zhFAivt6TJ/1781600107816.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma7nmdSL4nmNsGe2e9TD1tRJnUihim9xCAxXYKkJGQPQm/1781600107899.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWd7PAGnCCU92jVEA993Hqp8MyVfGcVP6cQk2N5Zi5AJR/1781600107998.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfNi5fp91giXZWXYXjSBpKf5kcM9rc3M984ZTKE6uL9GK/1781600108051.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUEUV3pXL4QdsTtMAF3B2uTsbDbtiwsFG4UfTMuS9a6WM/1781600108095.jpg)

Continuing the walk along the promenade, you will reach the Jardin Albert 1er park, where there are several monuments.
One huge metal arch \

which symbolizes the curvature of the Bay of Nice, and was installed in 1988 to celebrate the centenary of the naming of Nice.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmestGxcp445REJET1JxGsPR8LP46YLSBpmrr2YNJhAQ6r/1781600314991.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdMMzjMbnjjD5TNZFDeA212VZ81BA19vyM63bZMpXMw16/1781600357960.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPvPxBJFr3FPRZVr9pxj32JMEgzfox1wzuK4WJ5WgL6Dg/1781600315070.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbhfLS7XFpCT2yDPQz3FXiNHLwWBvZdszFMi4siVK6jMU/1781600315147.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdJjzoyfHe5GjuL1TrQ68Wtmk1iMJtQL12qA3cJwt2M63/1781600315231.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbYNwhbapgxbmb3g8Y8NEPkA6XcR7sCD4BmMuVyGCLDQF/1781600315302.jpg)

From this sculpture, further towards Place Massena, you will find Nice's most famous fountain, Fontaine du Soleil.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRXFwPKgQ32fHdEUxJbwosCP3ohfKMsSKEr15bcxLnb6g/1781600399636.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSVFt6DjKW1YC5TTpcNWawGFr4F7v6MHQhRudjr61WryD/1781600399863.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbg8hfwSSkKJi3SP74jjZ8m5qDtCukQLGm3LYgMhhTcXi/1781600399934.jpg)

This attraction was often on our route, no matter how many times we passed this park at any time of the day. For this reason, I have photos both during the day and in the evening, maybe even some at night.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTsG91Rd7ZjyAcefAkg37k6q5pJzE9uXVNox53VJLJei2/1781600496978.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaKyBZMAwuyCyKhii1tmvv8Q1WJTDLZ4c7goKVbanZ3cg/1781600497138.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdrWQhZkMVgSALQzM8a8HHVaRCDA2EFtuhgo8f7eXk6rQ/1781600497211.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNWuhQtqaCLEsHitUwHridkaRNuGm534RFiy5S3Jcnxdk/1781600497290.jpg)

On Massena square there is a somewhat strange installation of statues in different colors on pillars \

, which was created in 2007 by the Catalan artist Jaume Plensa. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc4bm1ZnjCaSTgMUymKhtXXkgMAhUdwSvrfoaeJuCCiFW/1781600624322.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSYL8NPr3gAKabeFvFxEJMyNji4WD9NBJxPoK5B6yJokN/1781600624417.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaGYutagHVUXsBLk12fiDLeQaQT725yNHsvRniURyAToU/1781600624491.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdCeeJqMSK9bwzmUutLPdKgFmkkYDV9yKZauJYgG7DXiA/1781600624569.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWaqywEkFhRuTnPGrTnnv47ATrC6L3MpASwmnQgCacUbA/1781600624621.jpg)

The sculptures symbolize the flow of communication between the seven continents of the world. 
During the night, the sculptures light up in different colors and fade in color, which symbolizes the exchange of words.

From Massena Square, walking through the park we passed another popular fountain, especially on hot summer days, when park visitors use it to cool off a little.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSbEgG9DpbzAoMc3gYVxgeNYyYgfMNdHytnkXW713yBes/1781600668529.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUbBdw8QqbDLoeUmZpzDQ6SDuzfVNzJvJrXfXpNSWjX7m/1781600668628.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme4KLb462aMYwfZdbncuvwJ93F1V7V568JmfiFHJWiRDJ/1781600668689.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZBKX9PJCZYhBZMCeAbmVG1D72Kai3di1iPGof4tv5GQU/1781600668768.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSVCD5XBCr3CsEcGjR9jm6VkDLGh8bEgtHJKP8jPN38Tb/1781600668862.jpg)

After we freshened up a bit and wet our hands (and feet, but not on purpose 🙂), we took a break on one of the green areas.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNTUQsZZdUkx6bABHzGENqvTNpZ1B5kHqD1Aa8jfARcXE/1781600749408.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTtBR6uJtj5yKv2E2uspxmMoLjVrNWPoAq9q2Y4gjScqt/1781600749516.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYFVkzXPKCKkkwp1aPvWzdr7vaATPLEhiW5frdvQmTinZ/1781600749614.jpg)

Following the parks of this promenade, when we reached the Modern and Contemporary Art Museum, we turned to Garibaldi Square.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc6PT1CM1r395BVWg7Vw1KUEvJcKQhuK9EJJj7QU9KNRd/1781600769413.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdsMZN1oVVULmVtXtaYESk7Zhn2e59pqB31T4rMesRrXB/1781600769517.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYdc7rR6kFFe7LKv3CWsbN7DLN3dNRVzZiHK2Cybduqu2/1781600769626.jpg)

I will present a visit to this square when I write about the old town.

For now, we headed to the opposite side, to see the Basilique Notre-Dame de l'Assomption, which was closed, so we contented ourselves with taking photos and walking along the wide boulevard full of shops and buildings of interesting architecture.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmedSJJ5xiBgBVrTnoqPwH2hpMpnrhrZfc9bXKBVncaAMV/1781600820631.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSLUpniz2179JkoJW6eMMFhbUqZxMPaCaAHUDUZzddoDg/1781600820719.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRzUJoANLhoTG6eedCBraVK25dt8oTjxrNkKzur8u5EjD/1781600820786.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTC6yi696udCkhXy9BSNCkxAmHi1v3H9SaTvSJvYq177K/1781600820856.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbKBN1G1dxA4TESoKHXM2VvPwWsfRCjKj8dKCXTqzNbdq/1781600820952.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmexrDgLfSi4jm2excdhrfrA5okVi3qL3FzMyWxhr3oQXh/1781600847850.jpg)

I had the opportunity to see such narrow buildings only in Amsterdam, and I was surprised why they made them so narrow, when there was certainly free space at the time of their construction... 
Perhaps the creativity of the architects?

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSDV3XUp68MigWYpVpNPgx8hMg7pjshqML6KmBvhwig6v/1781600933581.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUFUMphF4Hap5GH6AoqAhdF3JucbxxfmQnfNCwCJejAAD/1781600933663.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXMWgrKJ6YZfjapBbkLnH6AcG69H7ZRKe18hvkk5id1HK/1781600933743.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbwR89BtoHECa2NdJjr5YhAbXpMRmCUhfNhjnfu4ChenW/1781600933811.jpg)

We went out on the promenade again at the sculpture
\

which is the work of the French artist Bernard Venet.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX1vkt7qmGZ35xVazgVMvreP1e4WdjP4F8Yy8oczByVRA/1781600992892.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcizLahWJhueTR4MKrJXucFJfKzARJcMQkMPsmMXei5oN/1781600992988.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmav2pMtF8DfsCVU1Z5XVaKiDjTcELy3zbvZRafpPt1hYg/1781600993068.jpg)

Each of the nine steel beams of this sculpture represents one of the nine valleys of the former county of Nice and the surrounding mountains that rise towards the sky. It was erected to mark the 150th anniversary of the annexation of Nice to France, which took place in 1860.

Almost like the dessert of this walk along the promenade is the moment when you head further from this sculpture past the Opera House, past the old town, and below the viewpoint on the hill you reach the position of the sundial and the favorite photo spot \

.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYKNra4aX7QXtTjosSNNU8EBtdQftQE7JFWFaFwGgXNtM/1781601052394.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZMosDPi4RRehFt2a5NoS9EXcTBbtYvHQGg1KajrDFYU6/1781601052503.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQnbmGqqQcpeJ5CB7xiHcHRK6t5WFkxcgTvBbcKL395gb/1781601052579.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPa7pG12ReVEHvt6mjwbKQaFLCdN6kTiYU2PK3pCVMEdA/1781601052677.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNkorv3swmeEVZCaxpzNLxZf2Rgw99epwFjB6oXGQgTwX/1781601052771.jpg)

The view of the open sea from here is fantastic.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZzTfVE5kxwN31Tb3TjbfvhgdrRJGKzaBMPCp6bkV2wna/1781601103485.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeTfU6oiZRr7DAhPuC7NmtKfWr4om4VKFoCiyr4MBEFpH/1781601103578.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRDNPA6icR1jQU6NDDE62jExM2RKHGvK5UVJ1Srw1JscB/1781601103666.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSpdfcdtng7mfdBkcaXeSsYyi88NsKiCdPWym9YEiV9sU/1781601103740.jpg)

Further along the coast, you will come to the Monument aux Morts de Rauba-Capeù carved into the rock, dedicated to the victims of the inhabitants of Nice in World War I (after World War II, the names of new victims were added..

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmd7VBwaDcM1S3242Upj3rUzZKvnZrCW3M1J4nNkAwTzch/1781601134774.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfUCx8YM4H3RmwnVAHjzhVcA9gwwJoYr14zsFZ9EQ6nS1/1781601134911.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSyhtXF1Ckog3nLLd4octBW8e79yjyBrvL4R84Fv4vjfq/1781601135013.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWHH2b5wqqQqkJsMXzvQpUSSyKkMTNbsN8Azdd58RrjLM/1781601135099.jpg)

And after passing the monument, you enter the area of ​​the marina and port of Lympia, where the vessels are not overly luxurious like in some other city on the Côte d'Azur.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme4CkhNNKS5mwjajmxnyqDby8iZeTk6m5eAjsRAMMS7hW/1781601175567.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWFPyKTc5TLyvuXESrsDHUE9NSkZE8WRh8wZNDDnsCFTu/1781601175694.jpg)

summary.body:
В эпоху цифровых технологий мир спортивных прогнозов претерпел колоссальные изменения. Сегодня для того, чтобы заключить пари на матч любимой команды, больше не нужно искать наземные пункты приема ставок. Все, что требуется от современного болельщика - это стабильный интернет и надежная платформа под рукой. Профессиональные игроки прекрасно знают, что качество сервиса, скорость выплат и разнообразие линий определяют конечный успех не меньше, чем глубокая аналитика самого спортивного события.

Выбор правильной площадки - это первый и самый важный шаг как для новичка, так и для опытного каппера. Надежные ресурсы стремятся предложить пользователям максимально комфортные условия: от интуитивно понятного интерфейса до круглосуточной службы поддержки. Именно на таких сайтах, как [букмекер Pinco](https://pinco-bets.kz/) , пользователи получают не просто инструмент для заключения пари, а полноценную экосистему с подробной статистикой, трансляциями и бонусами. Современный беттинг давно вышел за рамки классического футбола или хоккея. Сегодня в тренде динамичные лайв-ставки, где коэффициенты меняются каждую секунду, а также стремительно растущий сектор киберспорта. Виртуальные сражения в Counter-Strike или Dota 2 собирают миллионные аудитории, и возможность составить точный прогноз на эти дисциплины привлекает новое поколение аналитиков.

В условиях жесткой конкуренции букмекеры борются за каждого клиента, улучшая мобильные приложения и оптимизируя финансовые шлюзы для мгновенного вывода средств. Безопасность личных данных и прозрачность правил становятся главными критериями доверия. body.title: A night in Montreal, Canada
body.body:
A beautiful evening in Old Montreal 

Rue Saint-Paul 
The oldest Street in Canada 

Rue Saint-Paul (Saint Paul Street) is Montreal's oldest street, laid out in 1672 along a path that bordered the city's earliest fort. Located in Old Montreal, this iconic cobblestone street is home to historic landmarks like the Bonsecours Market and the Notre-Dame-de-Bon-Secours Chapel.

Origins: It was officially paved in 1672 and named after Paul de Chomedey de Maisonneuve, the founder of Montreal.

Lined with 19th-century stone buildings, it blends historic European charm with modern art galleries, cafes, and boutiques.

Pedestrian Access: Between April and October, parts of Rue Saint-Paul (from Boulevard Saint-Laurent to Rue du Marché-Bonsecours) are converted into a pedestrian-only zone.

body.title: [ESP/ENG] La riqueza de ser pobre / The richness of being poor
body.body: <div class=\

>Llevo días dándole vueltas a aquella visita, incapaz de sacudirme la sensación de que fui yo quien recibió un regalo mucho mayor del que fui a entregar. Fui a llevar un par de víveres y algo de ropa usada, convencido de que mi papel era el del afortunado que compartía su abundancia con un necesitado.

Pero la vida, con su inagotable sabiduría, me tenía preparada una lección que jamás imaginé: la verdadera pobreza no estaba en aquella casa inundada por las aguas caídas durante días, sino en mi propia ceguera para valorar lo esencial. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYrG587GKpkp8Dj1quDWbT37xLgnZLceefJ5NFkgrGXvN/img_20260610_wa0010.jpg) La puerta se abrió y me recibió una sonrisa limpia, sin el menor rastro de amargura. Doña Elena, así la llamaré, no tendría más de sesenta años, pero sus manos callosas hablaban de una vida de trabajo duro. Me invitó a pasar como si yo fuera un rey. la casa era sencilla, pero estaba inmaculado. Sobre una mesa de madera desvencijada, un mantel de plástico con florecillas descoloridas. Allí, en ese reducto de humildad, comenzó el milagro. No llevaba ni cinco minutos cuando me ofreció un asiento, el único que había medianamente cómodo, mientras ella se sentaba en un taburete bajo. Luego, sin preguntar si tenía sed, porque para ella la sed era una certeza que había que calmar, fue a la cocina y volvió con un vaso de agua fresca. No era agua del grifo; le había echado unas rodajas de limón y unas hojitas de hierbabuena que crecían en una maceta rota en el patio. Me explicó, casi con disculpa, que era agüita de sabor para que estuviera más rica. En ese gesto, en esa necesidad de embellecer lo poco que tenía para ofrecérmelo como un tesoro, vi más grandeza que en todas las fiestas a las que he asistido. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbjx3YMKdAZR7evPbYW1g587vxPUKDXpTsTuUdgiAFpb6/img_20260610_wa0009.jpg) Charlamos durante horas. Ella hablaba de sus hijos, que trabajaban en la ciudad y la visitaban cada quince días, con un orgullo que iluminaba la penumbra de la estancia. Hablaba de sus gallinas, a las que nombraba una por una, y de cómo compartía los huevos con la vecina que estaba enferma. Nunca mencionó carencias. No dijo me falta. Dijo tengo suficiente. Y cuando se acercó la hora de comer, me invitó a quedarme. Con mis propios ojos vi cómo convertía un puñado de frijoles, un poco de arroz y una tortilla en un festín. Partió su ración en dos y me puso la mitad más grande en el plato. Mientras comíamos, me preguntaba por mi familia, por mis preocupaciones, escuchando con una atención tan profunda que me sentí, por primera vez en mucho tiempo, verdaderamente visto. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbxbMLjNAE2dnqc2YC2JF1PwKSCZscwnCNfZN1pgQEpny/img_20260610_wa0008.jpg) Salí de allí con el corazón encogido y, a la vez, desbordado. En mi mundo, el de la \

, la gente suele medir el cariño por lo que gasta. Se confunde generosidad con derroche, y hospitalidad con ostentación. 

Doña Elena no tenía nada material que ofrecerme, y sin embargo me lo dio todo. Me regaló su tiempo, su atención sin celular que interrumpiera, su comida, su sonrisa genuina y, sobre todo, su dignidad intacta que no mendiga, sino que comparte.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma4iGnN1H4ngmcsBA9LGkj3F9HcfYaE9wZ7paowLA62eT/img_20260610_wa0007.jpg)





Esa noche comprendí que ser pobre no es no tener cosas. Es no tener esperanza, no tener solidaridad, no tener amor para dar. 

Doña Elena, con su modesta casa y su corazón de oro, era inmensamente rica. Me demostró que los valores, los sentimientos y las buenas maneras no se compran con dinero; se cultivan en el alma, a menudo con más esmero en la tierra árida de las carencias que en el jardín regado del exceso. 

Ella me dio una lección que ningún libro de autoayuda podría igualar: la verdadera riqueza consiste en tener poco que ofrecer y, aun así, ofrecerlo todo.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUV5dRxW9TtWmtApwUGgtudk2zcDF7SBZZjjjutaKwRm5/img_20260610_wa0006.jpg)



**A manera de conclusión**

La protagonista de esta publicación no me autorizó a subir fotos de ella ni de su casa. Solo me dio luz verde para publicar las imágenes de su vivienda anegada en agua y, eso, después de mucho pedirle autorización y conocer el motivo de mi petición.

*Nota: Utilicé el traductor DeepL Translate*.
*Las imágenes las tomé con mi teléfono Samsung J2*.



***ENGLISH***

I've been turning that visit over in my mind for days, unable to shake the feeling that I was the one who received a far greater gift than the one I went to give. I went to deliver a few groceries and some used clothes, convinced that my role was that of the fortunate one sharing his abundance with someone in need.

But life, with its inexhaustible wisdom, had a lesson in store for me that I never imagined: true poverty wasn't in that house flooded by the rains that had fallen for days, but in my own blindness to what truly matters.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYrG587GKpkp8Dj1quDWbT37xLgnZLceefJ5NFkgrGXvN/img_20260610_wa0010.jpg)

The door opened and I was greeted by a genuine smile, without the slightest trace of bitterness. Doña Elena, as I'll call her, couldn't have been more than sixty, but her calloused hands spoke of a life of hard work. She invited me in as if I were a king. The house was simple, but immaculate. On a rickety wooden table lay a plastic tablecloth with faded flowers. There, in that bastion of humility, the miracle began.

I hadn't been there five minutes when she offered me a seat, the only one that was even remotely comfortable, while she sat down on a low stool. Then, without asking if I was thirsty—because for her, thirst was a certainty that had to be quenched—she went to the kitchen and returned with a glass of fresh water. It wasn't tap water; she'd added some lemon slices and a few sprigs of mint that grew in a broken pot in the patio. She explained, almost apologetically, that it was flavored water to make it taste better. In that gesture, in that need to embellish the little she had and offer it to me like a treasure, I saw greater grandeur than in all the parties I've ever attended.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbjx3YMKdAZR7evPbYW1g587vxPUKDXpTsTuUdgiAFpb6/img_20260610_wa0009.jpg)

We talked for hours. She spoke of her children, who worked in the city and visited her every two weeks, with a pride that illuminated the dimness of the room. She spoke of her chickens, naming them one by one, and how she shared her eggs with the neighbor who was sick. She never mentioned any lack. She didn't say \
She said \

And when lunchtime approached, she invited me to stay.

With my own eyes, I saw her transform a handful of beans, some rice, and a tortilla into a feast. She divided her portion in two and placed the larger half on my plate. As we ate, she asked about my family, about my worries, listening with such deep attention that I felt, for the first time in a long time, truly seen.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbxbMLjNAE2dnqc2YC2JF1PwKSCZscwnCNfZN1pgQEpny/img_20260610_wa0008.jpg)

I left there with a heavy heart, yet overflowing with joy. In my world, the world of \

people often measure affection by what they spend. Generosity is confused with extravagance, and hospitality with ostentation. Doña Elena had nothing material to offer me, and yet she gave me everything. She gave me her time, her uninterrupted attention, her food, her genuine smile, and above all, her undiminished dignity, which doesn't beg, but shares. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma4iGnN1H4ngmcsBA9LGkj3F9HcfYaE9wZ7paowLA62eT/img_20260610_wa0007.jpg) That night I understood that being poor isn't about lacking things. It's about lacking hope, lacking solidarity, lacking love to give. Doña Elena, with her modest house and her heart of gold, was immensely rich. She showed me that values, feelings, and good manners can't be bought with money; they are cultivated in the soul, often with more care in the arid land of want than in the irrigated garden of excess. She taught me a lesson no self-help book could ever match: true wealth lies in having little to offer and yet offering everything. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUV5dRxW9TtWmtApwUGgtudk2zcDF7SBZZjjjutaKwRm5/img_20260610_wa0006.jpg) **In conclusion** The subject of this post did not authorize me to upload photos of herself or her house. She only gave me permission to publish the images of her flooded home, and even then, only after much pleading and understanding of the reason for my request. *Note: I used DeepL Translate*. *The images were taken with my Samsung J2 phone*.

body.title: The Rampage of Joker.
body.body:
https://play.3speak.tv/embed?v=yakubnoyon/89zj19d5

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVRPJo7n5jhe44xkdojaJzLNcPjUuQhhXyJXEuyr8qfVr/gaming_photography_2_.gif)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfLkCbX8HdtmDTH7X24hr1zWN22iroqEQdFS7dn5PdFhU/snapshot.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRhWwoVKvtk49EB1x3CrbD5aeaAzL8zJ2n8h2wRKzbRTb/snapshot_1.png)

In the last episode, we saw Batman captured by Scarecrow and injected with a deadly fear toxin. Immediately after that, we arrive at a scene where Batman does not exist.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaGsmZBmaAgLCv3cx7v7Yc4iArbHotjRHwoJ6s3TGBYv8/snapshot_2.png)

There, Penguin, Two-Face and Riddler are having fun by trapping the Joker and planning to kill him. Just then, the unconscious Joker regains consciousness. He is not afraid at all, but starts reacting in his familiar style. In this part, the Joker's dialogue and acting were so energetic that it felt like I was watching a movie, not a game.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSvHzdrqAtwkUSpeN776pQDjBqS6WmoKTTBZ4KLLzGKBr/snapshot_3.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRqM2eV1LDrvSkMPnJyhVTVMSkPEXb2m88t7CV3Du2XtK/snapshot_4.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmS3yrj87GCLVeWA8wdr4efSRqUHL27fk3Qb4Yk9bSwPjj/snapshot_5.png)

Meanwhile, the Jokermobile makes a dramatic entry. Yes, friends, we have been driving the Batmobile for so long, and today the Jokermobile appears on the screen. The look of the car was terrifyingly beautiful. As you can see in the picture, I personally like its getup. Not only in looks, but it will surpass the Batmobile in firing power as well.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSL6qzbAHvsquFseFoZXxFvjXAoPEStPy7BPohbUZ7Lnn/snapshot_6.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNnabeB2w69BAyJ5JJQVbTcH8vLcLjhpQQzKZdtWKebGi/snapshot_7.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXsvZoKvHxNL8mWdKnc1ZVj8tZXDnLNfTqkhbv6cGa9M4/snapshot_8.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUjsmXkuQgNnM5FXiN3P2gXowwmQxVGxULnN2Gw96H2Jm/snapshot_9.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZhXKRN8NpXDVepxYHkvrxnDVGuEwdknCDXewJ6mFZbWm/snapshot_10.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQpXAidcwgdMjVthAoGfy4d2wF7hF2ELkW6EneHkwqbZu/snapshot_11.png)

Joker got into the car and started shooting at the military soldiers around him. Even though they fired grenades and bullets, nothing happened to the car. On the contrary, the entire area was reduced to rubble with each shot from the Joker mobile's cannon. The most interesting thing is that while the Batmobile can fire 5 missiles at a time, I fired about 50 selective missiles at a time from this Joker mobile. Believe me, I've just become a fan. If only Batman had the car.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNvZ4Tbp2fYMjQNdMnNm8q8ajAB5PxXQhmivGVCPnB71u/snapshot_12.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfQvpkoqPktXG2MqBw9UPoQsxyk3A6akpn5AF98gHfp2D/snapshot_13.png)

After killing all the soldiers around him, Joker got out of the car and started walking through a closed corridor. First, he met Penguin. He was begging Joker for his life by showing him money. But you know what? This is Joker. He didn't even give Penguin a chance to speak, he finished him off right there with a direct shot.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYBTNmvamrxarNqK1uBeyCGqxK1qziFsD8KuYnpvsFvLw/snapshot_14.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWfcudMKGAt862546C3Kep6BEpztLDdd3YwrrNevv3D5x/snapshot_15.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXBw5KojEU1VqCyXQ8pdrDT37KHtqJEipSpPvFxFRNmsd/snapshot_16.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWjvS3gHCv5VS5SwtUuSkqN7EmZkV7B6hWgjU94YyTFJt/snapshot_17.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZsu2Y7ifXMLsaWtjkYAYE7RW5vSoCHUVXHDDFZ3cosi2/snapshot_18.png)

As he moves forward, he sees the Riddler and Two-Face. The Riddler is holding a woman hostage and threatening the Joker, \

The Joker just laughs and opens fire. Well, both the Riddler and the woman are dead on the spot. Then the same thing happens to Two-Face, the Joker shoots him too and opens the door and comes out. When he comes out, he sees the entire Gotham City on fire, just like the Joker had dreamed.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVFv4vUT5yuZV2tmb1bYQEKsywjhnsDXoyqC3WMrU9nNC/snapshot_19.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma3KHkYVT4NkYi3NcfJ7VANPYrcnqT2Pjmj5Eu1Na2V1i/snapshot_20.png)

This is where the cutscene ends and we return to the real scene of Arkham Asylum. But this time the twist is that the Joker is imprisoned in the chair instead of Batman. Scarecrow tries to scare him in various ways, but the Joker keeps laughing like crazy. This makes Scarecrow extremely angry and pushes more fear toxin into the Joker's body. And then the whole atmosphere changes and the surroundings start getting dark.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWhsJuc6fBUExQZWcYXgesdwBwxySLT7EGWpTfyiPHZY7/snapshot_21.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYwhCvwnHFF1JniXMQDXsn3EjX1piZ2RVcp4hDGB7Vruj/snapshot_22.png)

Joker realizes that this time it's Batman himself coming towards him. He welcomes Batman. Just then, everything goes black. When Joker turns on his gun's light, he sees himself walking into a safe room and in front of him is a huge picture. There, Batman is seen standing with the Joker's dead body in his hands. 

---

* **Thank you for reading. See you all on my next blog.**

body.title: Apartment Moving Checklist: Everything You Need Before Moving Day\n
body.body:
Moving into a new apartment can be exciting, but without proper planning, it can also become overwhelming very quickly. Between packing, organizing paperwork, coordinating schedules, and preparing for moving day, there are many details that homeowners and renters often overlook.

Creating a clear apartment moving checklist is one of the best ways to stay organized and reduce unnecessary stress. With the right preparation and help from experienced professionals like Relief Movers, apartment moves can become far more efficient and manageable.

Whether you are moving across town or relocating to another city, this complete checklist will help ensure you are fully prepared before moving day arrives.

## 6-8 Weeks Before Moving Day

Starting early gives you enough time to organize every step without feeling rushed.

### Create a Moving Plan

Begin by outlining important tasks such as:

*   Setting a moving budget

*   Choosing your moving date

*   Organizing paperwork

*   Researching professional movers

*   Notifying your landlord if required

If you are searching for the [best movers in Woodbury](https://reliefmovers.com/woodbury-mn/), working with a reliable company early helps secure your preferred moving schedule and avoids last-minute availability issues.

### Declutter Your Apartment

Apartment moves are the perfect opportunity to reduce clutter and avoid transporting items you no longer need.

Separate belongings into:

*   Keep

*   Donate

*   Sell

*   Recycle

*   Discard

Decluttering can lower moving costs and make unpacking much easier in your new apartment.

## 4-6 Weeks Before Moving Day

As moving day approaches, focus on packing preparation and service arrangements.

### Gather Packing Supplies

Stock up on quality materials, including:

*   Moving boxes

*   Packing tape

*   Bubble wrap

*   Packing paper

*   Labels and markers

*   Furniture covers

Using durable supplies helps protect your belongings during transportation.

### Book Professional Movers

Hiring experienced movers early can save time and reduce stress significantly. Professional local movers St Paul, MN residents trust can assist with:

*   Heavy lifting

*   Furniture protection

*   Efficient loading and unloading

*   Transportation logistics

Relief Movers helps apartment residents move safely and efficiently while minimizing disruptions throughout the process.

## 2-4 Weeks Before Moving Day

This stage is ideal for handling administrative updates and beginning the packing process.

### Update Your Address

Notify important contacts and services about your new address, including:

*   Banks

*   Insurance providers

*   Employers

*   Subscription services

*   Government records

You should also arrange mail forwarding through your postal service.

### Transfer Utilities

Schedule utility transfers or set up appointments for:

*   Electricity

*   Water

*   Internet

*   Gas

*   Trash collection

Completing these tasks early helps ensure your new apartment is ready when you arrive.

### Begin Packing Non-Essentials

Start packing items you do not use daily, such as:

*   Seasonal clothing

*   Decorations

*   Books

*   Extra kitchenware

Packing gradually reduces last-minute pressure and keeps the process organized.

## 1 Week Before Moving Day

The final week is all about preparing for a smooth transition.

### Confirm Moving Details

Double-check all arrangements with your movers, including:

*   Arrival times

*   Parking access

*   Building regulations

*   Elevator reservations

Apartment buildings often have specific moving requirements, so confirming details ahead of time can prevent delays.

### Label Boxes Clearly

Clearly mark each box with:

*   Room destination

*   Contents

*   Fragile instructions

Organized labeling helps movers place boxes efficiently and simplifies unpacking later.

### Pack an Essentials Box

Prepare a separate box or bag with items you will need immediately after the move, including:

*   Toiletries

*   Medications

*   Chargers

*   Important documents

*   Snacks

*   Basic kitchen items

*   A few changes of clothes

Keeping essentials accessible prevents unnecessary frustration during your first night in the new apartment.

## Moving Day Checklist

A little preparation on moving day itself can make the experience far smoother.

### Protect Your Apartment

Before movers arrive:

*   Cover floors if necessary

*   Protect doorways and walls

*   Keep hallways clear

*   Secure pets in a safe area

This helps avoid damage and keeps the moving process efficient.

### Do a Final Walkthrough

Before leaving your old apartment:

*   Check closets and cabinets

*   Inspect storage spaces

*   Confirm windows are closed

*   Turn off the lights

*   Return keys if required

A final walkthrough ensures nothing important gets left behind.

### Communicate With Movers

Stay available to answer questions and provide directions during loading and unloading.

Working with the best movers in Woodbury can help streamline the entire process while reducing physical strain and moving-related stress.

## After Arriving at Your New Apartment

Once you arrive, focus on settling in gradually instead of rushing through everything at once.

### Unpack Essentials First

Start with:

*   Bedroom items

*   Bathroom supplies

*   Kitchen basics

Setting up key living spaces first helps make the apartment feel comfortable more quickly.

### Inspect Your Belongings

Check furniture and boxes for any damage during transportation and notify movers promptly if necessary.

### Get Familiar With the Building

Take time to locate:

*   Emergency exits

*   Parking areas

*   Mailboxes

*   Trash disposal areas

*   Building amenities

Getting comfortable with your new environment helps make the transition easier.

## Final Thoughts

Apartment moves involve many details, but proper planning can make the experience far less stressful. Following a detailed checklist helps homeowners and renters stay organized, avoid common mistakes, and prepare confidently for moving day.

Whether you are searching for trusted [local movers that St. Paul, MN](https://reliefmovers.com/saint-paul-mn/) residents rely on or looking for the best movers in Woodbury, Relief Movers provides dependable moving services designed to simplify apartment relocations from start to finish.

With the right preparation and professional support, your next apartment move can be smooth, organized, and stress-free.

body.title: With one million my future is secured
body.body:
I can’t imagine myself winning $1 million; it will be a dream come true. The majority of people will go for a luxurious lifestyle, spending the money on expensive cars, shopping, and so on. To be honest, there is nothing wrong with spending a little of the money; a million dollars is capable of changing someone's life if the person has proper planning. I will not lie; seeing a one-million-dollar drop in my account will be the best day of my life. I will be so excited. Here comes the main thing: I will focus and make decisions that I will benefit from for a long period of time rather than spending the money to support a soft life.





Even before the $1 million drop in my account, I had a lot of things on my mind, but what was holding me was capital, to be honest. Having such a sum in my account, I would be tempted to spend the money, but the best thing I can do at the moment is avoid making sudden purchases. According to history, many people who win the lottery end up losing the money because they spend too quickly. When it comes to me, I will take my time and make a decision because if I make the wrong decision, it will affect me in the future.



![D15C3E10-2CAA-47EB-8A2F-7839F131A541.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cindynancy/242YGaXkpLB8FrCYAouXepYJ4sdHmd9AWFStcjKzdqJkrDW1DTDExncFyE6KFX6axXzsF.png)



It has always been my desire and wish to have my own fashion house. Since I was a child, I have always had a passion for fashion. Winning this huge amount of money will really mean a lot to me; it will be a dream come true for me. It is not just a fashion house but also a beauty home. With that amount of money, my fashion house will be one of the best in town; it will be well equipped. There is this inner joy that I will have when people wear my brand. I am not only after making money; I am also going to train people who have passion for fashion.



Next is my family; I will make sure that my family is secure because they are the foundation of my life, and setting them up is one of my priorities. If my family is okay, my mind will be at peace. With the money, I will make sure they live a comfortable life; they don’t have to stress themselves to get anything they want.







Education is the next place I will invest my money. Knowledge is power; with knowledge, it will help me generate value for a lifetime. Learning never ends. I will use part of the money for new skills because the world is becoming digital and I need to top up. One thing about me is I am not selfish; I will help people I can extend hands to. I give people scholarships and help the old and the sick. People are really suffering, even if it means giving a small percentage of $1 million will really make a difference in the lives of people, just like some groups in the #hiveghana community are doing some community projects. I will also do that for my community. The money is not just only for me; I should be able to change lives with the money.




![5EA2930E-1125-42A3-BF95-FBB6D45113E0.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cindynancy/243zkFpbHFSfbssZKBngz4zMTnCFVde1RvR8Tu141ZaFcUuQBC8HDH4N7mt8Y1vrG6Tui.png)



After I have planned my future, the remaining money should be for my personal enjoyment. Building my finances does not mean I should never enjoy the rewards of my success. There are places in my mind I have always longed to travel to, explore different things and food, and create memories that I will not forget. The best thing is to balance it, enjoying life while still planning for the future.





Lastly, I will never stop pursuing my ambition and goals. Winning $1 million will not stop me from working, nor will it make me abandon my dreams. Money can provide opportunities and freedom. For me, winning $1 million tomorrow is not all about creating riches; it will be an opportunity to create stability and build myself. It all depends on how wisely we spend the money.





This is my response to the weekly prompt #IndiaUnited topic. What Would You Do If You Won $1 Million Tomorrow?



Thank you for stopping by my blog. I appreciate your comments, support, and upvotes. Do have a lovely evening.

body.title: Batman: Arkham Asylum [Let's Play] - 02
body.body: *Joker seems to not want to leave the Asylum! Well, he did take it over, after all... Still, this \

he keeps referring to... Can't be anything good!*

-----

**[Batman: Arkham Asylum](https://store.steampowered.com/sub/320795/)** is *the* superhero game! Set within the walls of Gotham's infamous psychiatric hospital, the game follows Batman as he fights through hordes of escaped inmates and iconic villains to stop Joker's sinister plan. 

**Arkham Asylum**'s [combat system](https://arkhamcity.fandom.com/wiki/Freeflow_Combat) makes you feel like a true martial arts master. The game also introduces stealth mechanics using Batman's full arsenal of gadgets and one of the first games to feature a Detective Mode button.


 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmYdkQELS1qtcr4Q3wtxoMnJt7dijhDrTRFPUsMSQMC1ZQ/batman-arkham-asylum-wallpaper.webp 


I wanted to play this game for years and only got to it now... It's actually my brother who bought it for his Steam account, which made finally experiencing it myself. . Arkham Asylum didn't disappoint! I really love the combat system, and I'm impressed that Arkham Asylum is supposed to have the weakest version of it..., If this is the \

it gets, then I can't wait to see how the sequels refine it further. The game absolutely made me feel like Batman!

While I'd recommend this game to any Batman (or really, any action-adventure game) fan, the stealth missions weren't as easy. As soon as I was found out, I was dead. Still, it makes me feel great when I finally overcome the challenge!! Funnily enough, the Scarecrow missions weren't very bad compared to normal stealth missions with mob enemies...

I love how Batman tools are introduced graudally, giving players a lot of time to adapt to each one. It also made me know what's the most likely tool to use in a puzzle: always the newest aquired tool! It wasn't easy to switch between tools mid-combat, though, so I fought mostly bare-handed~
